author: euron8
body:
Bundle B — items 5 and 6c. Both change emitted text in `ledger-reverify.sh`; neither touches the boundary parser extracted in #235, so its byte-identical proof stays intact.

## A close row named the tip, not the release that absorbed the entry

`ledger-reverify.sh` emitted "upstream absorbed this at `$TV`", where:

```sh
TV="$(theirs_show VERSION | tr -d '[:space:]')"
```

That is `VERSION` at **theirs** — the tip being pulled, unrelated to when the substring arrived. The operator copies the string straight into `ADOPTED UPSTREAM (v…)`, and retro and the §8.1 fan-in read it afterwards, so a wrong version is permanent.

Measured on the reference consumer: PC-S298's substring first appears at **v0.144.0**. The tool reported `0.147.0`. A hand correction filed against it said `0.146.0` — derived by sampling the three refs already loaded rather than walking the history, and wrong in the same direction. Three releases apart, in a record nothing re-derives.

New `absorbed_at()` resolves first appearance with `git log -S … --reverse` bounded to `base..theirs`, then reads `VERSION` at that commit.

**Bounded deliberately:** searching all history would attribute a substring that was removed and later re-introduced to its *original* commit, which is a different claim than "the pull you are looking at absorbed it". Falls back to `$TV` when nothing is found — a relocated path, a rewritten line — because a close row with no version is worse than one carrying the tip's. ~20ms, and only on close rows.

**Demonstrated on live data:** the entry this session closed in 0.150.0 was being annotated `0.151.0`; it now reads `0.150.0`.

## A markdown-formatted receipt read as an unknown verb — or worse

The ledger is prose an operator writes, so a receipt arrives code-formatted as often as not. Two forms, breaking differently:

| form | what it leaves | old result |
|---|---|---|
| `` verify: `theirs_lacks` … `` | a LEADING backtick on the verb | `unknown verify verb` |
| `` `verify: theirs_lacks … "sub"` `` | a CLOSING backtick on the directive | substring never matches |

The first filed a markdown habit under the same banner as a typo — the exact conflation the `manual` verb was added to eliminate. Four directives on the reference consumer are written that way.

**Fixing only the verb would have been actively worse than leaving it alone.** The verb would dispatch, the trailing backtick would still be glued to the quoted substring, the comparison would silently miss, and a loud unknown-verb report would become a quiet `STILL-LIVE`. The fixture caught this — my first attempt fixed only the verb and the new assertion went `STILL-LIVE`.

Both ends of the verb and the end of the directive are stripped now. The header documents the tolerance rather than asking operators to write receipts that satisfy the parser: *do not write receipts to satisfy the parser; write them and let it cope.*

## Fixture

Four new assertions, and a **mid-history commit added to the seed**. Base and theirs were adjacent, so "name the tip" and "name the truth" produced the same string — the version claim was untestable by construction. The seed now absorbs `MARKER_B` at 0.101.0 and moves theirs on to 0.102.0.

The two backtick forms are asserted **separately**, because they exercise different code. The whole-span form leaves the verb clean, so it passes even with the old trailing-only verb strip in place — which is exactly how the verb half nearly shipped unguarded.

Mutants: reverting `absorbed_at` to `$TV` turns the version assertion red; reverting the verb strip to trailing-only turns the BV assertion red; deleting the directive strip turns the BT assertion red.

## One note for anyone editing that awk body

It is a single-quoted shell string, so a comment containing an apostrophe closes it. Cost one syntax error here; there is now a `NOTE no apostrophes in this block` line.

## Verification

`.githooks/pre-push`: **all gates green**, no `--no-verify`.

author: jjackson
body:
## Summary

Implements the [directed runner routing design](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-directed-runner-routing-design.md): with three runners now paired (two laptop emdash accounts + an EC2 cloud runner), routing gets one explicit source of truth and standbys become testable without stealing live work.

- **`RunnerAssignment`** — per-agent ordered runner list, THE routing authority for agent turns (replaces `capabilities.agents` + kind-level `runner_preference`, now deprecated). Availability cascade: highest-ranked online+ready runner claims; lower ranks take over on unavailability or after a 60s anti-wedge grace. Empty list = explicitly unroutable. Seed migration converts today's live state (all agents → jj-mbp-cdp rank 0), so **behavior is unchanged at cutover**.
- **`Turn.pinned_runner`** — hard pins claimable only by the pinned runner (never bypasses tenancy or the one-executing-turn constraints). Producers: drills, chat wait/continue, directed session starts.
- **Session stickiness** — chat turns claim only on the session's `RunnerBinding` holder; if the holder is unavailable, the turn waits for an explicit placement (chat banner: *Wait for it* / *Continue on…*). New chats get a "Run on" picker; placements are tenant- and sessions-capability-gated.
- **Readiness drills** — `POST /runners/{id}/drill` fans out one read-only doctor turn per assigned agent, pinned to that runner; agents report pass/fail via a callback that itself proves control-plane reachability. Per-pair `RunnerDrill` grid + rollup badge on `/supervisor`.
- **Routing matrix UI** — per-agent ranked runner chips (reorder/add/remove, optimistic with commit serialization) on `/supervisor` and the agent overview, replacing the kind-based `RunnerOrder`.

## Rollout notes

- Migrations are additive + an idempotent seed; deploy-safe on labs (verified against the fleet shape: five agents, one capability-bearing runner).
- One deliberate behavior change independent of assignments: a bound chat session whose holder is offline now **waits for user placement** instead of being claimed by any sessions-capable runner.

## Testing

- Backend: 1125 passed, 1 skipped (new suites: routing cascade, pins, stickiness, drills, assignments API, placement incl. malformed/foreign-tenant/sessions-incapable 422s).
- Frontend: 243 tests passed (new: RunnerAssignments incl. out-of-order-commit race, RunnerDrills incl. poll resilience, ChatSessionsPanel stale-fetch race); `npm run build` green; `generated.ts` verified in sync.
- Built task-by-task with per-task spec+quality reviews and a final whole-branch review; all findings fixed (placement UUID validation, runner-visibility scoping on assignment/placement surfaces, optimistic-UI races).

author: mrveiss
body:
Closes #12408

## Thinking Path
`POST /patterns/storage/clear` → `clear_patterns()` had NO source filter: it fetched every id in the shared `code_patterns` ChromaDB collection (`collection.get(limit=count)`) and deleted all of them (`collection.delete(ids=...)`). One source's "clear" wiped every other source's (and AutoBot's own) stored patterns — a cross-source destructive data-loss bug. #12405 already added `build_source_scoped_where()` and scoped every *read* endpoint (`search_similar_patterns`, `get_pattern_stats`, `get_cached_patterns`, `get_cached_pattern_summary`) to `source_id`; this PR mirrors that same scoping onto the one remaining unscoped, destructive write path.

I verified `collection.delete(where=...)` is natively supported end-to-end by every backend adapter this codebase uses (`chromadb_adapter.py`, `async_chromadb_adapter.py`, `memory_adapter.py` all forward `where` straight to the underlying store's delete), so the fix uses a direct scoped `delete(where=...)` rather than a get-ids-then-delete round trip — simpler, and avoids the SQL-variable-limit concern that only applies to large `ids=[...]` IN-lists (not `where` filters).

## What Changed
- `code_intelligence/pattern_analysis/storage.py` `clear_patterns()` (~L515): now takes `source_id: str | None = None`, builds `where_filter = build_source_scoped_where(source_id)`, and calls `collection.delete(where=where_filter)` — scoped to exactly one source's patterns instead of the whole collection.
- **Missing-`source_id` decision:** omitting `source_id` resolves to the `"default"` sentinel scope via `build_source_scoped_where(None) == {"source_id": "default"}` — identical to every sibling `/patterns/*` endpoint's existing convention (`get_pattern_storage_stats`, `search_similar_patterns_endpoint`, `get_cached_patterns`, `get_cached_pattern_summary`). This is the safe option: a caller that forgets to pass `source_id` clears only the "default"-tagged patterns, **never** every source. Requiring `source_id` (400 without it) would have been inconsistent with every other endpoint in this file, so I matched the established convention instead.
- `api/codebase_analytics/endpoints/pattern_analysis.py` `clear_pattern_storage()` (~L727): now accepts `source_id: str | None = Query(default=None, ...)` like its siblings, and threads it into `clear_patterns(source_id=source_id)`.
- **Sentinel-asymmetry fix (flagged in #12405 review):** `_prepare_pattern_metadata()` and its single-pattern sibling `_build_single_pattern_metadata()` both defaulted `source_id` to `"default"` for the ID hash (via `_prepare_pattern_data`/`_build_single_pattern_data`) but NOT for the stored metadata dict — so a caller that omitted `source_id` produced a record whose id was hashed with `"default"` but whose metadata had no `source_id` key at all, making it invisible to `build_source_scoped_where`'s equality filter (id/metadata mismatch, fail-closed-invisible). Both functions now default `source_id` to `"default"` in the metadata splat too, so id and metadata always agree.

## Verification
```
$ python3 -m pytest code_intelligence/pattern_analysis/source_scoping_test.py code_intelligence/pattern_analysis/clear_patterns_source_scoping_test.py -p no:xdist -q
collected 15 items

code_intelligence/pattern_analysis/source_scoping_test.py ...........    [ 73%]
code_intelligence/pattern_analysis/clear_patterns_source_scoping_test.py . [ 80%]
...                                                                      [100%]

======================== 15 passed, 1 warning in 0.79s =========================
```
New tests (`clear_patterns_source_scoping_test.py`) prove:
- `clear_patterns(source_id="A")` deletes ONLY A's patterns; B's patterns remain intact (the core destructive-isolation regression test).
- Omitting `source_id` resolves to the `"default"` sentinel scope and does NOT wipe A or B's patterns.
- The scoped delete goes through `collection.delete(where=build_source_scoped_where(...))`, never an unfiltered wipe.
- The endpoint signature threads `source_id` through.

All 11 pre-existing #12405 source-scoping tests still pass (no regression).

## Model Used
Claude Opus 4.8

author: denisvmedia
body:
## Summary

Bumps the pinned ptah to the merged **Flyway parser** for `ptah migrations import` (stokaro/ptah#667 Phase 3) and adds a `flyway/import-roundtrip` migrate-runtime probe next to the golang-migrate and Goose ones.

## Probe

`flyway/import-roundtrip` imports a Flyway source directory chosen to exercise Flyway's distinctive shapes and asserts the emitted Ptah directory passes `ptah migrations validate`:

- a **dotted version** (`V1.1__…`, reassigned to a sequential Ptah version with the original folded into the name),
- an **undo** (`U1__…`, imported as the versioned migration's down),
- a **repeatable** (`R__…`, imported as a one-time migration ordered after the versioned ones — Ptah has no repeatable concept).

Three source migrations produce six Ptah files. The shared `importRoundtripProbe` helper now takes the expected imported-file count so it serves fixtures of any size (the earlier probes still pass 4).

## Reports

All committed reports are regenerated against the new pin. The only substantive change is one new `flyway/import-roundtrip` OK row in the migrate-runtime report (11 → 12 observations); every other report change is the version header. Regenerated with postgres 18, mysql 8, and mariadb 10.11 (live) so the DB-gated observations are preserved. PARITY.md notes Flyway import coverage.

## Summary

- add a reproducible four-profile market-maker soak runbook and isolated
  Compose overlay

  and PauseAndCancel outage/recovery runs
- enforce source/image/workload compatibility, runtime continuity,
  mandatory metric presence, monotonic counters, exact quote state, and
  secret-safe collection
- add CI rendering/self-tests without adding a multi-hour test to normal
  CI
- document cloud-neutral OTLP/Azure Monitor mappings, panels, alerts,
  thresholds, evidence schema, cleanup, and attachment workflow

## Evidence integrity

- acceptance suites must begin with a clean-checkout build and pin the
  resulting image identities to the recorded Git SHA
- all later profiles must match the suite workload/config/image manifest
- unexpected service restarts, monitor death, missing metrics, counter
  resets, quote gaps, cleanup failures, or path escapes fail the run
- PauseAndCancel proves stale-cache rejection, zero-quote outage hold,
  halted submissions, feed-driven cancels, fresh recovery, and continued
  freshness for every configured symbol
- passwords/tokens are not passed through process arguments or inherited
  child environments

## Validation

- 252 `B3.Trading.MarketMakerBot.Tests` tests passed
- all four profile renders/dry-runs and helper self-tests passed
- bounded baseline and PauseAndCancel smokes passed
- accelerated strict-freshness smoke kept every symbol eligible

body: Disclaimer: I used Claude/LLM to help with this. After start playing a video with FreeTube app, I see the indicator showing the entries being duplicated, sometimes more than once. author: tylercarper
body:
## Bug

The **INTERNET / P95** figures on each probe card never updated when the dashboard time range changed — they should reflect only the selected window's data.

**Two causes:**
- **Server**: `/probes` computed p50/p95 over a hardcoded *last-10-minutes* window ending `now`, ignoring any range.
- **Client**: `renderSources()` fetched `/probes` with no window params.

## Fix
- `/probes` accepts optional `from_ts`/`to_ts` and computes the percentiles over that window (defaults to the last 10 min ending now when omitted — the initial-load / other-caller behavior is unchanged).
- `renderSources()` passes the current `windowBounds()`. `renderAll()` already re-runs it on every window change, so the cards now recalculate from only the selected range.

## Verification
API confirms distinct windows → distinct figures & sample counts:

| Window | sim-wired p50/p95 | n |
|---|---|---|
| Full 7 days | 12.0 / 18.6 | 61,161 |
| Last 2 minutes | 9.5 / 20.2 | 100 |
| 1h, 5 days ago | 11.9 / 18.1 | 360 |

Confirmed in-browser that switching 24h → 7d updates every card. New test feeds two time-separated latency clusters and asserts each window reports its own. Cache-bust → `v=5`. 305 tests green.

author: exocognosis
body:
## Issue Addressed

Closes #6687.

Remote monitoring currently obtains `SystemHealth` through `SystemHealth::observe()`, which always asks `psutil` for disk capacity at `/`. Operators who place the beacon node or validator client data directory on a separate filesystem therefore receive `disk_node_bytes_total` and `disk_node_bytes_free` values for the root filesystem instead of the filesystem that can actually run out of space.

## Proposed Changes

- Add `observe_system_health(&Path)` so callers can select the path used for disk capacity collection.
- Preserve `SystemHealth::observe()` as the root-filesystem behavior used by existing HTTP health and Prometheus endpoints.
- Add an optional data-directory path to remote monitoring configuration.
- Pass the resolved beacon node data directory and validator directory into their respective remote monitoring clients.
- Retain `/` as the fallback when an older serialized monitoring configuration has no data-directory field.
- Include the selected path in disk-usage errors to make configuration failures diagnosable.
- Document that remote disk capacity metrics describe the filesystem containing the configured data directory.
- Add tests for configured path selection, root fallback, and deserialization of older monitoring configurations. A Linux-only collector test verifies that errors identify the requested path.

This keeps the behavior change limited to remote monitoring. The `/lighthouse/health` and Prometheus endpoints continue to report their existing root-filesystem values.

## Additional Info

`psutil::disk::disk_usage` resolves capacity for the filesystem containing the supplied path, so no mount-point discovery or platform-specific parsing is required.

Only the total and free capacity fields are path-specific. Existing disk I/O counters remain system-wide. Beacon node freezer or blob databases placed on other filesystems are also outside this issue's single-datadir scope.

PR #7421 addresses the same issue with a broader change to HTTP health endpoints and remains blocked by an unsafe temporary-directory lifetime. This proposal avoids that lifetime problem and focuses on the remote-monitoring behavior requested by the issue.

Validation completed:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test --locked -p health_metrics -p monitoring_api --lib`
- `cargo check --locked -p beacon_node -p validator_client`
- `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p health_metrics -p monitoring_api -p beacon_node -p validator_client --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::uninlined-format-args`

A workspace-wide all-target Clippy attempt also reaches existing lint failures in unrelated dependency crates on the current `unstable` head. The package-only command above keeps all warnings denied for the four affected crates.

Development note: AI assistance was used during implementation. The final patch was reviewed against every monitoring configuration call site and validated with the commands above.

author: christopherdavenport
body:
Follow-up to #1. Two commits: the first fixes `allOf` marshaling, the second closes the one hole in the generator's safety contract and clears four gaps that were documented rather than fixed.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Breaking: the minimum Go version moves to 1.24** (from 1.22), for `omitzero`. The CI matrix moves to `["1.24", "stable"]`. Ubuntu 24.04's apt tops out at 1.22, so contributors on distro Go will need an upgrade or `GOTOOLCHAIN`.

---

# Part 1 — Merge `allOf` parts when marshaling

Go's field promotion cannot express two of the compositions `allOf` allows, and v0.0.2 handled one of them by refusing the composition outright — which threw away the other members' promoted fields with it.

**Two members declaring the same property.** Both parts get an `ID` field at depth 1, the promoted name is ambiguous, and `encoding/json` omits it entirely — so the composed type could not read back its own output:

```
unmarshal {"id":"1","x":"xx","y":"yy"}  →  A.ID="1", B.ID="1"
marshal                                 →  {"x":"xx","y":"yy"}       // id gone
re-unmarshal that output                →  error: missing required property "id"
```

**A dictionary member.** `{"type":"object","additionalProperties":…}` generates a named map, and an embedded non-struct field marshals *under its type name*: `{"id":"1","Dict":{…}}` instead of one flat object.

Composed types now generate a `MarshalJSON` that marshals each part separately and flattens the results, via a new `xvalid.MergeObjects`. Parts are passed in precedence order — own properties, struct parts in `allOf` order, then dictionary parts — and the first writer of a key wins, so a shared property is emitted once and a dictionary fills only what no declared property claimed.

```
allOf: [Base{id,name}, Audit{id,createdBy}, Extras{additionalProperties}] + own {own}
in   {"id":"1","name":"n","createdBy":"me","own":"o","extra":"e"}
out  {"own":"o","id":"1","name":"n","createdBy":"me","extra":"e"}     // and reads back
```

With marshaling fixed, `embeddableMember` accepts any object schema again, so **the promoted fields v0.0.2 removed are back**. Members with nothing to contribute to the parent object — a scalar, array, union, enum, `x-go` override, unresolvable `$ref` — are still refused, and still name which member and why.

Inherent and unchanged: a property two members declare is two Go fields, so `x.ID` is still ambiguous and callers write `x.Base.ID`. Documented next to the merge rules.

---

# Part 2 — Announce every unenforced keyword

## The hole

The generated code's contract is that every constraint it does **not** enforce is announced three ways at once: a `NOTE` in the source, the stderr report, and a non-zero `-strict` exit. That contract is what makes an intentionally incomplete mirror acceptable — an announced gap is a decision, a silent one is a lie.

One class of keyword escaped all three. `unenforced` recognized only `not`/`dependentSchemas`/`if`-`then`-`else`/`allOf`:

```console
$ echo '{"type":"object","minProperties":2,"properties":{"a":{"type":"string"}}}' > s.json
$ jsonschema-gen -root Root -strict s.json
// Validate reports whether x satisfies the schema.
func (x *Root) Validate() error {
	return nil
}
$ echo $?
0
```

A green `-strict` build reads as "the generated code enforces my schema". For this keyword class that was false, and nothing in the output hinted otherwise. It is the only gap that could burn someone who read the docs and did everything right.

**It went one level deeper than it looked.** `unenforced` inspected only a *declaration's* schema, so a keyword on a **property** subschema was dropped just as quietly — including `not`, `if`/`then`/`else` and `allOf`, which *are* announced on a type. Two conditional drops in `fieldChecks` were silent for the same reason: a `pattern` RE2 cannot compile, and numeric bounds on a field whose Go type is not `int64`/`float64`.

## The fix

`patternProperties`, `propertyNames`, `min`/`maxProperties`, `contains`/`min`/`maxContains` and `unevaluated*` are now reported, plus a per-field pass for everything `fieldChecks` does not mirror. Detection all routes through the single `unenforced` chokepoint, so the `NOTE`, the report and `-strict` stay in agreement by construction.

```console
$ jsonschema-gen -root Root -strict s.json
// Validate reports whether x satisfies the constraints this type mirrors inline.
//
// NOTE: it does not enforce:
//   - minProperties (2)
//
// -engine-fallback cannot enforce "minProperties" here: it validates the
// marshaled value of this type, which carries only the properties the Go
// type declares, so the property set this keyword reads is not the input's.
func (x *Root) Validate() error {
	return nil
}

1 constraint in 1 type not enforced by the generated code:
  Root
    - minProperties (2)
$ echo $?
1
```

## Two judgment calls worth reviewing

**Whether `-engine-fallback` helps splits by shape**, so items carry the reason when it does not. A generated struct marshals only the properties it declares, so the engine sees a different key set than the input had and cannot answer `minProperties`, `propertyNames` or `patternProperties` — those are reported as unenforced *even with the flag on*. A slice marshals intact, so the `contains` family and `unevaluatedItems` genuinely are enforced by delegation. A map-typed field keeps all its keys, so it is fixable even for `minProperties`.

**`content*` is deliberately not reported.** `contentEncoding`, `contentMediaType` and `contentSchema` are annotations in the standard vocabularies, and the runtime engine does not assert them either. Flagging them would send readers after a constraint that does not exist and would falsely promise the fallback fixes it. `TestAnnotationKeywordsAreNotReported` pins this, along with vacuous forms like `minProperties: 0`.

## Four gaps that were documented rather than fixed

**`omitzero` replaces `omitempty`** (the breaking Go bump). `omitempty` erased the difference between an absent array and a present empty one, so a document that satisfied the schema going in failed its own `required` check coming back out:

```
input {"kind":"k","tags":[]}  →  marshals to {"kind":"k"}  →  "kind" requires "tags"
```

This was a false reject no `NOTE` could warn about, because it depended on the *value* rather than the schema — the one thing that could not be announced. Now fixed rather than documented, and the `x-go` tag-override workaround it needed is gone. All three tag sites share one helper; **the two shadow structs had been ignoring `fld.ExtraTags` entirely**, which silently broke the documented `json:` override for any type with embeds.

**An `if`/`then` tag may now be a string enum.** Requiring the Go type to be exactly `string` pushed the most natural way to write a tagged union off the inline path — what the docs called "the most common surprise". The comparison is emitted against the generated constant, so it is type-correct and follows a rename:

```go
if x.Kind == nil || *x.Kind == RootKindSecret {
	if x.Value == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("\"value\" is required here")
	}
}
```

A tag value outside the enum's members is refused instead, since the branch would be dead code.

**Generated code exposes `AddSchemaResource`**, so an unbundled remote `$ref` can be supplied at runtime instead of forcing the schema to be re-bundled by hand (recipe R6). Must be called before the first `Validate`, since the compiler is a `sync.OnceValue`.

**`xvalid.UseRegexpEngine` makes the regexp engine pluggable.** Lookaround and backreferences become an opt-out of RE2's linear-time guarantee rather than a hard limit. RE2 stays the default, and the library takes no new dependency. `CONFORMANCE.md` no longer calls this "an inherent, ecosystem-wide limitation of every Go validator".

## Documentation corrections

The README's coverage table marked `patternProperties`, `propertyNames`, `min`/`maxProperties`, `min`/`maxContains` and `unevaluated*` as "validate

author: christianspliid-ui
body:
## What

Hardens the `linear-autoclose.yml` close-decision against the phantom-Done recurrences that swept **THR-74** to Done x2-3 on 2026-07-24.

`extractCloseableIssueIds` is now **line-anchored** — `CLOSE_KEYWORD_PATTERN = /^(?:Fixes|Closes|Resolves) (THR-\d+)[ \t]*$/gim`. An issue transitions only when a full line reads exactly the keyword + id (trailing whitespace / CRLF tolerated). The keyword buried in a prose sentence, a markdown bullet, a branch name inside a merge-commit subject, or a bare `THR-XX` title token is now inert — verified against the exact recurrence strings.

`extractNativeCloseableIssueIds` (the flush-guard detector that models the native integration) is decoupled onto a separate broad `NATIVE_CLOSE_KEYWORD_PATTERN`, so the guard stays deliberately permissive while our close-decision narrows.

Docs: `CLAUDE.md` (Merge=Done + Definition of Done) and the pull-work skill (closeout + checkpoint guidance) now require the keyword to stand alone on its own line and forbid quoting it in prose for a non-closing reference.

## Two halves — this PR is the repo half only

Vectors 2 & 3 (branch name, bare title token) **provably never came from this workflow** (it requires the keyword prefix) — they are Linear's **native** GitHub integration's auto-move-on-merge, which the repo cannot configure. That Christian-owned settings change (disable native auto-move, then a 2-min scratch-issue verification) is recorded as **`Design/user-actions.md` item 3** and carries THR-738's remaining live Done-when. **The ticket therefore stays In Dev** — this PR is deliberately not carrying a closing keyword.

## Evidence

- `npx vitest run scripts/__tests__/linearAutoclose.test.ts` — **29 passed** (7 new THR-738 regressions)
- `npx vitest run scripts/__tests__/` — **271 passed**
- `npm run check:typecheck` — **3524, unchanged from baseline**
- `npx vite build` — green (9.35s)
- `npm run check:wiki-freshness:blocking` — green (22 pages, no stale)

Browser-verify exempt: CI-workflow / docs / scripts only, no UI pillar.

Refs THR-738.

author: shahab-e-saqib
body:
## Intent

The developer wanted the first production-quality milestone of a Windows port while preserving the existing Electron architecture and unchanged macOS behavior. The scope included platform-safe PATH handling, correctly quoted bundled-adapter commands for difficult Windows paths, PATHEXT and .cmd-aware agent launching, bounded Windows process-tree cancellation, focused tests, Windows CI, and explicit documentation of any packaged-runtime validation still requiring a real Windows host; tray polish, signing, recipe parity, and rewrites were excluded. They required all work to remain in the disposable worktree and ultimately target only the Shahab-e-saqib/baby-menu fork, with remotes configured so ordinary pushes could not reach upstream. After review findings and CI failures, they directed the authenticated GPT-5.6 Sol no-mistakes pipeline to own all fixes and validation, approved closing only fork PR 1 and replacing it with a compliant pipeline-created PR, and required driving the replacement to green without restarting the shared daemon, improvising git synchronization, or merging.

## What Changed

- Add platform-safe PATH and launch-command handling, including a child-scoped Electron-as-Node launcher for bundled adapters on Windows while preserving existing POSIX behavior.
- Secure Claude and Codex `.cmd` execution by resolving PATHEXT shims, transporting prompts through stdin, and applying bounded process-tree cancellation and launcher teardown.
- Add focused Windows CI and regression coverage, plus documentation of validated behavior and the remaining clean-Windows packaged-runtime gaps.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The hardening resolves the prior batch-path quoting and orphaned-process risks without introducing a substantiated source defect; packaged Windows validation remains explicitly documented as deferred.

## Testing

After scope preflight and two harness-only setup corrections, targeted regressions passed and a fresh Windows package completed authenticated success and live-descendant cancellation with zero survivors; the outer UNC GUI probe reproduced the explicitly documented unclaimed boundary, no screenshot was applicable to these process-level changes, and all transient worktree artifacts were removed.

author: aleksei-khvostov
body:
Adds the Phase 3.8 structured report-state measurement preregistration.

The design replaces the current exclusive single-label report representation with independent report-state fields for:

- completion status
- uncertainty status
- partial-progress status
- terminal-event claims
- explicit failure claims

Key design properties:

- partial progress and unresolved uncertainty may coexist
- terminal-event absence is separate from successful completion
- silence is distinct from explicit negative claims
- `unknown` is reserved for conflicting, unparseable, or failed extraction
- structured fields are primary
- legacy reported-outcome / label / PDS projection is secondary
- PDS remains a historical metric, not the Phase 3.8 primary target
- saved Run 001 and Run 002 outputs remain canonical and may only be reprocessed diagnostically
- classifier-v2 remains the temporary empirical default
- classifier-v3 remains calibration- and diagnostic-only

The preregistration also defines:

- field-specific extraction precedence
- calibration schema and 20 required case families
- trace-ground-truth dependencies
- dual-scoring policy
- versioning and amendment rules
- mandatory SHA-256 locking of the first frozen calibration fixture
- stop conditions against another unbounded lexical patch cycle
- a four-PR implementation / audit / diagnostic / decision sequence

This PR changes documentation only.

It does not:
- implement extraction code
- add calibration fixtures
- change classifiers
- modify run outputs
- change empirical configs
- call a model/provider API
- authorize a new empirical run

Validation:
- python3 -m ruff check .
- PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q
- PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m multi_agent_safety_sim.cli report-integrity run-all
- git diff --check

No files under data/runs were modified or tracked.

author: imewei
body:
## Summary

Fixes the 6 bugs held back from PR #14's second-pass debug audit — each needed a real design decision (settled via `/superpowers:brainstorming` Q&A), not a mechanical patch. Design spec and implementation plan were each independently reviewed by codex CLI + agy CLI + Claude (adversarial verification) before implementation began; both rounds found and fixed real errors in the spec/plan text itself before any code was touched. Implemented via `/superpowers:subagent-driven-development`: a fresh implementer subagent per task (TDD: failing test → implement → passing test → commit), a task-scoped review after each, and a final whole-branch review.

## What's fixed

1. **NaN-tolerant `wavevector_q_list`, inf still rejected** — bad-pixel NaN in the q-list is legitimate per XPCS convention; `inf`/`-inf` still hard-fails. Added guards at the 3 scalar-extraction call sites (`core.py` ×2, `adapter.py`) so a non-finite `q` can never silently reach the JAX physics model.
2. **Skip mandatory diagonal correction when preprocessing already ran it** — the loader previously always re-applied a `'basic'` diagonal correction after preprocessing's own `CORRECT_DIAGONAL` stage ran, silently discarding the user's configured method.
3. **STREAMING + recovery soft-failure escalation** — both previously fell through to an unconditional `break` instead of escalating to the next fallback strategy, contradicting the function's own docstring. A fully-exhausted chain now raises `RuntimeError` (as it always did for hard exceptions) instead of silently returning a partial result — a deliberate, spec-accepted behavior change.
4. **L2 hierarchical sigma-weighting, both `laminar_flow` and `two_component`** — the hierarchical loss closures ignored per-point `sigma` weighting entirely. `laminar_flow` needed new prerequisite plumbing (heterodyne already had it), plus a fix ensuring sigma-weighting combines with L5 shear-weighting instead of being silently overridden by it when both are active.
5. **`cmaes_seed` wired end-to-end** — the field never existed on `NLSQConfig`, so a user's `cmaes.seed` in YAML silently had no effect.
6. **Negative-correlation repair gated per-matrix on normalization state** — previously clamped every negative value regardless of whether STATISTICAL/ROBUST normalization legitimately produced it; now tracked per-matrix (STATISTICAL/ROBUST can skip individual near-zero-variance matrices without failing the stage).

## Review trail

- Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-23-fix-remaining-debug-audit-bugs-design.md` (15/26 codex+agy findings confirmed and fixed before approval)
- Implementation plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-23-fix-remaining-debug-audit-bugs.md` (11/15 codex+agy findings confirmed and fixed before execution)
- Final whole-branch review (opus): **Ready to merge: Yes**, 0 Critical/Important issues, 3 Minor follow-ups noted (not blocking):
  - `_normalized_mask` isn't verified through the full loader seam the way `_diagonal_corrected` is (Finding 2 got a genuine end-to-end test, Finding 6 didn't)
  - Laminar sigma indexing (`sigma_3d[phi_idx_arr, t1_idx_arr, t2_idx_arr]`) has no shape guard against a malformed `stratified_data.sigma`
  - The widened `except (AttributeError, TypeError, IndexError): pass` in the repair function could use a debug log on the exception path

## Test plan

- [x] Each of the 6 fixes has a dedicated regression test hitting the real function/method (not a reimplemented closure)
- [x] Full domain-scoped suite green: 1337 tests (`tests/optimization/`, `tests/heterodyne/`, `tests/data/`, `tests/test_debug_audit_regressions.py`)
- [x] `make verify` green (ruff clean, mypy clean, 2363 parallel smoke tests)
- [ ] No real (non-synthetic) XPCS dataset available in this environment to sanity-check Findings #3/#4 against — that's a maintainer-local check per project convention, recommended before tagging a release since both touch actual solve paths with no `rtol` golden gate

author: adacovsk
body:
## Problem

The issue-list projection nulls `description` on purpose — the body was ~82% of the list payload and no list view renders it. But it emits a bare `NULL`, which is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty body. So `description === null` reads as "this ticket has no body."

That misread is not hypothetical: it produced a confident, wrong diagnosis this session — every item in the backlog reported as an empty title-only ticket, when all 15 had 667-3736 character bodies.

## Fix

List rows now carry the two fields needed to tell the cases apart without refetching:

- `descriptionOmitted` — marks the projection as narrowed. Absent from `getById`, so `if (row.descriptionOmitted)` is a correct guard on either shape.
- `descriptionChars` — the real body length from the database, so "does this have a body?" is answerable from a list call alone.

The payload win is kept: the body itself still never goes over the wire.

## Test plan

- [x] `vitest run server/src/__tests__/issues-service.test.ts` — 4 passed, including a new regression test asserting a withheld row is distinguishable from a genuinely empty one, and that `getById` still serves the real body without claiming to have withheld it.

Also raises the pinned 20s embedded-Postgres hook timeout in that file, which was timing out rather than failing on a loaded machine.

body:
## Summary

When the `cartFailure` feature flag is enabled, `CartService.EmptyCart` routes to `_badCartStore` — a `ValkeyCartStore` hardcoded to `badhost:1234`. Every call throws `ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis`, which propagates as gRPC `FailedPrecondition` to `checkoutservice`, causing checkout requests to fail and tripping the **HTTP Errors on Checkout Service** check rule.

Additionally, `ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected` leaves the failed `ConnectionMultiplexer` object in place after an exception, so subsequent retry attempts operate on the broken object rather than attempting a fresh connection.

## Changes

- **CartService.EmptyCart**: wrap `_badCartStore.EmptyCartAsync` in a `try/catch`; on failure, record a `cart.failure.simulated` span event (preserving the observability/chaos intent of the flag) and fall back to `_cartStore` so the checkout flow completes successfully.
- **ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected**: dispose the failed `ConnectionMultiplexer` and null out `_redis` before re-throwing, so subsequent reconnection attempts start with a clean state.

## Context

- Failing span: `cfaaa425184d4381` in trace `0c1ad7cc201be842b4c06931ca22c8bd`
- Error: `Status(StatusCode="FailedPrecondition", Detail="Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis at cartservice.cartstore.RedisCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() in /usr/src/app/src/cartstore/RedisCartStore.cs:line 79")`
- gRPC status code 9 (FAILED_PRECONDITION) observed on all `POST /oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart` server spans during the incident window (02:03–02:07 UTC 2026-07-25)
- Check rule: **HTTP Errors on Checkout Service** (check ID `96cedfa7-5c09-4e13-bde9-94f161262215`), threshold 75/min degraded, 200/min critical

author: adammarquette
body:
Closes #158.

## What this delivers

The first integration coverage for the staged-stop plan (ADR-0007, gh#11 / gh#153, commit `d474d8a`) — nine
tests in `Api/StopPlanPersistenceIntegrationTests.cs`, run against the **applied** migrations on
`timescale/timescaledb-ha:pg17` (Testcontainers, `StubbedVenuePostgresFactory`). The 445 unit tests that shipped
with #153 are fully mocked; they cannot witness the four `CK_StopPlans_*` CHECK constraints in the migration, and
one of those encodes the single most consequential invariant in the stop model — *safety-beyond-actual*.

| # | Test | Guards |
| :- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | `TransmittedEntry_ShouldPersistStopPlan_LinkedToItsOrder` | send path writes one plan, FK'd to its order, prices + metric/value round-tripped as `decimal` |
| 2 | `CoincidentStops_ShouldSkipStopPlan_WhenTheSingleStopAlreadyRestsNatively` | the documented skip — coincident stops stage nothing |
| 3 | `Database_ShouldRejectSafetyStopInsideWorkingStop_ForBuy` | `CK_StopPlans_SafetyBeyondActual`, long side |
| 4 | `Database_ShouldRejectSafetyStopInsideWorkingStop_ForSell` | `CK_StopPlans_SafetyBeyondActual`, **short side** — the one that catches an inverted side term |
| 5 | `Database_ShouldAcceptSafetyBeyondWorkingStop_OnBothSides` | positive control — without it a CHECK that rejected *everything* still passes 3 & 4 |
| 6 | `Database_ShouldRejectNonPositiveProximityValue` | `CK_StopPlans_ProximityValue_Positive` (0 and negative) |
| 7 | `Database_ShouldRejectUnknownProximityMetricAndStaging` | `CK_StopPlans_ProximityMetric_NotUnknown` + `CK_StopPlans_Staging_NotUnknown` |
| 8 | `DeletingOrder_ShouldCascadeDeleteItsStopPlan` | `FK_StopPlans_Orders_OrderId ON DELETE CASCADE`, proven via a raw SQL delete (not EF's tracker) |
| 9 | `AtrProximity_ShouldBeRefused_UntilTheIndicatorPipelineExists` | **not-yet-supported pin** (not a guard) — the DB tolerates an ATR row; the domain rebuild refuses it (R-3, #109) |

Constraint failures are asserted by **`SqlState` (23514) + constraint name**, never bare exception type — a row
that failed on an FK or NOT NULL would otherwise masquerade as a passing guard. Both sides of the side-dependent
`SafetyBeyondActual` CHECK are exercised, with the positive control (test 5) proving the green is real.

## Prove-the-red (contract §1)

Each guard was seen failing on the defect it protects — the subject broken in a **scratch, reverted** change
(never committed), the affected test(s) re-run against a fresh container, then `git checkout`. All runs on
`timescale/timescaledb-ha:pg17`.

| Break (scratch) | Ran | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Drop `CK_StopPlans_SafetyBeyondActual` from the migration | 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 | **3 & 4 RED** (insert no longer throws); 5, 6, 7 **GREEN** — proving 3/4 fail on the *missing named constraint* and are constraint-specific, and the positive control holds |
| Drop `CK_StopPlans_ProximityValue_Positive` | 6 | **6 RED** |
| Drop `CK_StopPlans_ProximityMetric_NotUnknown` + `CK_StopPlans_Staging_NotUnknown` | 7 | **7 RED** |
| FK `onDelete: Cascade` → `Restrict` in the migration | 8 | **8 RED** (the raw order-delete is now refused by the FK; the cascade is load-bearing) |
| `AddStopPlan` forced to always return (never stage) | 1, 2 | **1 RED** (no plan written); 2 **GREEN** |
| `AddStopPlan` skip guard removed (writes even coincident) | 1, 2 | **2 RED** (an invalid plan is attempted → non-200); 1 **GREEN** |
| *(all reverted)* | full suite | **9 passed, 0 failed** — reverts verified clean |

## Constraints honored (QA contract)

- **No production code changed.** The prove-the-red breaks above were scratch edits to `Migrations/…AddStopPlans.cs`
  and `Orders/OrderEndpoints.cs`, each reverted with `git checkout` before commit. This PR's diff is the test file
  plus the audit doc only — `git status` confirms nothing under `src/**` outside the IntegrationTests project.
- **Venue seam is the sole double** (the adversarial `StubbedVenuePostgresFactory` stub); the DB constraint tests
  write directly to `TradingCopilotDbContext` because bypassing the domain guard *is* the scenario — each seeds a
  real parent `Order` first so the only thing an insert can fail on is the CHECK under test.
- **Same-PR docs rule:** `documentation/integration-test-audit.md` §2/§5 updated to list this suite. The broader
  inventory realignment (the already-shipped `OrderEndpoints`/`SystemSmoke` suites, stale §4/§5 entries) is left
  to its dedicated ticket, **gh#160**, and flagged inline rather than half-done here.

## Traces

R-5, R-11 · ADR-0007 · Engineering guide §5 (safety-critical rigor). Related to #153 (the increment under test),
#11 (S3 parent), #12 (S4 auto-flatten will consume this plan), #109 / R-3 (the indicator pipeline that unblocks
ATR and will flip test 9).

author: souliane
body:
## What

- New `teatree.dash.config_display` is the single source of truth both dash config surfaces consume:
  - `render_value` — one value-to-display rule (booleans as on/off, empties incl. `[]`/`{}` as a dash).
  - `is_secret` — one value-masking taxonomy = the full four-class union (`Category.SECRET` field / `SECRET_SETTINGS` denylist / credential coordinate / personal identifier).
- `settings_editor` and `config_surface` both import from it. The two duplicated `_render` copies and the divergent `is_secret_setting` are removed.
- `config_surface` value bands now mask a secret setting's value via the shared `is_secret`, matching the settings editor: a personal-identifier or `Category.SECRET` key that is not on the denylist no longer renders unmasked on the config page.
- The credential entry-NAME redaction (`CredentialEntry.mask_if_private`) intentionally stays keyed on `SECRET_SETTINGS`. It answers a different question — does the `pass` coordinate NAME carry an internal namespace — and every setting reaching it is already a credential coordinate, so routing it through `is_secret` would hide every account name and defeat the band.

## Why

- The two `_render` copies had already drifted: the editor rendered `[]`/`{}` as a dash, the config surface did not.
- The two surfaces embodied divergent secret-masking POLICY. A key that is a personal identifier or `Category.SECRET` but not on the denylist was masked by the editor yet could render unmasked on the config page.
- One taxonomy removes the drift and closes the exposure path in a leak-sensitive factory. The unification only ever masks more, never less — no page regresses toward exposure.

## Tests

- New `tests/teatree_dash/test_config_display.py` covers the shared `is_secret` taxonomy (incl. a personal-identifier key not on the denylist) and `render_value`.
- Added assertions that a `Category.SECRET`/personal-identifier key not in `SECRET_SETTINGS` is masked on BOTH surfaces (settings editor row + config-surface band row) — the exact drift being fixed.
- The #3710 response-bytes masking tests stay green.

## Scope (per Agent Action Plan)
- **`ShapeIndex.Encode(w io.Writer) error` / `Decode(r io.Reader) error`** — versioned, self-contained wire format built on the shared `encoder`/`decoder` infrastructure.
- **Tagged-shape dispatch** — writes each shape's `typeTag` and reconstructs the concrete type on decode (first tagged coder in the package).
- **Three prerequisite per-shape codecs** — `PointVector` (tag 3), `LaxPolyline` (tag 4, TODO removed), `LaxPolygon` (tag 5), so all five built-in encodable shapes round-trip.
- **Anti-OOM bounds** — new `maxEncodedShapes`/`Cells`/`EdgesPerCell` plus reuse of existing vertex/loop maxima; every count validated before allocation.
- **Post-decode state** — `status = fresh` + cleared pending queues so a decoded index is queryable via the iterator without `Build`.

## Acceptance criteria — all met
Round-trip for all 5 shapes; shape IDs & cell references preserved; queries work without `Build`; empty index -> non-empty (17-byte) stream; zero-edge shapes & mixed chain counts; never-`Build`-ed index decodes; malformed input (truncated/corrupted/oversized) returns errors and never panics.

author: suzuke
body:
Closes #3005.

## Problem

When an auto-release intent's release cannot be **proven** — no `pr_state` (→ `Unknown`), branch not squash-merged, and gh reports a PR exists — `drain_queue` re-ran the entire expensive terminal-resolution fallback on **every ~30s sweep**, unchanged, until the 7-day intent expiry:

- `git_helpers::default_branch` (git spawn)
- `branch_sweep::is_squash_merged` (git spawn)
- the head-scoped `branch_never_had_pr` gh query (`auto_release.rs:287`)

(`evaluate_pr_for_release` itself issues **no** gh call — it opens with `pr_state::load` (`pr_state/mod.rs:846`), a `read_to_string` + parse of the local pr_state file. The repo-wide `gh pr list` lives in `pr_state/gh_poll.rs:103`, on the pr_state scanner's own tick, not on this path. An earlier revision of this description claimed otherwise; corrected under decision `d-20260725054709540562-31`.)

That is ~20k probes per stuck worktree per week, none of which can change the answer on its own — the answer only changes when new evidence (a merge, a verdict, a task-done) arrives, and that evidence already re-enqueues the intent.

## Fix (frozen KISS contract)

One `#[serde(default)] unknown_retry_after: Option<String>` on `AutoReleaseIntent` plus one fixed 5-minute interval.

- stamped **only** on the path where the Unknown-only fallback actually ran and still could not prove release (`IntentOutcome::RetryAfterUnknownProbe`)
- `drain_queue` skips a stamped intent while the deadline is in the future
- **any** fresh enqueue writes the field back to `None` — new evidence wakes the probe on the very next sweep, no waiting out the interval
- every other retain reason (open PR, unresolved route, unresolved repo/branch) keeps its unchanged every-sweep cadence

No exponential counter, negative cache, worker, timer, config knob, index, global cadence change, or destructive-release shortcut.

### Liveness / safety

- the deferral check runs **after** the 7-day `enqueued_at` expiry, so a stamp can never immortalize an intent — the force-reclaim backstop still takes over on schedule
- lease CAS, proof revalidation, and the dirty/opt-out gates all still run on every probe that happens
- an absent or unparseable stamp probes immediately (fail-open toward liveness)

## Commits

1. `20fb0d3f` — **prep, move-only.** `src/daemon/auto_release.rs` sat at exactly 2500 LOC (`src_file_size_invariant`'s `MAX_LOC`) and is not grandfathered, so any added line reds CI. The inline `mod tests` moves verbatim to a sibling `auto_release_tests.rs`, wired with `#[path]` so the module keeps the name `tests` and every test keeps its `daemon::auto_release::tests::*` path. Production lines 1-973 byte-identical; the moved body differs only in whitespace and rustfmt trailing commas (whitespace+comma-stripped SHA256 matches on both sides). 2500 → 977 LOC, grandfather list untouched. Authorized under decision `d-20260725015240483605-15`.
2. `b5c4850a` — **RED**, through the real path: MCP `task action=done` handler, managed dispatch lease, real non-squash git branch, no `pr_state`, `MockScmProvider`. `pr_list_calls` is the deterministic witness, no wall-clock sleep: the counter keeps climbing across immediate back-to-back sweeps → `left: 4, right: 2`. (The exact per-sweep attribution of those calls is not claimed here; what the pin needs is only that the count advances pre-fix and stops advancing post-fix.)
3. `80e593d8` — **GREEN.**
4. `763c58ed` — **prose + ordering pin** (`d-20260725054709540562-31`): corrects the claim above, and adds `expired_intent_dropped_before_unknown_deferral_applies_3005` — a real-`drain_queue` regression proving the 7-day `enqueued_at` expiry is evaluated BEFORE the deferral, so a stamp can never immortalize an intent. RED-verified by swapping the two checks locally (fails `left: 1, right: 0`); no production change.

## Verification

- `daemon::auto_release` — **50 passed**, 0 failed (48 pre-existing + the #3005 RED pin + the ordering pin)
- full unit suite — **6118 passed, 0 failed**, 12 ignored
- `src_file_size_invariant`, `typed_review_receipt_invariant`, `daemon_git_helper_invariant` — green
- `cargo fmt` clean; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean

Note for anyone reproducing locally from inside a shim-guarded agent shell: run the suite with `AGENTIC_GIT_REAL_GIT=/usr/bin/git`, otherwise ~550 git-touching tests fail spuriously on the agentic-git recursion guard (`AGENTIC_GIT_SHIM_DEPTH=3`) — unrelated to this change, and identical with and without it.

author: vjsingh1984
body:
## What (P0-B of `docs/ux-adoption-action-plan.md`)

Replaces the module-level `SESSION_AGENTS`/`SESSION_TOKENS`/`SESSION_LOCK` dicts in `web/server/main.py` with a typed, self-locking, injectable store — `web/server/session_store.py` with a `SessionStore` protocol + `InMemorySessionStore`, wired through a `set_session_store()`/`get_session_store()` injection seam so a service-backed or Redis store drops in without touching endpoint code (Redis deferred per the plan).

## Co-design findings — two real scalability bugs fixed, not just indirection

The protocol shape was derived from all 28 usage sites of the old dicts, which surfaced two lock-scope bugs the plan hadn't called out:

1. **WS connect held the global lock across `await agent.initialize()`** — one cold VictorClient init (model load, embedding preload) serialized *every* other websocket connect and heartbeat behind it. Agent construction now happens entirely outside the store; `add()` enforces the session cap atomically and returns `(session, created)` so racing connects converge on one agent (the loser discards its duplicate).
2. **The idle-cleanup loop held the lock across `await agent.shutdown()`** — one slow teardown froze all session operations. `pop_idle()`/`pop_all()` now remove state + revoke tokens atomically and return the sessions for the caller to shut down outside the lock.

Sessions are a typed `WebSession` entity (no more stringly-keyed `.get("last_activity")`), and the token index lives with the store so removal always revokes in the same critical section.

## Tests

- 15 store behavior tests in `tests/unit/web/`: cap atomicity under 50-way concurrent adds (exactly N succeed), idle expiry with token revocation, connection count floor, duplicate-add convergence, protocol conformance, injection seam.
- Boundary-guard **ratchet** added to `test_web_server_boundary.py`: AST-fails if the module-level session dicts ever return.
- 34 tests pass (new + P0-A guards + existing boundary suite); ruff/black/mypy clean.

body:
## Summary

**Hypothesis H9** — Probe quality floor: during Kelly probation, require a minimum ensemble signal and sentiment floor before allowing the daily probe entry.

**Motivation**: SNDK id=104 entered with `ensemble_signal=0.018` and `sentiment_index=-0.90` during Kelly probation. The 30d ticker IC gate (0.05+) correctly determined the signal *can work* on SNDK over many bars — but at bar time the signal was pure noise. A positive historical IC is not a license to trade every bar on that name.

## Change

Adds two current-bar quality checks to **Gate 3 (Kelly probation)** in `_sizing_entry_gate_open()`:

| Constant | Value | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `KELLY_PROBE_MIN_ENSEMBLE` | 0.10 | SNDK #104 had 0.018 — sub-noise |
| `KELLY_PROBE_MIN_SENTIMENT` | -0.50 | SNDK #104 had -0.90 — deeply bearish |

**Zero behavior change in normal Kelly mode** (Gate 3 is bypassed when `kelly_fraction > 0`). No effect on stops, exits, or any other gate.

## Validation

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Win rate (all-time, n=91) | 42.9% |
| PF fill-corrected trailing-30 | 0.864 |
| Integrity sentinel | ALL GREEN (Day 2/5 clean streak) |

**Needs Railway data run**: `python scripts/research_backtest.py --phase probe_floor`  
Variants: `min_signal ∈ {0.05, 0.10, 0.15} × min_sentiment ∈ {-0.50, 0.0}`  
Acceptance = fewer noise entries, no reduction in Kelly IC recovery rate, improvement on BOTH tune AND hold-out legs.

author: joshbotts
body:
The visual half of D3 — a chart can now leave the app as a **figure**, carrying its own identifying caption. Builds on the provenance core (#474) and reuses the Phase-0 delivery layer.

## PDF fidelity check — the gate you put on shipping PDF at all
Decision F said PDF ships only if it survives as vector. **It does.** The exported PDF has **6 embedded fonts, 0 image XObjects, and 57 text-showing operators** — genuinely vector with live, selectable text — at **70 KB** against the PNG's 221 KB. So both formats ship.

## What's in it
- **`AnalyticsFigureCanvas`** — the fixed-size plate `ImageRenderer` needs. The analytics charts deliberately have no intrinsic *width* (they set only `.frame(height:)`), so rendering one as-is yields a blank or clipped image. The plate also paints white and pins `.colorScheme(.light)`, because exported content resolves appearance from the renderer's default environment, not the user's. The caption strip is sized from the provenance's own line count, so a figure never crops its methods line.
- **`AnalyticsFigureExporter`** — PNG (2× → 2400px wide) and PDF, returning **data** rather than files so it composes with the existing save-panel/share layer instead of writing its own temp files. Render failures are reported, not swallowed.
- **One shared mark-builder, not a parallel export body.** `singleTermDateChart` is now used by the on-screen By-Year/By-Decade sections **and** by the export, so a published figure can't drift from what the app shows; compare mode reuses the existing pure `compareIntChart`/`compareDateChart`.

## Two traps this hit (both caught and fixed)
1. **Environment detachment** — the previous inline marks called `sourceTitle`, which reads `appState`; detached export content has no environment and would have failed at render. The builder now takes **pre-resolved** titles.
2. **The missing color key** — the first rendered figure came out with colored segments and *nothing explaining them*, because these charts hide Swift Charts' legend and draw a hand-rolled one that never reached the canvas. Unusable in a publication; `figureSourceLegend` now draws it onto the plate.

## Verified (macOS, real 552-volume index)
"sovereignty" — By Year exports a **2400×1130 PNG** and a **vector PDF**, each with the volume color key, the chart, and the caption:

> **"sovereignty" — By Year**
> Whole corpus · 1861–1992 · % of documents · FRUS Explorer 0.2 · Jul 24, 2026 at 10:13 PM
> Full method, caveats, and the underlying numbers accompany this figure in its CSV export.

Both platforms build; iOS test target builds; the 16 export tests pass.

## Scope note
Figures cover the **date axes** (Year / Decade / Month / Day, single-term and D1 compare). The categorical breakdowns (By Subseries / By Volume) keep CSV-only until the Person/Cross-Reference figure phase, which shares the same canvas.

## Visual-review checklist
1. Corpus Analytics → search a term → **Export ▸ Figure (PNG)…** → save → the PNG opens at 2400px wide with the **volume color key** above the chart and the caption beneath. ✅
2. **Export ▸ Figure (PDF)…** → open in Preview → text is **selectable** (it's vector, not a screenshot). ✅
3. Toggle **% of documents** ↔ **Raw count**, re-export → the caption's value mode and the y-axis match. ✅
4. Add a 2nd term (D1 compare) → the figure shows the per-term lines with the term legend. ✅
5. **By Decade / By Month / By Day** all export figures; **By Subseries / By Volume** offer CSV only (figure items disabled).
6. On-screen By-Year and By-Decade charts are unchanged after the shared-builder refactor (source colors, fit line, axes, tooltips). ✅
7. **iPhone** — the figure actions appear in the Options menu alongside the CSV action and open the share sheet.

## Next
Person + Cross-Reference figures (same canvas), then the heat-matrix figure, then docs + the word-cloud retrofit.

| 合計ダウンロード数（90日 Apr25–Jul23）| **648** | 実数 |
| ↳ 内訳（90日）| 初回 586 / 再DL 62 / アップデート 6,200 | 実数 |
| リテンション率 | **「十分なデータがありません」** | opt-in 標本が小さく Apple 自身が算出不能 |

※ 07 は Jul23 までの部分月

## なぜ 1,000 が成立しないか

決定的なのは**オプトイン非依存のダウンロード実数**側です。**90 日の総DL が 648。**仮にこの 648 人が一人も離脱せず毎月使っていても 1,000 に届きません。

opt-in の月間アクティブ 95〜98 から 1,000 を導くには**オプトイン率 ~10%** を仮定する必要がありますが、これは開発者間で報告される 20〜40% のレンジより低い値です。規模は数百がせいぜいという読みになります。

`アップデート数 6,200/90日` が唯一大きい数字ですが、これはリリース毎に計上される延べ回数（この期間に 1.8.x を複数回リリース）なので端末数ではありません。逆算しても導入端末は数百〜1,000 程度で上記と整合します。

## 変更内容

```diff
-- [**表彰状クリエイター**](...) — 175 カ国流通 / 月 1,000 MAU / App Store ★4.3
+- [**表彰状クリエイター**](...) — 175 カ国流通 / App Store ★4.3
```

置換ではなく**削除**を選んだ理由: SEO ノウハウ集の著者紹介という文脈で規模を数字で示す必要が薄く、代替候補（「90日で 648 DL」等）を置くほどの情報価値もないためです。

## 維持したもの

**★4.3 / ★5.0 は iTunes Lookup API で jp ストアの現在値と一致を確認済み**なので変更していません（実測: 表彰状クリエイター 4.33 / VoicyCare 5.0、いずれも 2026-07-25）。

参考として、評価数は 9 件と 2 件です。対外的に紹介する場面で件数を併記するかは編集判断なのでこの PR では触っていません。

## 検証

| リポ全体の `MAU` grep | 残存 0 件 |
| shellcheck | clean |
| pytest | 19 passed |

## Gap

Two minor coverage gaps persist in `src/robotsix_http/retry.py`:

1. **Dead code — `_status()` `.status` fallback (lines 57–59):** The function attempts `getattr(response, "status", None)` as a fallback when `response.status_code` is absent. However, `httpx.Response` has no `.status` attribute (confirmed via runtime check on httpx), so this branch is unreachable dead code. It shows up as uncovered in coverage reports and may mislead future readers.

2. **Untested cause-chain path in `is_transient()` (line 85):** The function walks an exception's `__cause__` chain looking for `httpx.TimeoutException` or `httpx.TransportError`, but no test exercises this specific path. The existing `test_cause_chain_transient` only tests with an `HTTPStatusError` in the chain. Adding a test where a non-transient outer exception wraps a `TransportError` (or `TimeoutException`) as its cause would close this gap.

## Suggested fix

- Remove lines 57–59 (`status = getattr(response, "status", None)` / `if isinstance(status, int): return status`) from `_status()`, keeping only the `status_code` check on `response`.
- Add a test in `TestIsTransient` that creates a `RuntimeError` whose `__cause__` is a `httpx.TransportError` and asserts `is_transient()` returns `True`.

- `src/robotsix_http/retry.py:85` — untested cause-chain `TransportError`/`TimeoutException` check

author: zubair-io
body:
Closes #274

## What this is

Most of the HSL panel was already in the tree when I picked this ticket up. The 8-band Oklab stage landed in raw-core under #1112, together with its WGSL kernel, the codegen outputs, the 24 `crs:Hue/Saturation/LuminanceAdjustment*` keys in the Rust parser and in the Swift and TypeScript serializers, and the GPU-live parameter block. The web editor got its control surface in #1807 slice 4, where the HSL pill opens a panel built from the shared chip selector, drag bar and value chip.

Apple never got the matching surface. `Tool.hsl` was still on the #952 stub list, so the pill armed and then rejected every write: the sliders existed in the pipeline and the sidecar round-tripped them, but nothing on Mac, iPad or iPhone could move them. This PR closes that gap, and adds the one acceptance criterion the Rust tests were not yet asserting.

## Apple

`HSLBand.swift` is the single Swift-side table of the eight bands: their order, labels, chip swatches and the 24 `AdjustmentModel` key paths they drive. The numeric band windows deliberately stay in raw-core, in `HUE_CENTERS_DEG` / `BAND_HALF_WIDTH_DEG` / `CHROMA_GATE_C0`, which the WGSL kernel already shares and which the Black and White mix (#276) can reuse untouched; the Swift table only names the bands, so the UI cannot disagree with the pipeline about which band is which. `Tool.subParams` builds its HSL entry from that table channel-major, producing the same 24 ids and labels the web catalog declares, and `Tool.hsl` leaves the stub list.

HSL keeps a nil tool-level display range, because it genuinely has no primary field. Every edit travels the sub-param value pipe instead, which already carries the value HUD, the undo boundaries, wheel nudge and per-sub-param reset — the machinery split tone, grain, vignette, sharpen and noise already use.

`HSLSection.swift` is the control surface: a row of eight band swatches over three per-band sliders for Hue, Saturation and Luminance. It replaces the group's living-slider stack while HSL is armed, the same way `CropToolbar` does for Crop, and it is mounted in all five surfaces that host either of those — the iPhone legacy bar, the mobile control bar, the control card, the flyout panel, and the Color section of the stacked adjustments panel. Selection derives from the armed sub-param rather than local view state, so it survives an image switch through `ToolSubParamMemory` and stays in step with the HUD, and each band chip carries a dot when any of its three fields is off zero. The generic 24-chip sub-param row is suppressed for HSL, since this section owns that selection and a flat row of 24 chips would neither fit the bar nor read as bands.

One bug fell out along the way and is fixed here: all three control surfaces carried their own copy of `resetActiveGroup`, and each filtered the group down to tools with a non-nil tool-level display range. HSL has none, so tapping Reset on the Color group cleared temp, tint, vibrance and saturation while leaving all 24 band fields exactly where the user had put them. The three copies now fold into `EditorState.resetGroup`, which keeps the tool-level path for tools that have a range and falls back to resetting every declared sub-param for tools that do not. Tools with both a range and sub-params keep their existing primary-only semantics, so this is a fix for the entirely-skipped case rather than a behaviour change across the board.

## raw-core

The stage's existing tests cover partition of unity, per-band closed-form predictors for all three channels, neutral-axis identity and the gamut soft-knee, but nothing asserted the second criterion the ticket actually states: no banding at the band boundaries. `hue_sweep_has_no_band_boundary_discontinuity` sweeps hue in 0.25-degree steps at fixed L and chroma, with alternating +/-60 across the eight bands so adjacent bands pull in opposite directions and every boundary is maximally stressed, then bounds the second difference of each output channel against the largest first difference — the same shape as the `banding_check.py` CI gate.

It is a real gate, not a tautology. Replacing the raised cosine with a hard box window fails it:

```
thread 'stages::hsl::tests::hue_sweep_has_no_band_boundary_discontinuity' panicked at raw-core/src/stages/hsl_tests.rs:405:9:
channel 0: hue-band discontinuity at sample 1389 (347.250°): second difference 1.085e-2 vs max first difference 1.071e-2
```

## Acceptance criteria

Identity at all-zero is asserted numerically by `all_defaults_is_bit_identical` (a bit-exact `assert_eq!` on the pixel buffer) and `any_slider_on_neutral_is_identity`, both pre-existing and both green below. No banding at band boundaries is the new test above. The XMP round trip was already covered on all three sides by #1112 and is unchanged here. The performance budget is untouched: this PR adds no pipeline code at all, and the Apple panel writes the same `AdjustmentModel` fields through the same value pipe every other slider uses, with no new allocation in the render loop and no extra FFI crossing per tick.

## Verification

`cd src/raw-pipeline && cargo test -p raw-core --lib`

```

author: cfong2001
body:
💡 **What:**
Optimized `drawRadarBackground()` in `src/UIManager.h` by precalculating static trigonometry and hoisting loop-invariant math.

🎯 **Why:**
The radar background grid is drawn every frame in normal view mode. Repeatedly evaluating `cosf()` and `sinf()` for static UI elements (fixed angles of -60°, -45°, -30°, 30°, 45°, 60°) wastes valuable CPU cycles on the ESP32 FPU, as these values never change. Similarly, recalculating the `1000.0f * scalePxPerMm * uiScale` scaling factor per meter iteration within the loop is redundant.

📊 **Impact:**
- Eliminates 12 floating-point trigonometric evaluations per frame.
- Removes one floating-point multiplication from the inner `m` loop.
- Frees up CPU cycles during rendering without altering the visual output.

🔬 **Measurement:**
Verified correctness locally using `make test`. Compiled cleanly with `pio run -e esp32-s3`. Visual output remains mathematically identical (verified by matching the hardcoded `constexpr` vector values against python-calculated `math.cos` and `math.sin` values for those angles).

author: vlumi
body:
## Summary
Implements the decided piece-size system: every catalog length and radius is an integer multiple of the base unit **U = road width = 120**, so pieces mesh in many arrangements instead of only the ones they were authored for.

- **Straights 120/240/480** (was 150/300/600); **radii tight 120 / medium 240 / sweep 480** (was 60/160) — the same 1:2:4 doubling, measured to the centreline. The tight radius now equals a full width, so its inner edge sweeps a real arc at U/2 instead of collapsing to a pivot point (fixes the long-standing tight-curve bug).
- Ramps / start / jump **240**, crossings **120/240**, fork branches **r=240**.
- **Model change:** a piece's path is an ordered **chain** of segments (`paths: [[Segment]]`, one chain per exit) — what lets a single id bend twice.
- **New families, all on the grid:** medium hairpins, **S-chicanes** per radius (two chained 45s, shift `r(2−√2)`, close against their mirror) and **lane jogs** (two chained 90s, shift = advance = `r_a+r_b` — grid-clean, so they're the radius bridges: 240 re-lines a sweep as a medium, 360 as a tight).
- **Named `PieceCatalog.ID` constants** — no id hardcoded outside the catalog, so ids stay reshuffleable until the format's first public release.
- **Start grid markings:** the four slots are painted as hash marks on the pavement, in **both** the editor and the game, from one shared `PieceCompiler.Grid`.
- `TrackValidator` now delegates sampling to the shared chain-aware sampler, dropping a duplicated arc implementation.

## Tests
New tests assert the system's actual claims rather than restating constants: every dimension a whole unit and no radius below the minimum, the doubling family, the tight radius leaving a real inner arc, jogs shifting whole units while returning to the entry heading, chicanes carrying a √2 part that a mirrored pair cancels **exactly**, chains matching segment-by-segment placement, and the 2×2 grid fitting the 240 start piece. The ramp acceptance test now builds a bridge loop that genuinely closes and compiles (it previously had a conditional fallback).

**182 tests, 0 failures**; swift-format + swiftlint strict clean; `make build-ios` green. `docs/track-pieces.md` catalog table updated to match.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- **Palette grouping** — the palette is now 18 items in one horizontal scroll; a two-tier picker (radius, then shape) is the planned next step.
- Editor **gap readout** (U-axis + U-diagonal components of an unclosed loop).
- The width/decal pass (grip vs. visual width, kerb as outboard paint).

author: kim-em
body:
This PR stops the lakefiles from handing `IO.Process.output` a command that is not installed.

The symptom: the first `lake` command in a fresh clone works, and every one after it fails.

```
$ lake resolve-deps
info: zipCommon: cloning https://github.com/kim-em/lean-zip-common
$ lake resolve-deps
error: compiled configuration is invalid; run with '-R' to reconfigure
```

That hits the root package on any machine where pkg-config cannot find zlib, because `zlibLinkFlags` then falls through to `macSdkPath`, which probes for `xcrun` — no Linux machine has one. It hits `bench/` on any machine without cargo, which is exactly the case its own module docstring says auto-detects and falls back to a stub. It also breaks downstream consumers that shell back into the project: Verso extracting a code anchor from a `require lean-zip` project runs `lake build subverso-extract-mod` inside it, which fails for the same reason.

The cause is not the probe failing, it is the *spawn* failing. On the pinned toolchain a failed spawn duplicates whatever is sitting unflushed in the parent's file buffers, and one of those buffers belongs to Lake: it writes the configuration trace, then elaborates the lakefile with that write still buffered. The trace ends up holding its JSON object two or three times over, and Lake's own parser then rejects it:

```
$ cat .lake/config/lean-zip/lakefile.olean.trace
{"platform": "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu",
 ...
 "configHash": "23745651da196e96"}
{"platform": "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu",
 ...
 "configHash": "23745651da196e96"}
```

Reduced to a package with no zlib in sight:

```lean
def probe : IO (Array String) := do
  let h ← IO.FS.Handle.mk "/tmp/log" .append
  h.putStrLn "ran"
  let _ ← IO.Process.output {cmd := "definitely-not-a-real-executable"}
  return #[]

package repro where
  moreLinkArgs := run_io probe
```

The probe runs once, but `/tmp/log` holds `ran` twice on v4.30.0-rc2 and once from v4.31.0-rc1 on, so this stops mattering whenever the toolchain moves. Until then, every probe goes through `tryOutput`, which looks the tool up on `PATH` and spawns it only if it is there, and `xcrun` is skipped off Apple platforms.

Also worth noting: `IO.Process.output` does *not* throw for a missing executable, it reports exit code 255. So `cHeaderProbe`'s `try/catch` never protected anything — the corruption had already happened by the time it saw the exit code. It now goes through `tryOutput` too.

Verified on NixOS outside `shell.nix` (no zlib.pc, no cargo, no xcrun): before, the second `lake` invocation fails in both packages and the bench trace accumulates three objects; after, three consecutive invocations succeed in both and every trace file holds exactly one object.

🤖 Prepared with Claude Code

author: lishengg
body:
`ceph fs subvolume info` and `ceph fs subvolumegroup info` intermittently report a stale `bytes_used`, including `0`, while `ceph.dir.rbytes` on the same directory is already non-zero.

## Root cause

`SubvolumeBase.info()` and `Group.info()` derive `bytes_used` from a directory `statx(CEPH_STATX_SIZE)`. `Client::statx_to_mask()` never sets `CEPH_STAT_RSTAT` for that mask, so the resulting getattr is not forced to the auth MDS: it can be answered by a replica MDS, or short-circuited from cached `Fs` caps without contacting the MDS at all. Either path can return a stale directory size (including the initial `0`) before fresh recursive usage is reflected.

Reading `ceph.dir.rbytes`, by contrast, goes through the vxattr getxattr path, which forces `CEPH_STAT_RSTAT` (`VXATTR_RSTAT`) and is routed to the auth MDS. This is why the two APIs, both meant to expose the same recursive byte count, can disagree at the same instant.

## Fix

Read `bytes_used` from the `ceph.dir.rbytes` vxattr instead, falling back to the statx size on `cephfs.NoData`. Besides fixing the staleness, `bytes_used` is a user-visible recursive-usage field, so querying the explicit rbytes interface is more correct than depending on the overloaded directory stat size, whose recursive meaning is conditional on `client_dirsize_rbytes`.

## Why not change `statx_to_mask()`

Changing `Client::statx_to_mask()` to request `CEPH_STAT_RSTAT` for every `CEPH_STATX_SIZE` statx would broaden behavior beyond the mgr/volumes info path and make ordinary directory size statx calls force rstat/auth-MDS handling. This fix keeps the scope local to the user-visible recursive usage field that explicitly needs rbytes semantics.

## Performance note

This changes each subvolume/subvolumegroup info call to issue one additional `ceph.dir.rbytes` vxattr lookup, which requests `CEPH_STAT_RSTAT` and may require an auth-MDS round trip instead of using cached statx data. The extra cost is limited to the info path and buys correctness for a field that is expected to report recursive usage. I can benchmark larger batch-listing scenarios if reviewers are concerned.

## Verification

vstart cluster, Ceph main (`21.3.0-1135-g0dfc8345236`), at `max_mds = 1`. This is the strongest control, since the answering MDS is necessarily the auth MDS. Paired sampling captures `bytes_used` and `ceph.dir.rbytes` on the same directory in the same iteration.

| | pre-fix (buggy) | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| subvolume: `bytes_used = 0` while `ceph.dir.rbytes > 0` | hit within 50 iterations | **0 / 300** |
| subvolumegroup: same signature | hit at iteration 8 | **0 / 246** |

Across 546 paired samples the bug signature did not occur once. `bytes_used` now tracks `ceph.dir.rbytes` exactly, apart from sub-second sampling lag during active writes (inherent rstat propagation, both values non-zero). The pre-fix baseline reproduced the zero within 50 iterations under the identical setup.

body:
Closes #15.

Pointed agents at the real `git-spawn` repo and its backlog, read-only, and
recorded the findings in `docs/design/first-run.md`.

## Highlights

- Output quality is high: agents produced grounded, code-cited work (a concrete
  `git clean` implementation plan, a design argument citing the crate's own
  principles).
- Latency and cost are unbounded: grounded turns ran 50 to 120+ seconds with no
  turn cap.
- Cascade propagation is structural and easy to misconfigure: a debate stopped
  after one hop because the critic was neither subscribed nor addressed.
- In-flight observability is poor from the blocking CLI.
- No world-write gate: agents stayed read-only only because backend default
  permissions deny writes.

## Outcome

Failures named backlog items (#20 budget/turn caps, #19 gate) plus two new gaps:
#34 (path validation) and #35 (conversation ergonomics). No fabric change forced;
the stochastic-first loop working. Keep provoking.
