author: papadanico
body:
## Why

The domain is live, so the app should say so. This matters more than a config change usually would: the URL goes into every WhatsApp summary a user forwards and into the link preview anyone sees before they ever open the site. A link shared today has to still work in a year — which is exactly what a launch subdomain cannot promise.

## What changed

**One constant instead of four copies.** The address was written out in `layout.tsx`, `ladder/page.tsx`, `portfolio/page.tsx` and the share test. It is now `APP_URL` in `src/lib/share.ts`.

A move that half-happens is worse than one that has not started, because the links it leaves behind look fine to everyone except the people clicking them. So there is a test asserting the constant is not a deploy-generated host — which would also catch a per-PR `deploy-preview-*` hostname finding its way into a shared summary.

**`metadataBase`** drives every relative URL in the page metadata, so the `og:image` WhatsApp fetches for the preview card now resolves against the real domain.

## Deliberately not done

**No `netlify.toml` redirect from the old subdomain.** That is what Netlify's "primary domain" setting already does, and hand-writing a host redirect would duplicate it while risking the per-PR deploy-preview hostnames. Noted in the roadmap so the dashboard setting gets confirmed instead — worth checking that primary domain is set to `mwangazayield.org`.

**`ics.ts` keeps its `@mwangazayield` UID suffix.** iCal UIDs identify an event across re-exports; changing the scheme would make a re-exported auction reminder create a duplicate in someone's calendar rather than update the existing one.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 121 passing, including 2 new pinning the URL
- `npm run build` — compiles clean; no `netlify.app` remains anywhere in `out/`, and `og:image` reads `https://mwangazayield.org/og.png`
- All ten pages render in a real browser with no console errors

I could not reach the domain from this sandbox to confirm it resolves — outbound to that host is blocked by the proxy (403 on CONNECT), so this goes on the maintainer's word that it is up.

author: rhjensen79
body:
Closes the build-out half of #95. All 8 rows of set 1 are written and validated; this wires them into the blog and fixes the problems the runs exposed.

## The set

| # | slug | words | releases | validator |
|---|------|-------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | `how-long-does-a-kitchen-renovation-take` | 1,592 | 27 Jul | pass |
| 2 | `how-long-does-a-bathroom-renovation-take` | 2,278 | 28 Jul | pass (long) |
| 3 | `how-long-does-it-take-to-rewire-a-house` | 1,917 | 29 Jul | pass |
| 4 | `how-long-does-it-take-to-replace-windows` | 1,807 | 30 Jul | pass |
| 5 | `how-long-does-it-take-to-install-flooring` | 2,147 | 31 Jul | pass (long) |
| 6 | `how-long-does-a-roof-replacement-take` | 1,504 | 1 Aug | pass |
| 7 | `how-long-does-a-house-extension-take` | 2,408 | 2 Aug | pass (long) |
| 8 | `how-long-does-a-loft-conversion-take` | 1,885 | 3 Aug | pass |

**0 errors across all eight.** Each releases on its own day; none are visible yet.

## What the runs exposed

**The set was orphaned.** The cron can only link backwards, so the finished set was a chain, not a cluster — every post pointed at rows 1–2, row 1 pointed at nothing, and **not one of the 17 established posts linked into the set**. Eight pages reachable only from the sitemap, on a site with no external links, is precisely how pages end up crawled and never indexed.

Fixed with inbound links placed where they genuinely belong:
- `home-renovation-phases` → all seven duration posts, in the phase-5 paragraph about how long construction actually runs
- `kitchen-renovation-timeline` → the kitchen post (reciprocating the differentiation link) and flooring, in the week-6 section
- `where-to-start-renovating-new-house` → rewire, windows, roof, in the Bucket-A paragraph about work that displaces everything else
- the kitchen post → rewiring, where finding knob-and-tube changes the question being asked

**A date collision was about to happen.** The next cron run is Monday 27 July — the set's first release date. It would have written a second post onto that day, breaking the one-post-per-day rule. `prompt.md` §5 now says to walk forward to the first free date, because a page set can occupy dates weeks ahead.

## New checks

- **orphan check** — counts *inbound* links, scanning every post on disk. Outbound links are easy to satisfy and mean little alone; what moves crawl priority is whether anything points at a post. This is what found the problem above.
- **sibling rule now looks backwards only** — the version in #101 failed row 1 the moment row 2 landed, since row 1 cannot link forward in time. Left alone, every post would have failed as the next arrived.
- **tighter word ceiling for set posts** (2,100) — replaces a heading-similarity check I wrote, tested and deleted: it missed the case it was written for and threw a false positive on `kitchen-renovation-timeline`, where "Week 2: Rough-in" and "Week 7: Rough-in review" are legitimately different sections.

## Also surfaced, not fixed here

The orphan check found four **pre-existing** orphans: `best-home-improvement-apps`, `homezada-vs-houzz-pro`, `renovation-cost-overrun-statistics`, `where-to-start-renovating-new-house`. Straight #96 material.

## Verification

- 8/8 rows validate with 0 errors
- Build clean — 17 live posts, 0 of the set visible, correct until 27 July
- Orphan check reports no set post orphaned after the link pass

## Description

The current best practice recommends monitoring only tool performance and suggests refactoring tools with success rates below 95% or high average latency. This guidance is overly simplistic and does not reflect the more comprehensive recommendations of the AWS Well-Architected Framework [Agentic AI Lens AGENTPERF01-BP03](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/agentic-ai-lens/agentperf01-bp03.html).

The AI Lens recommends monitoring performance across agents, tools, and execution stages, using latency percentiles (p50, p90, and p99) for both individual stages and end-to-end execution over a rolling window, evaluated against defined service level objectives (SLOs). It also recommends prioritizing optimizations based on both contribution to end-to-end latency and optimization potential (also known as "addressable variance"), rather than focusing solely on the largest latency contributors.

This PR updates the guidance to better align with the AWS Well-Architected Framework Agentic AI Lens and adds a reference for readers who would like additional implementation guidance.

author: azizrahmanyaad
body:
## Summary

Investigated a report that the cash balance stayed stale, and that the same figure was showing for a user of a different company. Verified exhaustively that neither is a backend bug:

- A full HTTP round trip through the real controller + validation + policy layers correctly debits the cash account, both on the receive-and-pay endpoint and the standalone payment endpoint.
- Two separately-provisioned tenants each only ever see their own cash account and balance — no cross-tenant leak in the API.

Added two regression tests proving both of the above in `TenantIsolationTest`.

The remaining suspect: a shared-hosting reverse proxy or a browser caching a GET API response by URL alone, ignoring the session cookie that actually determines whose tenant data it is. That would explain a stale number (refreshing doesn't help a proxy-level cache) and the same number appearing for a different company (if the proxy serves back whichever tenant's response it happened to cache first for that URL).

- Added `PreventApiCaching` middleware, applied to the whole `api` group, marking every API response `no-store, no-cache, private` — the same fix already applied to the SPA shell in a previous PR (#50), now extended to the data API itself.

## Test plan
- [x] `php artisan test --testsuite=Feature` — 150 passed (2 new: cash-account isolation across tenants after a real payment, and every API response carries the no-cache header)

## Summary

Reworks the WhatsApp attendance-share output in `ViewAttendance` into a cleaner, more scannable format, driven by a single reusable message builder. Based on the design brief in `whatsapp-attendance-sharing-fe-feedback.md` (included).

### New message format
```
🎶 *VOB CHOIR ATTENDANCE*

*Thursday Rehearsal*
📅 Thu 09 Jul 26

✅ Present: 7  |  🟡 Apology: 3

*PRESENT MEMBERS*

*Soprano — 2*
Sis Anozie Rachael
Sis Chinaza Ugwuneke
...

*APOLOGIES — 3*
Sis Modeva Gloria — Soprano
Sis Peter Alice — Alto
Bro Kalu Samuel — Bass

🔴 *Absent Members: 2*

_Every rehearsal strengthens the sound we create together..._
```

### Changes
- **Header** derives the choir name from `org.name` (no hardcoded label), with a compact `Present | Apology` summary. Absent is shown once, at the bottom.
- **Present members** grouped by voice part with per-part counts; apologies are one combined list with each member's part beside the name.
- **Tone-selected** encouraging closing paragraph (strong / low / many-apologies / general).
- Handles empty parts, zero apologies, and unknown parts (`Other`).

### Bug fixes folded in
- Removed the hardcoded recipient number → now uses `wa.me/?text=` (no fixed recipient).
- Dropped leftover `console.log`s.
- Header counts now reconcile with the rendered lists (present list no longer mixes in apologies).

### Deferred
Session-name auto-generation (feedback doc §6) is intentionally **not** included — it needs a start-time field on the attendance record and reliable category names. Currently still uses the stored session name.

- Message output verified by simulating the builder with mixed sample data.

## Summary

- package bundled script entrypoints so the installed Node CLI executes `convert-to-cbz` without importing TypeScript source
- parse EPUB container, OPF spine, XHTML images, and SVG `href` / `xlink:href` references while preserving compatible source image bytes and repeated page occurrences
- classify PDF pages for extract-first conversion, preserving compatible embedded scans and rendering only composed or uncertain pages
- validate deterministic CBZ page entries, write through sibling partial archives, clean owned workspaces, skip conflicts by default, and support safe `--overwrite`
- refresh committed CLI distribution artifacts, add cross-platform build/check scripts, tests, documentation, and the completed OpenSpec change

## Why

The locally installed `chc` command discovered bundled scripts from the source tree and attempted to load TypeScript under Node. The previous converter also missed SVG-based fixed-layout EPUB pages, emitted placeholder image content for zero-page EPUBs, re-rendered every PDF page, leaked temporary workspaces, and wrote directly to final CBZ targets.

## Impact

- installed/local-mode `chc scripts run convert-to-cbz` now runs from packaged JavaScript
- existing CBZ targets are skipped unless `--overwrite` is explicitly provided
- PDF work requires `pdfinfo`, `pdfimages`, and `pdftoppm`; EPUB-only batches do not require Poppler
- MOBI, nested archives, loose image directories, metadata lookup, deduplication, and library organization remain preprocessing/out-of-scope concerns

body:
Auditoria do front (agora que e a unica pele) achou 7 decisoes na camada errada. A licao geral: o vazamento nao e teorico, ele APODRECE — a prova e que o nome do slot do arsenal ja tinha divergido: a tela dizia "Acessorio", o item que cai nela nasce "Manopla". A tela mostrava um nome que o item nao tem.

FRONT decidindo REGRA -> devolvido ao service:
- ArsenalService.NomeDoSlot(fase): nomeia o slot E o item que cai nele, uma tabela so (a tela precisa nomear slot VAZIO, que e por isso que ela tinha a copia). Teste trava os dois juntos.
- CapitulosService.FaccoesDaCampanha(): o mapa E a lista de capitulos, na ordem. O front deduzia "todas as faccoes menos Humanos" e acertava por coincidencia da ordem do enum.
- CampanhaService.PosicaoNoMapa()/SalvarPosicao(): o "ultimo lugar" e PROGRESSAO. O front gravava direto na porta de save — a unica gravacao do jogo fora de um service — enquanto o PerfilService ja apagava a mesma chave no wipe de conta. Dois donos.
- ArsenalService.EquiparItem PERSISTE sozinho: quando havia duas cascas, cada uma escolheu sua politica de quando salvar. Quem manda no dado decide quando ele e duravel.
- PerfilService.AvatarInicial()/PodeUsarAvatar(): a cara do jogador e trofeu de campanha.

MOTOR decidindo PELE -> devolvido a tela:
- Item.ValorFormatado()/NomeStat() SAIRAM do Domain: ":F0" e sufixo "%" sao exibicao. O Item guarda Valor + TipoStat; cada pele escreve do seu jeito.
- IApresentacao.AguardarAnimacao(Momento) no lugar de (int ms). O motor mandava 1500 em 10 lugares e a pele DIVIDIA o numero pra corrigir — sintoma de quem nao devia escolher, escolhendo. Agora o motor diz a BATIDA (Tick/Narracao/Golpe/Preparacao) e a pele da a duracao. Todas em 1500 hoje, DE PROPOSITO: mudou o dono, nao o sentimento da batalha. E o seam do MODO AUTOMATICO — uma pele que devolve ~0 e o motor nao sabe de nada.

NAO mexido porque esta certo: a validacao duplicada (o front valida pra UX, o back valida porque nao confia na tela) e a SessaoDoFront inteira (ids, lado esquerdo/direito, o _mostrado que segura a barra de vida ate o numero ser narrado) — presentation pura, no lugar certo.

Registrado sem pagar: emoji (Simbolo) no Domain e render dentro das regras, mas so DOI quando os sprites entrarem; pagar hoje custa tocar 36 champs por uma dor que nao existe. Gatilho nomeado, sem data (ROADMAP §CADA DECISAO NA SUA CAMADA).

+7 testes (87 verdes): NomeDoSlot casa com o item, EquiparItem persiste sozinho, posicao no mapa, FaccoesDaCampanha, e as 3 regras de avatar. Build 0 erros/0 avisos. Docs: CLAUDE.md dizia "Console hoje" (drift) e listava portas que nao existem mais.

author: riuch
body:
## What changed

**Question of the Day lives on Home now.** One prompt a day, same on both phones, and it no longer changes when you refresh — it's dealt from a date-seeded *deck* instead of a blind draw, so nothing repeats until the whole pool is used up and two days in a row can never match. (The old version collided ~5×/year and only surfaced 127 of 135 questions in a year — the birthday problem, not a broken PRNG. Verified: 0 consecutive repeats and every prompt exactly once per cycle, across 925 simulated days.)

**The Daily Q tab is now 🎭 Talk · Flirt · Dare.** Three decks — tap one, get a prompt, tap again for another. Drawn live rather than seeded, since one phone runs it while you're on a call.

**One switch: 💞 Together vs ✈️ Apart.** It decides what's physically possible (a dare you can do from 1,800 miles away is a different animal from one that needs a room) and runs the app hot — the red palette and filthier hearts now ride on Together, replacing the old After Dark toggle entirely.

| Deck | ✈️ Apart | 💞 Together |
|---|---|---|
| 💬 Talk | deep + romantic + long-distance | deep + romantic + funny |
| 😏 Flirt | spicy + nasty + filthy | same |
| 🔥 Dare | 55 remote dares | 50 in-person dares |

**Bank: 135 → 345 prompts.** +80 questions, a new `filthy` deck, and four Dare decks (apart/together × playful/explicit). Explicit content is deliberately *in* the decks — Home draws only from `QOTD_CATS` (funny + romantic + long-distance), so the always-visible page stays sweet.

## Database

Already applied to the live project — additively. `supabase/append_questions.py` inserts only what's missing and aborts if the stored rows are no longer a prefix of `BANK`, since order drift there would make an online phone and an offline one deal different decks. Nothing was deleted; verified 345 rows matching `BANK` exactly.

## Verified

Home card renders and survives reload; every deck draws from the right pool in both modes; mode switch flips theme, subtitle, hint, chips and redeals; all four tabs; mobile (375px) and desktop grid; no console errors.

## 目标

在固定 24 行虚拟化与最多 6 轮自动目录整理基础上，继续优化大世界目录的内存路径和玩家定位体验。

author: avipeltz
body: ## Summary - Adds a **sort mode** for sidebar projects — Manual (existing drag order, default), Date created, Last updated — persisted per-user in `v2UserPreferences` and switchable from a new radio dropdown in the PROJECTS header. - Adds an **inline filter**: a `VscListFilter` icon in the PROJECTS header expands into a text input; case-insensitive substring match over project, workspace, and section names. ## Why / Context The project list was ordered solely by manual drag (`tabOrder`), with no way to find a project/workspace by name or surface recently active work. Inspired by PostHog Code's sidebar (sort by created/updated + searchable switcher). ## How It Works - Sorting/filtering are applied as derived memos in `DashboardSidebar` — the data hook (`useDashboardSidebarData`) and the persisted `tabOrder` remain untouched, so switching back to Manual restores the hand-arranged order exactly. - **"Last updated" sorts by the most recently updated workspace** in each project (including inside sections), not the project's own `updatedAt` — the host only bumps project `updatedAt` on metadata patches (e.g. rename), so workspace timestamps are the real activity signal. - The filter helper returns derived project/section objects with `isCollapsed: false` so matches are auto-expanded and non-matching siblings pruned; persisted collapse state is never written. In the default state (manual + empty query) the original array references pass through, preserving existing memo stability. - Drag-to-reorder is disabled (`useSortable({ disabled })` + drag-start/end guards) while a non-manual sort or filter is active, so a sorted/pruned order can never be persisted into `tabOrder`. - Filter state is ephemeral `useState`; it auto-clears when the sidebar collapses to icon-only (the input is hidden there, and an invisible filter would silently hide projects). Shortcut labels (⌘1–⌘9) are computed from the sorted-but-unfiltered list so they stay stable while typing. ## Manual QA Checklist ### Sort - [ ] Switching Manual → Date created → Last updated reorders projects; drag handles are inert in non-manual modes - [ ] Sort mode persists after app restart - [ ] Switching back to Manual restores the original drag order; dragging works again - [ ] Touching a workspace raises its project in "Last updated" ### Filter - [ ] Typing a workspace-name match auto-expands its project/section and prunes non-matching siblings - [ ] A project-name match keeps all its children - [ ] Garbage query shows the "No projects match" row; Esc clears and restores collapse state and DnD - [ ] Expanding the filter while the PROJECTS list is collapsed expands the list - [ ] Collapsing the sidebar to icon-only with an active filter shows all projects again - [ ] ⌘1–⌘9 target the same workspaces while a filter is typed ## Testing - `bun run typecheck` - `bun run lint` - `bun test src/renderer/routes/_authenticated/_dashboard/components/DashboardSidebar/utils` — 11 new tests for the sort/filter helpers ## Design Decisions - **Sort in the component, not the data hook**: sort is a view preference with one consumer; keeping `useDashboardSidebarData` on `tabOrder` preserves its referential-stability machinery and the optimistic drag path. - **Derived expansion instead of a `forceExpanded` prop**: avoids threading a prop through 3+ components and guarantees persisted collapse state is never mutated by filtering. - **No branch-name matching**: v2 workspace names are branch-derived; matching hidden text would surface rows whose visible label doesn't contain the query. https://claude.ai/code/session_01MycxWhiezTmQAbvPR4tcYW --- --- ## Summary by cubic Adds sorting and inline filtering to Projects in the dashboard sidebar so you can quickly find work and organize lists. “Last updated” uses recent workspace activity and the chosen sort persists per user. - **New Features** - Sort menu in the PROJECTS header: Manual (default), Last updated, Date created; preference saved in `v2UserPreferences`. Switching back to Manual restores drag order. Uses a list-filter icon and a dim “Sort by” label with checkmarks. - Inline filter with a magnifier; case-insensitive match on project, section, and workspace names. Matches auto-expand, non-matching siblings are hidden, and a “No projects match” message appears when empty. Esc clears, and the filter auto-clears when the sidebar collapses. - Dragging is gated to protect ordering: project drag is disabled while a non-manual sort or a filter is active; workspace/section drag is disabled while a filter is active so pruned lists can’t write a bad `tabOrder`. ⌘1–⌘9 shortcuts remain stable while typing. - **Bug Fixes** - Clicking items in the sort menu or Add Project menu no longer toggles the Projects collapse; dropdown events are stopped from bubbling. - Filter clear button is keyboard-operable and doesn’t blur the input. - Filtering preserves object identity when items don’t change, keeping memoized rows stable and avoiding flicker. - Use the theme’s destructive color for failed automation statuses for better contrast across themes. Written for commit 119f90ada9b4886f0f7202410016c9f02b020fc9. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added dashboard sidebar sorting controls (manual, created, recent activity) with your selection saved for future sessions. * Added an inline project filter that searches projects, workspaces, and sections; matching items auto-expand, and a “No projects match …” message appears when nothing matches. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved header interactions so filter/sort controls don’t unintentionally collapse the sidebar. * Disabled drag-and-drop reordering while filtering is active or when sorting isn’t set to manual. * **Tests** * Added coverage for sorting (including tie-breaking) and filtering behavior.

author: pichaautobot
body:
Resolves #954

Generated by orchestrator (claude session `10edac59-1a9e-47c2-9987-e496cce8d24d`).

---
_Last agent message:_

Done — committed as `49577d6 refactor: finalize the github client and narrow the package surface` (64 files, +515/−610). Working tree clean, nothing pushed.

## What changed

**Production**
- `orchestrator/_github_internals.py` **deleted**; its three cross-cutting seams (`_for_worker_thread`, `_cached_label`, `_emit_stage_enter`) now live on the concrete `GitHubClient` in `orchestrator/github/client.py`, which composes `GitHubReviewMixin, GitHubLabelMixin, GitHubChecksMixin` directly. Token resolution, PyGithub init, worker cloning, the label cache, and the analytics/audit stage-enter hook are byte-for-byte the same logic.
- `orchestrator/github/__init__.py` is now four lines of ordinary owner imports plus a narrow documented `__all__ = ("GitHubClient", "PinnedState")`. The lazy `__getattr__` and the `_PINNED_STATE_/_REVIEW_/_CHECK_EXPORTS` tuples, all private re-exports (`_iter_new_non_pr_issues`, `_review_state_for_head`, `_normalize_check_runs`, …), the label/event re-exports, and the four dead `_HTTP_*` constants are gone. No `_github_*` module remains in production.
  - Eager binding is cycle-safe here because the initializer imports only *submodules*, never facade names — a submodule import binds on the parent package even mid-initialization. `tests/github/test_imports.py` subprocess-imports all nine modules cold to pin this.
- 13 export manifests retargeted from `orchestrator.github` to `orchestrator.github.client` / `.pinned_state`, matching the rule from #948 that a lazily-resolved binding must name the owner, not a facade that holds an eager copy.
- `.flake8` github scope `WPS413` → `WPS410`, and that scope is now documented in `docs/configuration.md`'s CI section (previously undocumented).

**Tests**
- New `tests/support/github/`: the eight fake-client modules moved there via `git mv` with the `fake_github_` prefix dropped, plus `factories.py` for `make_issue`, leaving `tests/fakes.py` as a pure-binding bridge for the still-flat workflow tests.
- `tests/test_workflow_list_pollable.py` → `tests/github/test_list_pollable.py` (polling contract) plus a new `tests/github/test_client.py` (label cache, worker-clone login reuse moved out of `test_pinned_state.py`, and new coverage for explicit-token / `repo_spec`-slug / empty-token construction).
- Five per-owner `*FacadeOwnershipTest` classes replaced by one `PublicSurfaceTest` (exact `__all__`, owner identity, `AttributeError` for owner-only names); ~18 flat tests and the `tests/github/` suite now import owners (`orchestrator.github.labels`, `.pinned_state`, `.client`).

**Docs**: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/observability.md`, and the develop skill's fakes pointer.

## Verification
- `ruff check orchestrator tests` — clean; `flake8 orchestrator tests --select=WPS` — clean; `git diff --check` — clean.
- `env -u CLOSED_ISSUE_SWEEP_EVERY_N_TICKS pytest tests` — 2287 passed, 36 skipped (plotly-optional).
- With this shell's exported `CLOSED_ISSUE_SWEEP_EVERY_N_TICKS=10`, `ClosedSweepCadenceTest::test_default_runs_closed_sweep_every_tick` fails — the known env-fragile baseline, now in `tests/github/test_list_pollable.py`. Reproduced identically on an `origin/main` worktree (`1 failed, 10 passed` with the var set; `11 passed` with `env -u`), so it is not from this diff.

One note on the issue text: `_github_api.py` no longer existed (it was deleted in #953), so "replace `_github_api.py` with ordinary explicit owner imports" was carried out against the construct that had taken over its role — the facade's lazy `__getattr__` and export tuples.

author: orlandoburli
body:
## Summary

- Adds a permission check to both \`.env\` loading paths (\`internal/config/config.go\` and \`internal/cli/root.go\`)
- **If the \`.env\` file is group- or world-readable (\`mode & 0o044 != 0\`), loading is refused**: an error message naming the file, its current mode, and the remediation command (\`chmod 0600 <path>\`) is printed, and credentials are never set in the process environment
- Matches the existing plugin-directory permission stance (\`checkDirOwnerOnly\`), which skips group/world-writable dirs for the same reason
- Unix-specific check is behind \`//go:build !windows\`; a no-op stub covers Windows (ACLs, not Unix permission bits)

## Migration

Any \`.env\` with permissions broader than \`0600\` will be skipped after this change. Run:

\`\`\`sh
chmod 0600 .env
\`\`\`

before upgrading, or move secrets to shell exports / a secrets manager.

## What changed vs. previous PRs

- **PR #269** — hard refusal but title falsely claimed "warn-and-continue" (Correctness veto)
- **PR #300 (previous push)** — warn-only; doesn't satisfy the P1 acceptance criteria
- **This push** — honest hard refusal: title, commit, summary, and tests all say "refuse"

## Test plan

- [x] \`TestCheckDotEnvPerms\` — 0600 (ok), 0640 (error), 0644 (error), missing file (nil)
- [x] \`TestLoadDotEnvRefuseOnBadPerms\` — 0644 file: error on stderr AND key not set
- [x] \`TestLoadDotEnvLoadsOnGoodPerms\` — 0600 file: key loaded normally
- [x] \`go test ./internal/config/... ./internal/cli/...\` — all green
- [x] \`go build ./...\` — clean build

Closes #248

author: kadragon
body:
buildMessages proved completeness by index contiguity plus a starts-at-0
check. Neither bounds the trailing end: a walk that stops short yields
0..k, which passes both and exports as a plausible partial (AGENTS.md #4).

Claude declares the conversation's whole row count on every row via
div[role="article"][aria-setsize], so a shortfall against it is proof.
Extraction now fails loud, splitting the message the same two ways an
interior gap already does. The same total gives the walk a real
termination condition: it stops once it holds every declared row and has
gone quiet for CONTENT_QUIET_ROUNDS. The quiet requirement is
load-bearing -- a position being filled is not a turn being finished, so
ending on the count alone would export a still-streaming response at
whatever fragment was rendered.

Earned by a live Playwright session, not assumed: four conversations
walked end to end (14/16/26/56 rows), all 112 rows carried the attribute,
the value was constant across each walk, and it counts rows not messages
(56 vs 58 turn nodes, 26 vs 27). Twelve more spot-checked. The declared
total tracks the live list (2 -> 4 across one exchange), which is why the
adapter reads the smallest observed value; a hydration trace found no low
intermediate value to latch onto. Recorded in docs/live-dom-verification.md.

Where no total is declared, both the gate and the early exit are skipped
and behavior is unchanged -- markup drift must degrade, not fail closed.

Five new tests (424 -> 429), each verified to fail under targeted
neutralization of the code it covers.

author: chriscase
body:
## What changed

- removes untrusted Confluence response bodies and raw transport URLs from public/core diagnostics while preserving the stable status taxonomy and actionable 401/403/404/429/CQL/network guidance
- makes every Confluence Read API return its bounded retry/recovery trail with the parsed value, preventing convenience wrappers from silently discarding recovery evidence
- retries GET requests only for HTTP 429 and 500–599, with at most two additional attempts and the documented 200 ms / 400 ms schedule
- distinguishes `rate_limited` from `transient_server` trails across search, page fetch, children/root browse, ancestors, attachments, space listing, Settings probe, and sync observation
- leaves create/update mutation requests non-retrying and documents that mid-request cancellation remains unsupported

## Why

Reopened issues #457 and #459 identified two literal close-proof gaps: a hostile Confluence/proxy response could reflect credentials into returned error text, and retry notes were dropped by most Read product paths. This change closes those gaps without altering SSRF, keychain, or allowlist ownership.

Addresses #457 and #459. Both issues will be closed manually only after this exact head passes hosted CI and the merged main path is re-verified.

## Focused proof

- `cargo test -p cd-core confluence_ro::tests:: -- --nocapture` — 26 passed
- `cargo test -p cd-core confluence_read_tools_surface_retry_recovery_trails -- --nocapture` — 1 passed
- fixtures cover reflected Bearer/API/Basic/userinfo/query/body credential material, 429/500/503 recovery, bounded persistent-5xx exhaustion, one-request 400/401/403/404 behavior, one-request mutation failure, success without a retry trail, Settings probe redaction, and all representative Read tools

## Full local gate (feature head `c654f652dbc7986fb115a3933ddb59ea54d4d472`)

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace` — 581 core passed, 5 ignored; 50 server passed; golden/doc tests passed
- Tauri fmt, Clippy, and check
- `npx tsc -b`
- `npm run lint` — zero errors (six pre-existing warnings)
- `npm test -- --run` — 163 Vitest + 5 Node tests passed
- `npm run build`
- `sh scripts/check_claims.sh`
- `git diff --check`; clean worktree

No root Cargo profile, CI workflow, DuckDB dependency, runner-disk, test-skip, or unrelated feature changes.

Part 1/5 of stack #12296, which routes `wandb.login()`'s network logic through wandb-core.

author: wolfiesch
body:
## What

- Mark `mnemopi.embeddingApiKey` and `mnemopi.llmApiKey` as `secret` in `SETTINGS_SCHEMA`.
- Add a schema test that fails when a credential-shaped setting the settings panel can display is added without masking.

## Why

I was walking `SETTINGS_SCHEMA` to see which settings are safe to expose to an external client, and noticed both Mnemopi keys have `ui` metadata but no `secret: true`. Masking is driven by `ui.secret` (`settings-defs.ts` -> `settings-selector.ts`), so today the panel renders both API keys in plain text in the settings row, and the text editor shows them unmasked while you type. Of 439 settings, `hindsight.apiToken` was the only one marked.

To be precise about the fix: the editor still preloads the current value (`settings-selector.ts:1139` passes it to `TextInputSubmenu`, which sets `input.mask` and then `setValue`). What changes is that the row and the input render as dots instead of the key.

The test's name heuristic is a review aid for the test only, deliberately not a runtime check: a setting name is not a security property, and it both misses and false-positives. Its exemption list is itself asserted against real setting paths so a renamed setting cannot leave a stale excuse behind.

Out of scope: `auth.broker.token`, `searxng.token`, `searxng.basicPassword` and `dev.autoqaPush.token` are also credentials, but they have no `ui` block, so the panel never displays them and `ui.secret` has nowhere to live. Marking those needs a metadata field outside `ui`, which felt like a separate change rather than something to fold in here.

## Testing

- `bun test test/settings-schema-secrets.test.ts`: covers that no UI-visible credential-shaped setting is unmasked, that the three known credential settings stay marked, that only string settings are marked secret, and that every heuristic exemption still maps to a real setting path.
- `bun test test/settings-manager.test.ts test/selector-settings-side-effects.test.ts test/settings-schema-secrets.test.ts`: green.
- `bun run check`: clean (biome + tsgo + cargo).
- Confirmed `getUi("mnemopi.embeddingApiKey").secret === true` and that `pathToSettingDef` now yields `{ type: "text", secret: true }`, which is the flag `settings-selector` passes to `TextInputSubmenu` as `input.mask`.

body: Closes the session-management asks: **each session shows its memory usage and has a terminate button to safely unregister + close its tmux window**, plus a root-cause guard so a reused tmux `%N` can't re-bind a stale transcript. ## 1. Per-session memory - `lib/sessions.js`: `buildProcMemTable()` takes ONE `ps -A -o pid,ppid,rss` snapshot per refresh; `sumTreeRssMB(panePid, table)` sums the RSS of the pane's whole process subtree (claude + MCP servers + node + caffeinate…). body:
Two of the issues the PR5 harness ([ADR-0015](../blob/main/docs/architecture/adr/0015-accessibility-and-e2e-testing.md)) surfaced — both real fixes. The broader `color-contrast` rule stays baselined (see below).

## 🐛 Duplicate `id="app"` (structural)

`App.vue`'s root reused `id="app"` — the same id as the `index.html` mount point — so Vue nested **two `id="app"` elements**. Root is now `class="app-root"`; the rule is `#app, .app-root { min-height: 100vh }`, so **both** elements keep the exact same computed style (zero visual change) and the DOM has a single `id="app"`.

## Dimmed nav-tree labels (contrast)

`TOCTree.vue` applied `opacity: 0.9` / `0.8` to `.sector-label` / `.industry-label`. That dimmed already-muted text below AA:

| element | token (solid) | dimmed → effective |
|---|---|---|
| count badge | `--text-muted` #6E6E6E (5.1:1) | ~#7d7d7d ≈ **4.1:1** |
| industry label | `--text-secondary` #595959 (7.5:1) | ~#7a7a7a ≈ **4.3:1** |

Removed both opacities — the token colors already encode the muted hierarchy accessibly, and size/weight/uppercase still separate the levels.

## Why `color-contrast` stays baselined

The full-page scan showed contrast is **app-wide**, dominated by a design decision this batch shouldn't make unilaterally: **~93% of failing nodes are the semantic price colors on white** — up-green `#22ab94` (~2.5:1) and down-red `#f7525f` (~3.3:1). Meeting AA there means restyling the up/down language app-wide → left baselined for a dedicated a11y pass. This PR removes the nav-tree contributor and corrects ADR-0015 to describe the true scope.

## Verification

- `npm run test:e2e` — **4 passed** (contrast still baselined ⇒ gate green; the e2e CI job re-verifies)
- `vitest run` — **565 passed**; `vue-tsc --noEmit` — **0**; `vite build` — **✓ built**

## Scope

- ✅ In: duplicate-id fix, nav-tree opacity fix, ADR-0015 correction.
- ❌ Out: the semantic up/down color contrast (design decision) and other polish items (own PR).

author: dmitryduev
body:
Description
-----------
Part 2/5 of stack #12296.

Adds an `AuthHandler` to `core/internal/wbapi` that serves `AuthenticateRequest` by running the `Viewer` GraphQL query. Works identically for API keys and identity token files (federated identity). The `Viewer` query now also selects `username` and `email`, which the response includes along with the default entity, teams, and user flags.

Credentials are considered valid exactly if the server resolves a viewer: null fields (including the entity) and field-level GraphQL errors with partial data are accepted, matching how permissive verification was before this stack (unusual accounts and old server versions may omit fields). 

Also fixes two pre-existing bugs in the OAuth2 credential provider that the new verification path would otherwise inherit: the identity token file is stripped of surrounding whitespace (a trailing newline from `echo` or an editor used to be sent as part of the token and rejected), and the assertion is URL-encoded in the token exchange request.

An alternative was to extend the connection-level `ServerAuthenticateRequest` used by the experimental C# client, but that message is API-key-only and its handler is already marked for deprecation in favor of the API-instance workflow used here.

author: dmitryduev
body:
Description
-----------
Part 3/5 of stack #12296.

Adds `ServiceApi.authenticate()` and replaces `wandb.sdk.lib.server` with `wandb.sdk.lib.identity`: `SessionIdentity` lazily resolves the session credentials to a typed, frozen `Identity` (default entity, username, email, teams, flags) through wandb-core instead of querying the backend with the `requests` on the python side.

Naming notes: "Identity" rather than "user" because credentials may belong e.g. to a service account; the docstring bridges to the server-side term for this, the "viewer". The old `Server` name predated wandb-core and described where the data came from, not what the object is for. `SessionIdentity` owns its `ServiceApi` (created in `__init__`, lazy) and caches successful resolution (failures are retried on the next access, preserving the pre-stack behavior where a transient error at banner time did not drop the email/save_code user settings for the session); its lifetime is one credentials epoch, and `wandb_setup.update_user_settings()` invalidates by discarding the instance. This also retires the old thread-based `util.async_call` timeout hack: the mailbox wait in `ServiceApi` bounds the request properly, and a hang no longer leaks a Python thread.

`AuthIdentityTokenFile` now stores absolute paths for the token and credentials files: they are read and written by the wandb-core service process, whose working directory can differ from the client's (e.g. a pre-started shared service, or `chdir` after setup).

author: jmanuelrosa
body:
Two changes to the staff-engineer seat fleet under `roles/ai/files/claude/plugins/`.

## Reference naming

The failure-modes reference covering how a failure surfaces had drifted to five different filenames across the 14 seats. Five renames bring that down to two names, chosen on what the files actually contain:

| Seat | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `observability.md` | `failure-visibility.md` |
| data | `errors-and-observability.md` | `failure-visibility.md` |
| gtm | `errors-and-observability.md` | `failure-visibility.md` |
| mobile | `errors-and-observability.md` | `failure-visibility.md` |
| design | `errors-and-observability.md` | `errors-and-resilience.md` |

`failure-visibility.md` now covers 10 seats and is about instrumentation: whether a failure surfaces with enough identity to correlate it. `errors-and-resilience.md` covers 2 and is about UI error boundaries, fallback states, and retry semantics.

`design` moves to the resilience name rather than the observability one because its content is unmodeled error states, uncaught render errors, and torn-out tracking. That is `frontend`'s domain, not `backend`'s instrumentation. Grouping it by filename would have put it in the wrong place.

Six seats already used `failure-visibility.md` (analytics, cloud, database, dx, platform, qa) and `frontend` already used `errors-and-resilience.md`, so those are untouched.

Two seats are excluded on purpose. `security` is a read-only advisor seat and has no reference of this kind; its `detection-and-evidence.md` is a different domain. `sre` is the observability seat itself and splits the concern across nine specialized references, so there is nothing to rename.

## CLAUDE.md

The 14 seat plugins had no mention in CLAUDE.md even though the skill and agent registries are documented in detail directly above. A reader would reasonably assume seats are registered the same way, and they are not.

The new section records the plugin layout, the decision that seats carry no registry rows (`plugin.json` is their metadata and `claude-agent` discovers seats by scanning `plugins/`), the implementer and advisor variants, the failure-modes router shape, and the two shared reference names so the next seat does not coin a third.

## Verification

- 126 trigger-table links across all 14 seats resolve, with 0 broken and 0 orphaned references
- none of the three retired filenames remain anywhere under `roles/ai/files/claude/`
- the H1 heading matches the new filename in all five renamed files
- `claude-agent list` still discovers all 14 seat plugins
- git records each of the five as a rename, not a delete plus add

`make lint` and `make syntax` were not run. Both need the interactive vault password, which is not available in a headless session. The diff is Markdown only and touches no YAML.

author: dmitryduev
body:
Description
-----------
Part 4/5 of stack #12296. Related to #11722.

`wandb.login(verify=True)` and `wandb login --verify` now verify identity token (federated identity) credentials instead of silently skipping them, and API key verification goes through wandb-core like (most of? :)) the rest of the SDK's network traffic.

`_verify_login()` now takes a `wbauth.Auth` and sends an `Authenticate` request through the service API. Its exception contract is preserved: any failure, including failures to start or connect to the wandb-core service process, raises the documented `AuthenticationError`. `wandb_login` no longer references the `requests` library, yay. Also the previous `requests.ConnectionError` handler was dead code, since `ServiceApi` raises `WandbApiFailedError`, oops.

- [x] I updated CHANGELOG.unreleased.md, or it's not applicable

author: poulditlev
body:
## Formål

Trin 3 af 3 — **sløjfen lukkes**: borgeren ansøger via selvbetjening, systemet opretter en sag, sagsbehandleren afgør den og kan effektuere den til en ydelse.

Bygget oven på den eksisterende adgangsmodel og borgerflade. Ingen ny adgangsregel-motor, og **domænelaget er uændret** — ansøgningsindholdet ligger som data på sagen. En borger må fortsat **aldrig** oprette ydelser, forny eller danne opkrævninger direkte; det håndhæves på serveren.

## DEL 1 — En ansøgning skaber en sag, ikke en ydelse

- Borgeren kan ansøge om **ekstra beholder**, **anden beholderstørrelse**, **ekstra sæt sække til farligt affald** og **afmelding af en løbende ydelse**.
- Ansøgningen opretter en **sag** (status `MODTAGET`, kanal `SELVBETJENING`) med ansøgningens indhold (art, størrelse, ønsket dato) gemt på sagen. Den ændrer aldrig ydelser/materiel direkte.
- Nyt endpoint `POST /api/ejendomme/:id/ansoegninger`. Serveren kræver borgerrettigheden `ANSOEG_SELVBETJENING` **og** adgang til egen ejendom, og afviser alt andet end at oprette en sag (403). Serveren udleder selv sagstype og materieltype — frontend kan ikke smugle andet igennem.

## DEL 2 — Sagsbehandlerens side af sløjfen

- Selvbetjeningssager er tydeligt markeret i sagslisten (kanal-badge + hvad der er ansøgt om).
- En **imødekommende afgørelse** (hjemmel obligatorisk, som hidtil) kan **effektueres** som en eksplicit handling (`POST /api/sager/:id/effektuer`), der opretter den ansøgte ydelse ved at **genbruge** den eksisterende ydelses-oprettelse med korrekt periode. Afgørelsens hjemmel bæres videre til ydelsen. Kun sagsbehandler (`EFFEKTUER_ANSOEGNING`); kan kun ske én gang.

## DEL 3 — Borgerens overblik

Efter ansøgningen ser borgeren sagen under "Mine sager" med status i klar tale (Modtaget → Under behandling → Afgjort: imødekommet/afslag) og hvad der blev ansøgt om. Borgeren kan følge sagen — men ikke ændre eller trække den tilbage endnu.

## DEL 4 — Kvalitet og sporbarhed

- **Sporbarhed:** hele forløbet — ansøgning (med hvem *og* i hvilken rolle), afgørelse og effektuering — står i sagens append-only journal.
- **Tests** (alle **128** grønne, +6 nye i `adgang.integration.test.ts`):
  - borgers ansøgning → sag med kanal `SELVBETJENING` og status `MODTAGET`;
  - ansøgning opretter **ikke** en ydelse direkte;
  - borger kan kun ansøge på egen ejendom (403 på andres);
  - borger må ikke effektuere (403);
  - sagsbehandler effektuerer imødekommet ansøgning → ydelse med korrekt periode (start + binding); dobbelt-effektuering afvises;
  - imødekommet ansøgning uden hjemmel afvises (allerede på afgørelsestrinnet).
- **WCAG 2.1 AA** i ansøgningsdialogen: fokusstyring (fokus ind ved åbning, tilbage ved luk), labels på alle felter, feltbundne fejl (`aria-describedby`/`aria-invalid`), fejloversigt med `role="alert"`.
- Rettet en latent kollision: nye sagsnumre startede på et sagsnummer der allerede var brugt i seed.
- `datamodel.md` (ansøgningens indhold på sagen, afsnit 5; roller udvidet, afsnit 6) og `README.md` (Lag 7) opdateret.

## Verifikation

`npm run typecheck` rent. Manuelt (Playwright) bekræftet hele sløjfen: borger ansøger om en 660 l beholder → sagen dukker op under "Mine sager" (Modtaget, selvbetjening); sagsbehandler ser SELVBETJENING-markering + "Ansøgt om", træffer imødekommende afgørelse, effektuerer → den løbende ydelse oprettes (2026-10-01 – 2027-10-01) og sagen viser **Effektueret**.

author: blazesgl
body:
Closes #487

## Summary
Adds pattern fills beyond color on ApiUsage statuses so that users with color vision deficiencies (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia) can distinguish call-history statuses by texture as well as by color. This satisfies WCAG 1.4.1 (Use of Color).

## Changes

### `src/index.css`
- Added a diagonal-stripe SVG background pattern to `.status-cell.error` so the error status is visually distinct from success without relying on color alone
- `.status-cell.success` retains a solid fill as the baseline reference state (no supplemental pattern)
- The pattern uses `currentColor` so it inherits the status token color (`--danger`) at low opacity, keeping it subtle

### `src/components/CallHistoryRow.tsx`
- Added `data-pattern="baseline"` attribute to success status cells
- Added `data-pattern="stripes"` attribute to error status cells
- These attributes expose the pattern semantics for assistive technology and testing

### `src/components/CallHistoryRow.test.tsx`
- Added 4 focused tests under a `Pattern fills for color-blind accessibility` section:
  - Success cell has `data-pattern="baseline"` (no fill pattern)
  - Error cell has `data-pattern="stripes"` (diagonal pattern fill)
  - Error cell references a CSS data-URI pattern in the stylesheet
  - Success and error cells expose different pattern semantics

## Accessibility
- WCAG 1.4.1 compliant: status indicators are distinguishable by texture as well as color
- Follows the same pattern-fill convention already established in `StatusBadge` and `patterns.css`

## Testing
- All 18 `CallHistoryRow` tests pass
- All 5 `ApiUsage` tests pass
- All 33 `ApiDetailPage` tests pass
- No regressions in existing test suite

author: manfredas370
body:
Closes Dependabot alert #17.

## Why

`sharp@0.34.5` carries inherited libvips vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-33327, CVE-2026-33328,
CVE-2026-35590, CVE-2026-35591 — **high**), patched in `sharp@0.35.0`.

It reaches this repo only through the dev toolchain: `wrangler` → `miniflare` → `sharp`. That's
why CI never caught it — the audit gate runs `--omit=dev`. It also means **real exposure is nil**:
sharp runs inside miniflare for local `wrangler dev`, never ships to the Worker, and the CVEs
require processing untrusted images locally. This is about clearing a High badge, not closing an
open door.

## What

`wrangler` 4.113.0 → **4.114.0**, which pulls `miniflare` 4.20260722.0 → **`sharp@0.35.2`**.

A patch bump inside the existing `^4.113.0` range; the manifest range moves to `^4.114.0` so a
regenerated lockfile can't slide back.

## Verification

- `npm audit --audit-level=high` across the **full** tree now exits **0** (it failed on sharp before).
- `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` — the CI gate — still exits 0.
- CI proves the toolchain itself on a clean `npm ci`: `npm run lint`, `npm test`, and
  `npm run build` (`wrangler deploy --dry-run`) all exercise the new wrangler. Tests are
  unaffected by the miniflare bump — `vitest.config.mts` uses the plain `node` environment,
  not `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`.

## What this does *not* fix

The remaining Dependabot alert — `@hono/node-server` **moderate**, `serve-static` path traversal
on Windows — is **not actionable**:

- Patched in 2.0.5, but `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.29.0` is already the latest published version
  and still pins `@hono/node-server: ^1.19.9`. No SDK version resolves it.
- `npm audit fix --force` "fixes" it by **downgrading** the SDK to 1.24.3 — a regression.
- Production runs on workerd, not Node, so `@hono/node-server` never executes there.

Leaving it for upstream to move to hono-node-server v2.

body:
## 📝 작업 내용

- **2중 가드레일 기반 에러 메시지 UX 연동 (`sanitizeErrorMessage`)**
  - E2E 퀴즈 준비/생성 파이프라인(본문 추출 ➔ AI 검증 ➔ 지식 연결 ➔ 퀴즈 생성) 및 퀴즈 풀기/채점/리포트 영역 전반에 **2중 에러 가드레일**을 도입했습니다.
  - **1차 (백엔드 에러 계약 화이트리스트)**: `BAD_WORD`, `NOT_DEVELOPMENT_RELATED`, `PROMPT_INJECTION_DETECTED`, `QUIZ_NOT_FOUND` 등 명시적으로 약속된 유저 안내용 비즈니스 에러 코드만 `message` 출력을 허용하고, 미분류/시스템 예외 코드는 안전한 Fallback 메시지로 자동 전환합니다.
  - **2차 (기술 아티팩트 실시간 필터링)**: 백엔드 개발자 디버깅 문구(예: `validationScore`, `NullPointer`, `Exception`, `SQL`, `PASSED`, `{}` 등)가 섞여 유출되는 것을 차단하며, 표준 한국어 표현(예: `개발/기술`)은 안전하게 허용합니다.
- **페이지별 에러 바인딩 및 정밀 Fallback 처리**
  - `LearningPreparationPage`: 콘텐츠 검증 거절(`REJECTED`), 실패(`FAILED`), 퀴즈 생성 에러, 폴링 네트워크 단선 시 `sanitizeErrorMessage`를 거친 정돈된 메시지 렌더링
  - `QuizPage`: 퀴즈 시작 및 상세 문제 조회 실패 시 `ApiError` 및 일반 `Error`에 대해 2중 가드레일 적용 및 미사용 상태/컴포넌트 정리
  - `GradingPage`: 제출 및 채점 예외 발생 시 코드 없는 일반 `Error` 객체는 범용 Fallback 메시지를 유지하고, 409 중복 제출 재조회 실패 시 2차 에러 처리 보존
  - `ResultReportPage`: 404/403 등 정해진 UX 고정 안내 문구를 우선 보호하고, 사유가 불분명한 `unknown-error` 시에만 2중 가드레일을 통과한 메시지 바인딩
- **웹 접근성(a11y) 알림 속성 보완**
  - `LearningPreparationPage` 내 `ErrorFeedbackPanel`에 `role="alert"` 및 `aria-live="assertive"` 속성을 추가하여, 동적으로 발생하는 검증·생성 에러가 보조기기(스크린 리더) 사용자에게 실시간 전달되도록 개선
- **단위 및 통합 테스트 보완**
  - `LearningPreparationPage.test.tsx`: 검증 거절(`REJECTED`), 실패(`FAILED`), 폴링 네트워크 에러(`isValidationError`), 퀴즈 생성 API 에러 렌더링 테스트 5종 추가 및 타입 헬퍼 정비

## 🧪 기술적 의사결정 및 검증 (성능/정합성 필수!)

- **선택한 기술 및 배경:**
  - 단순 하드코딩 문구에 묻히던 백엔드의 친절한 사유 메시지를 유저에게 우선 전달하되, 개발자용 내부 기술 문구가 유출되지 않도록 **백엔드 에러 코드 화이트리스트 + 기술 아티팩트 필터링**을 조합한 **2중 안심 가드레일 아키텍처**를 수립했습니다.
- **데이터 기반 검증 결과:**
  - `npm run test`: **테스트 파일, 단위/통합 테스트 통과**
- **트러블슈팅:**
  - 백엔드 에러 코드가 없는 일반 예외 발생 시 디버깅 문구가 유출되던 위험 해결: `sanitizeErrorMessage` 1차 검증에서 코드 미제공 시 무조건 안전한 Fallback 메시지 반환
  - `GradingPage`에서 일반 `Error` 인스턴스의 Raw `message`가 저장되던 문제 해결: 409 중복 제출 처리 및 API 에러 외 일반 예외는 Generic Fallback이 유지되도록 정비

## 📌 주요 변경사항

- 추가: `src/shared/api/error.ts` 내 `ALLOWED_USER_FACING_ERROR_CODES` 화이트리스트 및 `sanitizeErrorMessage` 2중 가드레일 함수

author: motoki-n
body:
## 概要

技術書執筆支援（親Issue #93）の実体。`personas` / `review_profiles` にジャンル概念を導入し、技術書向け標準ペルソナ2人＋レビュープロファイル3種を同梱、プロジェクトの執筆ジャンルに応じた**既定選択の自動適用**を実装した。選択肢の絞り込みはしない（クロスジャンルの手動選択は従来どおり可能）。着手時インタビューで仕様を確定し `docs/SPEC-genre-profiles.md` を新規策定。

## 影響範囲分析の要約

- `writing_genre` は両テーブルとも nullable（null=全ジャンル共通）。既存標準行のタグ付けは標準行がRLSで書き込み不可のためマイグレーション内UPDATEで実施（前例踏襲）
- ジャンル優先ソート（一致→共通→他ジャンル）は PostgREST の order() で表現できないため取得後のJS側ソート（`lib/genre-priority.ts`・安定ソートで is_default desc→created_at を同順位内維持）
- レビューパネルの既定選択は「一覧先頭」ではなく `initialProfileId` のサーバー計算だったため、`find(is_default)` をソート後先頭採用に変更（running セッション優先は維持）。講評UIは一覧先頭採用のためサーバーソートのみで効く。**UI コンポーネントはパネル側無変更**
- 校正は選択UIなしの固定UUID直引きだったため、**サーバー側ジャンル解決**（target_phase='proofreading' の標準行限定をジャンル優先で1件解決）へ変更。ユーザー作成プロファイルが校正経路を暗黙に乗っ取らない従来セマンティクスを維持
- 「その他」ジャンルは一致行なし→共通→created_at順（novel が先）となり、現行既定が維持される（仕様どおり）
- 技術書企画書レビューの判定行は parseVerdict の正規表現互換で一字一句同一、技術書校正の出力形式節は streamObject（original_text/suggested_text/reason）互換で校正・校閲と一字一句同一
- 構成レビューの技術書版は #96 とセット（本PRに含まない）。`resolveProfileForPhase`（実行時再検証）はジャンルで絞らない＝クロスジャンル仕様と整合のため無変更

## 変更点

- **マイグレーション** `20260725000003_genre_personas_and_profiles.sql`: カラム追加＋既存行タグ付け＋シード（適用・型再生成済み）
- **`lib/genre-priority.ts`**（新規）: `genreRank` / `sortByGenrePriority`（review / critique / proofread の3経路で共用）
- **`lib/actions/review.ts`**: `getReviewPanelBootstrap` に `resolveTarget` 経由のジャンル解決＋ソート＋既定選択の簡約
- **`lib/actions/critique.ts`**: proposals select に writing_genre 追加＋プロファイルのソート
- **`app/api/proofread/route.ts`**: 固定UUID直引き→ジャンル解決
- **設定画面**: 一覧にジャンル表示・ダイアログに対象ジャンル select（persona-list / profile-list / labels）・zod・duplicate のコピー対象追加
- **`lib/ai/personas.ts`**: 新固定UUID定数5本
- **SPEC**: SPEC-genre-profiles.md 新規、SPEC-genre §6・SPEC-dashboard-critique-settings §7・review-profiles スキル（9種未追随だった記述を12種＋ジャンル概念に更新）

## 検証結果

- `npm run typecheck` / `npm run lint` 通過
- ブラウザ確認:
  - 設定画面: 全14ペルソナ・12プロファイルのジャンル表示が仕分けどおり。新規ダイアログに「対象ジャンル」select（共通/小説/技術書/その他）
  - **技術書プロジェクト**（開発記を一時的に技術書へ変更して検証・検証後に原状復帰）: 企画書レビューパネルの初期選択=技術書企画書レビュー・担当=技術書編集者。一覧順=一致→他ジャンル
  - **小説プロジェクト回帰**（人魚の唄）: 初期選択=企画書レビュー・担当編集（従来どおり）。技術書プロファイルは選択肢末尾に並びクロスジャンル選択可能
- セルフレビュー（subagent）: **指摘なし**（判定行の正規表現マッチ実行確認・E文字列のエスケープ機械検査・select漏れ全数確認・安定ソート前提の確認済み）
- **環境制約で未実施**: 講評パネル・校正実行の実走E2E（ローカルの両プロジェクトとも原稿ファイル0件のため講評ボタンが disabled・校正も実行不可）。両経路とも同一の `sortByGenrePriority` でレビューパネルと同型のため、ドッグフーディングでの実走確認を残タスクとする

## 残タスク（マージ後・ユーザー作業）

- 「ネコノテAI 開発記」の執筆ジャンルを企画書画面で「技術書」に設定する（検証時は原状復帰済み。設定すると技術書向け既定選択が有効になる）
- 原稿のあるプロジェクトで技術書講評・技術書校正の実走確認

Closes #95

Description
-----------
Part 5/5 of stack #12296.

- Fixes #11722

Adds a `federated_identity` fixture that runs a fake W&B server implementing the OIDC token exchange (`/oidc/token`) and a Bearer-only `/graphql` endpoint, and uses it to cover `wandb.Api()` and `wandb.login(verify=True)` end to end through wandb-core: the identity token is exchanged for an access token, and every backend request authenticates with it as a Bearer token. The token exchange endpoint requires the exact token as the assertion, and the fixture writes the token file with a trailing newline, pinning the token-file whitespace handling fixed in #12292.

Investigating #11722 showed its headline problems were already fixed (#11243, plus routing GraphQL and file downloads through wandb-core); the remaining gap — `verify=True` skipping identity tokens — is fixed in #12294. These tests lock the behavior in, and replace `test_login_with_token_file`, which was skipped because it required network access.

Attribution note: `test_initialize_api_with_federated_identity` also passes on current `main` — the `wandb.Api()` half of the issue was already fixed before this stack. Only `test_login_verify_with_token_file` pins behavior new to this stack (verification and the token-exchange/Bearer assertions fail on `main` because verify was skipped for identity tokens).

- [x] I updated CHANGELOG.unreleased.md, or it's not applicable

author: sallvainian
body:
## Problem

The window could be resized but never dragged.

Root cause is the ACL, not the markup. `data-tauri-drag-region` works by invoking the `start_dragging` command, and `core:window:default` expands to 28 permissions that do **not** include `allow-start-dragging` — verified against the autogenerated permission set in the build output. So the drag region shipped in `Sidebar.tsx` had never actually worked; every drag was silently rejected. Resizing kept working because that is the native window frame, not IPC.

Two further gaps meant the permission alone would not have been enough:

- Only the sidebar reserved the overlay title bar (`pt-[38px]`). The main column started flush at y=0 with no drag surface, so only the 240px sidebar band would have dragged.
- A bare `data-tauri-drag-region` matches only `el === composedPath[0]` (tauri 2.11.5 `src/window/scripts/drag.js:66`), so the sidebar's logo glyph and wordmark spans swallowed the mousedown.

## Changes

- `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` — grant `core:window:allow-start-dragging`.
- `src/components/shell/AppLayout.tsx` — 38px title-bar reserve above `<main>`, marked as a drag region. Shifts main-column content down 38px and aligns it with the sidebar wordmark.
- `src/components/shell/Sidebar.tsx` — promote to `data-tauri-drag-region="deep"` so the logo and wordmark drag.

A full-width fixed overlay was rejected: `ManagerPane`'s header controls sit at roughly y=14–46, so an overlay would have eaten the top half of the Refresh button's click target.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npm test` — 133/133 across 23 files
- `npm run build` — succeeds
- `cargo check --locked` — compiles; ACL accepts the new permission identifier
- Manually confirmed by dragging the running app via `npm run tauri dev`

## Security note

This grants a window-manipulation command under `security.csp: null`. The project's own standing rule treats any capability change as security-sensitive. Deferred follow-ups are recorded in `deferred-work.md`, including a DECISIONS entry for the grant and a decision on whether to tighten the CSP.

## Deferred

Six items appended to `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/deferred-work.md`, notably: `project-context.md:136` still claims the capability file grants only `core:default` and `opener:default`, and `docs/SPEC.md:212` still describes only the sidebar drag strip. Both are workflow output and need regenerating rather than hand-editing.

author: malammar
body:
## Summary

`_conds_cache` in `engine.py` is unbounded. It is keyed by `(path, mtime, exaggeration)` and cleared only by `unload_model()`, so every distinct reference voice a server ever handles pins GPU tensors for the lifetime of the process.

Each entry costs **~175 MB of VRAM**. On a 6 GB card that is enough to take the server from healthy to failing every request within an hour of ordinary traffic.

This adds an LRU bound (`CONDS_CACHE_MAX`, default 4) and refreshes recency on cache hits so a rotating voice workload evicts least-recently-used rather than by insertion order.

## How it fails today

Observed on a live deployment: a worker served correctly for ~45 minutes, then began returning 500 for every generation with `CUDA out of memory: Tried to allocate 2.00 MiB`, while `/api/model-info` still reported `{"loaded": true}` and `/docs` still returned 200.

The tell is the size of the failing allocation. Failing to obtain 2 MiB while holding ~260 MB reserved-but-free is not an oversized model, it is a cache that has eaten the working headroom.

## Measurements

P106-100 (5.93 GiB usable), `chatterbox-turbo`, three 10-minute soaks cycling 28 reference voices at ~45 req/min with text lengths varying 40–520 chars:

| `CONDS_CACHE_MAX` | requests | failed | live tensors at end | headroom |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| unbounded (today) | 453 | **406 (90%)** | 5.46 GiB | 0.11 GiB |
| 2 | 89 | 1 (1.1%) | 4.58 GiB | 0.10–0.49 GiB |
| 0 | 88 | **0** | 4.37 GiB | 0.28–0.40 GiB |

Model footprint on a fresh load is 4.09 GiB, so the +1.37 GiB of retained tensors is exactly 8 cached voices × ~175 MB.

Two controls confirm the cache is the cause rather than allocator fragmentation:

- **Same load, one voice, unbounded cache: 50/50 requests succeeded**, live tensors flat at 4.34 GiB. Voice variety is the variable, not request volume or text length.
- `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` alone does **not** fix it. It helps a separate fragmentation effect (reserved memory grows while live tensors stay flat), but it cannot free tensors the cache still references.

## Cost of a smaller cache

A miss only re-encodes the reference audio. Measured on an RTX 4070 against a 3.8 MB reference:

| request | miss | hit | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 84 chars | 1.23s | 1.09s | +0.14s (+13%) |
| 240 chars | 3.30s | 3.32s | within noise |

It is a **fixed** per-request cost that does not scale with output length, so it is a small percentage on anything but very short requests. Cheap relative to 175 MB of VRAM per entry.

## Choosing the default

4 entries (~700 MB) leaves a 6 GB card ~1.1 GiB for generation after the model. It is deliberately conservative: an oversized cache takes a card out of service entirely, while an undersized one costs ~0.14s on a miss. Deployments with VRAM to spare can raise it — 16 is comfortable on 12 GB — and orchestration layers can size it per device from `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` at launch.

Happy to change the default, or gate the whole thing behind an opt-in flag if you would rather not alter behaviour for existing users. I would suggest against leaving it unbounded even so, since the failure is silent and looks like a hung GPU rather than a cache problem.

## Testing

author: jeremyjpj0916
body:
## Summary

The admin listener bounded exactly one window: an HTTP/1.1 message head that took too long to arrive. Request bodies were capped in size but not in time, HTTP/2 streams had no header deadline at all, and one HTTP/2 connection could multiplex an unbounded number of stalled streams past the listener's connection cap. An authenticated low-privilege client could therefore hold admin request tasks and buffers open indefinitely.

Closes #2404 (review unit **ADM-01 — Listener and transport boundary**).

## Changes

### Transport bounds — `src/admin/mod.rs`

- Both admin listeners now drive connections through one shared `serve_admin_io`. The plaintext listener moves from the HTTP/1-only builder to the same `hyper_util` auto builder the TLS listener already used, so plaintext (h2c prior knowledge) and TLS (ALPN `h2`) get **identical** protections instead of the plaintext path being HTTP/1-only.
- Admin HTTP/2 connections advertise bounded `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` and `SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE`, so one connection can neither multiplex unbounded streams nor accumulate an unbounded `HEADERS`/`CONTINUATION` block per stream. hyper's default header-list bound is 16 MiB, which is what made an incomplete HTTP/2 header block expensive.
- A connection-level watchdog (`AdminConnActivity`) closes connections that neither deliver a new request nor hold one in flight for a whole `FERRUM_HTTP_HEADER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` window. This reaches the two windows hyper's HTTP/1 timer cannot see: the auto builder's version-sniff read (a peer that connects and sends nothing never reaches the HTTP/1 timer) and HTTP/2 streams whose header block never completes.
  - A response still being written counts as in flight — the guard lives inside the response body and drops when hyper drops it — so a slow reader pulling a large `GET /backup` is not interrupted.
  - HTTP/1.1 keeps hyper's native `header_read_timeout`, unchanged. The global `AdminConnLimiter` cap is untouched.
  - Connection-level errors log at `debug` rather than `error` so a slowloris flood cannot turn into a log flood.

### Body bounds — `src/util/body_limit.rs`, `src/admin/mod.rs`, `src/admin/api_specs/handlers.rs`

- `collect_body_with_limits` pairs the existing size cap with an absolute deadline and reports which bound fired (`TooLarge` / `Timeout` / `Transport`). The deadline is derived from the route's own size cap by `AdminRequestLimits::body_read_timeout_for`, so the bound is one shared **minimum throughput** rather than a flat wall clock: 30s for a 1 MiB body, 750s for a 25 MiB `/api-specs` body, 3000s for a 100 MiB `/restore` body. A single flat value would have been 100x tighter on exactly the route sized for the largest payload — the ~80 MB backups `/restore` exists to accept need ~22 Mbit/s sustained to fit inside 30s — and raising the knob for a slow restore link would have loosened every 1 MiB route by the same factor. Both the shared admin body read and the API-spec body reads go through it, so the API-spec path is no longer size-only. On timeout the collect future is dropped, releasing the HTTP/1 connection or resetting the HTTP/2 stream, and the caller returns `408`.
- The body is now read **only** for routes that consume it, and only after that route's role gate (`body_consuming_route_role`, enumerated against every `&body_bytes` call site). Unknown paths, methods a known path does not route, read/delete routes, and callers the route would reject with `403` are all answered with the request-body receiver dropped rather than buffered. The in-arm `require_admin_role` gates stay authoritative and simply re-run idempotently, matching the existing pre-body pagination gate's pattern. Authentication already ran before this point, so an unauthenticated caller cannot pin a collecting task either.
- `POST /batch` and `POST /restore` now also re-run `require_admin_role` in their route arms. Their handlers carry no role check of their own, so without this their `admin` requirement would live only in `body_consuming_route_role` — a table whose documented job is deciding whether a body is buffered, not who may call a route. Every other body-consuming arm already re-ran its gate idempotently; these two now match, keeping the admission table a pure optimization on the two most destructive admin routes rather than their sole authority. Guarded by `operator_cannot_bulk_write_through_batch_or_restore` in `tests/integration/admin_audit_rbac_tests.rs`.

### Configuration and docs

New `FERRUM_*` settings, each with parsing + clamp, `EnvConfig` default, `ferrum.conf` entry, `docs/configuration.md` row, and a `PUBLIC_FERRUM_ENV_SETTINGS` inventory entry:

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FERRUM_ADMIN_BODY_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `30` | Absolute deadline for reading a **1 MiB** admin request body; routes with a larger size cap scale it by that cap (`0` disables) |
| `FERRUM_ADMIN_HTTP2_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` | `64` | Advertised `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` (min 1) |
| `FERRUM_ADMIN_HTTP2_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE_BYTES` | `65536` | Advertised `SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE` (min 1024) |

`FERRUM_HTTP_HEADER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` gains documented additional scope on the admin listeners. `openapi.yaml` adds a shared `RequestTimeout` (`408`) component response, references it from `/restore` and `POST`/`PUT /api-specs`, and documents the body time bound, the pre-body route/role admission rule, and the admin HTTP/2 bounds in `info.description`. `docs/admin_api.md` gains matching "Request body admission" and "Admin listener transport bounds" sections.

## Behaviour changes worth calling out

- **Plaintext admin now accepts h2c prior knowledge.** Same authentication, same bounds; this is what makes the HTTP/2 protections apply on both listeners rather than TLS only.
- **An idle keep-alive admin connection is closed after `FERRUM_HTTP_HEADER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`** and the client reconnects. That is what hyper's HTTP/1 header timer already did; the watchdog extends it to HTTP/2 and the version-sniff window. Documented in `ferrum.conf`, `docs/configuration.md`, and `docs/admin_api.md`.
- **A request on a body-less route that carries a body no longer keeps HTTP/1 keep-alive**, because the unread body means hyper closes after the response. Requests without a body are unaffected.

## Scope decision: no listener-wide in-flight cap

The per-connection `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` bound is deliberately *not* paired with a listener-wide in-flight request cap. There is no listener-wide budget for concurrently buffered bodies, so the theoretical ceiling on retained body bytes is `FERRUM_ADMIN_MAX_CONNECTIONS` x `FERRUM_ADMIN_HTTP2_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` x the route's size cap. Three things bound the real exposure:

- **Bodies are role-gated before collection.** Every body-consuming route requires `operator` or `admin`, and that gate runs before the body is read, so an unauthenticated peer can never pin a collecting task.
- **Partial HTTP/2 header blocks do not multiply per stream.** RFC 9113 6.10 requires `CONTINUATION` frames to follow their `HEADERS` frame immediately on the same stream, so a connection can hold at most one incomplete header block, bounded by the advertised `SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE` (64 KiB) — and h2 0.4.14 already carries the CONTINUATION-flood fix.
- **The binding constraint is attacker bandwidth, not the stream product.** A caller can only hold what it has actually transmitted, so held bytes are bounded by upload rate x body deadline. A listener-wide *request* cap would not change that number; only a listener-wide *byte* budget would, and that is a separate admission-control feature rather than part of this transport-boundary unit.

Net against the pre-PR state this is a strict improvement: the TLS admin listener already spoke HTTP/2 with hyper's default 200 streams, a 16 MiB header-list bound, and no time bound at all. `docs/admin_api.md` now carries an expli

author: jckdotim
body:
## Problem

The driver skips LLM turns entirely when no human player is in sight (the `has_nearby_human_players()` gate, at both the initial prompt and the main loop). When that gate was added in 0f473d16 the agent-client was operator-NPC-only (Rica, Karl), so "nobody watching, nothing to think about" was pure cost saving. With remote user agents in the picture, it now **turns off the brain of any agent that goes hunting alone.**

Observed live (Google-mode agent, sent to the spawn flats outside town by its schedule):

```
06:34:57 [Archy] Schedule transition: moving to field hours: hunt monsters ...
06:35:47 Monster AI: managing m389_17 (type=kobold, aggressive=false)
06:35:47 Monster AI: managing m389_18 (type=goblin, aggressive=false)
   ...   (monsters keep spawning around the agent)
06:36:29 [Archy] LLM driver: no human players nearby, skipping initial prompt
   ...   (5+ minutes: zero LLM calls, zero attacks — standing sword in hand next to a kobold)
```

`doc/REMOTE_AGENT_CLIENT.md` states the primary goal as "the LLM plays the game as an ordinary player — roams, **fights**, talks, grows", and its decision table keeps agents eligible for ambient spawns precisely because they "must receive the same rules as humans to **grow through hunting**". A brain that only boots for a human audience cannot do that.

## Fix

Add `has_nearby_monsters()` to `SharedState` (same `NPC_SIGHT_RADIUS` as the human check) and relax both skip sites from "no humans" to "**no humans and no monsters**".

- Towns are no-spawn zones, so NPCs parked in town still idle for free
- The `is_sleeping` skip is untouched
- Operator NPCs only change behavior when a monster strays into sight with no players around — arguably exactly when a guard should react

## Verification

- `cargo test -p agent-client` 42/42 passing; clippy clean for the changed code (the pre-existing `collapsible_match` warning at state.rs:586 is unrelated, left untouched)
- Confirmed on prod: before the patch, a full hunting schedule produced zero attacks; after, the very first turn picks a target, closes in, attacks, and kills (+2 XP):

```
<<< FROM CLAUDE: {"thought": "It's field hours ... The nearest kobold is m398_17 at
roughly 22 units away. I'll move to it and attack.", "actions": [
  {"type": "move", "x": -1508.7, "y": 0.7, "z": 4444.6},
  {"type": "attack", "monster_id": "m398_17"}]}
[MonsterDead] m398_17
[XP] +2 (total: 2, level: 1)
```

author: lucas-barake
body:
Closes #28.

`RpcPeerTransport` hands consumers a `receive` stream backed by an **unscoped** queue created inside Effect's own `RpcClient`. `Connection.close` closes `connectionScope`, but the only relevant finalizer there deletes the request entry and sends an interrupt upstream — it never ends that queue. And because the entry is already deleted, the server's eventual `Exit` response is discarded, so the `Queue.end` that would normally terminate the stream is unreachable. A fiber consuming `receive` stayed parked in `Queue.takeAll` until the enclosing scope closed.

`PeerSession` makes that window reachable: it forks the receive fiber and the terminal-failure watcher as siblings into the same ambient scope with no interruption edge between them, so when the watcher calls `connection.close` the receive fiber just lingers.

The fix interrupts the returned stream when the existing `closeCompleted` deferred resolves, so termination follows from `close` rather than from scope timing.

## Why the trigger ends in `Effect.interrupt`

This is the non-obvious part, and it is why the one comment in the diff exists.

`Stream.interruptWhen` chooses its terminal state from the *trigger*, not the combinator. A trigger that merely succeeds reaches `Cause.done` and ends the stream **normally**. `PeerSession` appends `Effect.fail(StorageUnavailable("Peer connection receive stream ended"))` after `Stream.runForEach`, and `supervise` only swallows causes where `Cause.hasInterruptsOnly` holds — so a normal end manufactures a retryable transport error on a clean close, and the README documents `StorageUnavailable` as the retry classification.

Typechecking cannot catch this: an isolated `tsc --strict` compile infers an **identical type** with and without `Effect.andThen(Effect.interrupt)`. The regression tests are the only guard, which is why removing it fails three of them.

```ts
const interruptOnClose = Deferred.await(closeCompleted).pipe(Effect.andThen(Effect.interrupt))

receive: remainder.pipe(
  Stream.mapEffect(/* ... */),
  Stream.interruptWhen(interruptOnClose)
)
```

Driving it from `closeCompleted` means the guarantee holds on every teardown path that yields a connection — explicit close, the non-owner path that awaits the same deferred, and the `lifetimeScope` finalizer — without adding a second close-state representation.

## What this does and does not guarantee

Stated precisely, because the mechanism is weaker than the issue title suggests:

- A consumer **parked in the pull** is interrupted and observes an interrupt-only `Exit`. Termination is observed by joining that fiber, not by `close` returning.
- A consumer **inside its element handler** is not interrupted mid-handler. It finishes the handler and observes the interrupt at its next pull. Ambient scope teardown still hard-interrupts mid-handler, as before.
- `Stream.interruptWhen` merges through a rendezvous queue, so a payload the transport already pulled **may** still be handed off before the interrupt lands. Whether it is depends on whether the pending offer registered before the close trigger failed that queue; both orders are legal. The tests assert order and absence of duplicates rather than an exact delivery, and the README says "may still receive".
- Over a real socket the interrupt is gated behind `Scope.close(connectionScope)`, which blocks on the RPC client's `sendInterrupt` write (bounded at ~1s). So the fiber can linger a bounded interval after close is requested — versus indefinitely today.

## Scope, and what is left over

The guarantee is scoped to `RpcPeerTransport`. `PeerRpcServer.sessionTransport` is also production and its `close` is a bare `Effect.void`, so server-hosted sessions still rely on `revoke`/`detach`/`finishCleanup` and the titled defect survives there. Documenting a stronger contract on `PeerTransport.Connection` would make the interface false for that implementation, so the interface is unchanged and the remainder is tracked in #80.

A `Queue.shutdown`-based design was rejected rather than merely not chosen: `asQueue: true` hands back a `Queue.Dequeue`, and every `effect/Queue` completion API requires `Enqueue`, so it cannot be written without an unsound cast into a handle Effect deliberately makes read-only.

author: sandrabrayer
body:
## What

A read-only **digest export** so the coordinators app can consume Logistics data with **zero access to financial fields**.

Because Google Sheets sharing is **per-file, not per-tab**, putting digest tabs in the main Logistics sheet would expose `estimated_cost` / `actual_cost`. So the digest is its **own spreadsheet**, holding **exactly two tabs** (`OpenTickets`, `WeeklyCounts`) and nothing else. `brayersandra@gmail.com` gets **Viewer** on that file only. This app is the sole writer of these tabs — the coordinators repo is untouched.

## Changes

**`apps-script/digest.gs` (new)**
- `setupDigest()` — run once manually: creates the digest spreadsheet (or reuses an existing `DIGEST_SHEET_ID`), writes both header rows, grants Viewer, stores the id in Script Property `DIGEST_SHEET_ID`, and `Logger.log()`s it. Idempotent.
- `rebuildDigest()` — wipes and rewrites both tabs from `Requests` / `AuditLog` / `Houses` / `InventoryCounts`. `LockService`-wrapped, fully idempotent, and defensive (no-op until set up, errors logged not thrown) so a digest hiccup can't break a staff write.
- `installDigestTrigger()` — 15-minute time-driven backstop.

**`apps-script/Code.gs`** — every write handler calls `rebuildDigest()` on its success path (16 call sites across 15 handlers).

**`src/digest.js` + `test/digest.test.js` (new)** — dependency-free pure helpers mirrored verbatim in `digest.gs`: house-id map, active-ticket filter, money scrubber, title truncation (single line, ≤80 chars, ellipsis), Sunday (Israeli) week-start, last-N-week-starts. 21 tests via `node --test`.

**`DIGEST-CONTRACT.md` (new)** — the frozen schema. **`CHANGELOG.md`** — entry added.

## Contract highlights

- **House ids:** רעננה→raanana, רמות השבים→ramot, קיסריה עפרוני→efroni, ריהאב→rehab. הפרדס / שדה אליעזר excluded (pre-opening). Unmapped houses are **omitted, never guessed**.
- **OpenTickets** included when status is NOT `סגור` and NOT `לא מאושר`.
- **Money scrubber** on `title` and `shortagesSummary`: strips `₪`, `ש"ח`, `שח`, `NIS`, `ILS` and adjacent digit groups; **bare quantities stay** (counts, not prices); marker letters inside real words (משחק, TENNIS) are boundary-guarded.
- **WeeklyCounts** always emits 4 houses × last 8 weeks so gaps surface as `לא בוצעה`. Inventory is still MONTHLY — an optional `week_start` column is read if present; until it exists every row is `לא בוצעה` with an empty `shortagesSummary`. Monthly counts are **never fabricated** into weekly data.
- **Invariants:** no financial fields ever; columns append-only; consumers read by header name.

## Deploy

After redeploy, run `setupDigest()` once, then `installDigestTrigger()` once.

## Testing

`node --test` — full suite green (171 tests; 21 new in `test/digest.test.js`).
