author: suvarna4
body:
Adds `docs/confit-design-v0.6.md`.

`CLAUDE.md` and the implementation plan both name the design doc as authoritative for product decisions, but the doc itself was not in the repo. This adds it.

## What's in v0.6

Supersedes v0.5. The substantive changes it records:

- **[E9]** Client-side encryption removed by decision; both memory tiers consolidated onto XTrace. The privacy claim moves from "nobody can read this" to "we hold this, and we don't sell or expose it," and the §1 wedge is re-grounded on collection design.
- **[E10]** The k≥5 cohort floor and the §9 duty of care become the primary structural protections rather than the second layer behind encryption.
- **[E11]** Confessions are ingested as raw prose for platform extraction; the five chips remain as a consent and quality gate, not a redaction boundary.
- **[E12]** Ingest durability becomes a correctness requirement (verify-and-retry), since XTrace is the sole store.
- **[E13]** Model ids corrected — `claude-sonnet-5` for Ask assembly, `claude-haiku-4-5` for the chip preview.

Also includes the §14 evidence appendix sourcing the empirical claims behind those decisions.

## Note for follow-up

`docs/confit-implementation-plan.md` states it is governed by design doc **v0.3**. v0.6 retires several v0.3 decisions — [C3] signed tombstones and the ordered Forget-me sequence, [C6]'s redaction framing, [C7] the vault scope question, [C13] the x-vec contingency — most consequentially the entire encryption architecture. Reconciling the plan against v0.6 is not part of this PR.

Docs only; no code changes.

body:
## What

Recaptures the benchmark on two machines, adds a quality column so the numbers can be read honestly, and charts them.

- **PSNR is now a real column.** `webpbench` and `rustbench` decode each engine's own output and score it against the pixels that engine was handed, emitted as `psnr_db` (`-` for lossless, which is exact).
- **Results recaptured on arm64 and amd64** at commit 7e5e084: Apple M4 Pro (macOS) and Ryzen 7 5700G (Arch). Encoder output is identical across both, so the tables share the PSNR column and differ only in timings.
- **Two SVG figures**, generated from the tables in `results.md` itself so they cannot drift from the numbers.

## Why the conclusions changed

The previous results.md ranked encoders by output size alone, which rewards whichever one quantizes hardest. It read our own and webp-rust's small lossy-slow files as a compression win over libwebp — "often ~half of libwebp's for the same quality". With PSNR alongside size:

- vs libwebp at `lossy-slow` we are 0.84-1.00x the size at 0.3-1.1 dB lower quality (2.9 dB on one image), for 14-24x the encode time.
- at `lossy-fast` quality matches within 0.5 dB but our files are 10-62% bigger.
- webp-rust's `lossy-slow` files are smallest and 1.5-3 dB worse: over-quantization, not compression.

## A bug found upstream

`webp-rust`'s `lossy-fast` output is corrupt on 3 of the 7 test images — 6.35, 9.38 and 16.44 dB against ~40 dB for the rest. Its own decoder and ours agree on those figures to the hundredth of a dB, including on the images that encode fine, so the bitstream is bad rather than the decode. It is the token-partition desync that 7e5e084 fixed on our side; still present in webp-rust v0.2.1.

## Charts

Both figures ship in light and dark variants, selected by GitHub's `#gh-light-mode-only` / `#gh-dark-mode-only` anchors.

- **Size and quality** — a scatter of output size and PSNR relative to libwebp, one point per image, faceted by lossy mode. libwebp is the origin; wasm shares that point because it encodes byte-identically (verified by hash). The three corrupt webp-rust files are pinned to the floor as triangles rather than flattening the scale.
- **Encode time** — linear, one panel per mode and machine. A shared axis would crush 63 ms against 136 s, so each panel scales itself, and a bar more than twice the next tallest fades out under an arrow instead of setting the scale for everything else.

Regenerate with `benchmark/chart/chart.go`, whose first line is a comment to Go and a command to `sh`, so it runs as a script or as `go run ./chart`.

## Notes for review

- Timings were captured before the tools emitted PSNR, so that column was measured in a separate pass at the same settings and matched to each row by byte size; a fresh run of both tools reproduces the table values exactly. `results.md` says so.
- I confirmed the faulty skip-signaling gate exists in webp-rust's source and that its output decodes as garbage, but did not build an instrumented webp-rust to prove that path fires on those three specific images. The mechanism is strongly supported, not directly traced.

body:
战报卡二维码与 OG 的正式地址，从 `bond-back-yanzhuo-lius-projects.vercel.app` 换成 `bond-back-psi.vercel.app`。两个是同一份生产部署的别名，长的仍然可用。

## 为什么换

短 18 个字符，二维码从 version 4（33×33 模块）降到 version 3（29×29）。卡上二维码只显示 88px —— 每个模块从 2.7px 涨到 3.0px，别人举着手机扫你屏幕时这一档差别看得见。长的那串读起来也像预览链接。

改动只在 `lib/site.ts` 一个常量（战报卡二维码与 OG 的 `metadataBase` 都吃它），外加 `CLAUDE.md` / `README.md` / `docs/prd/README.md` 里记的部署地址。00 那行保留了「长别名仍可用」的说明，免得以后有人以为它废了。

## 顺带记录 iPhone 微信实测（2026-07-25）

- ✅ 战报卡长按存图正常，并成功转发进聊天
- ✅ PDF 直接下载成功，微信没拦 —— 「复制全文」兜底保留但不是必经路径
- ⬜ 微信安卓深色模式强制反色：**未测**

iOS 微信是三个环境里最宽松的，前两项通过属于预期。安卓那一轮的风险独立存在：强制反色是安卓微信独有行为，PDF 下载在安卓微信里也常被直接拦，那边「复制全文」才是主路径。详见 `docs/prd/05-polish.md`。

另外纠正一条此前写进文档的预期：**微信里粘裸链接不出卡片，出的是文字链接**。卡片只在页面内「右上角 ⋯ → 发送给朋友」时才生成，且微信不完整读 Open Graph（标题取 `<title>`，描述与缩略图另有一套，完整控制需认证公众号 + JS-SDK）。OG meta 对 Slack / X / Telegram / 飞书 / 钉钉 / iMessage 仍然完全有效。

## 验证

`check:tokens` / `test:analysis` / `tsc --noEmit` / `eslint` / `build` 五项全清；token 逃生舱仍是 3 处。

author: yq-wang
body:
Relates to #26 and #540. Opening this as a draft to ask whether the change is wanted before polishing it.

- [x] Tests pass
- [ ] Appropriate changes to documentation are included in the PR — no user-facing change; the CLI README's description of a background port-forward tunnel stays accurate

## Summary

`kubectl ate` reaches ateapi through client-go's `PortForwarder`, which binds a localhost TCP listener, accepts a connection from our own gRPC client, and copies bytes between that connection and the Kubernetes port-forward stream. This exposes the port-forward stream directly as gRPC's `net.Conn`, so the listener and the copy goroutines go away.

- dial ateapi directly over Kubernetes port-forward streams instead of a localhost TCP bridge
- honor cancellation during SPDY negotiation and stream setup
- close direct stream connections on setup and remote-stream errors, with lifecycle tests

That buys three things: no localhost listener bound for the lifetime of each command, gRPC able to redial transparently where the current single tunnel is a permanent failure if it drops, and one less copy hop per RPC. It also removes the reset behind #26 at its source, since that copy loop is what observes the RST — but #540 keeps the message away from users regardless, so this should stand or fall as a transport change.

The adapter follows Kubernetes' own direct-stream pattern, which is not importable: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.36.0/test/e2e/framework/pod/dial.go

## Questions I would like input on

1. Is this worth roughly 200 lines of production code here, given that the user-visible symptom is already handled?
2. Would this be better pursued upstream as a client-go API that exposes a pod port-forward stream as a `net.Conn`? Anyone wanting gRPC over port-forward reimplements this today.
3. If it stays here, `internal/e2e/portforward.go` is a second consumer that could share it.

## Not ready for a detailed review

`watchErrors` reports through `slog.Error`, and since `kubectl-ate` configures no handler that lands on the user's terminal as `2026/07/25 02:41:27 ERROR Port-forward connection failed remotePort=443 error="..."`. That is the same kind of message as #26, and #540 does not suppress it because #540 replaces `utilruntime.ErrorHandlers` rather than touching slog. Closing the connection and letting gRPC report the transport error is the better shape.

Beyond that: the deadline methods are no-ops that grpc-go's teardown relies on (grpc/grpc-go#8425), `Close` evaluates `Stream.Close()` before `streamConn.Close()` without the `Reset()` that upstream uses to discard unsent data, `RemoveStreams` is never called, the now-unused `cancel` field can go, and moving dial failures from client construction to the first RPC needs a UX check for cases like an unready api pod or an RBAC denial.

## Validation

`go test -race -count=100 ./internal/ateclient`, `go test ./cmd/kubectl-ate/...`, `go mod tidy -diff` and `make verify` pass. Coverage is fake-based.

The transport has not been exercised against a live cluster at volume yet; that and an e2e assertion that a successful command leaves stderr clean belong on the list above. Note that the reset itself is timing-dependent and 1,500 CLI invocations on macOS/kind produced none, so a load test has to run on Linux to say anything.

Moving port-forward transport to WebSockets would not eliminate this reset class: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubectl/issues/1620#issuecomment-2291359257

author: iroha1203
body:
## 概要

Closes #3734

再照準後スコープ(2026-07-25 本文改訂)に基づき、SAGA の equation 側入力への
**equation-system production route** を
`Formal/AG/SemanticRepair/Saga/EquationProduction.lean` に実装する。
**生成するのは χ^E(命題6.1A)であり、P_E(定義5.3)は生成せず生成 `Q_E` 上へ
固定する** — 数学本文 X.§1 の selected / generated / proved 三分類
(Q_E: generated、χ^E: selected 対応 + generated 値式、P_E: selected)を厳守する。

- **χ^E**: 命題6.1A の selected 対応 `λ ↦ (i_λ, A_λ)` は selected のまま、
  support Atom を通じて factor する特殊形(`SupportAtomEquationSelection`)で
  受ける。命題6.1A の唯一の条件「restriction と可換する」は field 供給ではなく
  `projection_natural` + `occRestrict_atom` で**証明により放電**する
  (`SupportAtomEquationSelection.realization`)。produced `χ^E` の値は
  III.定理11.4 の generated interpretation と **rfl で一致**し
  (`realization_chiE_eq_interpret`)、#3732/#3733 の生成 chain を再証明せず
  再利用する。restriction 面も `restrict_defect`(#3733)/
  `obstructionQuotientRestrict_mk`(#3732)で宣言名追跡できる
  (`displayedSource_defect_restrict` / `realization_chiE_restrict_eq_defect_class`)。
- **P_E**: 定義5.3 の「幾何側入力規律」に正確に従う。典型例経路の named
  surface `LiftFiberData.equationLiftSystem`(**実体は C2 `liftSystem` の
  alias** — 新規の型・証明なしと docstring に明示)と、equation system の
  生成物だけから作れる self-lift fiber instance(`equationSelfLiftFiber`:
  `0 → Q_E → Q_E → 0 → 0`、零 base reading)で route を型どおり発火させる。
  この instance は **`B_E = 0` の退化 member**(lift problem の非自明な内容は
  発火せず、residual は恒等的に零)であることを Implementation notes に申告。
  P_E 本体の selected 性(X.§1 入力6)は変えない。
- **packet**: 定理1.1 入力束の production 組み立て**面**
  (`SagaEquationPacket.ofProduction`)。completeness 対(入力4)は従来どおり
  定理仮定のまま。universe 境界(`y := u` 固定)と、**具体 packet instance は
  本 PR 時点で存在しない**(circle packet の `liftSystem` は `LiftFiberData`
  形でないため流せない)ことを claim boundary として docstring に明示。
- **発火 witness**: C7 circle witness の B.9.3 定数 realization が production
  route の生成物と rfl 一致(`realization_eq_production`、到達可能性 witness)。
  加えて projection が 2 Atom を読む witness 専用 presentation
  (`twoAtomPresentation`)上で、Atom 非定数の選択(`variantSelection`)から
  生成した `variantWitnessRealization` が **realization 層で実際に非定数**で
  あることを固定(`variantWitnessRealization_archReading_ne`)。witness の
  主張範囲は realization 層まで(circle の `equationResidual` は定数のため
  χ^E 層には現れない。thin fixture 固有の naturality は rfl でも書けるため
  「rfl 不可能性」は主張しない)— 各 boundary を docstring に明記。
- 凍結ファイル(`LawEquationGeneratedPair.lean` / `SagaComparison.lean` /
  `SemanticRepairPart10.lean`)への新規依存なし。旧 route の存廃は C8(#3769)。

## material premise 三分類申告

- **本文由来(selected、X.§1)**: `SupportAtomEquationSelection` の 2 field
  (入力3 の生成源への selected 入力)、`LiftFiberData`(入力6)、
  `R` / `P`(入力1)、`Psem` / `repairAtlas`(入力5a/5b)、`stateCorrespondence`(入力7)、
  `normalization`(入力8)、vanishing 補題の theorem premise
  (`hmem` / `hholds`)。
- **放電済み(条件付き)**: 命題6.1A の restriction 可換性(`realization` の
  naturality 2 field、`projection_natural` + `occRestrict_atom` による証明)。
  ただしこの放電は**「対応が support Atom を通じて factor する」という入力型の
  制限(本文にない Lean 側の追加前提)の下で**成立する。この factoring 制限は
  selected 側の追加 premise として申告する(命題6.1A の一般面は従来どおり
  `EquationSemanticRealization` の supplied naturality field が担う)。
- **未放電**: なし(結論相当 field の新設なし)。

## 受け入れ要件への対応

| Issueの受け入れ要件 | 対応内容 | 確認証拠 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EquationSemanticRealization`(χ^E)を #3732/#3733 生成 API 由来 data から構成する constructor | `SupportAtomEquationSelection.realization`(naturality を証明で放電) | `realization_chiE_apply` が `equationResidual` + `obstructionIdeal` 経由であることは rfl。realization 層の非定数発火は `variantWitnessRealization` |
| 定義5.3 の幾何側入力規律を生成 `Q_E` 上で固定する named surface + 生成物のみからの発火 instance(**AC2 は査読3巡の所見に基づき本文整合の形へ改訂済み** — Issue コメント参照) | `LiftFiberData.equationLiftSystem`(C2 engine の alias と明示)+ `equationSelfLiftFiber`(生成物のみから構成した instance。`B_E = 0` の退化 member であることを申告) | `equationSelfLiftAtlas_residual`(零 atlas の零 residual、engine の型どおりの発火)。P_E の selected 性は本文どおり維持(claim boundary 節) |
| 生成 chain を #3732/#3733 の宣言名で追跡できる | 値: `realization_chiE_eq_interpret`(`interpret`)。零化: `realization_chiE_eq_zero_iff_defect_mem_obstructionIdeal` / `..._of_defect_mem_witnessIdeal` / `realization_chiE_eq_zero_of_equationHolds`(`witnessIdeal_le_obstructionIdeal` / `equationHolds_defect_quotient_eq_zero`)。**restriction: `displayedSource_defect_restrict`(`restrict_defect`)/ `realization_chiE_restrict_eq_defect_class`(`obstructionQuotientRestrict_mk`)** | 各証明本文が #3732/#3733 宣言を `exact` / `rw` で直接適用 |
| 旧 `Law.holds`・manual equation core・membership certificate を standard 入力に取らない | 新規宣言の入力は selection / lift-fiber datum / selected 入力のみ | `EquationProduction.lean` 全文(該当語彙の参照なし) |
| 凍結ファイルへ新規依存を作らない | import は `Saga.EquationRealization` のみ | 査読 Lean B レーンが import 推移閉包(60/63 modules)で独立確認 |
| #3718 の非恒等 comparison instance を再実装しない | C7 witness への追加は production 接続宣言のみ | `CircleWitness.lean` 差分 |
| 結論相当 field を新設しない | 新規 structure は selection(data 2 field)のみ | `SupportAtomEquationSelection` 定義 |
| focused Lean 検証・placeholder scan・PR CI・AxiomAudit 収載・math-lean-review 記録 | 下記「実施したテスト」+ AxiomAudit alias 33件(structure 型を除く全新規宣言収載)+ 4並列査読 1・2巡目実施・finding 対応済み(PR コメントの査読サマリ参照) | 本PR のチェック結果と査読サマリコメント |

## 証明した定理

- `SupportAtomEquationSelection.realization`(命題6.1A の restriction 可換性の証明放電)
- `realization_lawIndex` / `realization_archReading` / `realization_chiE_apply`
- `realization_chiE_eq_interpret`
- `realization_chiE_eq_zero_iff_defect_mem_obstructionIdeal` / `realization_chiE_eq_zero_of_defect_mem_witnessIdeal` / `realization_chiE_eq_zero_of_equationHolds`

## 編集したドキュメント

- なし(Lean docstring と `Saga.lean` aggregator header のみ。保護対象の数学本文は未編集)

author: jaftdelgado
body:
This pull request introduces the new Chip component for @shizen-ui/svelte.
 
Chip is a compact, non-interactive component intended for metadata, status labels, tags, and lightweight contextual
information. The implementation includes the Svelte component, typed public API, style variants, CSS classes,
examples, and full documentation.
 
## What Was Added
 
### Chip Component
 
Added a new Chip component with support for:
 
| Feature       | Description                                                          |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `variant`      | Controls visual emphasis: `primary`, `secondary`, `ghost`, `soft`      |
| `color`        | Applies semantic tone: `default`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` |
| `size`         | Supports `sm`, `md`, and `lg`                                          |
| `startContent` | Renders leading content through a Svelte snippet                       |
| `endContent`   | Renders trailing content through a Svelte snippet                      |
| `class`        | Allows styling overrides through Tailwind utility classes              |
| `ref`          | Exposes the root `HTMLSpanElement`                                     |
 
Example usage:
 
```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { Chip } from "@shizen-ui/svelte";
  import Icon from "@components/svelte/Icon.svelte";
  import { BadgeCheckIcon } from "@hugeicons/core-free-icons";
</script>
 
<Chip variant="soft" color="success">
  {#snippet startContent()}
    <Icon icon={BadgeCheckIcon} />
  {/snippet}
 
  Verified
</Chip>
```
 
The icon content API is snippet-only, keeping the component consistent with Svelte composition patterns.
 
```ts
type ChipIconContent = Snippet<[]>;
```
 
## Styling System
 
The PR adds dedicated Chip styling across both the CSS layer and the Tailwind Variants layer.
 
### CSS Classes
 
The component includes structured classes for styling and customization:
 
| Class Group | Examples                                                                 |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Base         | `chip`, `chip__content`, `chip__icon`, `chip__label`                      |
| Variants     | `chip--primary`, `chip--secondary`, `chip--ghost`, `chip--soft`           |
| Colors       | `chip--default`, `chip--accent`, `chip--success`, `chip--warning`, `chip--danger` |
| Sizes        | `chip--sm`, `chip--md`, `chip--lg`                                        |
 
The styling model separates visual emphasis from semantic color. For example:
 
```css
.chip--soft {
  --chip-bg: var(--chip-tone-soft-bg);
  --chip-fg: var(--chip-tone-text);
}
 
.chip--success {
  --chip-tone-solid: var(--color-success);
  --chip-tone-solid-fg: var(--color-success-foreground);
  --chip-tone-text: var(--color-success);
}
```
 
This keeps variants reusable across all supported colors.
 
### Tailwind Variants
 
A `chipStyles` variant definition was added to support programmatic class composition:
 
```ts
chipStyles({
  variant: "soft",
  color: "success",
  size: "md"
});
```
 
## Documentation
 
A new Chip documentation page was added with:
 
- Import example
- Live examples for colors, variants, sizes, and start/end content
- Tailwind customization example
- Custom CSS example
- CSS class reference
- API reference
The docs also include usage examples that demonstrate common scenarios such as:
 
- Status indicators
- Metadata chips
- Chips with icons
- Custom Tailwind styling
- CSS-layer customization
## Additional Updates
 
- Integrated Chip styles into the global component styles entrypoint.
- Exported Chip from the Svelte package public API.
- Added Chip style exports to the styles package.
- Updated supporting design-system styling needed by the new Chip presentation.
- Included docs layout adjustments for better visual balance in the component documentation.

author: sttts
body:
## Summary

* Resolve a component's per-node GPU count from user-supplied `ResourceClaim` and `ResourceClaimTemplate` objects when no scalar GPU resource is present.
* Pass the lazy, memoized count through both Grove and LeaderWorkerSet rendering. vLLM consumes it for multinode MP/Ray and hybrid-DP launch flags; TensorRT-LLM consumes it for the multinode leader's `mpirun` world size.
* Preserve pure DRA allocation: the operator reads claim metadata for launch planning but never adds a synthetic `nvidia.com/gpu` request or limit.
* Watch referenced `ResourceClaim` and `ResourceClaimTemplate` objects and relevant cluster-scoped `DeviceClass` objects so dependency changes re-render existing workloads.
* Add the required ResourceClaim and DeviceClass read/watch RBAC and regenerate the operator and Helm RBAC manifests.
* Reject ambiguous or non-deterministic device requests instead of silently rendering broken distributed launch flags.

Fixes ai-dynamo/dynamo#12164

## Root cause

The multinode backend logic derived the per-container GPU count only from scalar entries in `resources.requests` and `resources.limits`. A pure-DRA container has `resources.claims` instead, so vLLM saw a count of zero and skipped the normal multinode launch setup. Leader and worker could consequently receive effectively identical commands.

Operator-managed GMS DRA did not expose this gap because its scalar GPU count remains present while backend arguments are rendered and is converted to a claim afterward. User-supplied DRA has no temporary scalar count.

## Implementation

`dra.ResolveGPUCount` keeps scalar resources authoritative for compatibility. When no scalar GPU is present, it maps the main container's claim references to the pod's `resourceClaims` and reads the referenced `resource.k8s.io/v1` `ResourceClaim` or `ResourceClaimTemplate`.

The resolver:

* supports deterministic `ExactCount` GPU requests, including Kubernetes' default count of one;
* supports `firstAvailable` when every alternative is a GPU class and all alternatives request the same count;
* respects the optional container request selector and deduplicates repeated claim/request references;
* ignores requests that are deterministically non-GPU;
* rejects `allocationMode: All`, mixed GPU/non-GPU alternatives, differing alternative counts, missing request names, missing claim objects, and unclassifiable DeviceClasses with actionable reconciliation errors;
* classifies DeviceClasses by `extendedResourceName`, unambiguous conjunctive `device.driver == ...` selectors, or a conventional GPU class name only when no selectors are present.

Rendering passes a `ContainerGPUCount` closure rather than eagerly resolving every component. `sync.OnceValues` shares the result and error across all roles of one component:

* multinode vLLM resolves it when producing distributed launch flags;
* multinode TensorRT-LLM resolves it only for the leader;
* SGLang, Noop, and single-node vLLM do not resolve it because they do not consume the count.

DCD and DGD controllers watch DRA dependencies. Claim/template events enqueue only multinode components that reference the changed object; DeviceClass events enqueue relevant DRA-backed multinode workloads. DGD dependency watches are limited to the Grove pathway because LWS rendering is owned by the DCD controller.

For two nodes with one DRA GPU each and `--tensor-parallel-size 2`, vLLM now enters the same MP/Ray launch path as two scalar-GPU pods. With MP selected, the leader receives `--nnodes 2`, `--node-rank 0`, and rendezvous flags; the worker receives its computed nonzero rank plus `--headless`. Hybrid-DP similarly derives `--data-parallel-size-local` and the per-node start rank from the resolved count.

## RBAC

The generated operator and Helm roles include:

* `get/list/watch` for `resourceclaims`;
* `get/list/watch` for cluster-scoped `deviceclasses`;
* `get/list/watch` for `resourceclaimtemplates` in addition to the existing lifecycle permissions required by operator-managed templates.

## Validation

After rebasing onto `e523f7ceb9`:

* `go test ./internal/dra ./internal/dynamo`
* `go test ./internal/controller -run '^(TestRenderMultinodePodTemplateSpecs_VLLMMultinodeDRA|TestGenerateWorkerPodTemplateSpecDoesNotRequireGPUResource|TestDynamoComponentDeploymentReconciler_.*WorkloadComponentType)$'`
* `git diff --check`

Coverage includes direct ResourceClaim and ResourceClaimTemplate resolution, request filtering and deduplication, default counts, DeviceClass classification, ambiguous request rejection, scalar precedence, lazy backend consumption, dependency event mapping, Grove TP/MP rendering, LeaderWorkerSet TP/MP rendering, TensorRT-LLM world-size calculation, and hybrid-DP flag injection.

  * Preserved resource claims while generating leader and worker pod configurations.
  * Added support for resolving GPU counts from resource claims when scalar GPU resources are unavailable.

* **Bug Fixes**

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [github.com/getkin/kin-openapi](https://redirect.github.com/getkin/kin-openapi) | `v0.137.0` → `v0.144.0` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/go/github.com%2fgetkin%2fkin-openapi/v0.144.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/go/github.com%2fgetkin%2fkin-openapi/v0.137.0/v0.144.0?slim=true) |

---

### kin-openapi: ValidationHandler.Load() Fail-Open Authentication Bypass via NoopAuthenticationFunc Default
[GHSA-r277-6w6q-xmqw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-r277-6w6q-xmqw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary
`ValidationHandler.Load()` in `getkin/kin-openapi` silently replaces a nil `AuthenticationFunc` with `NoopAuthenticationFunc`, which always returns `nil` without performing any credential check. Because this substitution happens unconditionally when the caller omits the field, every OpenAPI `security` requirement declared in the spec is silently satisfied for unauthenticated requests. An unauthenticated remote attacker can reach handlers for routes whose OpenAPI operation requires an API key, OAuth token, or any other security scheme if the application relies on `ValidationHandler` as its enforcement middleware. 

##### Details
`ValidationHandler` is an HTTP middleware exported by `openapi3filter` that validates incoming requests and responses against a loaded OpenAPI specification. Its `Load()` method initialises default fields before the handler begins serving:

```go
// openapi3filter/validation_handler.go:47-49
if h.AuthenticationFunc == nil {
    h.AuthenticationFunc = NoopAuthenticationFunc
}
```

`NoopAuthenticationFunc` is defined as:

```go
// openapi3filter/validation_handler.go:17-18
func NoopAuthenticationFunc(context.Context, *AuthenticationInput) error { return nil }
```

It always returns `nil`, meaning every security scheme check it handles is automatically approved.

When a request arrives, `ServeHTTP` → `before` → `validateRequest` assembles a `RequestValidationInput` with the current `AuthenticationFunc` (now the no-op) injected into `Options`:

```go
// openapi3filter/validation_handler.go:91-103
options := &Options{
    AuthenticationFunc: h.AuthenticationFunc,
}
requestValidationInput := &RequestValidationInput{
    Request:    r,
    PathParams: pathParams,
    Route:      route,
    Options:    options,
}
if err = ValidateRequest(r.Context(), requestValidationInput); err != nil {
    return err
}
```

Inside `ValidateRequest`, each security requirement calls `options.AuthenticationFunc`:

```go
// openapi3filter/validate_request.go:436-438
f := options.AuthenticationFunc
if f == nil {
    return ErrAuthenticationServiceMissing   // fail-closed path — never reached via ValidationHandler
}
// ...
// openapi3filter/validate_request.go:497-503
if err := f(ctx, &AuthenticationInput{...}); err != nil {
    return err
}
```

Because `f` is the no-op (not `nil`), the `ErrAuthenticationServiceMissing` guard is never triggered and `f(...)` returns `nil`, clearing the security requirement. Control then proceeds to the protected handler (`validation_handler.go:61-62`).

The critical contradiction is that callers who use `ValidateRequest` directly with a nil `AuthenticationFunc` get fail-closed behavior (`ErrAuthenticationServiceMissing`), while callers who use the higher-level `ValidationHandler` with a nil `AuthenticationFunc` get fail-open behavior. Since omitting `AuthenticationFunc` is the natural default, the majority of real-world integrations are vulnerable.

Affected source file and line: `openapi3filter/validation_handler.go:47–49` (commit `30e2923`, tag `v0.143.0`).

##### PoC
**Environment**

```
Docker (any version supporting multi-stage builds)
Go 1.25 (inside the container via golang:1.25-alpine)
getkin/kin-openapi v0.143.0 (local source copy)
```

**Step 1 — Build the Docker image**

From the repository root (parent of `vuln-001/`):

```bash
docker build \
  -t vuln001-auth-bypass-poc \
  -f vuln-001/Dockerfile \
  reports/github_web_233_getkin__kin-openapi
```

The `Dockerfile` copies the local `kin-openapi` source into `/kin-openapi/` inside the image and builds a Go binary (`/poc-binary`) from `main.go`. The `go.mod` inside the image uses a `replace` directive pointing to `/kin-openapi`, so no network access to the Go module proxy is required.

**Step 2 — Run the container**

```bash
docker run --rm --network none vuln001-auth-bypass-poc
```

**Step 3 (alternative) — Use the Python helper**

```bash
python3 vuln-001/poc.py --no-cleanup
```

**What the PoC does**

`main.go` creates a temporary OpenAPI 3.0 spec that declares `GET /secret` as protected by an `apiKey` security scheme:

```yaml
paths:
  /secret:
    get:
      security:
        - apiKey: []
components:
  securitySchemes:
    apiKey:
      type: apiKey
      name: X-Api-Key
      in: header
```

It then constructs a `ValidationHandler` **without** setting `AuthenticationFunc`, calls `Load()`, and sends a request with no `X-Api-Key` header:

```http
GET /secret HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test

##### X-Api-Key header is intentionally absent
```

**Expected (vulnerable) output**

```
=== CONTRAST: Direct ValidateRequest with nil AuthenticationFunc ===
  Direct ValidateRequest (nil auth) => ERROR: security requirements failed: missing AuthenticationFunc
  -> Fail-CLOSED behavior confirmed: missing auth function is rejected

=== EXPLOIT: ValidationHandler.Load() with nil AuthenticationFunc ===
  OpenAPI spec defines: security: [{apiKey: []}] on GET /secret
  ValidationHandler.AuthenticationFunc: NOT SET (nil)
  Load() will inject NoopAuthenticationFunc, which always returns nil

  Request:  GET /secret  (X-Api-Key header: absent)
  Response: status=200  body="SECRET_DATA\n"

[EXPLOIT SUCCESS] Auth bypass confirmed!
  Protected resource /secret returned SECRET_DATA without credentials.
  ValidationHandler.Load() silently injected NoopAuthenticationFunc.
  Security requirement was bypassed. VULN-001 REPRODUCED.
```

The contrast block confirms fail-closed behavior when `ValidateRequest` is called directly. The exploit block confirms fail-open behavior through `ValidationHandler`. Status 200 and `SECRET_DATA` are returned without any credential.

**Remediation patch**

```diff
--- a/openapi3filter/validation_handler.go
+++ b/openapi3filter/validation_handler.go
@​@​
  if h.Handler == nil {
      h.Handler = http.DefaultServeMux
  }
- if h.AuthenticationFunc == nil {
-     h.AuthenticationFunc = NoopAuthenticationFunc
- }
  if h.ErrorEncoder == nil {
      h.ErrorEncoder = DefaultErrorEncoder
  }
```

After this change, a nil `AuthenticationFunc` propagates into `ValidateRequest`, which returns `ErrAuthenticationServiceMissing` and rejects the request. Callers who genuinely want to skip authentication can still opt in explicitly: `h.AuthenticationFunc = openapi3filter.NoopAuthenticationFunc`.

##### Impact
This is an **authentication bypass** vulnerability (CWE-287). Any application that:

1. uses `openapi3filter.ValidationHandler` as its HTTP middleware, and
2. declares one or more `security` requirements in its OpenAPI specification, and
3. does **not** explicitly set `AuthenticationFunc`,

is fully exposed. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send requests to any protected endpoint without supplying credentials; the middleware accepts the request and forwards it to the underlying handler as if authentication had succeeded.

Affected parties include all Go services that adopt `ValidationHandler` as a drop-in validation layer and rely on OpenAPI `security` declarations for access control without adding a separate authentication layer upstream (e.g., an API gateway or reverse proxy). ## Summary

- **Stage gating (US2)**: a stage→ceiling table intersected into the spec-021 grant derivation at both load sites (bundle-narrowing idiom), so declaration/prose/door gating inherit the stage with structural absence beyond it. Stage-1 instruction lock: the effective charter is the world's preset constant; player edits get an honest notice naming the unlocking stage. Cross-stage determinism proven (same seed ⇒ identical world histories; only the agent's surface differs). Stage-1 roster (ratified from the TASK-119 artifact): send_omen, send_vision, monitor_and_act, cancel_order.
- **Creation UX (US1)**: `promptworld stages` (identities, concepts, grants, unlock evidence, earned state) + `promptworld new --stage/--override/--charter-preset` — earned stages offered normally, unearned via an explicit informed override recorded in the manifest. Stage on status surfaces (CLI live+offline, IPC, TUI).
- **Unlock chain (US3)**: `curriculum.exercise_passed`/`stage_unlocked` events (executor emission class, contract-first for TASK-119; fixture-proven end-to-end), gate-conjunct evaluation (`EvaluateUnlock` + the sanctioned `CharterObservedEvidence` constructor over 044's real fingerprint event), chronicle narration, and a per-user `~/.promptworld/unlocks.json` under the worlds-registry advisory-never-authority doctrine with auditable evidence pointers.
- **Exercises (US4)**: *first-night* (stage 1) and *the-law* (stage 2) as parseable, TASK-119-consumable definitions; every rubric term is a cataloged event type; the-law's rubric requires a player-authored charter revision in force (SC-004's honest grader).

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/personalizationdemo/agent-runs/6a6474274fb70ddc9dbddbdc

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** The Netlify deploy errored, with the following guidance provided:

The error at [line 56](#L56) shows `vite: Permission denied`, which indicates the Vite binary in `node_modules/.bin/vite` does not have execute permissions. This is a known issue that...

✅ **Result:** ## Summary

The deploy was failing to build because the `vite` command could not be run. The site's build environment either did not have the project's dependencies installed at the point the build command executed, or restored a stale/incomplete dependency cache from an earlier build (the one where `node_modules` had been committed with the wrong file permissions). Either way, `node_modules/.bin/vite` was missing or unusable when `npm run build` ran, so the build exited with `vite: not found`.

`node_modules` was already correctly excluded from version control via `.gitignore`, so the fix focuses on making the build resilient regardless of what state the dependency cache is in.

## Fix

The `build` script now has a `prebuild` step that npm runs automatically beforehand. It performs a fast, idempotent `npm install` to guarantee all dependencies (including `vite`) are actually present in `node_modules`, and it also ensures the installed binaries in `node_modules/.bin` are executable. This removes the build's dependency on any external caching behavior working correctly and protects against both failure modes seen so far: the binary being missing entirely, and the binary existing without execute permissions.

author: prisis
body:
The two follow-ups flagged during the benchmark/perf audit in #185, which were out of scope there. Independent of that PR — this branches off `alpha` directly.

## 1. `codegen` — schema snapshot ordering was locale-dependent

`packages/codegen/src/schema-drift.ts` sorted table names and migration ids with `localeCompare`. That resolves against the runtime's default locale and ICU version, so it is not stable across machines — which defeats the entire point, since `.lunora-schema.json` is a **committed** file and the sort exists specifically to make it byte-stable.

The failure mode: two developers, or a developer and CI, or one machine either side of a Node upgrade, regenerate the same schema and get different bytes. That reads as a spurious diff and a false drift signal.

Now sorted by UTF-16 code unit, which is locale-independent. Same bug class as the two instances fixed in `@lunora/replica` in #185 — this was the third, in a different package.

**No committed snapshot changes.** I checked all 9 in-repo `.lunora-schema.json` files object-by-object (191 objects) and no key ordering differs between the two comparators: every table and migration name is lowercase ASCII, where ICU collation and code-unit order agree. So no fixture regeneration, and the diff is confined to source plus a test.

The new test uses fixtures where the two orderings genuinely disagree (`Berries` / `_hidden` / `apples`, and `A_one` / `b_two`), so a regression to a locale-aware comparator flips it. Without that, a test using ordinary lowercase names would pass under either comparator and guard nothing.

Field / index / relation keys are left in declaration order — they were never locale-sorted, and that is now documented rather than left ambiguous.

## 2. `cli` — the init smoke suite runs against too tight a timeout

Each case scaffolds a whole project, parses its schema and function modules through `runCodegen` (a real TypeScript parse), and runs the wrangler validator. That is far more work than a unit test, and it lands against the shared 10s local budget (`tools/get-vitest-config.ts`; CI gets 30s).

On an unloaded machine the heaviest case takes ~6.4s of that 10s — thin enough that running anything else concurrently tips it over. It failed exactly that way twice during the #185 audit and passed on re-run, while CI stayed green. Each occurrence costs a full re-run to diagnose.

Scoped to this suite via `describe(name, { timeout }, fn)` rather than raising the global default, so genuinely hung unit tests elsewhere still fail fast.

Worth noting for anyone who saw my earlier description of this: the suite is **offline** — it scaffolds via `--from` against the local templates root, not giget. The cost is CPU, not network.

## Verification

`codegen` 864 tests, `cli` 684 tests, types clean, zero eslint errors. Affected run green across 6 projects.

author: gianlucamazza
body:
## What

Two verified build-flag defects, one per target:

**Linux (`CMakeLists.txt`)** — `LLAMA_NATIVE OFF` + `LLAMA_AVX2/F16C/FMA ON` were inert: llama.cpp's `llama_option_depr` maps deprecated vars only when truthy, and the three ISA ones have no `GGML_*` mapping at all. Real cache before this PR: `GGML_NATIVE=ON, GGML_AVX2/FMA/F16C=OFF` — i.e. `-march=native`, so the CI `xllama-cli-linux` artifact was pinned to the runner's CPU. Now the `GGML_*` vars are set directly; `XLLAMA_NATIVE_OPT` (default OFF) opts back into host tuning for local builds. `-march=znver2 -mavx2 -O3` is dropped from `xllama-cli` — it only covered `src/main.cpp` (not the `xllama` lib, not ggml) and contradicted the portable artifact.

**UWP (`uwp/ggml-uwp.vcxproj`)** — `repack.cpp` / `arch/x86/repack.cpp` were compiled but `GGML_USE_CPU_REPACK` was never defined, so the repacked-weight GEMM path (`ggml-cpu.cpp:64,632` guards; covers Q4_0/**Q4_K**/Q8_0/IQ4_NL — the shipped GGUF default is Q4_K_M) was dead code on console. Linux already had it (`GGML_CPU_REPACK=ON`). Now defined project-wide (single unconditional `ItemDefinitionGroup`, covers Debug and Release).

## How verified

- Fresh `cmake --preset linux-test` configure: cache now reads `GGML_NATIVE=OFF, GGML_AVX2=ON, GGML_F16C=ON, GGML_FMA=ON` (was `NATIVE=ON`, rest `OFF`).
- Full `linux-test` build + `ctest` running locally; CI runs the same suite on this PR.
- UWP compile is exercised by `build-uwp.yml` on this PR (llamacpp lane); a console before/after GGUF bench (`bench-xbox-ort.sh`, 3 runs with `run_index`) is planned as the Fase D validation window before any perf claim lands in docs.

No doc updates needed: no `.md` references `znver2`, `LLAMA_AVX2`, `LLAMA_NATIVE` or `CPU_REPACK` (grepped).

author: abians
body:
Work in progress, opened early so it can start picking up reviews rather than sitting on a branch.

## What changed

The landing is no longer a documentation page. It used to be `content/index.mdx` — a one-line MDX file whose entire body was `<LandingPage />`, which put it through the whole Nextra pipeline and then switched off six theme features one at a time. It is now `app/page.tsx`, and the docs theme has moved into an `(docs)` route group, so the landing opts in to nothing and there is nothing to opt out of. Three blocks of CSS that existed only to undo the layout it had been given are gone with it.

Every route keeps the URL it had.

## The page

Built on a ruled frame: two vertical hairlines running from the nav to the footer, with each band closing against them. One display scale, one easing curve, one duration scale.

The product screens are real DOM rather than screenshots, recreated from `apps/webview-ui` and driven by scroll position — one progress value per screen, with every mark inside it a function of that number. Scroll back up and a screen plays backwards. They are code-split and `ssr: false`, since they are `aria-hidden` decoration and every claim they illustrate is server-rendered in its heading.

Sections: hero, SDK strip, day one, manifesto, platform (five chapters with a sticky rail), migrate, alerts, engine, scale, install, sponsors, closing.

## Known incomplete

- **The engine section.** The isometric server diagram works and the choreography is in place, but the framing is still being tuned against a real browser. It has been through several passes; the current one uses a single static symmetric viewBox with no re-framing animation, after two attempts at animating the frame caused clipping and then a competing second motion.
- The ownership argument lost its home when that band became the engine. The strongest line ("GPL-3.0, one Rust binary, and the source that built it") has not been folded in anywhere yet.

## Verification

`next build` and `tsc --noEmit` pass, Biome is clean. Geometry for the isometric scene was checked numerically rather than by eye — the drawing never leaves its viewBox at any point in the opening, and the cube is horizontally centred at every moment.

Not reviewed in a browser by me; the visual pass is on Abian.

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
## Summary

The robotsix-chat agent emitted an `---AUTONOMOUS COMPLETE---` end-of-session marker while a periodic monitor subsession it had just spawned was still actively running. A session is not complete while it owns in-flight background work; closing as COMPLETE in that state is misleading and violates the intended contract ("complete" should imply no outstanding agent-owned work).

## Reproduction

1. Start an autonomous session that performs remediation (e.g. the www.robotsix.net P1 outage session, 2026-07-25).
2. As the final action, spawn a periodic monitor subsession to watch a long-running condition to a terminal state (here: monitor `7142f796`, 5-min interval, watching GitHub Actions deploy run #14 → site probe).
3. Immediately after spawning it, the agent prints `---AUTONOMOUS COMPLETE---`.

Observed: session declared COMPLETE with subsession `7142f796` still running (verified via `list_subsessions`).
Expected: the session must NOT be marked COMPLETE while any agent-owned subsession/background check is still running. It should either (a) report an intermediate/held status ("work in flight, monitor N running") and only declare COMPLETE once the subsession closes, or (b) treat spawning a durable monitor as an explicitly non-terminal state.

## Session details

- Session subject: restore www.robotsix.net (P1, HTTP 501); re-dispatched deploy-ovh.yml, run #14 in_progress.
- Offending marker: final assistant turn ending in `---AUTONOMOUS COMPLETE---`.
- Live in-flight subsession at close time: periodic monitor `7142f796`.
- Board/date: robotsix-chat, 2026-07-25.

## Suggested fix

Before emitting any session-complete marker, the agent should call `list_subsessions` and, if any subsession it owns is still running, suppress the COMPLETE marker in favor of a "monitoring in progress" status. COMPLETE is only valid once all owned subsessions have closed (or were intentionally handed off as standing/periodic with that fact stated explicitly rather than as "complete").

Reported by robotsix-chat at operator request.

---

author: copilot
body:
The `deploy` GitHub Actions job was failing during `azure/login` with `AADSTS700213` because the workflow emitted a ref-scoped OIDC subject that did not match the federated identity credential expected by Azure. This PR aligns the deploy job identity context with the configured Azure trust relationship.

- **Root cause**
  - `deploy` job ran without a GitHub Environment, so OIDC subject resolved to `...:ref:refs/heads/master` instead of an environment-scoped subject.

- **Workflow change**
  - Added `environment: Production` to the `deploy` job in `.github/workflows/master_mabati.yml`.
  - Kept existing deploy flow (artifact download, Azure login, webapp deploy) unchanged.

- **Resulting behavior**
  - `azure/login@v2` now requests a token with the expected environment-based subject, matching Azure federated credential configuration.

```yaml
deploy:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  needs: build
  environment:
    name: Production
  permissions:
    id-token: write
    contents: read
```

author: jkosmo
body:
## #796 — content import is now atomic (→ 2.4.0)

A module/course import previously wrote its components independently, so a failure partway through left **half-imported state**: standalone modules/sections, partial version chains, orphaned asset blobs, and no final course or import audit. Now the whole graph is built in **ONE transaction**.

### What changed
- `importModuleFromEnvelope` / `importCourseFromEnvelope` build the entire graph (module(s) + rubric/prompt/mcq versions + module versions + publish flips; for courses: the course + sections + their asset rows + ordered items + publish flip) inside one `runInTransaction` (30s timeout). Any failure rolls the whole import back; the import audit commits in the same tx.
- The import-called commands gained an **optional external tx client**, and their precondition **reads** run on that tx client during an import so they see rows created earlier in the same transaction.
- Section-asset blobs are **staged before the tx** (validate + upload, no DB), keyed by the section's pre-generated id — no blob I/O inside the tx. `SectionAsset` rows are created in-tx from the staged data; a rolled-back import **reclaims every staged blob** (no orphaned storage).

### Safety
- **No schema change** (pure code) → code-only deploy.
- **No behaviour change outside the import path** — the optional tx args are omitted everywhere else (full unit suite unchanged at 847/847).

### Verification
- `tsc` 0 · unit **847/847**
- New: `test/m2-import-atomicity` (real Postgres) — module + course mid-graph failures persist nothing; successes persist the full graph + audit.
- Existing export/import round-trips (incl. SVG asset remapping) — **14/14** green.

First of the EPIC #779 durability batch. #726 (idempotency-key) + #795 (transactional outbox) follow as a separate batch.

author: jaeyoon-enerzai
body:
## Summary

  Adds an INT4 weight-quantization pipeline for Gemma-3 270M Instruct (google/gemma-3-270m-it): GPTQ quantization → ONNX QDQ export → accuracy validation. Produces an NPU-friendly QDQ ONNX graph (no block_size
  attribute, no runtime Transpose) with a selectable in_feature (default) or out_feature grouping axis. Runs on CUDA or, without an NVIDIA GPU, on CPU.

 ## Changes

  ### New quantization pipeline (src/torq/models/gemma3/int4quant/)

  - Stage 0 — template (quantize_matmul.py): Converts each MatMul weight of the base ONNX into a q4_k QDQ skeleton that Stage 2 reuses as the export template (its values are overwritten, only the structure
  matters).
  - Stage 1 — GPTQ (run_gptq.py): Loads the HF PyTorch model, runs GPTQ INT4 (asymmetric, group_size 32) with ultrachat calibration, and emits compressed safetensors. Selectable in_feature/out_feature axis;
  --device auto|cuda|cpu with a CUDA-free CPU path (Apple Silicon runs on CPU — compressed_tensors has no MPS offload backend).
  - Stage 2 — export (safetensors_to_onnx_qdq.py): Writes the GPTQ weights into the ONNX QDQ graph, auto-generating the template from the base ONNX when absent (127 Linear layers replaced).
  - Stage 3 — accuracy: test_snr.py (logit cos_sim / SNR vs the fp32 base via ONNX Runtime) and compare_onnx_generation.py (base vs quant generation comparison).
  - Automation (select_best_gptq.py): Repeats Stage 1+2+3 N times across a GPU pool (or sequentially on CPU) and selects the highest-cos_sim result, since GPTQ has large run-to-run variance.
  - Shared utils (quant_utils.py): BF16↔FP32 helpers, quantization math (Q4_0/Q4_K, per-block/per-channel), ONNX graph builders (DequantizeLinear subgraph, bf16→fp32), and accuracy utilities.
  - Optional (extract_lm_head_embeddings.py): Dequantizes the quantized lm_head into a token-embedding table for consistent -emb inference (Gemma ties embed_tokens/lm_head).
  - Docs & config: README.md (background concepts, staged workflow, accuracy interpretation, troubleshooting), requirements.txt, and a scoped .gitignore excluding large binaries (*.onnx, *.safetensors, *.npy, quant
  output dirs).

 ### Notes
  
  - Verified end-to-end CUDA-free on Apple Silicon (CPU): Stage 1→2→3 pass, single-run cos_sim ≈ 0.954, snr_db ≈ 9.75 — matching the documented good-run range (cos_sim ≈ 0.95).

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: A Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability existed due to pipe deadlocks in `Process` execution. If a child process writes more data than the OS pipe buffer can hold, it blocks. If the parent is blocked on `waitUntilExit()`, a deadlock occurs.
🎯 Impact: The application could hang indefinitely when executing shell commands or external tools that output large amounts of data.
🔧 Fix: Moved pipe reads (`readDataToEndOfFile()`) to occur *before* calling `process.waitUntilExit()` in `OBSWebSocketLiveIntegrationTests.swift` and `AutomationExecutor.swift`, ensuring the pipe buffer is continuously drained.
✅ Verification: Static code analysis confirms reads happen before waits. Tested with static syntax validation.

author: eliasmagdaleno
body:
> **Stacked on #8** — base is `recommender-golden-harness`, since #8 is still open. Merge #8 first; this then retargets to `main` automatically.

## What changed

**1. The agreement bonus is now proportional.**

```swift
score += agreementBonus * (tagNorm * malNorm).squareRoot()   // was: flat += overlapBonus
```

The geometric mean tracks the **weaker** of the two signals: topping both pools earns the full bonus, incidental co-occurrence deep in both earns almost nothing. It's also zero whenever either pool omits the title, so non-overlap needs no special case — the intersection loop is now an optimization rather than a rule.

The old flat `+0.25` was enormous against scores that live in `[0,1]`. Solving `1.85t + 0.25 > 1.0` gives `t > 0.405`: a title at only ~40% of top strength in *both* pools outranked the single best recommendation either signal had on its own. Both rules are defensible — "agreement wins" vs "strength wins, agreement breaks ties" — but they're different products, and this picks the second.

**The constant stays at 0.25 on purpose.** Changing a formula and its scale simultaneously makes the golden diff unreadable. Worth noting the geometric bonus is always ≤ the flat one it replaces, so 0.25 is now a candidate for retuning — as a separate, individually-reviewable change.

**2. Sub-providers break ties on id.** `TagCandidateProvider` and `MALCandidateProvider` now match what `CompositeCandidateProvider` has done since 5fb47f9. Swift's sort isn't stable and dictionary iteration order is randomized per process, so tied candidates could reorder between launches and a tie straddling `limit` could change pool *membership*. Their reason-string attribution (`bestTag`/`bestSeed`) had the same defect via task-group completion order and now resolves on name/title.

## Evidence

The golden diff — which is the entire reason #8 exists:

```diff
-2  Alpha Blade  0.9677  0.2778  0.2500  1.4539
+2  Alpha Blade  0.9677  0.2778  0.1296  1.3335
```

Alpha Blade agrees only weakly (MAL has it at 0.2778) and its bonus roughly halves. Crimson Vow — top of *both* pools — keeps the full 0.2500, unchanged. That's precisely the intended property.

Rank order is unchanged in this fixture, because no title happens to sit in the window where the old rule flipped an ordering. So that case is covered directly by a behaviour test instead: `testAgreementDoesNotPromoteMidRankedTitleOverStrongSingleSignal` builds a title mid-ranked in both pools and asserts it lands *below* a title topping one pool (0.7770, third) — under the flat bonus it scored 0.9345 and came second.

## Tests

172 unit tests green (167 + 5 in the golden suite). New:

- `testAgreementDoesNotPromoteMidRankedTitleOverStrongSingleSignal` — the semantic contract above
- `testTagProviderBreaksTiesOnIdAscending` / `testMALProviderBreaksTiesOnIdAscending` — two engineered exact ties, asserted to resolve id-ascending

`testCompositeBlendsNormalizesAndBoostsOverlap` is renamed to `...BoostsAgreement` and its expected score updated 1.60 → 1.5268, with the arithmetic shown in a comment.

SwiftLint contribution from these changes is zero. (The repo total reads higher only because of unrelated uncommitted work in the tree; `file_length` on `Manga_ReaderTests.swift` was already violated at 2202 lines before this branch.)

Also renames `overlapBonus` → `agreementBonus` — "overlap" implied the old binary rule — and updates the glossary entry.

author: ailvenliu
body:
## Summary

- Add a trusted `master-merge-gate` GitHub Actions workflow and deterministic policy check for master-bound PRs.
- Restrict `master` PR sources to same-repository `develop`, `release/*`, and `hotfix/*`; reject development-stage assets and all `docs/` changes outside `docs/changelog/`.
- Add the branch-governance skill, release-shim guidance, master-only automatic release/deployment authority, and dedicated-data-root deployment rules.
- Propagate the constraints, skills, CI workflow, and checklists to generated Python, C++, and hybrid projects.

## Why

Production promotion needs a clear trust boundary: only reviewed changes entering `master` may automatically publish or deploy, and a deployment must promote the immutable artefact for that exact master SHA. Development-only agent assets must not cross into master through normal PR flow. Dedicated data roots avoid treating system-owned paths such as `/var` or `/srv` as the default service-release location.

## Impact

Generated projects receive the `master-merge-gate` workflow, branch-governance skill, master PR/MR checklist, and a default automatic-promotion contract. Without a durable, reviewed project-specific exception, automatic server deployments use `/data/...`, `~/data/...`, or another approved dedicated data volume; they reject system-owned roots.

## Hosted configuration required

Configure GitHub branch rules/rulesets to require `master-merge-gate`, profile validation, pull requests, independent review, and no direct or force pushes. A checked-in workflow cannot establish those hosted controls by itself.

## Validation

- `.agents/bin/agent-check-constraints`
- `.agents/bin/agent-precommit` -- passed all 6 checks (environment, dependency manifest, ruff format, ruff check, mypy, pytest)
- Cross-platform skill verification and focused master-gate/deployment-policy regressions

author: bender0oo0
body:
Closes #1517

## Problem

`/api/stream` dispatched its gate sequence (feature-toggle/rate-limit/access/Zod-validation) on the stream generator's first `.next()` pull, which happened inside `streamSSE`'s callback — after the response's 200 headers were already flushed. A 403/404/400/429 gate failure therefore always shipped as HTTP 200 with an SSE `error` frame, so access logs, metrics, and WAF/edge rate-limit rules that key off status codes never saw the real outcome — brute-force and rate-limit bypass on this endpoint weren't detectable from outside.

## Fix

The route now pulls the generator's first `.next()` **before** calling `streamSSE()` and maps a thrown gate error through the same `queryErrorResponse` path `/api/query` uses — a real HTTP status, no SSE stream opened. `pumpStream` takes that pre-pulled outcome as an optional 4th param so the generator isn't pulled a second time once the SSE stream is opened.

Failures from the **second** chunk onward are unchanged: the SSE response is already open by then, so they still surface as HTTP 200 + an `error` frame — pinned by a new test (`item:tail-fail-mid`).

## Why not the `prepareStream()` extraction suggested in the issue

The issue proposed pulling the gate sequence into an exported `prepareStream()` called by the route, with `executeStream` reusing it. That requires either a new public `Dispatcher` method (touching 5 test-stub dispatchers) or re-running gates for the actual stream execution — which would double-consume `enforceRateLimit`'s rate-limit budget per request and split `runStreamInstrumented`'s span/metrics into two per logical stream call.

Pre-pulling the existing generator achieves the same fix with a single gate pass, no `Dispatcher` interface change, and no double rate-limit consumption. `dispatcher-live.ts` (the client) already handles a non-SSE JSON response on `/api/stream` ("Pre-SSE gate failures ... return a normal JSON error envelope — map them like /api/query"), so this isn't a new contract from the client's perspective.

## Notes

- No production `r.streamHandler` exists yet in framework/enterprise (only test fixtures) — the `stream.onAbort` cleanup handler is now registered slightly later (after the pre-pull instead of before), which only matters if a handler holds a resource across `yield` (DB cursor, subscription). None currently do.
- 429 isn't separately tested — it runs through the identical `queryErrorResponse` gate-mapping path as the 403 case covered here, and would need a `context.rateLimit` resolver wired into the test's `buildServer` setup.

## Test plan
- [x] `../scripts/check-wt.sh` (tsc -b, biome, full unit suite) — green, 4939 pass / 0 fail
- [x] New tests: 403 (access-denied), 404 (unknown handler), 400 (validation), and the chunk-2-then-fail boundary case (200 + error frame, unchanged)

## Summary
Refactors `distortions/text.py` to be grapheme-cluster-aware (not code-point-based) and adds script-aware `typo_injection` and `homoglyph_substitution` functions with dedicated character maps for Arabic, Cyrillic, CJK, and Devanagari.

## Motivation
The existing character-level distortions (`char_swap`, `char_insert`, `char_delete`, `keyboard_typo`) split text with `list(text)`, which operates on raw Unicode code points. This breaks combining marks (Arabic tashkeel, Devanagari matras, accented Latin letters) apart from their base character, and there was no `typo_injection` or homoglyph substitution capability at all for non-Latin scripts. This limited NightmareNet's applicability to English-only NLP tasks.

Closes #310

## Changes
- `nightmarenet/distortions/text.py`:
  - Added `_graphemes()` helper using `regex.findall(r"\X", text)` (Unicode extended grapheme clusters) and switched `char_swap`, `char_insert`, `char_delete`, and `keyboard_typo` to operate on graphemes instead of raw code points.
  - `char_insert` now draws inserted characters from the same script as the surrounding text (via `char_maps.detect_script`) instead of always inserting ASCII lowercase, so non-Latin text doesn't get random Latin noise spliced in.
  - Added `typo_injection()`: script-aware typo simulation, dispatches to the correct per-script typo map for each grapheme.
  - Added `homoglyph_substitution()`: Unicode confusables-based substitution, using curated per-script confusables tables.
  - `KEYBOARD_ADJACENT` is now an alias for `char_maps.latin.TYPO_MAP` (single source of truth), so existing imports still work.
  - `typo_injection` and `homoglyph_substitution` are registered in `apply_text_distortions`'s `distortion_funcs` dict but intentionally **not** added to `default_config`, to avoid changing existing pipeline output for anyone using the default distortion mix. They're available via a custom `config` dict.
- `nightmarenet/distortions/char_maps/` (new package):
  - `latin.py`, `cyrillic.py`, `arabic.py`, `cjk.py`: `TYPO_MAP` + `CONFUSABLES` tables for each required script.
  - `devanagari.py`: same, added as bonus coverage since the issue's Problem section names Devanagari even though Acceptance Criteria only requires Arabic/Cyrillic/CJK.
  - `__init__.py`: `detect_script()` (Unicode range-based script bucketing), `get_typo_map()`, `get_confusables()`, `is_rtl()`.
- `tests/test_distortions_multilingual.py` (new): grapheme-cluster integrity tests, script detection tests, typo_injection/homoglyph_substitution coverage per script, RTL base-direction preservation tests, and roundtrip validation for Arabic/Cyrillic/CJK/Devanagari.
- `pyproject.toml`: added `regex>=2023.0.0` dependency (stdlib `re` has no `\X` grapheme-cluster support).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `char_swap` works correctly on CJK strings (no broken grapheme clusters)
- [x] `typo_injection` has character maps for Arabic, Cyrillic, and CJK
- [x] Homoglyph substitution uses Unicode confusables for non-Latin (curated subset — see Reviewer Notes)
- [x] RTL text maintains correct directionality after distortion
- [x] Tests cover at least 3 non-Latin scripts with roundtrip validation (Arabic, Cyrillic, CJK, plus Devanagari as bonus)
- [x] Existing Latin-alphabet tests still pass (no regression) — 40/40 pre-existing tests pass unchanged, plus 32 new tests

## Type
- [x] Feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Tests

---

## Pre-submission Requirements
- [x] I have **starred** this repository ⭐
- [x] I have **followed** [@Adit-Jain-srm](https://github.com/Adit-Jain-srm)
- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Adit-Jain-srm/NightmareNet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) in full

## Quality Checklist
- [x] `ruff check nightmarenet/ scripts/ tests/` — 0 errors
- [ ] `mypy nightmarenet/ --ignore-missing-imports` — not yet run, will confirm
- [x] `pytest tests/` — `test_distortions.py` + `test_distortions_multilingual.py` pass (72/72)
- [x] New functionality has corresponding tests
- [x] Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`feat:`)
- [x] No `from __future__ import annotations` added under `nightmarenet/api/`
- [x] No new imports of hosted-only libraries (`sqlalchemy`, `redis`, `celery`)

## Documentation
- [x] Docstrings added/updated (Google style, public APIs only)

## AI Disclosure
- [x] This PR includes AI-assisted code (Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) — I have reviewed every line and can explain it

## Security Considerations
- [x] Not applicable (no security-sensitive changes)

## Breaking Changes
N/A — new functions are additive and opt-in; existing `default_config` behavior is unchanged.

---

<details>
<summary>Reviewer notes</summary>

- The homoglyph confusables tables are a **curated subset**, not a live sync of Unicode's `confusables.txt` — this sandbox/dev environment has no network access to unicode.org. Extending these tables with the full database is a natural follow-up.
- CJK `typo_injection` uses visually/structurally similar Han character confusion rather than keyboard adjacency, since CJK input goes through an IME and has no meaningful "adjacent key" concept. Documented in `char_maps/cjk.py`.
- Arabic `typo_injection` uses dotted-letter confusion (e.g. ب/ت/ث) rather than a guessed keyboard layout, since Arabic keyboard layouts vary significantly by OS/region. Documented in `char_maps/arabic.py`.
- RTL correctness is verified via first-strong-character base direction (Unicode Bidi rule P2/P3) before/after distortion, since Python `str` already preserves logical (not visual) order — the real risk was injecting foreign-script noise that could shift the paragraph's base direction, which `char_insert`'s script-awareness now prevents.
- Devanagari support goes beyond the acceptance criteria's minimum (3 scripts) since the issue's Problem section explicitly names it.
- `typo_injection`/`homoglyph_substitution` are opt-in (not in `default_config`) by design — happy to wire them into the default pipeline mix if that's preferred, just flagging the decision for review.

</details>

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added Unicode-aware text distortions across Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, CJK, and Devanagari scripts.
  - Added script-appropriate typo injection and homoglyph substitution.
  - Improved character swapping, insertion, and deletion while preserving grapheme clusters and text direction.
  - Added automatic script and right-to-left detection.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Reduced the risk of breaking combined characters and multilingual text during distortions.

author: lestephen
body:
Works through the backlog from the strict-tool-schema deploy. Four issues, one per commit, each verified by seeing its guard fail before trusting it.

Based on `d7a34d8`, the commit currently deployed as `v0.131.1-eki.5`, so this stacks on lestephen/ms-365-mcp-server#2. Retarget to `eki/v0.131.1-broker` once that merges.

## `1d51655` fixes #29, a regression from the hybrid deploy

`get-tool-schema` answered with `{ name, method, path, parameters }` and nothing about how to invoke the thing. In hybrid mode some tools really are callable by name and some are reachable only through `execute-tool`, so a payload whose `name` field looks callable leads a model to call it directly and get `MCP error -32602`. That is what happened to `delete-mail-attachment`: schema loaded, call failed, caller fell back to `graph-batch`. On a destructive operation a failed call is ambiguous until state is re-inspected, which is what made it worse than a plainly absent tool.

The reporter framed it as "expose the tool or drop it from the catalog". Neither is right: `search-tools` and `get-tool-schema` exist precisely to describe tools that are not registered, so the catalog was not wrong, it was silent about the contract. Now:

- `get-tool-schema` returns an `invocation` block: `via: "direct"`, or `via: "execute-tool"` with a note and an example carrying the exact `tool_name`
- `search-tools` marks `invoke_via` on every result, so the schema fetch is not the first hint
- the hybrid instructions say plainly not to call a tool by name unless it is in the tool list

Verified with the production patterns: `delete-mail-attachment` reports `execute-tool` with a worked example, `get-mail-message` reports `direct`.

## `98be003` fixes the cheap half of #24

`--blocked-tools` removed the tools, but scopes are derived from the endpoint catalogue, so blocking `send-mail` still left `Mail.Send` on the token. `graph-batch` declares no scopes of its own, so the prohibited operation stayed fully authorized. Blocked tools are now excluded from both scope paths. Verified end to end: `--list-permissions` drops 60 → 59, and the one removed is `Mail.Send`.

This does not close the passthrough, the larger half of #24. It means the token can no longer perform the operation the operator prohibited, whatever route asks for it.

## `ba4d8e6` fixes #27

The specs are pinned to an immutable upstream commit in `openapi-pin.json` with expected size and sha256 per spec. Checksumming a moving branch would have gone red on every upstream metadata push while still not making any single build reproducible; pinning the commit gives reproducibility with no ongoing noise.

Verification runs on downloads **and** on an existing local file, because a stale copy quietly becoming the build input is the developer half of this bug. Not hypothetical: the first run rejected a worktree still carrying the May 9 spec (37,057,635 bytes) against the pinned 38,050,122.

`npm run generate -- --refresh-spec` fetches master, reports the new digest, and asks for a deliberate pin update.

**One bug found by running it rather than reasoning about it:** my first content-length check compared the *decoded* body against the declared length. `raw.githubusercontent.com` gzips these specs (~2 MB compressed vs ~38 MB decoded) and `fetch` decompresses transparently, so that check failed *every* download. It now applies only to unencoded bodies; the pinned size and digest are authoritative regardless.

## `4bb357f` fixes #25

`writable-body-invariants` catches a writable property disappearing. It cannot catch the reverse: a newly published navigation property is dropped silently, because the allowlist has no entry for something that did not exist when it was written.

`nav-property-classification.json` records a decision for all **130** reachable navigation properties (33 keep, 97 drop). The test recomputes the reachable set and fails on anything unclassified, naming each one and stating the two valid responses. It also rejects stale entries and cross-checks the record against the code in both directions, so the file cannot drift into describing decisions the codegen does not implement.

Deliberately **not** derived from the allowlist: a record generated from it would lose its own assertion whenever an entry was deleted, which is what the other guard exists to catch. Together they are bidirectional.

Verified by injecting a synthetic property: the test fails naming `microsoft.graph.mailFolder.brandNewThing`, and passes once removed.

## Also filed, not fixed here

**#30**, found while verifying the scope subtraction: the drafts-only policy blocks six tools but leaves `reply-shared-mailbox-mail`, `reply-all-shared-mailbox-mail` and `forward-shared-mailbox-mail` open. The gap is internally inconsistent, blocking reply/forward on the personal mailbox and send on a shared one, and it predates the blocklist work: the deployed pattern was derived from the eki deny lists, so it inherited the gap. Fixing it means changing production policy in two places, so it is a decision rather than a patch.

## Verification

933 tests pass (68 files), up from 912 at the base. `tsc` output identical to the deployed commit. Prettier clean. No production change: this is fork code, not yet vendored or tagged.

author: lavan96
body:
### Motivation

- Close an authorization/integrity gap where the `generate-chart-analysis` Edge Function accepted caller-supplied `chartId` and `chartData` and used a service-role client to overwrite authoritative `charts` rows without object-level checks.
- Prevent low-privileged authenticated users from persisting AI-generated analysis onto charts/reports they do not own or are not permitted to edit.

### Description

- Require deny-by-default charts edit permission by calling `requireModulePermission(..., 'charts', 'can_edit')` in `supabase/functions/generate-chart-analysis/index.ts` and return HTTP 403 when unauthorized.
- Stop trusting caller-supplied analysis inputs by loading the target chart and its `dataset`/`chart_config` and the linked `generated_reports` row server-side, then build the LLM prompt from that stored data instead of request body `chartData`/`reportContext`.
- Fail explicitly on missing chart or DB errors by returning HTTP 404 for not-found and throwing on persistence failures, and check the `update` result (`updateError`) after writing the authoritative `charts` row.
- Protect the generic service-role path `supabase/functions/manage-templates` by enforcing charts-module permissions for operations against `charts` and `chart_analysis` via `requireModulePermission` and `permForAction` so service-route updates are gated server-side.
- Prevent client-side automatic backfill from attempting writes for users without edit permission by gating the backfill in `src/pages/Charts.tsx` with `canEditCharts` and adding it to the hook dependency list.

### Testing

- `git diff --check` — passed with no whitespace or diff-check errors.
- Targeted Python assertions (quick source checks) — passed and validated presence of the authorization gate, server-bound chart data usage, `manage-templates` protection, and client-side edit gating.
- `node scripts/security/check-function-registry.mjs` — passed (registry integrity OK).
- `node scripts/security/scan-auth-patterns.mjs` — passed (static auth pattern scan OK).
- `node scripts/security/check-edge-functions.mjs` — partially run: static checks completed but the Deno-backed runtime portion could not run because `deno` is not installed in the environment.
- `npm ci` / ESLint (dependency-backed linting) — could not complete because dependency installation failed due to remote registry access returning HTTP 403, so full lint/test runs requiring npm packages were not executed.

All changes are limited to server-side authorization and minimal client gating to remediate the integrity issue while preserving existing functionality and behavior when callers are authorized.

author: jcosta33
body:
Closes the last known OE-5 / WB-5 / M-109 crossing. Campaign follow-up from #716; transport proven in #788.

## Defect

`get_plugin_state` returned `Vec<u8>`, `set_plugin_state` took `Vec<u8>`. Tauri serializes both as a JSON array of decimal numbers.

PH-3's base64 does not spare them: `readPluginState` calls `bytesToBase64` **after** the crossing.

## Measured

Representative 65,536-byte chunk (bytes spread across 0..255, as real compressed plugin state is):

| Path | Wire bytes | Ratio |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ instanceId, pluginState: number[] }` | 234,023 | 3.571x |
| raw body | 65,536 | 1.000x |

Red-first: `pluginStateBinaryIpc.spec.ts` failed 13/17 before the fix. The inflation assertions passed at both ends and still pin the ratio.

## Transport

Reuses #788's mechanism. No second transport invented.

| Command | Direction | Instance id | Body |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `get_plugin_state_bytes` | bytes out | JSON arg | `tauri::ipc::Response` |
| `set_plugin_state_bytes` | bytes in | `x-sourdaw-plugin-instance` header, percent-encoded | `InvokeBody::Raw` |

**Asymmetry is deliberate.** The read request carries nothing but an id, so it stays JSON — exactly as `read_file_bytes` keeps its `path` argument. Only the write direction has its body fully occupied, the same constraint that forced `x-sourdaw-path`.

**Rejected: handle command.** A JSON sibling call returning a token costs a second round trip, adds server-side handle state with lifetime and eviction concerns, and invents a stale-handle failure mode. Buys nothing over a header that already exists and is proven. The instance id is already this domain's stable identity on every other command.

**Header validation not weakened.** Extracted #788's chain into `commands::binary_ipc` — present, ASCII, well-formed escapes, valid UTF-8. `write_file_bytes` now calls the same function; error strings byte-identical. Two raw-body commands cannot drift apart. Percent-decoder tests moved with the decoder; none dropped.

Instance-registry lookup is the authorization gate. Plugin state is keyed by instance, not path-addressed, so no filesystem allowlist applies. Unknown instance still yields `No plugin instance: {id}`.

## Enumeration

Every byte-carrying IPC crossing in PluginHost, not just the two cited:

| Crossing | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `get_plugin_state` | fixed |
| `set_plugin_state` | fixed |
| `process_plugin_audio` / `processAudioIPC` | **excluded** — per-block RT relay, fixed small blocks, RT lane owns it |
| `load/unload/scan_plugins`, `get/set_plugin_parameter`, `open/close_plugin_gui`, `get_default_plugin_paths`, `is_plugin_gui_supported`, `onPluginLatencyChanged` | no byte arrays — strings, numbers, DTOs |
| Faust engine, WAM host | browser-side, never cross Tauri |

Checked bare `Uint8Array` sites too, not only `Vec<u8>` greps — #788's lesson that Tauri's serializer calls `Array.from` on nested typed arrays, so they inflate identically while staying invisible to that grep. `plugin_gui.rs` carries no bytes.

## Wire format

Old commands deleted and unregistered. Grep confirms nothing else referenced them — only the two repository files. New payload shape, so new names.

## Byte fidelity

Round trips assert real equality, not liveness. Rust covers all 256 values plus a 0x00/high-byte response asserted to be the `Raw` variant — a JSON body fails the test. TS round-trips all 256 through base64, plus `0x00` / `0x80` / `0xFF`, subarray windows, and empty chunks.

Dropped two copies the `number[]` shape forced: `Uint8Array.from(bytes)` on read, `[...bytes]` on restore.

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `vitest run --changed origin/main --dir src` | 814 files, 5576 tests pass |
| `pnpm typecheck` / `typecheck:test` | 0 / 0 |
| oxlint + eslint (touched) | 0 errors |
| `cargo test -p sourdaw` | 66 pass |
| `pnpm deps:validate` | unchanged vs base |

## Reviewer flags

`deps:validate` exits 1 on this branch **and on untouched `d5f4b745a`** — two pre-existing unresolvable `vi.mock` paths in `Transport/.../startPlayheadScheduler.spec.ts` (`#/infra/logger/appLog` should be `appLogger`). Proved by stash round-trip; identical rows both ways. Not mine, not fixed here.

Added one `no-orphans` `pathNot` row for `src/utils/__tests__/serializeLikeTauri.ts` — the serializer reproduction extracted from `tauriBridge.spec.ts` so both payload-size specs share one copy. The main cruise excludes specs, so a spec-only helper reads as an orphan. Sits beside `automationCurveCases.ts`, same documented shape. Warn-only; CI passes either way. Object if you disagree.
