author: niko047
body:
<!-- parity-montage -->
### DOM→Figma parity — before / after

Each strip is **Target** (browser) · **Before** (this PR) · **After** (this PR).

**BG-06 — `radial-gradient` produced no paint at all (60.90% → 0.00%)**

![radial gradient before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/figitdesign/web-to-figma/parity-shots/bg-bg-06-radial.png)

**BG-03 — angled linear gradient was mirrored (42.21% → 0.00%)**

![angled gradient before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/figitdesign/web-to-figma/parity-shots/bg-bg-03-linear-angle.png)

**IMG-02 — `object-fit` was ignored; `contain` rendered as cover (17.58% → 0.00%)**

![object-fit before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/figitdesign/web-to-figma/parity-shots/img-img-02-object-fit.png)
<!-- /parity-montage -->




Three P0 converter fidelity bugs, each surfaced by a new oracle scene and verified against real Figma at tier 2.

## The bugs

**`radial-gradient` produced no paint at all.** `cssBackgroundToFigmaPaints` only matched `linear-gradient`, returned `[]`, and the element pasted as a blank box. `GRADIENT_RADIAL` was already in the kiwi schema — it was just missing from the TS paint union.

**Angled linear gradients were mirrored.** The transform's horizontal term was `cos(angle + 90) = -sin(angle)` where it needs `+sin(angle)`. That term vanishes at 0deg/180deg, so the default top-to-bottom ramp looked perfect and hid the bug for every other angle. The gradient line is now also scaled to the element's box (`|w·sin| + |h·cos|`), so the end stops land on the same corners the browser uses instead of a square approximation.

**`object-fit` was ignored.** `imageScaleMode` was hardcoded to `FILL` — which is Figma's name for *cover*, not CSS's default. CSS defaults to `fill`, i.e. Figma's `STRETCH`. Now `fill`/`cover`/`contain` map to `STRETCH`/`FILL`/`FIT`. The existing `img-01-raster` scene could never have caught this: it uses a 1×1 image, which looks identical in every scale mode.

## Tier-2, before → after

| Scene | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bg/bg-06-radial` | 60.90% | **0.00%** |
| `bg/bg-03-linear-angle` | 42.21% | **0.00%** |
| `img/img-02-object-fit` | 17.58% | **0.00%** |
| `05-exotic/gradients-effects` (pre-existing) | 26.46% | **9.35%** |

## Coverage

The catalog listed ~180 hypotheses but only 11 had scenes, so most of it was never actually measured. This adds **16 scenes** for unmeasured P0 hypotheses (borders, radii, gradients, box-shadow, SVG path fill, object-fit, transforms, grid, box-sizing) and annotates the catalog entries with them.

Full 63-scene tier-2 sweep: **53 scenes at exactly 0.00%**, no regressions. Remaining non-zero are pre-existing and unrelated to this change — `05-exotic/weird-shapes` 7.18%, `bord/bord-06-dotted` 3.74% and `bord/bord-05-dashed` 2.00% (dashed/dotted still render solid by explicit scope in `border-decomposition.ts`), `fx/fx-06-text-shadow` 2.80%, `rad/rad-04-percent-circle` 1.45% (antialiasing on the curve only — the shape is correct).

## One baseline caveat

The tier-2 baseline for `05-exotic/text-in-box` moves 3.50% → 3.77%. That is **not** from this PR: the scene contains no gradients or images, so none of the changed code paths run. Measured with this branch stashed, pristine `main` also reports 3.77% — pre-existing drift the baseline hadn't caught up with.

## Verification

`lint` pass · `check-types` pass · 312 tests pass (5 skipped) · tier-0 ratchet passes (63 scenes). Adds `gradient.test.ts` with 10 tests pinning the transform math, including a regression test for the mirrored angle.

Changeset: patch to `@figit/dom-to-figma` (0.2.1 → 0.2.2).

author: luckyrjain
body:
## Problem

Phase 5's Task 0 design pass (merged, #57) resolved the four named approval gates and moved contracts to Approved for Implementation, but built no code. This PR is the first real implementation slice: the data layer the rest of Phase 5's worker/adapter/approval machinery will build on.

## Solution

Implements exactly `workflow_definitions`/`workflow_versions`, `automation_policies`, `triggers` -- per `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-phase-5-automation-design.md` and `docs/phases/phase-005/DATA-MODEL.md`. Deliberately does **not** implement `workflow_runs`, `workflow_run_steps`, `approval_requests`, `compensation_steps`, or any `/simulate`/`/runs`/`/approvals` endpoint -- those depend on the durable worker/action-adapter machinery a later task builds, and nothing is stubbed ahead of that.

- **Migration `0038_phase5_workflow_schema.py`** -- reuses Phase 4's immutable-versioning idiom (migration `0029`'s trigger pattern) with two deliberate divergences: workspace-scoped (unlike Phase 4's global `prompt_versions`/`tool_definitions` catalog -- these are user-authored automations, not a platform catalog), and a separate `workflow_definitions` identity table so `automation_policies`/`triggers` have a stable FK target for "which workflow family" independent of any one version row's lifecycle (a real problem `prompt_versions`' single-table shape didn't have to solve). `trg_workflow_versions_immutability` rejects any change to `graph`/`trigger_refs`/`policy_ref`/`definition_hash` once a version leaves `draft`, enforced at the database layer. Two `CHECK` constraints on `triggers` enforce the design doc's "a schedule trigger always names its own timezone explicitly" / "an event trigger always names its filter" rules structurally, not only in application code.
- **`backend/ecc/domains/automation/`** (new package) -- `workflows.py`, `policy.py`, `triggers.py` (no HTTP router of its own -- `API-SCHEMAS.md` names no trigger endpoint at this task's scope, mirroring `ai_runtime.tools`'s router-less shape).
- **API surface (Task 1 scope only)**: `GET|POST /automations/workflows`, `GET /automations/workflows/{id}`, `POST .../publish|disable`, `GET|POST /automations/policies`, `POST /automations/policies/{id}/revoke`. Every mutating endpoint requires `AuthDep`/`CsrfDep` + `Idempotency-Key`; every endpoint resolves `workspace_id` server-side from the caller's session, never from a request body or path parameter (confused-deputy protection, matching Phase 4's precedent the design doc's Threat model section cites).
- `value_limit`/`count_limit` are required, non-nullable policy fields with **no system-wide default**, enforced at both the database (`NOT NULL`, no `server_default`) and HTTP (`422` if omitted) layers -- `APPROVAL-POLICY.md`'s resolved decision that a policy author must set both explicitly.

## Specification traceability

- Phase requirements: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-phase-5-automation-design.md` Decision 2 (workflow versioning), Decision 5/6 fields (`APPROVAL-POLICY.md`), Decision 7 (`triggers`' CHECK constraints)
- Contracts: `docs/phases/phase-005/DATA-MODEL.md`, `API-SCHEMAS.md`, `APPROVAL-POLICY.md`
- ADRs: n/a (no new technology; reuses Phase 4's already-established versioning-trigger idiom)

## Test evidence

66 new tests across three files (`test_automation_workflows_postgres.py`, `test_automation_policy_postgres.py`, `test_automation_triggers_postgres.py`). Covers, via direct SQL bypassing application code entirely: the immutability trigger rejecting a post-activation content edit, and the partial unique index rejecting a second `active` row. Also covers: cross-workspace isolation for workflows/policies/triggers (a resource from workspace A is `404`, never `403` or a visible-but-empty row, from workspace B -- `GET`, list, `publish`, `revoke` all independently verified); policy expiry/revocation state transitions; the `value_limit`/`count_limit` `NOT NULL` backstop at both the database and HTTP layers; the `triggers` table's two `CHECK` constraints.

Full regression (against live PostgreSQL): `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` clean, `mypy` clean (114 source files), migration cleanly reversible (`upgrade` → `downgrade -1` → `upgrade` verified), full suite **815 passed, 9 skipped, 1 failed** (`test_ranking_10000_eligible_entities_under_budget` -- the same pre-existing sandbox-load-sensitive flake documented throughout this project's audit history; unrelated to this change, confirmed by re-running it in isolation).

## Architecture impact

New backend package `backend/ecc/domains/automation/`, wired into `backend/ecc/main.py` alongside the existing Phase 1-4 routers. No change to any existing domain module.

## Security and privacy impact

Every read/write path is workspace-scoped server-side; no endpoint accepts a caller-supplied `workspace_id` override. `workflow_versions`' immutable-versioning trigger closes the same class of "silently mutate an already-referenced version" risk Phase 4's `prompt_versions` trigger closes. No secrets are handled by this task's scope (`secret_references` is a later task).

## Observability impact

Every mutation writes an `audit_events` row + `event_outbox` entry, matching every other domain's convention exactly.

## Breaking changes

None -- purely additive (new tables, new package, new routes).

## Rollback plan

`alembic downgrade -1` cleanly reverses the migration (verified). No existing table or route is touched.

## Checklist

- [x] Specification updated where behavior changed (contracts already Approved for Implementation from #57; this PR implements them as specified)
- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] Documentation updated (`docs/phases/phase-005/IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md` Task 1 evidence)
- [x] No secrets or sensitive data committed
- [x] Architecture boundaries preserved
- [ ] AI behavior is explainable and auditable where applicable (n/a -- no AI behavior in this task)
- [ ] State-changing AI actions require appropriate approval (n/a -- no run dispatch exists yet; this task is data layer only)

author: oliver-im
body:
## Why

The built-in `/code-review` sets `disable-model-invocation` — documented on Anthropic's Code Review page, deliberate, not a regression. jidoka shipped `unit_review: ["/code-review"]`, so a resuming agent could not reach it by **any** in-session route: the unit loop stalled at every unit with no signal that anything was wrong.

The fix is a config default, not schema work — the `mode: print|exec` axis already existed:

```jsonc
"unit_review": [
  { "run": "claude -p '/code-review {diff_range}' < /dev/null", "mode": "exec" }
]
```

`claude -p` puts the slash command in the **user-prompt slot at the CLI layer**, which the flag does not gate — the same Bash-not-SlashCommand boundary the shipped `codex exec` step already relied on. Verified empirically, not inferred: a run against a real range reviewed exactly the four files in that range and returned full findings on stdout.

## `{diff_range}` is load-bearing

`/code-review` **does not fail closed**. Given an empty or unresolvable target it reviews the most recent commit instead and returns confident, well-cited findings about unrelated code — so an unguarded gate can pass having reviewed the wrong diff, indistinguishably from a clean review. The resume protocol gained preconditions accordingly:

- resolvability via `git rev-parse --verify`, emptiness via `git rev-list --count` (**not** `git diff --quiet`, which reports a commit and its revert as empty)
- substitute a resolved **SHA**, never a ref name — the value lands inside single quotes with no escaping, and `feature/o'brien` and `a$(id)b` both pass `git check-ref-format`
- `{base}` is **stage-scoped**: the plan branch at unit stage, not `main`, which would widen every unit's review to Units 01..NN — the exact scope the unit gate exists to avoid

## Renderer fix (found by review, not caused by the default)

`renderGitWorkflowBlock` still emitted `git checkout main && git merge --no-ff plan/<id>` as part of a single close-out go-ahead — into **every** consumer's `progress.md`, instructing precisely the direct merge this repo's root `AGENTS.md` forbids. Tests pinned the string, so CI was protecting it. The block now stops at the archive commit and names no landing mechanism, since it renders into repos jidoka knows nothing about.

## One retraction

An earlier commit on this branch claimed `dist/cli.js` is a single-line minified ~1.4 MB bundle rebuilding as `1 file changed, 1 insertion`, and on that basis imposed a two-commit source-then-build ordering on every unit of every plan. Measured: **19,716 lines, 743 KB, not minified**; the `v0.4.5` release commit's dist diff is **one line**. Wrong on size, format, and diff behaviour — diagnosis and rule both withdrawn, recorded in the discussion doc rather than quietly dropped.

## Deliberately not done

- **No migration path.** Zod defaults fill only *absent* keys, so a config written by an earlier `jidoka:setup` keeps the old value. Author is the sole user; recorded in the discussion doc as the first thing that would owe users a warning if jidoka ever grows any.
- **Guardrails still don't ship.** They live in jidoka's own dogfooding doc, not the plugin. Tracked as `260725-2`, along with the `{base}` gap under `git_workflow: false`, overview-cell fencing, an unsubstituted-placeholder guard, and nine-site duplication.
- **Composer skill** (`260725-0`) — the real fix for everything a static string can't branch on.
- **`jidoka:setup` fidelity defects** (`260725-1`) — pre-existing, kept out so this stayed legible.

## Testing

217/217 vitest, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `dist/cli.js` rebuilt and verified in sync with source. Two independent review passes over the branch (one through the shipped `claude -p` form itself); findings addressed in `b24c094`.

author: lavan96
body:
### Motivation

- Close an authorization/integrity gap where the `generate-chart-analysis` Edge Function accepted caller-supplied `chartId` and `chartData` and used a service-role client to overwrite authoritative `charts` rows without object-level checks.
- Prevent low-privileged authenticated users from persisting AI-generated analysis onto charts/reports they do not own or are not permitted to edit.

### Description

- Require deny-by-default charts edit permission by calling `requireModulePermission(..., 'charts', 'can_edit')` in `supabase/functions/generate-chart-analysis/index.ts` and return HTTP 403 when unauthorized.
- Stop trusting caller-supplied analysis inputs by loading the target chart and its `dataset`/`chart_config` and the linked `generated_reports` row server-side, then build the LLM prompt from that stored data instead of request body `chartData`/`reportContext`.
- Fail explicitly on missing chart or DB errors by returning HTTP 404 for not-found and throwing on persistence failures, and check the `update` result (`updateError`) after writing the authoritative `charts` row.
- Protect the generic service-role path `supabase/functions/manage-templates` by enforcing charts-module permissions for operations against `charts` and `chart_analysis` via `requireModulePermission` and `permForAction` so service-route updates are gated server-side.
- Prevent client-side automatic backfill from attempting writes for users without edit permission by gating the backfill in `src/pages/Charts.tsx` with `canEditCharts` and adding it to the hook dependency list.

### Testing

- `git diff --check` — passed with no whitespace or diff-check errors.
- Targeted Python assertions (quick source checks) — passed and validated presence of the authorization gate, server-bound chart data usage, `manage-templates` protection, and client-side edit gating.
- `node scripts/security/check-function-registry.mjs` — passed (registry integrity OK).
- `node scripts/security/scan-auth-patterns.mjs` — passed (static auth pattern scan OK).
- `node scripts/security/check-edge-functions.mjs` — partially run: static checks completed but the Deno-backed runtime portion could not run because `deno` is not installed in the environment.
- `npm ci` / ESLint (dependency-backed linting) — could not complete because dependency installation failed due to remote registry access returning HTTP 403, so full lint/test runs requiring npm packages were not executed.

All changes are limited to server-side authorization and minimal client gating to remediate the integrity issue while preserving existing functionality and behavior when callers are authorized.

author: jumbo13th
body:
## Problem

Slotting JSON reaches the admin panel through the clipboard, and that is where the Arma lobby export loses its encoding. The mod hands the OS raw UTF-8 bytes as single-byte text, so Cyrillic role names arrive re-read as Windows-1252:

```
"role": "ÐšÐ¾Ð¼Ð°Ð½Ð´Ð¸Ñ€ Ð²Ð·Ð²Ð¾Ð´Ð°"     // should be "Командир взвода"
```

The mod's own workaround for that ships role names as `\uXXXX` escapes — correct data, but unreadable in the textarea:

```
"role": "Командир взвода"
```

## Change

Handle both at the single point the text enters the app — `onPaste` on the slotting JSON textarea.

New `src/features/games/domain/slottingText.ts`:

- **`repairWindows1252Mojibake()`** maps each character back to its CP1252 byte and re-decodes as strict UTF-8. It returns `null` — leaving the text untouched — for anything that is not that specific damage: text holding characters CP1252 cannot express (real Cyrillic, CJK, emoji) or a byte stream that is not valid UTF-8. That conservative bail is what makes it safe to run over every paste.
- **`normalizeSlottingJsonText()`** repairs, then re-serializes valid JSON so escapes render as the characters they stand for. A partial or hand-edited paste that is not valid JSON on its own is kept verbatim, with only the encoding repair applied.

Paste anything — escaped, mangled, or already clean — and the field shows the same text the mission page will render. Typing and hand-edits are untouched; nothing runs on `onChange`.

## Testing

- 10 new unit tests in `tests/features/games/domain/slottingText.unit.test.ts`, using mojibake strings captured from a real `/slotexport` paste rather than generated ones (Node's `TextDecoder('windows-1252')` decodes the `0x80`–`0x9F` block as latin-1, so it does not reproduce what Windows actually puts on the clipboard). Both flavours of the damage are covered.
- Full suite: 421 tests / 62 files passing.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` 0 errors on the touched files.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Improved slotting JSON paste handling in the admin game editor.
  * Automatically repairs common Windows-1252 encoding issues from clipboard content.
  * Reformats valid slotting JSON with consistent indentation while preserving partial or invalid text.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Prevents pasted Cyrillic and other special characters from appearing corrupted.
  * Preserves only the selected text range when normalized content is pasted.

author: notsajeed
body:
---

## Problem

The "Quantum Algorithms" example in the Quick Start section of README.md uses:

```python
grover = GroverSearch(num_qubits=3, oracle_type="custom")
```

Running this exact snippet raises:

```
TypeError: GroverSearch.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'oracle_type'
```

## Root Cause

`GroverSearch`'s actual constructor signature is:

```python
GroverSearch(num_qubits: int, target: str | None = None)
```

`oracle_type` is a valid parameter elsewhere in the SDK — but only on `DeutschJozsa` (see `qpiai_quantum/algorithms/deutsch_jozsa.py`), which supports multiple named oracle variants (`"constant_zero"`, `"constant_one"`, `"balanced"`) and branches on that string internally.

`GroverSearch` does have an oracle (`_oracle()`), but it's a single, fixed construction driven by the `target` bitstring — there's no selectable "type" for it to branch on. It looks like the Grover's search example was likely adapted from the Deutsch-Jozsa example and the parameter name was never updated to match `GroverSearch`'s real API.

## Fix

Updated the example to use the real `target` parameter, and added a `build_circuit()` call so the snippet demonstrates actual working usage:

```python
grover = GroverSearch(num_qubits=3, target="101")
circuit = grover.build_circuit()
```

## Testing

Verified the corrected snippet runs without error:

```python
from qpiai_quantum import GroverSearch

grover = GroverSearch(num_qubits=3, target="101")
circuit = grover.build_circuit()
```

12. `28b1132` — **화면을 받은 시안대로 다시 칠하고, 남은 옛 위젯(ttk)을 걷어내기**

현재 상태: 명령 **84개**, 시험 **448개**.

## 1. 기관 한정 기능 제거 → 사용자 양식 구조

기관 전용 함수·탭을 전부 삭제하고, 양식 폴더에 회사 `.hwp`/`.hwpx` 를 넣으면 UI 에 자동 등록되는 구조로 대체했습니다.
- 개인 양식 `%USERPROFILE%\.hwpkit\forms`, 공용 양식은 환경변수 `HWPKIT_FORMS`
- 누름틀(필드) 또는 `{{항목}}` 자리표시자를 `양식 채우기`·`메일머지`가 자동으로 채움

## 2. 중복 통합 — 하나의 파이프라인

`마크업 텍스트 → 요소 트리 → 렌더러 → 한/글 문서`

| 원본 | 통합 결과 |
|---|---|
| 대·소·중제목 함수 30여 개 | 마크업 `제목:` `소제목:` `중제목:` + `presets/styles.json` |
| 네모·원·바·점선/꺽쇠/서론/요지박스 20여 개 | `네모:` `원:` `바:` `참고:` `강조:` |
| 기본·심플·3단·5단·퍼센트표 등 40여 개 | `표 만들기(열·행·스타일)` + `presets/table_styles.json` |
| 정책·상황·검토·회의·행사·동향 보고 틀 16종 | `presets/report_templates.json` 표준 유형 12종 |
| 폰트×크기 버튼 100여 개 | `글자모양()` / `문단모양()` + 스타일 프리셋 |
| 문자 탭 버튼 49개 | `presets/symbols.json` |

## 3. 화면 — 사이드 패널 + 타일 격자

한/글 문서를 보면서 쓰는 프로그램인데 창이 화면 한가운데를 차지하고, 기능은 목록으로만 찾을 수 있었습니다.

**사이드 패널** — 화면 **왼쪽·오른쪽** 중 한 곳에 붙여 놓고 문서를 옆에 두고 씁니다. 고른 자리·패널 두께·타일 크기·항상 위·투명도는 `%USERPROFILE%\.hwpkit\ui.json` 에 남겨 다음에 켤 때 그대로 씁니다.

**타일 격자** — 주요 기능을 둥근 흰 카드로 늘어놓습니다. 분류 8개(블록 편집 / 표 / 서식 / 문서 / 보고서 만들기 / 양식·메일머지 / 일괄 처리 / 도구)마다 아이콘과 색이 달라 목록을 읽지 않고 눈으로 찾습니다. 칸 수는 패널 폭에 맞춰 저절로 바뀌고, `칸` 단추로 타일 크기를 세 단계로 바꿉니다. 검색칸·분류 칩으로 즉시 거릅니다.

**세부설정 판** — 타일을 누르면 격자를 치우지 않고 **아래쪽 빈자리에** 판이 열립니다(아래 10번). 입력칸은 명령 정의(`입력항목`)로부터 자동 생성되어, 기능마다 창을 손으로 만들 필요가 없습니다.

**투명도 · 항상 위** — 투명도는 도구줄 미끄럼자로 40~100% 사이에서 조절합니다. `항상 위`를 켜면 한/글을 눌러도 패널이 뒤로 숨지 않습니다.

배치하며 부딪친 것들:
- **분류 칩은 `grid` 가 아니라 `place` 로** 놓습니다. `grid` 는 열 너비를 줄끼리 나눠 쓰기 때문에, 아랫줄의 긴 칩(`양식·메일머지`)이 윗줄 열까지 넓혀 칩이 잘렸습니다.
- **스크롤 캔버스의 기본 크기(265px)** 가 grid 에서 자리를 먼저 차지해, 몫(weight)을 줘도 결과칸이 밀렸습니다. 작게 요청하고 남는 자리를 weight 로 받습니다.
- **작업 스레드에서 `after()` 로 tkinter 를 직접 건드리던 부분**을, 주 스레드가 큐를 꺼내 화면에 쓰는 방식으로 바꿨습니다. tkinter 는 다른 스레드에서 건드리면 안 됩니다.
- 타일 제목이 세 줄로 넘쳐 `선택 필요` 딱지를 가리던 문제. tkinter 가 **띄어쓰기 자리에서** 접는다는 것을 셈에 넣어야 합니다(`layout.제목자르기`).
- 창 크기를 바꾼 직후 닫으면 **엉뚱한 두께가 저장되던** 문제. 재기 전에 `update_idletasks()` 를 부릅니다.
- 상·하(가로) 자리도 한때 넣었다가 **없앴습니다**(`ed39b2f`). 눕히면 높이가 300px 남짓이라 타일이 두 줄뿐이었습니다.

## 4. 원본 결함 수정

- 셀 블록 인식이 **드래그 방향과 무관**해짐 (원본은 ↘ 방향만 정상 동작)
- 셀 주소를 A~Z 한 글자로만 계산하던 문제 → **AA열 이후** 처리
- 표 대량계산이 병합 셀에서 엉뚱한 칸을 쓰던 문제 수정
- 표 너비를 함수마다 다른 상수(205·196·161…)로 박아 둔 것 → 실제 본문 너비 계산
- `한글금액` 만/억 단위 오류 수정, 블록 계산기를 안전한 파서로 재작성(`eval` 미사용)
- 작업 실패 시 자동 되돌리기, 보안 모듈 등록으로 파일 접근 확인 창 제거

## 5. 새 기능

- **개인정보 검사·가리기**: 주민번호·연락처·계좌·카드·이메일·차량·여권번호 탐지 후 `900101-1******` 형태로 가림
- **공문(기안문) 만들기**(`4a14638`): 아래 12번 참조
- **공문서 규정 검사기**: 날짜·시간·금액 표기, 항목기호 단계, 붙임·끝 표시, 용지·여백 점검. **문서 종류(공문/보고서)를 갈라 봅니다**(아래 12번)
- **자동 목차**: 문서의 제목(□ ○ ㅇ 1. 가.)을 읽어 목차 표 생성
- **작업 묶음(매크로)**: 명령 순서를 저장해 일괄 실행
- **사진 대장**: 폴더 사진을 격자 표에 배치하고 캡션 채움
- **표 계산 확장**: 열별 합계·소계 행, 증감·증감률 열, 단위 환산(원↔천원↔백만원)
- **표 ↔ 엑셀**: 표를 CSV/XLSX 로 내보내고 CSV/XLSX 를 표로 가져오기 (엑셀 설치 불필요)
- **표 줄 세우기**(`ed39b2f`): 고른 셀 범위를 열 하나 기준으로 정렬. 머리글 행은 자리에 두고 셀 값만 바꿔 넣어 표 모양(테두리·배경·병합)은 남음
- **회사 양식 기준 서식 정리**(`aec7c9a`): 아래 9번 참조
- **폴더 일괄 처리**: 찾아바꾸기·서식 정리·PDF 변환 (미리보기 지원)
- **메일머지 개선**: CSV/XLSX 직접 읽기, 항목 개수 제한 없음, 파일 이름 서식
- **CLI**: `python -m hwpkit 실행 …` 으로 예약·자동 실행 (영문 별칭 `list`/`run`/`check`)
- **연결 진단**: 자동화 등록·실행 중인 한/글(ROT)·연결 시도·명령을 받을 상태인지를 차례로 점검
- **화면이 멈추지 않음**(`ecc9660`): 한/글 COM 은 모두 작업 스레드에서 부릅니다 (아래 13번)

## 6. exe 빌드와 보안 경고 대응

`build_win.bat` 한 번으로 `dist\한글문서도우미.exe`(한 파일), **`build_win_folder.bat` 으로는 폴더 형태**가 만들어집니다(가상환경 → 의존성 → 시험 → 빌드, 시험 실패 시 중단). 윈도우 PC 가 없으면 `build_wine.sh`(폴더 형태는 `HWPKIT_ONEDIR=1`)로 리눅스에서도 만들 수 있습니다.

경고를 줄이는 설정은 빌드에 반영했습니다 — UPX 끔(오탐 최대 원인), 아이콘·제조사·버전 정보 심기, `asInvoker`(권한 상승 창 없음), 미사용 대형 패키지 제외. 경고를 **없애는** 것은 코드 서명뿐이므로 `sign_win.bat`(SHA256 + RFC3161 시간 도장 + 검증 + 해시 출력)을 넣고, 인증서가 없을 때의 사내 배포 방법을 `배포안내.md` 에 정리했습니다.

## 7. 늦은 바인딩으로 옮기며 생긴 일 (`1752e87` → `ed39b2f`)

**(1) exe 에서 한/글에 붙지 못한 문제** — 원인은 win32com 캐시였습니다. `gencache.EnsureDispatch` 는 래퍼 모듈을 `site-packages/win32com/gen_py` 에 써야 하는데, exe 로 묶으면 그 경로가 읽기 전용이라 실패합니다(원본 exe 는 PyInstaller 의 `pyi_rth_win32comgenpy` 훅으로 넘어갔지만 PyInstaller 6.x 에는 그 훅이 없습니다). `Dispatch`(늦은 바인딩)로 바꾸고, 스레드별 COM 초기화(`threading.local` + `CoInitialize`)를 넣었습니다.

**(2) 그 대가로 생긴 `매개 변수의 개수가 잘못되었습니다`(-2147352562)** — 늦은 바인딩에서는 **생략 가능 인수를 파이썬이 채워 주지 않습니다.**

| 고친 곳 | 전 | 후 |
|---|---|---|
| 문서 처음/끝 이동 | `MovePos(코드)` | `MovePos(코드, 0, 0)` |
| 본문 읽기 | `InitScan(옵션, 범위)` | `InitScan(…, 0, 0, -1, -1)` |
| 사진 넣기 | `InsertPicture(…6개)` | `…8개` (너비·높이까지) |

다시 나지 않도록 두 겹으로 막았습니다 — 시험용 가짜 한/글의 인수 개수를 실제 API 와 똑같이 조이고(기본값·`*인자` 금지), 소스를 훑어 인수 부족 호출이 없는지 보는 시험을 넣었습니다.

**(3) 오류 메시지 한국말로** — 오류 번호를 풀어 무엇을 해야 할지 알려 줍니다. 화면과 CLI 가 같은 풀이를 씁니다.

## 8. 빌드 세트를 실제로 돌려 보고 고친 것 (`bfe3014`)

1. **`hwpkit.spec` 이 저장소에 없었습니다.** `.gitignore` 의 `*.spec` 규칙에 걸려 커밋되지 않아, 내려받은 사람은 빌드를 할 수 없었습니다. 규칙을 `/build/*.spec` 으로 좁히고 spec 을 커밋했습니다.
2. **`build_wine.sh` 가 첫 줄에서 죽었습니다.** 변수 이름을 한글로 썼는데, bash 는 한글 이름을 변수로 보지 않고 명령으로 실행하려 듭니다. 이름을 영문으로 바꿨습니다.
3. **Wine 에서 PyInstaller 가 표준 출력 초기화에 실패했습니다.** 로그를 파일로 바로 받으면 Wine 의 파이썬이 `init_sys_streams ... (WinError 6)` 로 죽습니다. 출력을 파이프로 넘기게 고쳤습니다.

같은 일이 다시 없도록 시험을 더 두었습니다 — 빌드 파일·프리셋이 정말 커밋됐는지(`git ls-files`), `bash -n` 통과와 ASCII 변수 이름, 문서에 적힌 시험 개수가 실제와 같은지.

## 9. 회사 보고서 양식 기준으로 `문서 서식 한 번에 정리` 재작성 (`aec7c9a`)

받은 회사 양식 파일 두 개(「보고서 작성 기본 편집요건」 15pt·14pt)에서 편집용지·문단모양·글자모양 값을 읽어 왔습니다. HWP 5.x 는 OLE 복합 파일이라 `DocInfo`/`BodyText/Section0` 를 raw deflate 로 풀고 레코드(`FACE_NAME`·`CHAR_SHAPE`·`PARA_SHAPE`·`PAGE_DEF`)를 훑었습니다.

**무엇이 문제였나** — 이 기능은 서식을 **지우는** 일만 했습니다. 지우면 한/글 기본값(함초롬바탕 10pt)이 되는데 양식은 신명조 15pt·줄간격 160%·여백 12.7/20mm 라서, 정리를 하고 나면 오히려 양식과 더 멀어졌습니다. 그래서 지운 뒤 양식 기준을 **입히도록** 바꿨습니다.

`presets/doc_standards.json` 에 담은 기준:

| 항목 | 값 |
|---|---|
| 용지·여백 | A4, 위·아래 12.7 / 좌·우 20 / 머리말·꼬리말 12.7mm |
| 본문 | 한양신명조 15pt, 줄간격 160%, 양쪽 정렬, 장평 100 / 자간 0 |
| 제목 | HY헤드라인M 22pt 가운데 |
| 수준별 | `□` 15pt 진하게(문단위 10pt) → `ㅇ` 8pt → `-` 5pt → `*` 중고딕 13pt 2pt |

적용하면서 조심한 것들(`features/doc_format.py`):
- **문단 번호로 뛰어다니지 않습니다.** 커서를 실제로 옮기며(`MoveNextParaBegin`) 자리가 더 움직이지 않을 때 끝난 것으로 봅니다.
- **표 안 문단은 건드리지 않습니다.**
- **본문 문단의 굵기는 손대지 않습니다.** 문장 안 강조를 정리가 지우면 안 됩니다.
- **글머리 기호 통일** — `○ ◦ ●` 를 한글 `ㅇ` 로. 기호 뒤 공백까지 묶어 찾으므로 `○○○팀` 은 바뀌지 않습니다.
- `2023. 9. 7.(목)` 같은 **날짜를 `1. 소제목` 으로 잘못 보지 않게** 걸러 냅니다.

곁들여: **자동 목차가 원 기호(`○`)만 보고 한글 `ㅇ` 를 빠뜨렸습니다.**

**남겨 둔 판단** — 글머리 수준의 **가로 들여쓰기는 건드리지 않았습니다.** 양식이 들여쓰기를 글머리 앞 공백으로 표현하고 있어, 왼쪽여백까지 밀면 이중이 됩니다.

## 10. 타일을 눌러도 격자를 두고, 아래쪽에 세부설정 판 (`07fe484`)

타일을 누르면 실행판이 격자 위에 겹쳐 올라와(`tkraise`) **격자가 사라졌습니다.** 이제 격자는 그대로 두고 아래쪽 빈자리에 판이 열립니다.

- 판 높이는 필요한 만큼(최대 70%), 격자는 남은 자리 — `layout.세부판높이` · `layout.격자칸높이`
- 고른 타일에 **파란 테**. 다른 타일을 그냥 누르면 판 내용이 바뀝니다.
- `← 목록` 을 `✕ 닫기` 로. 나가는 곳이 아니라 접는 곳입니다.
- 켬/끔 항목을 이름과 한 줄에 놓고 여백을 줄였습니다. 남는 자리는 결과칸보다 **입력칸에 먼저** 줍니다.

**남은 한 가지** — 입력이 많은 기능(여러줄 입력, `공문 만들기` 처럼 칸이 열 개가 넘는 것)은 판이 70% 상한에 걸려 입력칸을 스크롤해야 합니다.

## 11. 시안대로 다시 칠하고, 남은 옛 위젯을 걷어내기 (`28b1132`)

**배색**(`ui/theme.py`) — 살짝 파란 바탕(`#F4F6FC`) + 흰 카드, 주 색은 진한 남색빛 파랑(`#1F3FBF`) 하나. 입력칸은 테두리 대신 **옅은 파랑으로 채웁니다**.

**깊이** — tkinter 에는 투명도도 흐리기도 없어, 옅은 색 둥근네모를 몇 겹 겹쳐 그림자를 만들었습니

author: salonikashyap7899
body:
## Follow-up to #2–#4

After #4 the Vercel **build** succeeded, but hitting the deployed API returned:

```
500: INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR — FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED
```

### Root cause (from the runtime logs)

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module
  '/var/task/artifacts/api-server/node_modules/@workspace/api-zod/src/index.ts'
  imported from /var/task/artifacts/api-server/src/routes/health.js
```

`@vercel/node` transpiles the function's **own** files per-file (it does not bundle) and traces `node_modules` as-is. The workspace package `@workspace/api-zod` declares its export as **raw TypeScript** (`./src/index.ts`) — great for bundler consumers (Vite/esbuild), but Node cannot load a `.ts` file at runtime, so the function crashed on cold start.

`health.ts` was the **only** runtime importer of `@workspace/api-zod` (`@workspace/db` is declared but never imported), and it used it solely for the trivial generated schema `z.object({ status: z.string() })`.

### Fix

- Define that schema inline in `health.ts` using `zod` directly (zod ships compiled JS and loads fine at runtime).
- Add `zod` as a direct dependency of `@workspace/api-server` (it was previously only transitive via `@workspace/api-zod`).

No workspace package is imported anywhere in the function's runtime graph now, so the serverless function starts cleanly.

### Verification (local)

- No `@workspace/*` imports remain in `artifacts/api-server/src` ✅
- `zod` resolves to compiled JS (`zod/index.cjs`), and `z.object({status:z.string()}).parse({status:"ok"})` works ✅
- api-server `typecheck` and `build.mjs` both pass ✅

### Note

This makes the API run. The project is still rooted at `artifacts/api-server` (API only); to serve the full app (frontend + API) on one domain, change the Vercel project's **Root Directory** to the repo root (`./`) as described in `VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT.md`.

author: arathi-hlab
body:
## Summary

Three small, independent hardening fixes for the Intel XPU CI paths, all motivated by real failures observed in recent runs.

- **`nightly-test-intel.yml`** — wrap `hf auth login` in a 5-attempt retry with linear backoff + jitter. The 1/2/4-GPU matrix jobs run on the same runner and each call `hf auth login`, which hits HF's aggressively rate-limited `/whoami-v2` endpoint. When they fire in the same second under a scheduled run, HF returns 429 and the job fails before any test runs. Example failure: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30112109055/job/89543980819
- **`pr-test-xpu.yml`** — `git fetch origin '+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*' --force` inside the CI container before the sglang pip install, in both stage-a and stage-b jobs. `actions/checkout` doesn't fetch tags by default, so `setuptools_scm` couldn't resolve a real version at install time and fell back to `0.0.0`.
- **`release-docker-intel-xpu-nightly.yml`** — retry `docker push intel/sglang-dev:...` up to 5 times with linear backoff so a transient Docker Hub error doesn't fail the nightly publish. Mirrors the pattern used in `sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger `nightly-test-intel` manually via `workflow_dispatch` and confirm all three matrix jobs pass HF login even when they start concurrently.
- [ ] Open a PR touching a `python/sglang/**` file and confirm `pr-test-xpu.yml` installs sglang with a non-`0.0.0` version (visible in `pip show sglang` output during the Install step).
- [ ] Trigger `release-docker-intel-xpu-nightly` manually and confirm the push retries a transient failure instead of aborting.

author: adokav
body:
## Scope

This is the destructive cleanup requested for Signal Bot. It replaces the 15k-line multi-purpose agent with a 255-line production entry point that has exactly two responsibilities:

1. MEXC Liquid-100 Long Top 3
2. Verified MEXC New Listing explosion radar

## Removed from production

author: michaelbucolo
body:
Both found while researching Meshi-as-the-user and onboarding. Both verified by reading the code, not inferred.

---

## 1. Finishing onboarding removed you from discovery

```
showInDiscovery: bool("showInDiscovery", true) && meshVisibility !== "private"
```

`meshVisibility` defaults to `"private"` — in the schema (`schema.prisma:1000`) **and** in this function's own fallback three lines up (`actions.ts:787`). So for every account that took the default, this evaluated `true && false` and wrote `showInDiscovery: false`.

**Completing onboarding made you undiscoverable.** On a social product, where the first problem a new account has is that it knows nobody, that is close to the worst possible default — and it makes the empty-mesh cold start partly self-inflicted.

The onboarding client already carries a comment describing this exact symptom as fixed (`onboarding-flow.tsx:142`):

> *Findable and alive by default — these two silently defaulting the other way meant every account that finished onboarding vanished from discovery AND from live presence (nobody could ever see anyone's Meshi).*

It **was** fixed on the client, which sends `showInDiscovery: true`. It was then undone here by a server-side clause nobody connected to it.

`getDiscoverUsers` states the intended rule outright (`queries.ts:1213`):

> *Discoverable != public. A private account can still opt in to being **found** (and then approve followers), so discovery only requires `showInDiscovery` — content visibility stays governed by `isPublic` elsewhere.*

So the conflation is removed. Content visibility is still governed by `isPublic` and the per-post checks — it was never this switch's job. Anyone who wants to be unfindable turns the switch off, which now does what it says.

---

## 2. Meshi did not exist on phones

```
className="meshi-float-shell fixed z-40 hidden md:block"
```

Below 768px the one Meshi in the product was not hidden — it was never laid out at all. On a product shipping an iOS WebView, most people had never seen Meshi outside the mesh canvas. A mascot that is meant to be the branding, the mascot, the guide and the main event cannot be a desktop feature.

Two viewport gates went with it:

| gate | why it was wrong |
|---|---|
| `event.pointerType !== "mouse" \|\| window.innerWidth < 900` | pointer **type** is the correct test for "has a mouse"; the width floor additionally excluded every small laptop |
| `!canFollow() \|\| window.innerWidth < 768` | excluded phones from the one Meshi behaviour reachable by keyboard |

**Verified in a production build**, two viewports × three routes:

```
desktop  /feed       present, visible, (752, 482)
desktop  /messages   present, visible, (752, 482)
phone    /feed       present, visible, (171, 398)   <- previously did not exist
phone    /messages   present, visible, (171, 468)   <- previously did not exist
```

`getViewportBounds()` already reserves 80px at the bottom on mobile, so Meshi docks clear of the bottom nav.

---

## Deliberately not bodged here

Entering `/mesh` still unmounts the floating Meshi so the canvas can draw it. That keeps the singleton invariant honest, but it means Meshi pops out of existence at the route boundary — the opposite of fluid. Fluid means *handing off*, not unmounting, and that needs the canvas to accept a handoff position. It belongs with the rest of the Meshi work, not as a one-line patch.

## Verification

`tsc` · `eslint --max-warnings=0` · `knip` · `schema:check` · `privacy:check` · `contrast:check` · `type:check` · `consent:check` · `mesh:layout-check` · `mesh:seen-contract` · `reconciliation:check` · clean production build — all green.

author: bookasloth
body:
Second slice of the "feed people crave" program (idea #1 thread spine + #8 version tags). Turns islands of PR-notes into readable arcs and a feed-native changelog.

## How it works
Two opt-in PR-body lines, parsed exactly like the existing `Tweet:` line:
```
Thread: sign-in-wall
Version: v3.7
```
- `Thread:` groups notes into one feature arc → a chip **Part of: Sign-in wall** on the note → a story page `/community/thread/{key}` (the arc, oldest → newest).
- `Version:` tags the release → a chip **shipped in v3.7** → `/community/release/{version}` (release notes, newest first).
- No line → standalone note (most PRs).

## Design pivot from the spec
The spec proposed threading `p_thread`/`p_version` **filter params** through the `community_feed` RPC. Reading that RPC (viewer filters, controversial sort, seeded-shuffle Hot, reblog resolution) it's the fragile piece with a documented PostgREST exact-keyset gotcha. Instead:
- `community_feed`/`community_post` gain thread/version as **additive final return columns** — the exact drop-then-create pattern the `avatar_url` migration used. Params + grant signatures **unchanged**, so resolution and every caller are untouched.
- Thread/release pages are **lightweight public story lists** (a simple indexed select of tagged notes, each linking to its permalink) — no risky new filter params on the main feed, no duplicated hydration.

Same UX, far lower blast radius on the feed everything depends on.

## What's here
- Migration `20260726000001` (columns + partial indexes) + `20260726000002` (feed/post RPCs return thread/version).
- `extractThread`/`extractVersion` helpers (8 unit tests), wired through the GitHub webhook → `autoPost`.
- `NoteBadges` chips on note cards; `FeedPost` + row-map carry the fields.
- `/community/thread/[key]` + `/community/release/[version]` story pages.

## Before merge — ordering matters
1. Run `20260726000001` **and** `20260726000002` in Supabase first. If the columns don't exist when this merges, the auto-post insert (which now writes thread/version) fails silently on this very PR.
2. Then run the **backfill** SQL (handed separately) to tag the real sagas.

tsc + `next build` clean. Spec + plan in `docs/superpowers/`.

Tweet: Your notes here used to be islands — forty disconnected "shipped it"s. Now a note can say "part of: sign-in wall" and pull the whole arc: the idea, the bug where it parked on the reply button, the fix. Gave the feed a spine so the work reads like the story it actually was.

author: beinan
body:
Second step of #285. Adds `talon_worker::uring_serve` — the thread-per-core runtime the data plane will run on — plus the `data_plane_rings` knob that selects it. **The Tokio path stays the default and is untouched**; nothing calls this module yet, so it lands and is verified in isolation.

## The model

monoio has no work-stealing scheduler. It scales by running N independent single-threaded runtimes that share nothing:

```rust
for ring_id in 0..rings {
    thread::spawn(move || {
        monoio::utils::bind_to_cpu_set(vec![ring_id]);           // pin to a core
        let pool = DefaultThreadPool::new(blocking_threads);      // sendfile stays off-ring
        RuntimeBuilder::<IoUringDriver>::new()
            .attach_thread_pool(Box::new(pool))
            .build()?
            .block_on(async {
                // SO_REUSEPORT is default-true: every ring binds the same addr
                let l = TcpListener::bind_with_config(&addr, &ListenerConfig::default())?;
                loop { monoio::spawn(handler.handle(l.accept().await?.0)); }
            });
    });
}
```

The kernel distributes accepts by 4-tuple hash — no shared accept queue, no thundering herd. Measured at **8.05× scaling on 8 rings**, per-core throughput flat from 1 to 16 (#273).

The per-ring blocking pool is **not optional**: `sendfile`/`splice` are blocking syscalls that must never run on a ring, or one slow client stalls every connection that ring owns. monoio also panics outright if `spawn_blocking` is called without a pool attached.

## What is deliberately *not* sharded

Shared worker state stays shared, because #273 measured the alternative and it loses twice:

- **Cross-ring forwarding: −30 to −67% throughput.** Connections are distributed by TCP 4-tuple; blocks key on `block_id`. The two hashes are independent, so only ~1/N of requests land on the owning ring — 75–87% forwarding at 8 shards.
- **Per-shard eviction budgets waste capacity: up to −5.1pt hit rate.** 256 MiB blocks over 64 GiB leave only ~256 slots (32/shard at 8 rings), far too few for hash uniformity, so some shards evict while others sit below capacity.

So each ring holds an `Arc` of the same `WorkerRuntime`. That is sound: **`!Send` constrains futures crossing threads, not shared state read from within a ring.** The `RingHandler` trait encodes this — its future is deliberately not `Send`.

## Failure semantics

A **bind failure on any ring is fatal**, not degraded-but-running: a worker silently serving on fewer rings than configured would be an invisible capacity loss. A **pinning failure only warns** — pinning is an optimization, not a correctness requirement.

## Configuration

| | |
|---|---|
| `--data-plane-rings <N>` / `TALON_WORKER_DATA_PLANE_RINGS` | |
| unset (default) | portable Tokio data plane |
| `0` | one ring per available core |
| `N` | exactly N rings |

Wired through all six config layers (struct, default, patch, merge, env parse, schema) and the reference docs regenerated.

## Tests

- `resolve_ring_count` — explicit values honoured; `0` resolves to core count
- `rings_share_a_port_and_serve_traffic` — 4 rings, 40 real TCP roundtrips, asserts **more than one thread served**. This is the test that matters: it proves `SO_REUSEPORT` is actually distributing accepts rather than one ring taking everything.
- `handler_state_is_shared_across_rings` — a counter behind an `Arc` sees increments from whichever ring served, proving shared state is genuinely shared rather than per-ring copies

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` — 28 suites pass
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features` — clean
- config reference regenerated and drift-checked against the schema

## Next in #285

Port `handle_conn` / `handle_put` / `handle_delete` to this runtime, where `sendfile_payload` *simplifies* — the `into_std` → `set_nonblocking` → `from_std` round-trip disappears.

Refs #285, #273

## Summary

Fixes three issues in the payment flow:

### Issue 1 — Merchant name hardcoded
- Renamed the merchant display element to `id="merchant-display"` in `pay.html`.
- Merchant name is now read from the `?merchant=` URL query parameter with fallback `'Valmont-Pay'`:
  ```js
  const urlParams = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
  const merchantName = urlParams.get('merchant') || 'Valmont-Pay';
  document.getElementById('merchant-display').textContent = merchantName;
  ```
- Page title also reflects the active merchant (`Pay <merchant> — Valmont-Pay`).

### Issue 2 — "Proceed to Checkout" button was dead on first load
- The button had `disabled = true` set on load (when `currentAmount === 0`), which silently swallowed the inline `onclick` handler. Users clicking it saw no feedback at all.
- Removed the `disabled` property toggle. Visual opacity / `cursor-not-allowed` classes still hint at "no amount yet", but the button stays clickable so existing validation alerts ("Please select or enter an amount", email validation) always fire.
- Clearing the custom-amount input now resets `currentAmount` and the displayed amount back to `GH₵ 0.00` (previously left stale state).

### Issue 3 — Post-payment redirect ignored merchant callback_url; dashboard generator dropped merchant name
- `server.js` `/api/v1/transaction/initialize` now returns `callback_url` in its response data.
- `pay.html` forwards `callback_url` (along with `merchant`, `amount`, `email`) onto the checkout URL, and parses the absolute checkout URL returned by the API correctly instead of forcing `window.location.origin` (fixes local-dev vs Vercel redirects).
- `checkout.html` reads the `callback_url` param, and the success-screen "Close Checkout" button redirects to it, appending `?reference=VP-xxx&status=success` so merchants can verify the transaction.
- `dashboard.html` Quick Launch generator got a new "Merchant Name" field (default `Valmont Gadgets Ghana`) that is sent to the initialize endpoint, so dashboard-generated links render the correct merchant end-to-end instead of always falling back to `Valmont-Pay`.

## Test plan
- Visit `pay.html?merchant=Valmont+Gadgets+Ghana&amount=250` -> merchant display updates, amount pre-fills, button shows "Pay GH₵ 250".
- Visit bare `pay.html` -> clicking Proceed to Checkout now fires validation alerts instead of doing nothing.
- Generate a link from the dashboard with a custom merchant name; complete checkout -> Close Checkout lands on the callback URL with `reference` and `status` query params attached.

## Files changed
`pay.html`, `checkout.html`, `dashboard.html`, `server.js`

author: errooooor
body:
## Summary

Minecraft gameplay traffic is defined as one ordered byte stream, while RakNet order channels are
independently ordered. This draft refactors multichannel delivery around explicit causal safety
instead of assuming packet classes are independent.

## Implemented stages

### 1. Strict causal baseline

- Default unknown, modded, entity, world, container and custom-payload traffic to reliable ordered
  channel 7.
- Preserve bundle delimiters.
- Keep the original optimistic split behind
  `-Draknetify.multichannelProfile=aggressive`.
- Distinguish explicit channel 0 from an unmatched classifier.

### 2. Negotiated atomic bundles

- Negotiate versioned application capabilities on a reliable ordered Raknetify control frame.
- Encode a complete Minecraft bundle as one bounded envelope and reconstruct it synchronously.
- Limit envelopes to 4096 packets / 64 MiB and aggregate all original write promises.
- Keep old peers on the strict fallback when they do not advertise support.

### 3. Lossless fences and gameplay epochs

- Replace queue deletion, receive-index rewriting and false promise completion with an eight-channel
  drain marker and acknowledgement protocol.
- Queue later writes with their original promises until every channel reaches the fence.
- Frame gameplay messages with a negotiated epoch; hold future-epoch messages and reject stale
  messages after a transition.

### 4. Dependency domains and fair scheduling

- Classify traffic as `STRICT_WORLD`, `INDEPENDENT_CONTROL`, `EPHEMERAL_EFFECT` or
  `GUARDED_BULK`.
- Reopen only independent control (reliable ordered channel 1) and sound/particle/vibration effects
  (reliable ordered channel 4), and only after atomic bundle, lossless fence and epoch capabilities
  are all negotiated.
- Keep every custom payload and unknown packet strict, including payload formats that cannot be
  parsed by the current version.
- Identify Fabric chunk/light/biome bodies as guarded bulk, but keep them in the same FIFO and
  channel 7 as strict state until an explicit chunk-commit dependency exists.
- Schedule independent queues using work-conserving deficit round robin with a 4:2:1 byte quantum,
  preserving FIFO inside each queue and preserving one shared FIFO for strict state and guarded
  bulk.
- Remove the reflection-based replacement of the RakNet reliability queue.
- Export per-domain queued, sent and pending frame/byte arrays in JSONL metrics.

RakNet congestion control, pacing, retransmission, FEC, MTU discovery, fragmentation and
compression remain active below this application-level scheduler.

## Verification

- Common unit tests cover capability gating, atomic bundles, epoch hold/drop behavior, fence
  promises, conservative custom-payload handling, scheduler fairness/FIFO, cleanup failures and
  metrics formatting.
- `gradlew clean build` passes for Common, Fabric, Velocity and Bungee, including license checks and
  packaging (47 tasks; 31 executed in the clean verification run).

The remaining verification work is real integration/fault injection: repeated portal transitions
and proxy switches with Create/Touhou Little Maid under independent per-channel delay, reordering
and 1-5% loss.

Design and invariants: `docs/CAUSAL_MULTICHANNEL_REFACTOR.md`.

author: bimvoice
body:
Fixes #6301

## Problem

@theoryshaw reported that renaming an `IfcMaterialConstituent` does not update the name of the associated `IfcShapeAspect`, so the two names drift apart and the per-item style tied to that shape aspect is silently lost.

## Root cause

`tool.Geometry.get_shape_aspect_styles` (`src/bonsai/bonsai/tool/geometry.py`) pairs an `IfcShapeAspect` to an `IfcMaterialConstituent` purely by matching `Name` (`c.Name == shape_aspect.Name`). This is how Bonsai links a representation item's per-item style back to the material it represents. Renaming the constituent through the Object Materials UI (`EditMaterialSetItem` -> `ifcopenshell.api.material.edit_constituent`) only changed the constituent's `Name`, never the paired shape aspect's `Name`, breaking that pairing.

Reproduced live in headless Blender before the fix: after renaming a constituent from "Concrete Constituent" to "testing name change", the constituent's `Name` changed but the shape aspect kept the old name, so `shape_aspect.Name == constituent.Name` went from `True` to `False` and the style lookup stopped resolving.

## Fix

The rename is fixed at the point it happens (the `EditMaterialSetItem` operator, the authoring action behind the UI), not with a downstream repair pass. After the constituent is renamed, `tool.Geometry.sync_shape_aspects_with_constituent_rename` renames the shape aspects paired with it, scoped to elements that actually use that constituent's material set, so shape aspects belonging to unrelated elements that coincidentally share the old name are left alone.

## Testing

* Reproduced and verified live in headless Blender through the real `bpy.ops.bim.edit_material_set_item` operator path, before and after the fix (names diverge before, stay in sync after), inspecting the IFC entities directly via ifcopenshell.
* Added `TestSyncShapeAspectsWithConstituentRename` in `src/bonsai/test/tool/test_geometry.py` (rename propagates, unrelated shape aspects untouched, no-op when name is unchanged/absent).
* `test/tool/test_geometry.py`: 64 passed before -> 67 passed after (3 new tests, no regressions).
* `test/core/test_material.py` + `test/tool/test_material.py` + `test/tool/test_geometry.py` combined: 96 passed before -> 99 passed after (no regressions).
* black + ruff clean on all touched files.

author: ishiland
body:
## Summary

**#680 is merged; this now targets `main` directly.** The branch was rebuilt onto the post-merge `main` rather than rebased (its first commits predate two base commits that #680's squash folded into `main`); the rebuilt head is byte-identical to the reviewed head `87d4166`, verified with an empty `git diff`. Two of #680's review findings — the `__none__` group-by collision and the inflated truncation copy — were fixed here rather than on #680 because the panel had diverged, so they land with this PR.

Clip masks no longer have to be hand-drawn: both analysis endpoints accept `mask_dataset_id` as an alternative to the inline GeoJSON `mask`, clipping against the referenced polygon dataset's unioned geometries — "clip lakes to Brazil" instead of tracing Brazil by hand. This also removes the pointer-only-drawing accessibility dead end for clip and lays the first brick of the two-layer operations planned in #681 (a second dataset reference with its own access check is exactly what spatial join / select-by-location will reuse).

## How

- **API**: `mask_dataset_id: UUID` on `AnalysisPreviewRequest` and `AnalysisMaterializeRequest`; clip requires exactly one of `mask` / `mask_dataset_id` (422 otherwise). Additive — openapi + both SDKs + `api.generated.ts` regenerated.
- **SQL**: the mask layer unions **once** in a `MATERIALIZED` CTE (`render_mask_cte`, with `ST_MakeValid` inside the union); the clip expression and both WHERE terms reference it as a scalar subquery, so the union isn't evaluated three times. The dimension-preserving extract and `&&` index term from #680 apply unchanged. No vertex cap needed — nothing is inlined into SQL text; the 10s sandbox timeout bounds preview cost, the 300s statement timeout bounds materialize.
- **Authorization (Rule 1 on BOTH datasets)**: the mask dataset gets its own `check_dataset_access` on the preview path and the materialize fail-fast; the worker re-resolves the mask table at run time and re-validates it against `_SAFE_TABLE`. A private mask layer 404s for a non-grantee even when the source dataset is readable — pinned by an IDOR test.
- **Constraints**: mask datasets must be `POLYGON`/`MULTIPOLYGON` (unioning points/lines clips nothing meaningful) — 422 with a clear message.
- **Panel**: the clip section gains an "Or clip to a layer" select listing the map's other dataset layers (source layer excluded — a layer can't clip itself). Drawn and layer masks are mutually exclusive; picking one clears the other. Strings added to all four locales.

## Verification

- Backend: 45 analysis tests + layering + port-conformance + chat suites green (new: clip-by-layer preview, mask IDOR, non-polygon mask, both-sources 422, worker end-to-end, deleted-mask job failure).
- Frontend: 11 panel tests, `typecheck`, `lint`, `test:i18n` green.
- Live against the dev stack: lakes clipped by the 29-polygon QA layer → 200 with 29 features; `mask`+`mask_dataset_id` together → 422; MultiPoint dataset as mask → 422 "must reference a polygon dataset".

Chat's `run_analysis` deliberately stays buffer/centroid-only.

author: ivangabriele
body:
The French `imageFrozenAnnouncement` used `Déplacez-vous avec deux doigts`, which is reflexive: it tells the user to move *themselves*, not the frozen image. TalkBack announces this string the moment the image freezes, so blind users were getting the one instruction they need in a form that does not describe the gesture.

Now reads `Image figée. Faites glisser avec deux doigts.` — `faire glisser` is the standard French wording for a drag gesture on Android, it mirrors the objectless framing of the English hint (`Pan with two fingers.`), and it avoids the clumsy `Image figée. Déplacez l'image…` repetition in consecutive audio.

French only; the English master is unchanged. Generated l10n output is gitignored, so the `.arb` edit is the whole change.

Verified locally: `flutter gen-l10n`, `flutter analyze` (no issues), `flutter test` (70 passed).

author: brandonkindred
body:
## Summary

- `create_brand` (`backend/agents/branding_team/api/routes/brands.py`) attached an existing conversation to a newly created brand via separate, independently-committed store calls: check uniqueness (`get_conversation_brand_id`), attach the conversation (`attach_and_update_mission`), then patch the brand's `conversation_id` (`update_brand`). This left two race windows — a concurrent request could attach the same conversation between the uniqueness check and the write (stale check), and if the brand row was deleted after the conversation attach succeeded, the conversation was left pointing at a brand that never learned its id.
- Adds `BrandingStore.attach_conversation`, which locks the conversation row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) and updates both the `branding_conversations` and `branding_brands` rows in a single transaction, closing both races.
- `create_brand` now calls this one atomic method instead of the three-call sequence, mapping its result to the existing `404`/`409` responses.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest agents/branding_team/tests -q` (unit) — all green (191 passed, only integration/real-Postgres tests skipped, as expected without live infra)
- [x] `pytest agents/branding_team/tests -m integration -q` (`LLM_PROVIDER=dummy`) — new atomic-attach coverage passes; remaining failures are pre-existing infra gaps in this sandbox (no live job service / Temporal), unrelated to this change

author: shellie2003
body:
## Pourquoi cette PR

**PR de diagnostic, à fermer sans fusionner.**

Sur la PR #1, cinq tests échouent : `BackupRestoreDuplicationTest`, `DeletionTombstoneTest`, `ExampleRobolectricTest`, `GreetingScreenshotTest`, `Migration20To21Test`. Tous les tests Robolectric du projet, tous en `classMethod` — donc à l'amorçage de l'environnement Android, avant qu'une seule méthode de test ne s'exécute — avec `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException at DefaultSdkProvider.java:170`.

Deux lectures possibles, et attribuer la panne sans mesure serait une supposition :

- soit la panne est **antérieure** et tient à l'environnement (Robolectric 4.16.1 face à `@Config(sdk = [36])`, avec un `compileSdk` en 36.1) ;
- soit le lot photos/sauvegardes de la PR #1 en est la cause — deux de ces tests touchent précisément la sauvegarde et la restauration.

Cette branche ne contient **que le workflow de vérification**, posé sur `main` sans aucune modification applicative. Son résultat tranche :

| Résultat ici | Conclusion |
|---|---|
| Les 5 tests échouent aussi | Panne pré-existante, indépendante de la PR #1 — à corriger séparément |
| Les 5 tests passent | La PR #1 en est la cause, et il faut chercher dans son diff |

L'argument en faveur de la première hypothèse : `ExampleRobolectricTest` et `GreetingScreenshotTest` n'ont aucun rapport avec la sauvegarde, et un échec en `classMethod` signale un environnement qui ne démarre pas, pas une assertion métier. Mais un argument n'est pas une mesure.

## Ce que contient cette branche

Un seul fichier ajouté, `.github/workflows/verification.yml` : tests unitaires puis compilation de la variante release, sans production ni téléversement d'APK. `build_apk.yml` reste désactivé, `release.yml` reste seul responsable des paquets distribuables.

author: pradeep0153
body:
Closes #3373.

### Description
This PR executes a highly critical stabilization of our frontend architecture by eliminating dangerous "blind" data parsing, replacing generic `any` types with strict TypeScript interfaces, and implementing rigorous runtime validation via Zod for all core API payloads.

### Changes Made
- **Architecture Audit:** Investigated the centralized API Service layer. Identified that the frontend was universally accepting raw JSON payloads from the backend as untyped objects, creating a massive vulnerability where a backend schema change would cause the frontend to fail silently in production.
- **Interface Engineering:** Defined deterministic, highly specific TypeScript interfaces for our primary data models within a new `/types` directory (e.g., `IProduct`, `IOrder`, `ICart`, `IUser`).
- **Zod Schema Integration:** Installed the `zod` runtime validation library. Engineered strict validation schemas corresponding to the new TypeScript interfaces (e.g., `ProductSchema = z.object({ id: z.string(), price: z.number(), title: z.string() })`).
- **Validation Pipeline:** Upgraded the core HTTP client interceptors. Now, when a data-fetching method (like `api.getProducts()`) receives a 200 OK response from the server, the raw JSON payload is physically forced through the `ProductSchema.parse()` method *before* it is ever allowed to enter the React component tree or the Redux store.
- **Error Handling:** If the backend accidentally drops a required field (e.g., omitting the `price` key), Zod instantly catches the contract breach during runtime. During development, it throws a highly descriptive error, immediately alerting the engineer. In production, it intercepts the malformed data and gracefully triggers a generic error boundary, physically preventing the React application from crashing due to a `Cannot read property of undefined` exception.

### Impact
- **Application Stability & Developer Velocity:** Operating a frontend application without strict type validation at the network boundary is a recipe for catastrophic production bugs. If the backend team accidentally changes an API response structure, the frontend UI will inevitably break, and finding the source of that break is incredibly tedious. By implementing Zod runtime validation, we mathematically guarantee that the frontend only ever receives the exact data shapes it expects. We build a bulletproof shield at the network layer, catching API contract breaches instantly, entirely eliminating silent data failures, and massively accelerating the debugging process for the engineering team.

author: fredrivett
body:
## What & why

E2E has been intermittently red across PRs and on `main` (different specs on different runs) — a merge-gate blocker for every open PR, so this unblocks others too. Two independent root causes:

1. **Member-number signup race (also a production bug).** `handle_new_user` assigns member numbers with `SELECT MAX(member_number)+1` then `INSERT`, so two concurrent signups read the same MAX and collide on the `member_number` unique constraint — GoTrue returns "Database error creating new user". CI runs `workers=4`, so every spec that creates users races (and real users signing up simultaneously in prod hit it too). Fixed with a transaction-level advisory lock that serializes the read-modify-write while keeping numbering gapless (no sequence, no schema change).
2. **save-mfa typed the TOTP before the form hydrated.** The verify-mfa form is a client component; `input-otp` only fires `onComplete` once its controlled value reaches 6 digits. Keystrokes landing pre-hydration were dropped, so `onComplete` never fired and the page stalled on `/login/verify-mfa`. `enterMfaCode()` now retypes until the input holds all 6 digits, and `waitForTotpWindowAfter()` guarantees window runway so a code can't roll over mid-verify.

No retries / timeout bumps / `test.retry` — root causes fixed so each test passes first-run.

**Reliability evidence:** the member-number race reproduced directly — 20 concurrent inserts using the trigger's exact logic → 6/20 failed on the unique constraint, **0/20 after the fix**; the new migration deploys cleanly. save-mfa passes end-to-end with the hydration-safe entry helper.

## Checklist

- [x] User-facing change → PostHog event / funnel — N/A (test + trigger reliability; no new user-facing flow)
- [x] New error paths report via `captureServerException` / error boundary — N/A
- [x] New behavior covered by tests — the trigger fix is exercised by the whole E2E suite's concurrent user creation; MFA entry by save-mfa
- [x] Recurring defect → guardrail via `learn` skill — N/A (a concurrency race is hard to unit-assert; the fix itself is the mitigation)

## Notes

- **Migration** `..._fix_handle_new_user_member_number_race` replaces `handle_new_user` via `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` (advisory lock). Non-destructive — no data or schema change.
- Fixes intermittent "Database error creating new user" for simultaneous real signups in production, not just E2E.

## Issue relacionada

Closes #

## Resultado observável

A UI de `apps/web` deixou de ser um console escuro com painéis empilhados e passou a ser um design system claro em vidro, com informação organizada por superfície.

- **Design system**: Tailwind v4 com tokens CSS-first em `apps/web/app/theme.css`, base neutra fria e acento teal. Vidro (`backdrop-filter`) declarado em um único lugar e aplicado só em chrome — barra superior, tab strip, sheets, dialogs e alert strip. Conteúdo denso fica em cards sólidos.
- **Builder** (`/project/[id]`): os treze painéis empilhados viraram um workspace de três colunas — conversa, preview e um inspetor com seis abas (Atividade, Execução, Mudanças, Artefatos, Router, Versões) com estado na URL. Nada foi removido: `DESIGN.md` §5.3 traz a tabela de realocação painel a painel.
- **Home**: hero enxuto, composer e pipeline lado a lado, projetos em cards com faixa de progresso do pipeline.
- **Router** (`/router`): toolbar de filtros em vidro, tiles de KPI, tabela de decisões ordenável e sheet lateral de detalhe; criação de experimento saiu do formulário inline para um dialog.
- **Versões** (`/project/[id]/versions`): convertida para o design system.
- `apps/web/app/globals.css` (801 linhas originais) foi removido.

## Superfícies

Capturas da execução Playwright do golden flow. Versões em `docs/evidence/ui-redesign/`.

### Home — `/`

![Home](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eedsilva/agent-foundry/4290d6057f59a95bdd8668a1d5580812cf82ebcd/docs/evidence/ui-redesign/home.png)

Conversa à esquerda, preview ao centro, inspetor de seis abas à direita.

![Versoes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eedsilva/agent-foundry/4290d6057f59a95bdd8668a1d5580812cf82ebcd/docs/evidence/ui-redesign/versions.png)

## Evidência

- [x] Testes relevantes — `npm run check` passa (exit 0). Suíte completa: 1336 + 495 testes, 0 falhas.
- [x] Logs, trace, screenshot ou benchmark quando aplicável — screenshots das quatro superfícies em `test-results/`: `home-desktop.png`, `issue-43-knowledge-builder-desktop.png`, `router-dashboard-desktop.png`, `project-versions-desktop.png`.
- [x] Critérios de aceite demonstrados — e2e `golden-flow.spec.ts` e `dom-source-map.spec.ts` 14/14. O scan axe saiu de um único subtree (`[data-testid="preview-panel"]`) para cinco varreduras de página inteira (builder ×2, versões, router, home), com zero violações.

Contraste: todo texto atinge 4.5:1. `--ink-subtle` foi escurecido de `#8A97A3` para `#656E77` (2.98:1 → 5.19:1 em branco, 2.63:1 → 4.57:1 em `--surface-sunken`), e `DESIGN.md` §3.1 e `theme-tokens.test.ts` foram atualizados junto. Os tokens de status (`--ok`, `--warn`, `--err`, `--info`, `--accent`) passaram a carregar significado por ponto, wash e borda, com o texto sempre em `--ink`.

## Risco e falhas prováveis

Blast radius restrito a `apps/web` e aos specs e2e. Nenhuma mudança de API, orquestrador, worker ou persistência.

O risco real é regressão visual e de interação, não de dados. Mitigações:

- Tarefas 4 e 4b foram refatorações deliberadamente **sem mudança de comportamento**, revisadas separadamente antes de qualquer restyling, justamente para que uma regressão de comportamento não se confundisse com uma mudança de estilo.
- Os seletores e2e migraram de classes CSS para `data-testid`, então o restyling não podia quebrar os testes silenciosamente.
- Invariante importante documentado no código (`chat-pane.tsx`, `model-pin-panel.tsx`): o estado local dos painéis só é seguro porque eles nunca desmontam. As abas do inspetor escondem os painéis com o atributo `hidden`, não com renderização condicional. Uma futura tab strip que desmonte um painel perde `draft` no meio da digitação e deixa `classifyPromptRef` apontando para uma closure morta, tornando os botões "Continuar na conversa" do preview no-ops silenciosos.

## Segurança e dados

Não. Nenhuma alteração em execução de processos, filesystem, rede, secrets, permissões, dados sensíveis, autenticação ou isolamento.

Uma exceção fora do escopo de UI: o commit `0de0f24` foi cherry-picked de `854bf7e` (`fix: share execution secret ref schema`) porque o commit base do branch já estava vermelho — `packages/orchestrator` usava `secretRefs` sem que `packages/contracts/src/workflow.ts` declarasse o campo. Sem isso o `npm run typecheck` do repositório não passava.

## Migração e compatibilidade

Sem mudança de schema, artifact, workflow, API ou formato persistido.

Mudanças de compatibilidade internas ao frontend:

- `apps/web/app/globals.css` foi removido; o vocabulário compartilhado agora vive em `apps/web/lib/ui.ts`.
- `apps/web/app/project/[id]/page.tsx` (1868 linhas) foi dividido em ~20 módulos.
- `components.json` e as dependências `lucide-react` e `class-variance-authority` foram removidas — nenhum primitivo shadcn chegou a ser instalado e o `baseColor: "slate"` injetaria uma paleta fora dos tokens no próximo `shadcn add`. `DESIGN.md` §11 registra a decisão.

## Rollback ou contenção

`git revert` do merge commit. As mudanças são inteiramente de frontend e não deixam estado persistido, migração ou artefato para desfazer.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run check` passa
- [x] Documentação e ADR atualizados quando necessários — `DESIGN.md` é novo e traz os tokens, a arquitetura de informação e, em §11, as divergências aceitas em relação à especificação original
- [x] Nenhum segredo ou dado sensível foi incluído
- [x] `docs/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md` está satisfeito

## Divergências aceitas

Registradas em `DESIGN.md` §11. A que mais importa: o controle segmentado abaixo de 1000px descrito em §5.3 foi **deliberadamente rejeitado** — ele desmontaria os painéis e quebraria o invariante acima. Os três painéis empilham em uma coluna, com asserção e2e a 900px.

author: jarmandoanaya
body:
Closes #418 (WI-7 of the 2026-07 realism batch, #411 — **the last item**).

The Attributes pane had never been checked as a whole against the data model. Seven work items each added their own rows; this audits every selectable element against its model struct and against the command factories, commits the matrix, closes the gaps whose commands already existed, and files the rest.

## The audit

The full **element × parameter matrix** is committed to [`docs/roadmap/updates/2026-07-realism-batch.md`](../blob/main/docs/roadmap/updates/2026-07-realism-batch.md#wi-7-element--parameter-matrix), one table per element type, with a disposition per cell: `exposed` / `fixed here` / `tool` (authored elsewhere by design) / `read-only` / `follow-up #N`.

The rule applied, per the maintainer's scoping call: **fix every gap whose kernel command already existed; anything needing new kernel API becomes a follow-up** — with one exception, the signal mounting height, because the WI's acceptance names z-offset explicitly and no command carried it.

## Fixed here

**A prop's placement was almost entirely unreachable.** The pane showed `s`/`t` as one read-only line, its heading could only be authored by dragging the gizmo's yaw ring (#417's explicit handoff), and its `@zOffset` had **no authoring path anywhere in the product**. All four are now typeable and scrubbable — `s`/`t`/`Heading` through one `move_object`, the vertical through `update_objects` (the only command that carries it). The Heading spin steps by `defaults::kPropRotationSnap`, the ring's own detent, so the two cannot drift apart.

**A sign's mounting height.** New kernel command `edit::set_signal_z_offset` (§14.1 Table 122 `@zOffset`, required, meters — verbatim in 1.8.1, so no version gating), modelled on `set_signal_text`: value snapshot, byte-identical undo, no-op and non-finite refusals. Deliberately its own command rather than a fourth `move_signal` argument — raising a sign never re-aims it, so the vertical must not travel with the pose that carries the facing. Ships with its nanobind binding and a `place_signals.py` example.

**GW-4 was checking a readout that did not exist.** Step 12c (added by #417) asserts *"the Attributes pane still reports the same traffic direction"*. It did not: `refresh_signal` showed designation, type/subtype and country, never `@orientation`. There is now an **Applies to** row, and the GW step names it.

**`set_lane_direction` had shipped in P2 with no pane control** (the Lane Profile tool cycles it in the viewport). A Direction combo now sits next to Type, disabled on the centre lane — matching the kernel's own refusal, the `lane_width_is_constant` precedent.

**Road-mark colour was write-once.** Road styles author it (yellow centre lines, white lane lines, per #413) and nothing could change it afterwards. A colour combo now rides the same `set_road_mark` the type and width rows use.

**World position readouts** for props and signals, read from `ObjectInstance::position` / `SignalInstance::position` rather than recomputed — the mesher already resolves the reference line, elevation profile and `@zOffset`, so the row and the viewport cannot disagree.

**The rounding echo (#417's second handoff item).** The pose spins display three decimals, so a value carrying more precision — exactly a ring drag's output — was rounded when seeded, and a focus-out then committed that rounding as a `move_signal`. The no-op guard is now half the spin's own display quantum: a spin cannot *represent* a change smaller than that, so anything below it is the widget rounding its seed, never intent. **Verified failing before the fix** — the pre-fix build produces an extra undo entry and rewrites `h_offset` from `0.5235987755982988` to `0.524`.

## Deliberately not editable

A **marking instance**'s `s`/`t` stay read-only: a crosswalk's geometry lives in its `outlines` in road coordinates, so moving the origin alone would desync the two. Relocation is #307, which the issue puts out of scope. The pose rows join the existing per-kind `setRowVisible` switch.

## Follow-ups filed (added to #411's table ⇒ release-blocking)

- **#429** — a placed signal's designation and face dimensions are fixed after placement; re-designating means delete-and-replace, losing pose, text and posted value.
- **#430** — lane material `@friction`/`@roughness` are set once from the catalogue nominal and never adjustable, though `set_lane_material` already replaces the whole record.
- **#431** — a road's `predecessor`/`successor` are authorable by Link Ends but reported nowhere in the pane, so a mis-linked end is invisible until the mesh looks wrong.

## Tests

- `editor/tests/test_panels.cpp` — 10 new tests: seeds-without-pushing, one-undo-entry, byte-identical undo, no refresh echo, and the visibility predicates (pose rows hidden for a marking, Direction disabled on the centre lane). Includes the pre-fix-verified rounding regression and an assertion that the **Applies to** row exists.
- `core/tests/test_signal_ops.cpp` — 5 new tests for `set_signal_z_offset`: apply/revert byte-identity, a legal negative height, and the no-op / non-finite / stale-id refusals.
- `python/tests/test_signals.py` — the new binding, one undo step and the no-op refusal.

## Gates

- `ci-macos` build + `ctest`: **2133/2133**.
- `release-macos` **shared-kernel** build (mandatory here — `core/` changed; the #233/#234 hidden-visibility link trap).
- ASan+UBSan with the editor tests built in.
- `pytest python/tests`.
- `clang-format` over the whole tree, CI's exact command.

## Docs

Matrix + follow-up rows in the batch update doc · `docs/user-guide/attributes.md` and `objects-signals.md` · CHANGELOG Added + two Fixed entries · GW amendments (the batch's last): **GW-4 12c** now names the Applies-to row and adds a no-edit-on-focus-out check, **GW-4 12d** covers mounting height, **GW-2 16c** covers the prop pose rows and the marking exclusion.

Refs #411, #417, #416, #307.
