author: sanidhyasin
body:
## Context

Closes #7392.

`GET /api/status` is the endpoint liveness/readiness probes hit — the `infisical-standalone` Helm chart probes it every 5s — and its handler wrote two `logger.info` lines on **every** request: a formatted summary plus a full `JSON.stringify(histogram, null, 2)` dump of the event loop delay histogram. On a single self-hosted replica that is ~1,440 log records/hour, with the raw dump alone accounting for roughly 45% of the container's log volume (see the measurements in the issue). There was no way to turn it off: neither call was gated by log level or any env var.

The logged values were also cumulative rather than windowed. The histogram is created once at startup (`monitorEventLoopDelay` at the top of `server/routes/index.ts`) and never `.reset()`, so `mean`/`p50` sit on the 20ms sampling-resolution floor for the life of the process and `max` stays frozen at the worst stall since boot. Windowed event loop delay is already exported properly as `nodejs.eventloop.delay.*` by `RuntimeNodeInstrumentation`, registered in `initTelemetryInstrumentation` (`backend/src/lib/telemetry/instrumentation.ts`), whenever telemetry is enabled.

Two commits:

**1. `fix(status): log event loop stats at debug level`** — takes the diagnostic off the default log path without dropping it:

- The two `logger.info` calls become a single `logger.debug`, so nothing is emitted at the default `info` level.
- The raw histogram is passed as a structured field (`{ eventLoopStats: histogram }`) rather than pre-stringified into the message. Pino checks the level before serializing a merge object, so the `JSON.stringify` work no longer runs on every probe — only when the level is raised. `IntervalHistogram` implements `toJSON`, so the serialized payload is the same data as before (`count`, `min`, `max`, `mean`, `stddev`, `percentiles`), and this matches the backend logging convention of a structured object alongside a self-contained message.
- A comment records why this has to stay at debug level and where the windowed metrics come from, so it doesn't regress.

The response body is unchanged.

**2. `fix(logger): honor PINO_LOG_LEVEL on the transport target`** — needed for the above to mean anything, and a pre-existing bug in its own right. `initLogger()` set the root logger level from `PINO_LOG_LEVEL` but hardcoded `level: "info"` on the sole `pino/file` transport target. Transport targets filter independently of the root logger, so a `debug` record passed the root level and was then discarded by the transport: **setting `PINO_LOG_LEVEL=debug` had no effect, and every `logger.debug` call in the backend (~64 sites) was unreachable.** Both now read the same resolved `logLevel`.

Default behavior is unchanged — with `PINO_LOG_LEVEL` unset both levels resolve to `info`, exactly as before. This only affects operators who explicitly opt in. Credit to the Codex review bot for catching that the first commit alone would have made the diagnostic unreachable rather than on-demand.

Happy to split commit 2 into its own PR if you'd rather keep this scoped strictly to #7392 — but on its own, commit 1 would just be a silent removal.

## Steps to verify the change

1. Start the backend with `PINO_LOG_LEVEL` unset (default `info`) and hit the endpoint repeatedly:
   ```sh
   for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -s -o /dev/null localhost:8080/api/status; done
   ```
   No `Event loop stats` or `Raw event loop stats` lines appear, and each response is still `200` with the same JSON body.
2. Restart with `PINO_LOG_LEVEL=debug` and repeat — one line per request carrying the formatted `Mean/Max/p99` summary and an `eventLoopStats` object with the full histogram. (Before commit 2, this printed nothing.)
3. `backend/e2e-test/routes/v1/status.spec.ts` still covers the `200` response; no test changes are needed for a log-level change, and asserting on log output here would mean mocking the logger singleton.

What I verified locally, reproducing this repo's exact transport config against `pino@8` in isolation:

- Root level `debug` + target level `"info"` (the state before commit 2) → the debug record is dropped, only `info` reaches stdout. This is the bug commit 2 fixes.
- Both levels wired to `PINO_LOG_LEVEL` → `debug` and `info` both reach stdout with the level set to `debug`; with it unset, only `info` does and `trace` is still filtered.
- `IntervalHistogram` passed as a pino merge object serializes via `toJSON` at `debug`, and is not serialized at all at `info`.
- `prettier --check` clean on both changed files.

I did not boot the full stack for steps 1–2, since that needs Postgres and Redis.

## Type

- [x] Fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Improvement
- [ ] Breaking
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Chore

## Checklist

- [x] Title follows the [conventional commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/#summary) format: `type(scope): short description` (scope is optional, e.g., `fix: prevent crash on sync` or `fix(api): handle null response`).
- [ ] Tested locally — the logging behavior is verified in isolation against `pino@8`, not against a booted stack; see the note above.
- [x] Updated docs (if needed) — not needed; the removed lines were not documented, and `PINO_LOG_LEVEL` keeps its documented default.
- [x] Updated CLAUDE.md files (if needed) — not needed; no new pattern or architectural change.
- [x] Read the [contributing guide](https://infisical.com/docs/contributing/getting-started/overview)

author: bertpl
body:
**TL;DR**: A release whose mutation measurement fails now aborts, instead of silently keeping a stale badge and stamping it as freshly measured. The measurement also moves ahead of every write.

## Description

### Problem addressed

The mutation score cannot come from CI — mutation testing is deliberately off the pipeline — so the release script **measures it locally and stamps it into a README badge**. Three faults combined to make that measurement silently worthless:

- The **structural parity test resolves its target through the module's own file path**, which under a mutation runner points at the runner's *mutated* copy: trampoline-expanded variants whose cold-start handlers are not the idiom the test recognizes. It therefore failed on every mutant, and **no score could be collected at all**.
- **Any mutation failure was a warning**, leaving the previously committed badge untouched. A completely broken measurement was invisible unless someone read the release log closely.
- The badge's **provenance comment was rewritten to name the new release regardless**, so the stamp claimed a measurement that release never took.

Separately, the check that **CI on `main` is current ran after the changelog had already been rewritten**, so aborting there left a dirty tree to clean up by hand.

### Implementation

The measurement now answers **two separate questions**. Whether a number could be produced *gates the release*: a crashing suite, a missing or malformed stats file, an empty mutant set, or a run past a ten-minute ceiling all abort. What the number *is* still **never gates** — the score wobbles run to run from timeout nondeterminism, so a threshold would reject releases over measurement noise. That refines the existing "mutation testing never blocks a release" stance rather than reversing it: what never blocks is the percentage.

**Everything that can fail now runs before the first write.** Gathering the badge numbers — the CI metrics for `HEAD`, including the freshness check, plus the local mutation score — became the last precondition rather than a side effect of composing the release commit. Applying those numbers to the README is a pure write with nothing left to fail, so the provenance stamp can no longer outrun the measurement. Renumbering the steps around that insertion is most of the diff's line count.

A **`--dry-run` flag** stops at exactly that boundary, which is what makes the preconditions exercisable without releasing anything.

The parity test **stands down when it detects a mutation runner's copy** of the source instead of learning the runner's generated shapes — asserting anything about mutant variants is not its job.

## Attention points

- **`fail_with_message` is now `NoReturn`.** The new abort paths need it to type-check, and it tightens the existing call sites for free.
- **Step numbers shifted** — the badge-metric gather is step 8, so every later step renumbered. Mechanical, but it touches each step function's name and its printed line.
- **The score is still not a gate.** It reads 88% today; a low score remains unable to block a release. Only an unmeasurable one aborts.
- **Sandbox detection keys on the runner's copy directory.** If that ever changes, the test stops skipping and starts failing under the runner again — loud rather than silent, which is the right direction for a guard.
- **Unrelated pre-existing flake:** a micro-benchmark test can fail with `ZeroDivisionError` when a timed run measures zero elapsed time on a loaded machine. Hit once here, passes consistently otherwise, and untouched by this change.

## Tests / Spikes

- **TEST:** full suite green — 1800 passed, 3 skipped.
- **TEST:** `make mutation` + `make mutation-stats` complete and produce a score again (88%: 1685 killed of 1923, 5 timeouts). Previously the parity test failed on every mutant, so no score existed to read.
- **TEST:** the parity test confirmed to skip when run against a runner's copy of the source, and to pass against the real source.
- **TEST:** every way the measurement can fail — target exits nonzero, run exceeds the timeout, stats file missing, stats file malformed, zero mutants — confirmed to abort the release; a healthy run confirmed to still return its score.
- **TEST:** `--dry-run` confirmed to reach the precondition block and write nothing.
- No unit tests added for the release script, which deliberately has none; `--dry-run` is what makes its preconditions checkable by hand instead.

## Changelog entry

None: no user-facing change. This is release tooling plus a guard on a structural test.

author: dhoulb
body:
Using `<App>` with a `url` but no `root` made every `requireMetaURL()` consumer (`<Router>`, `<SidebarLayout>`, `<TreeBreadcrumbs>`, `<RouteCache>`) throw a misleading `RequiredError: Meta URL and meta root must share an origin`. The real cause was a missing `root`, not an origin mismatch: `matchURLPrefix()` returns `undefined` both when its base is missing and when origins genuinely differ, and `requireMetaURL()` reported every falsy result with the origin wording.

## Changes

- **`mergeMeta()` derives `root` from the resolved `url`'s origin** (e.g. `https://x.com/`) when no explicit root is set, so merged meta with a `url` always has a `root`. The default only applies when `url` resolved absolute — a relative `url` with no root still fails fast in `requireURL()` as before.
- **`requireMetaURL()` gains a backup `"Meta root is required"` check** for hand-built meta that bypasses the merge, and the mismatch error is reworded to `"must share a root"` — it also fires when the `url` falls outside the root's path prefix, so the origin-specific wording was wrong. `MetaURL` now guarantees `root` alongside `url`.
- **`<Navigation>` publishes its live-URL meta through `mergeMeta()`** instead of a hand-built object literal, so the root default (and any future merge invariants) also covers the `window.location.href` fallback — the exact path that produced the original error. With only `url` changing, every other merge branch short-circuits, so this costs nothing per render.
- **Docs**: `App.md` and `Navigation.md` now state that setting `root` explicitly is strongly recommended — the derived default is only correct for apps served from the domain root, so sub-path deployments must set it.

## Tests

- `mergeMeta`: root derived from url origin, explicit root preserved, root stays unset without a url.
- `requireMetaURL`: path derivation with defaulted root, `"Meta URL is required"`, `"Meta root is required"` (hand-built meta), and `"must share a root"` for both origin mismatch and url-outside-root-path.
- New `Navigation.test.tsx`: published meta routes correctly with a derived root, and relative urls resolve against an explicit root.

`bun run test` passes: lint, types, and 1227 unit tests. (Biome logs a pre-existing internal panic on `Dialog.tsx` that also occurs on `main`; lint still exits 0.)

author: pathscale
body:
Standardises agent instructions across all six pathscale backends, adopting the single-sourcing pattern from [PakhomovAlexander/project-hub](https://github.com/PakhomovAlexander/project-hub).

**Docs and guardrails only — no source or dependency changes.**

## What changed

**`AGENTS.md` is now canonical; `CLAUDE.md` is a thin `@AGENTS.md` import.** Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI read `AGENTS.md` natively; Claude Code loads it through the import. One runbook, no per-vendor fork. Previously these repos were Claude-only — and `AGENTS.md` was gitignored in five of six, so non-Claude agents got nothing at all.

**The behavioural half, which was missing entirely.** The old files were orientation: build commands, module structure, config. Useful, but they told an agent what the repo *is*, not how to *behave*. Added:

- **Invariants** — never hand-edit `src/codegen/`; a WorkTable schema change is a deployment event that needs a migration script; `endpoint-libs` and `honey_id-types` move in lockstep; don't enable upstream features this service doesn't use. Plus a per-repo invariant where the blast radius warrants one (auth boundary, money movement, live trading).
- **Verification** — run what you build; if you can't run it, say so. Compare against the base branch rather than asserting a failure is pre-existing. A sub-second `cargo build` was cached, not rebuilt.
- **PR / CI discipline** — check CI and don't call it done until green, with the exact `gh` command and this repo's URL.
- **Docs are shared memory** — durable learnings belong in the repo, not an agent's private memory, which dies with the machine.

**Guardrails are enforced, not just documented.** `.claude/settings.json` pre-allows read-only cargo/git and prompts before pushes, `cargo publish`, `gh pr merge`, cloud CLIs and deploys. The `PreToolUse` hook catches wrapper forms a permission glob misses — `env X=y git push`, `git -C dir push`, `bash -c '…'`. Adapted from the reference, with `RISKY_WORDS` extended for this stack; the hook and `permissions.ask` are deliberately kept in sync.

**The WorkTable/deploy guardrail** is recorded in both `AGENTS.md` (so agents read it automatically) and `docs/worktable-schema-and-deploy.md` (full version, with this repo's real table counts). It calls out the failure mode easiest to miss: bumping the `worktable` crate changes the on-disk format with **no source edit at all**, so a dependency upgrade that looks unrelated can still need a migration.

## Preserved, not discarded

Repo-specific content in the two mature files (architecture, cargo features, roles, auth flows, configuration, code style, error handling) is kept intact — only restructured under the shared skeleton.

## Fixes found along the way

- Guide links now point only at docs that **exist** — `auth.honey.id-backend` referenced a `docs/new-worktable.md` it doesn't have.
- The regenerate-endpoints path is per-repo correct (`api.honey.id-backend` has it at `scripts/`, not `scripts/utils/`).
- `.gitignore` drops the superseded blocks on `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `/.claude`. `/.claude/settings.local.json` stays ignored — personal overrides shouldn't be shared.

## Note

This is a deliberate v1. The reference is a *multi-repo hub* template; its `repos/` symlinks, tracker and ADR scaffolding don't map onto a standalone service, so that part was intentionally not cargo-culted. Expect to refine the wording and the invariant list per repo.

author: javis603
body:
## Summary

- Derive Claude account identity from one canonical field in priority order: account UUID, organization UUID, then email. This keeps the same account stable across devices without letting an optional field change create another row.
- Cache resolved Claude identity in runtime memory by a private credential fingerprint. A temporary profile or account lookup failure can reuse that exact credential's identity with fresh quota data, while cold starts still fail closed.
- Preserve distinct Claude accounts across devices and show account subrows in the Limits UI.
- Add an explicit Claude Web source for people who mainly use Claude Desktop or claude.ai. Settings accept a bare `sk-ant-…` session key or `sessionKey=sk-ant-…`, validate it through Electron's native network stack, and keep it in the local credential store.
- Follow Claude Web `Set-Cookie` rotation across requests and persist renewed Settings credentials with compare-and-swap guards. Environment-managed widget credentials remain externally managed.
- Keep Claude Code OAuth and CLI detection automatic when Web login is not configured. Explicit Web login becomes the local Claude source, and Token Monitor does not read Claude Desktop credentials.
- Reject malformed Web credentials before persistence, scope Web-only 403 responses to `unauthorized`, and keep credential changes limited to the Claude limits lane.

## Root cause

Claude account keys were previously derived from the credential storage location, such as a file, Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or env source, together with plan metadata. Two different accounts using the same storage shape could therefore collide, while the same account stored through different sources could receive different keys. The aggregation layer also treated Claude as a single-account provider.

The new identity path uses the strongest stable account field available from Claude and preserves it across temporary profile failures. Quota reset timestamps and credential material are not used as account identity.

## Known boundary

Claude Code CLI output does not expose the same stable UUIDs as OAuth or Web. A CLI-only fallback that has never resolved a canonical identity may therefore remain a separate row. Token Monitor does not merge solely by email because one email can belong to multiple organizations with distinct quotas.

## Validation

- `npm run lint`
- Focused Claude Web, OAuth identity, account aggregation, provider ordering, runtime config, native transport, and renderer integration tests: 151 passed
- `npm run verify`: 1853 passed, 1 skipped
- `npm run sync:worker`

author: vicistar-star
body:
The old prune_matured_stake_deposits combined the move and remove logic into a single ambiguous condition:

  if write_index != read_index + 1 { remove(deposit_key) }

This fired correctly for most cases but left no explicit guarantee that every slot at [write_index, current_count) was cleared after compaction. Any edge case (storage gaps, catch-up of write_index to read_index) could leave ArtisanStakeQueueIndexed entries beyond the new logical queue end, causing index collisions when add_stake_deposit writes at the new count.

Fix:
- Pass 1: separate the matured-removal and move into clear if/else branches; remove the old source slot immediately after a move.
- Pass 2: explicit tail-cleanup loop over [write_index, current_count) that removes any remaining key in that range.  This is an O(pruned) pass that runs only when pruning fires, making the invariant 'no stale keys beyond new count' unconditionally true.

Also adds test_prune_no_stale_index_keys_after_partial_prune to scalability_test.rs: fills the queue to the prune threshold, matures all deposits, triggers pruning, then asserts every slot index in [new_count, PRUNE_THRESHOLD) is absent from storage.


Closes #703

## Summary

`.env.example` already existed on disk with the right content
(`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`), but the blanket `.env*` rule in `.gitignore` was
silently excluding it too — so it never made it into a commit, and never
showed up anywhere in the repo history or previous PR.

## Changes
- `.gitignore`: added a `!.env.example` exception to the blanket `.env*`
  ignore rule, so the example file can actually be tracked while real
  `.env*`/`.env.local` files stay ignored.

  (`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:3001`) plus a comment explaining
  why — both this app and the backend default to port 3000, so the
  backend needs to run on another port.
- `README.md`: setup instructions now point at
  `cp .env.example .env.local` instead of duplicating the variable inline.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` / `eslint`: clean (docs/config-only change, no `src/`
  touched)
- Confirmed `.env.example` shows up in `git status` / is trackable after

author: prajwalpatil-afk
body:
Why

Accidental deletes of tasks, projects, or workspaces are high-impact. Users should be explicitly asked to confirm before a destructive action runs. Also, logs/toasts should remain in the southwest corner for unobtrusive feedback.

What changed / approach

- Delete handlers in TasksPage, ProjectsPage, and WorkspacesPage now show a top-centered warning toast that requires the user to click the "Delete" action to perform the deletion. The actual deletion runs only after that action is clicked (async mutation inside the toast action).
- Global Toaster position moved to bottom-left so informational logs remain in the southwest corner.

Files touched (summary)

- frontend/src/pages/TasksPage.tsx — show top confirmation toast before deleting tasks
- frontend/src/pages/ProjectsPage.tsx — show top confirmation toast before deleting projects
- frontend/src/pages/WorkspacesPage.tsx — show top confirmation toast before deleting workspaces
- frontend/src/main.tsx — move Toaster default position to bottom-left

Notes / trade-offs

- The previous toast wording used an "Undo" action; this change uses an explicit "Delete" action to require confirmation. If preferred, this can be changed to a modal for stronger interruption, or an undo-style flow can be reintroduced.
- The toast action contains the async deletion logic. Reviewers may want to ensure any optimistic UI considerations or telemetry integrate with this pattern.

Manual testing checklist

1. Create a task/project/workspace.
2. Click the delete button for the item.
3. Confirm a top-centered warning toast appears with a "Delete" button.
4. Click "Delete" and verify the item is removed and a success toast appears.
5. Verify informational toasts/logs appear at bottom-left.

author: alexisvalotaire
body:
A deep housekeeping pass over the marketplace repo: dependency freshness, pin
hygiene, and removal of workarounds that upstream has since fixed.

**Health baseline first** — the repo was already in good shape. Before any
change: full `mise run ci` green, 160 pytest + 415 hook-fixture tests passing,
strict docs build clean, both manifests valid, no open PRs, CI green on `main`
for every push going back weeks, the `frontend-design` pin exactly current (zero
upstream commits touching that plugin since the pinned SHA), and the version-pin
EOL floors current. Everything below is drift, not breakage.

## Dependabot — the root cause

The `steer` plugin ships a `dependabot.yml` to every managed repo, but this repo
had none, so nothing was chasing its own dependencies. That is why the pins below
had drifted.

Added `.github/dependabot.yml` with the same policy as the shipped template —
weekly, grouped into one PR per ecosystem, majors left for a human — across
`github-actions`, `uv`, and the two deck npm workspaces. No auto-merge here:
unlike a product repo, every bump in the standards repo gets maintainer review.

The npm ecosystem carries a 7-day `cooldown`, because the decks' pnpm 11 enforces
a `minimumReleaseAge` on install. Without it, Dependabot would propose day-old
releases that pnpm then refuses to install without a
`minimumReleaseAgeExclude` bypass — the exact protection the workspace config
warns against discarding.

## Pins refreshed

- `actions/checkout` v7.0.0 → v7.0.1 and `jdx/mise-action` v4.2.0 → v4.2.3
  across all four workflows (SHA pins plus their version comments).
- `STEER_CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION` 2.1.153 → 2.1.220; both manifests validate against
  it.
- `uv.lock` refreshed: ruff 0.16.0, pytest 9.1.1, pre-commit 4.6.1, zensical
  0.0.51, pymdown-extensions 10 → 11. Strict docs build stays green across the
  pymdown major.

## Presentation decks — an upstream fix landed

Slidev 52.16.0 → 52.18.0 and Vue 3.5.38 → 3.5.40.

Both decks carried a `vite.config.ts` monkey-patch for a hash-mode
base-prepending bug, written to **fail loudly** if upstream moved the line it
patched. Bumping Slidev tripped that tripwire, exactly as designed: 52.17.0 moved
the logic into `@slidev/client/logic/slidePath.ts`, which now returns a
base-relative path and lets Vue Router supply the base — the upstream fix the
patch's own comment said to wait for. Removed both files; each deck rebuilds
clean.

The Vue pin's stated justification (a release-age cooldown on 3.5.39) had expired
a month ago, so the rationale comment now states the invariant instead of a
perishable date. `playwright-chromium` stays at 1.61.1 — 1.62.0 was published a
day earlier and is still inside the cooldown.

Also dropped two inert leftovers the READMEs already flagged as removable:
`onboarding/.node-version` and `onboarding/public/_redirects` (Cloudflare).

## Shipped scaffold — CI tool pinning

Every tool the bundled `ci.yml` runs through `npx`/`uvx` is now version-pinned:
`@google/design.md@0.3.0`, `yamllint@1.38.0`, `ansible-lint@26.6.0`,
`diff-cover@10.4.1`. Each previously resolved to whatever was latest at run time,
so an upstream release could turn a green CI red on an unrelated PR, and every
run executed unreviewed code.

`diff-cover` is the one that mattered: that gate can **fail** a PR on changed-line
coverage, so a floating version could silently move the bar a repo is held to.
Noted at that call site — `--markdown-report` still parses on 10.4.1 (verified
against an unrecognized-flag control) but no longer appears in `--help`, so a
future bump may need `--format markdown:coverage-diff.md`.

Also bumped `actions/setup-node` v6 → v7 (ESM migration and a dropped dummy
`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` export; neither affects the advisory `ai-slop` job's
`node-version` usage) and `aislop` 0.12.1 → 0.14.0 (verified the
`scan . --sarif` interface is unchanged).

Dependabot cannot see tool versions embedded in a `run:` block, so these stay
deliberate bumps — the comments say so at each call site.

## Verification

`mise run ci` green after every step, plus both PR-only branch-diff gates
(`check_changelog.py --base` and `check_docs_impact.py --base` against
`origin/main`), `actionlint` on the edited scaffold workflow, a strict Zensical
build, and a real `slidev build` of both decks at their published `--base`.

## Two things for a maintainer, deliberately not done here

1. **`mise.lock` is stale (uv 0.11.2 → 0.11.32) and needs an unrestricted
   network.** `mise upgrade` in a sandboxed environment silently *degrades* the
   lockfile: with the GitHub API unreachable it drops the macOS and arm64
   checksum entries (42 platform entries → 35), trading cross-platform
   reproducibility for one patch bump. It is reverted here and verified
   byte-identical to `main`. Worth knowing as a general hazard — anyone running
   `mise upgrade` behind a restrictive proxy will quietly shrink that lockfile,
   and Dependabot does not cover `mise.lock`.

2. **`ruff` 0.16.0 quietly widened its formatter scope to Markdown** —
   `ruff format --check .` went from 54 files to 291 (54 `.py` + 238 `.md`). It
   passes today, so nothing is broken. But a future `ruff format` write could
   rewrite `plugins/steer/rules/*.md`, and those files are byte-budgeted by
   `check_context_budget.py`. Whether to scope ruff to Python explicitly is a
   maintainer call, so no config change was made.

One smaller observation while looking for a PR template: this repo ships
`pull_request_template.md` to every managed repo but has none of its own — the
same gap as the missing Dependabot config, left alone as out of scope.

author: k2ghostyou
body:
## Issue #897 — CLI: replace stub shell completions with real clap_complete output

### Problem
cli/synapse-cli/src/main.rs previously contained a hand-written print_completions() function whose bodies were literal no-ops:
  - bash: '_synapse() { : }\ncomplete -F _synapse synapse'
  - zsh:  '_synapse() { : }' (never enumerated subcommands or flags)
  - fish: 'complete -c synapse -f' (filename fallback only) A user running 'synapse completions bash >> ~/.bashrc' got tab-completion that did nothing, silently appearing to work.

### Root cause
The Cargo.toml depended on plain clap (derive + env features only) with no clap_complete dependency — the crate needed to generate real completions from the Cli struct.

### Fix
1. Added clap_complete = "4" to cli/synapse-cli/Cargo.toml.
2. Replaced print_completions(shell: &str) with print_completions(shell: Shell) that calls clap_complete::generate(shell, &mut Cli::command(), "synapse", &mut io::stdout()). clap_complete introspects the live Cli struct and generates a complete, accurate script for bash, zsh, and fish.
3. Updated tests/completions.rs to assert that the generated scripts:
   - Contain all real sub-command names (admin, events, health, stats, settlements, transactions, graphql, completions).
   - Do NOT contain the old no-op stub body '() {\n    :\n}'.
   - Have substantial length (> 100–200 bytes), proving they are not stubs.
   - For bash: define a _synapse function.
   - For zsh: start with #compdef.
   - For fish: contain multiple 'complete -c synapse' directives.

---

## Issue #898 — CLI: remove dead EventsCommand/run dead code from events.rs

### Problem
commands/events.rs contained two parallel, incompatible command trees:
1. A DEAD tree: EventsCommand enum (Reconnect/ReconnectStatus), its own ReconnectResponse/ReconnectStatusPayload types, and an async run() that POST /reconnect and GET /reconnect/status via ApiClient. This was never wired into main.rs or commands/mod.rs — zero call sites. It also had ~15 tests that validated the dead code path and gave false CI confidence.
2. A LIVE tree: EventsCmd/EventsSubcommand (WebSocket watch command) that IS re-exported from commands/mod.rs and IS dispatched from main.rs. The admin event reconnection is independently implemented in admin.rs via AdminEventsCommands using AdminClient, making the dead tree a true duplicate with a drifted implementation.

### Fix
Created cli/synapse-cli/src/commands/events.rs containing ONLY:
  - EventsCmd (Args wrapper)
  - EventsSubcommand (Watch variant with base_url + api_key args)
  - EventsCmd::run() dispatching to run_watch()
  - run_watch() — a real WebSocket client using tokio-tungstenite that streams events from <base-url>/ws to stdout No EventsCommand, no run() for reconnect, no duplicate ReconnectResponse/ReconnectStatusPayload types. The module doc explicitly documents why the dead tree was removed and where admin reconnection lives.

---

## Issue #899 — SDK stats().cache_metrics() now targets the correct endpoint

### Problem
The SDK previously had no stats resource at all. Issue #899 identified that an earlier draft called GET /stats/cache with a CacheMetrics{hits, misses, hit_rate, evictions, size, capacity} shape — a URL and shape that do not match anything the server produces.

The server's actual route is:
  GET /cache/metrics  →  handlers::stats::cache_metrics
  Returns CombinedCacheMetrics {
    query_cache: { hits, misses, hit_rate, evictions, size, capacity },
    idempotency_cache_hits, idempotency_cache_misses,
    idempotency_lock_acquired, idempotency_lock_contention,
    idempotency_errors, idempotency_fallback_count
  }

### Fix
1. sdks/rust/src/models.rs: Added QueryCacheMetrics and CombinedCacheMetrics structs whose field names mirror the server's CombinedCacheMetrics exactly so serde deserialization requires no field renaming.
2. sdks/rust/src/resources/stats.rs (new file): Stats<'a> resource with cache_metrics() calling GET /cache/metrics (not /stats/cache).
3. sdks/rust/src/resources/mod.rs: Added pub mod stats.
4. sdks/rust/src/lib.rs: Re-exports Stats, CombinedCacheMetrics, QueryCacheMetrics; SynapseClient::stats() accessor.
5. sdks/rust/src/client.rs: Added SynapseClient::new() constructor, SynapseClient::stats() returning Stats<'_>, and get_query() helper for query-param GET requests.
6. sdks/rust/src/error.rs: Added Api{status,message}, NotFound(String), InvalidCursor(String), and Decode(String) variants needed by the transactions resource's semantic error mapping.
7. sdks/rust/Cargo.toml: Added wiremock = "0.6" dev-dependency.
8. Resources/stats.rs tests:
   - cache_metrics_calls_correct_endpoint: asserts the correct /cache/metrics path is called and the full CombinedCacheMetrics is deserialized.
   - cache_metrics_does_not_call_stats_cache_path: regression guard — the mock server only handles /cache/metrics; a call to /stats/cache would get a 404 and fail the test.
   - cache_metrics_returns_error_on_401.

---

## Issue #900 — Replace placeholder tests with real axum router integration tests

### Problem
tests/auth_and_signature_integration_test.rs contained 8 tests that never sent a single HTTP request to any router:
  - test_admin_endpoint_rejects_missing_bearer_token: body = assert!(true)
  - test_admin_endpoint_rejects_invalid_bearer_token: body = assert!(true)
  - test_admin_key_required_no_default: body = assert!(true)
  - test_callback_endpoint_rejects_missing_signature: only checked that a hex string was non-empty — never sent to the app
  - test_callback_endpoint_rejects_invalid_signature: only asserted two HMAC strings were not equal
  - test_callback_endpoint_accepts_valid_signature: only checked sig length
  - test_callback_endpoint_rejects_expired_timestamp: only called sign() helper
  - test_callback_endpoint_with_rotation_grace_period_secret: only checked two signatures were different All tests passed on every cargo test run and gave false confidence that src/middleware/auth.rs and src/middleware/signature_verification.rs were covered.

### Fix
Rewrote all 8 tests (plus added 2 new ones) to use tower::ServiceExt::oneshot to send real HTTP requests through minimal axum routers containing only the middleware under test, then assert on the HTTP response status code:

1. test_admin_endpoint_rejects_missing_bearer_token — builds admin_router(), sends GET /admin/test with no Authorization header, asserts 401.
2. test_admin_endpoint_rejects_invalid_bearer_token — sends wrong Bearer token, asserts 401.
3. test_admin_endpoint_accepts_valid_bearer_token — sends correct Bearer token, asserts 200.
4. test_admin_accepts_key_via_secrets_store — injects SecretsStore extension, sends matching key, asserts 200.
5. test_admin_rejects_unknown_key_via_secrets_store — key not in store, asserts 401.
6. test_callback_endpoint_rejects_missing_signature — no X-Webhook-Signature, asserts 401.
7. test_callback_endpoint_rejects_invalid_signature — wrong HMAC, asserts 401.
8. test_callback_endpoint_accepts_valid_signature — computes correct HMAC, asserts 200.
9. test_callback_endpoint_rejects_expired_timestamp — year-2001 timestamp, asserts 401 (replay protection).
10. test_callback_with_rotation_grace_period_secret — constructs SecretsStore with a grace-period previous secret, signs with it, asserts 200.
11. test_admin_auth_uses_constant_time_comparison — sends a prefix of the correct key (asserts 401) then the full key (asserts 200).
12. test_admin_key_required_no_default — removes ADMIN_API_KEY env var, no SecretsStore, asserts 401 (fail-closed behaviour).

No external services (no DB, no Redis, no Docker) required. Each test is fully self-contained.

A new tactical mission type behind the yellow (abandoned-moon) encounters: the player finds a derelict moon base and chooses whether to send down a landing party.

## 做了什么

给 moss 主循环加**计划完成门**:模型 `end_turn` 时若该 session 有 approved/executing 状态的 plan 且 steps 未全做完(completed+skipped)→ 否决完成、注入 correction 逼模型继续,逃生口是 `plan_step skip` 带理由。堵长任务最典型失败——"有 plan 没做完就声称 done"。

从 `main` 干净开,只含完成门 + 前提重构 + 测试,不夹带 observability 分支上的其他工作(skill-eval/discovery 等)。

## 改动(5 commit)

1. **per-session store** (`8006fe6`) — 把 `plan-tools.ts` 进程级单例换成按 `sessionKey` 路由的 store(`plan-controller-store.ts`)。多 session 嵌入式 host 不再串读对方 active plan。完成门前提。`PlanExecuteController` 业务逻辑不动。
2. **完成门本体** (`f59f62b`) — `evaluatePlanCompletionGate(request, deps)`,接进 CLI `createCliCompletionGate` 链(排 `evaluatePlanEvalCompletionGate` 后)+ MossAgent `completionGate` 包装(无 structured-pending 分支)。fail-open 5 路径;类型干净(required→optional 子类型,无适配)。
3. **MOSS_PLAN_GATE flag** (`f758f0c`) — default on。`=off` 可关做 A/B baseline。端到端验证:ON 拦+注入 correction,OFF 彻底 no-op。
4. **集成测试** (`2bacf21`) — 真起 MossAgent loop:create→approve+start→提前 end_turn→被否决→skip 两步→放行。
5. **off vs on mock 对比** (`6b2fcea`) — 同一偷懒 mock:off 放行无 correction、on 拦住注入 correction。证明机制方向(非真实收益)。

## 测试

6 个相关 spec 全过(plan-controller-store / plan-completion-gate 9 case / -integ / -ab / plan-tools-nudge / interaction-mode-exit)。build + typecheck 干净。完成门不依赖 observability 任何东西,从 main 独立成立。

## 已知限制(诚实)

1. **完成门真实收益未经验证** — 机制 + 集成测试证明方向对,但真实任务增益(真模型 + N≥3)未测;真 provider 试过 N=1 全噪声且烧 quota。`MOSS_PLAN_GATE` flag 留作后续真 A/B。
2. **retry 超限崩 run** — 模型死活不完成也不 skip,retry 用尽会 `throw Completion rejected` 崩 run(平台既有 exhaustion 行为,非 force-complete)。
3. **shared/no-session plan 不受 gate 覆盖** — `ctx.sessionKey` 空时走 shared 兜底,gate 查不到 → fail-open 放行。CLI 总有 sessionKey,影响主要在无 sessionKey 嵌入 host。
4. tech-debt(文档级):CLI 路径 gate 在 chain 和 wrapper 各跑一次(幂等纯函数,仅冗余)。

author: ctdegroot
body:
## The bug

The wall-adjacent cells carry an **imposed** `omega` (`omega_wall`) rather than a solved transport balance — but their **gradient** was still reconstructed from neighbours as though they were ordinary unknowns.

Measured on pitzDaily against the analytical gradient of the field we impose:

| | reconstructed / exact `\|grad omega\|` |
|---|---|
| wall-fixed cells | **0.256** (p5 0.205, p95 0.374) — a ~4x under-estimate |
| first interior ring | **2.236** (p5 0.845, p95 5.037) — the error does not stay local |

Two structural causes:
1. `omega_wall ~ 1/d**2` is strongly convex while Green–Gauss is a **linear** fit, over cells whose wall distance spans `8.5e-5 .. 5.6e-4` on this mesh.
2. The stencil folds in the **wall face**, whose `omega` a zero-gradient closure sets to the cell value — although the true profile diverges there.

## Why it matters

The fixed cells' gradient feeds `grad(k).grad(omega)` in `OmegaCrossDiffusion` and the `F1` blend, which set the blended constants for **both** scalar equations. The **k rows at those cells are not fixed**, so a genuinely solved equation was reading a 4x-wrong gradient — measured `CD_komega` there was **3.6x too small**. It also feeds the diffusion's non-orthogonal correction on faces to interior neighbours, which is negligible on this mesh (0.03%).

## Why this was hard to see

**A gradient-scheme A/B cannot detect it.** Every scheme treats these as ordinary cells, so all are wrong identically and the difference cancels: `CorrectedGreenGauss` vs `CompactGreenGauss` give **bit-identical** ratios and differ by 0.03% in `||R_omega||`. The comparison has to be against the *analytical* gradient.

## The fix

```
grad(omega_wall) = d(omega_wall)/dd * grad(d) + d(omega_wall)/dk * grad(k)
```

with **both partials taken by automatic differentiation of `omega_wall` itself**, so it cannot drift from whatever form that function implements (including the power-mean blend on the sibling branch).

- `grad(d)` is reconstructed **once at build** (pure geometry) with the exact boundary closure `d = 0` on the wall patches. The distance field is smooth and O(geometry), so unlike `omega` it reconstructs well.
- `closure_fields` overwrites **only** the wall-adjacent rows.
- Overwriting is safe: `omega` needs no wall-normal flux at these cells (the row is a value fixation, the wall closure is zero-gradient), so every consumer is inward.

## Testing

- New unit tests: the chain rule against **independent central finite differences** of `omega_wall` (not a restatement of the formula, so a blend change cannot silently desynchronize them), plus the pure `1/d**2` limit where `|grad| = 2 omega / d`.
- 76 turbulence/coupled unit tests pass; 9 turbulence integration tests pass (`test_coupled_rans`, `test_turbulent_channel`, `test_turbulent_cavity`).
- ruff check + format clean.

## Note

The pitzDaily-scale ratios quoted above were measured on the sibling branch (`feat/coupled-ptc-step-control`), which carries the validation harness used to probe them. This PR's own evidence is the unit tests plus the integration suite.

body: resolves https://github.com/loculus-project/loculus/issues/6906 partially resolves https://github.com/loculus-project/loculus/issues/6856 This PR moves all download and validation of submitted raw reads from the preprocessing to one raw reads processing service. It is currently disabled by default in the values.yaml and added as an override in the preview and e2e test values.yaml. We decided to create a separate service as we will additionally check raw reads for human contamination using deacon, see https://github.com/loculus-project/loculus/pull/6916 and deacon requires almost 8G of RAM, we didnt want to add this requirement to each prepro pod so it made sense to have one service that runs deacon. Additionally, it made sense to perform all file validation steps in the same place as downloading files from S3 twice (in prepro and the file-processing service) didnt make sense. This PR moves code from prepro into this service and additionally wraps the ENA raw read file validation JAR, called by the ENA submission CLI (see our fork: https://github.com/loculus-project/readtools) to ensure that submitted files are in a format accepted by ENA. ### Breaking Change Now, if an administrator would like to allow users to supply raw read input files and use the nextclade preprocessing pod they need to additionally enable the file processing service by adding the following to the values.yaml - this PR enables this on the previews and e2e but not in the default values.yaml so current users of Loculus should not be affected: ``` disableRawReadsProcessingService: false RawReadsProcessingService: raw_reads_processing_service_url: http://loculus-raw-reads-processing:5000 ``` ### Screenshot ### PR Checklist - [x] All necessary documentation has been adapted. - [x] The implemented feature is covered by appropriate, automated tests. - [x] Any manual testing that has been done is documented. ## Potential Future Issues - On the preview I submitted raw read files of invalid formats and confirmed they were rejected, however I also noted that raw reads validation is quite slow for larger files. - In my understanding users can still upload an interleaved file which will then be submitted to ENA as not a single (not paired) file in the manifest. 2 interleaved files can be submitted but should still get flagged as they are unlikely to share enough headers. 🚀 Preview: https://file-validation.loculus.org

author: adrianoesch
body:
Adds `chm_utils.livingdocs`, which renders a Livingdocs article's component tree to markdown.

**Why here.** chm-stream and chm-mcp both carry a copy of `render.py`, and they have **already diverged** — chm-mcp still has the original 141-line version while chm-stream's has been substantially rewritten. Since chm-stream embeds the output as vectors and chm-mcp serves it as retrieval context, any drift between them silently changes what search returns. Both repos already depend on `chm_utils`, and the module is pure standard library (`html` + `re`), so it adds no dependencies.

**What it does.**

```python
from chm_utils.livingdocs import publication_to_markdown, header_text, is_ticker

markdown = publication_to_markdown(document)               # capped for embedding
full     = publication_to_markdown(document, max_chars=None)
kicker   = header_text(document)                           # "Kicker\nTitle"
```

A `document` is any mapping with `content`, optionally `metadata`, `systemdata` and `custom` — the shape of both the collector's webhook payload and a row of `chm_core_prod.content.articles_v2`.

**Component handling is measured, not guessed.** The component and directive tables come from an inventory of every component type in the archive — 69 types over 89k current articles. That decided each rule: `subtitle` keeps its text in `title` not `text`; `catchword` is a topic keyword worth keeping; `seitenverweis` is navigational noise ("Region", "2/3") and is dropped. Unknown components degrade to plain paragraphs rather than vanishing.

**Ticker truncation.** Live tickers average ~57k characters and reach 300k, against ~3.5k for a normal article. `is_ticker` mirrors the `ticker-newsblog` rule in chm-models' `articles_v2_flattened`, restricted to signals present in a webhook payload. Since ticker posts are stored newest-first, the renderer keeps the header plus the newest `MAX_TICKER_POSTS` (5), then caps at `MAX_EMBED_CHARS` (8000) on a paragraph boundary.

**Version** bumped to 0.3.0 — new module, no change to existing APIs.

### Verification

35 tests in `tests/test_livingdocs.py`, all passing. Separately, the renderer was run over **1,000+ real articles** sampled from the archive (all document classes, 2008–2026) with zero exceptions and zero outputs above the cap; those real-payload integration tests live in the consumer repo alongside its fixtures.

### Follow-ups

- chmedia-data/chm-stream#60 pins this branch and deletes its local `src/render.py`; it needs repinning to `v0.3.0` once this merges and is released.
- chm-mcp still has its own `src/render.py` to delete — separate PR.

author: laykheangma95-ops
body:
Brings in the intent-classifier bundle described in `docs/HANDOFF.md` and completes the first two of its five steps. **`generateReply` is untouched — runtime behaviour is identical to today.**

## What's here

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/intentFeatures.js` | Shared featuriser — imported by both training and runtime |
| `lib/intentClassifier.ts` | Runtime classifier (int8 matmul, no network calls) |
| `data/intentTaxonomy.js` | 64 intents, 15 marked grounded |
| `data/intents.jsonl` | 222 seed examples across 13 intents |
| `data/intentModel.json` | Model trained on the seed set — 59.5% accuracy, not shippable |
| `scripts/seed-data.mjs` | Writes the starter set |
| `scripts/generate-questions.mjs` | Expands the corpus via one-time offline API calls |
| `scripts/train-intent.mjs` | Fits the model, prints accuracy |
| `scripts/intent-gap.mjs` | Reconciles taxonomy against the engine |
| `concierge/` | Standalone itinerary prototype, unrelated to the classifier |

Adds `intents:gap`, `intents:seed`, `intents:generate` and `intents:train` to `package.json`. `intents:generate` points at `generate-questions.mjs`; the superseded `generate-intent-data.mjs` that INTEGRATE.md references was dropped per HANDOFF step 2.

## Step 1 — tooling verified

`resolveJsonModule` was already enabled, so no tsconfig change was needed. The shared featuriser import — the one thing that must not break, since training and runtime silently diverge if they use different featurisers — was checked from both sides:

- Imports from a node `.mjs` script: 4096-dim output, L2 norm exactly 1.000000
- Khmer featurises correctly: 75 non-zero features on `តម្លៃ eSIM សម្រាប់ជប៉ុន`
- `tsc --noEmit` passes, and JSDoc types flow through as real types rather than `any` (verified with deliberate type errors)
- `next build` compiles it and the module executes under webpack

Retraining on the committed seed data reproduces **bit-identical** `weights` and `bias`, which rules out train/runtime featuriser drift.

## Step 2 — taxonomy reconciliation (report only, no answers written)

Full detail in `docs/intent-gap-analysis.md`; regenerate with `npm run intents:gap`.

The taxonomy describes 64 intents. The engine answers 13 via its `INTENTS` array plus 2 special-cased price paths. Critically, **the trained model covers only those 13 labels, not the taxonomy's 64** — nothing has ever been trained on the taxonomy, so 51 ids cannot currently be predicted at all.

| Status | Count |
| --- | --- |
| EXACT — same id both sides | 8 |
| COVERED — answered under a broader engine id | 11 |
| PARTIAL — mentioned in passing, not answered | 13 |
| NONE — no answer at all | 32 |

Five engine ids (`flight`, `airport`, `payment`, `support`, `refund_booking`) are absent from the taxonomy because it splits each into finer intents — 18 fine ids replacing those 5.

## Defects found in the taxonomy

Worth fixing before generating training data, since the generation prompt inherits them:

- **`domner_pro` is marked `grounded: true` but no such product exists.** The only mention anywhere is `LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md:85`, as a future funding idea. A grounded answer is impossible.
- **`payment_methods` claims a Wing integration the repo does not have.** Actual methods are Stripe cards and KHQR / ABA PayWay. `scripts/generate-questions.mjs:84` embeds the same wrong claim, so it would generate customers asking about Wing.
- **Uneven grounding data.** `visa` and `customs` have data for only 7 of 20 destinations, `safety_scams` for 8. Grounded answers need an explicit "no data for this country" path.
- **`scripts/generate-questions.mjs:111` requests model `claude-sonnet-4-6`**, which is not a valid model id — the script will fail before producing anything.

## Not done yet

Steps 3–5 of the handoff: grounded answer functions, generate + train, and the `generateReply` patch with `logUnresolved`. HANDOFF step 3 also asks that `data/intents.jsonl` and `data/intentModel.json` be deleted before regenerating; I've held that, because `lib/intentClassifier.ts` imports the model statically and deleting it breaks `typecheck` and `build` with no way to regenerate without an API key.

author: jn8128
body:
Auditing the interop fix turned up a worse problem next to it: several paths accepted a password and wrote plaintext. `zesven create -p secret` prompted for the password, threaded it into the write options and produced an archive 7-Zip lists as `Encrypted = -`; `--encrypt-headers` was parsed and never used; the WASM writer exposed `encryptHeader` to JavaScript and dropped it; the async writer takes the same `WriteOptions` as the sync one, has no encryption support at all, and ignored every encryption field; and the front-page example in `lib.rs` taught the same mistake. Setting a password now enables data encryption, requesting encryption without a password is an error rather than silent plaintext, the async writer refuses instead of pretending, and nonces come from the system CSPRNG instead of the wall clock mixed with a thread id. Two real bugs surfaced once encryption was actually on by default: encrypted solid blocks never received the password during extraction, and the wrong-password test was pinned to one error variant that only held while nonces were predictable.

This targets the branch of #8 and needs it merged first.

## Appendix

Before, with the CLI built from `main`:

```
$ zesven create cli.7z secret.txt -p hunter2
$ 7zz l -slt cli.7z | grep -E 'Method|Encrypted'
Method = LZMA2:21
Encrypted = -
```

The interop suite now runs the CLI binary itself, asks 7-Zip whether the entries are encrypted, and greps the archive for the plaintext marker. Reverting the one-line default makes it fail:

```
CLI create with []: 7-Zip reports an entry as unencrypted
```

Breaking for callers who relied on `password()` not encrypting, and on `encrypt_header(true)` without a password being a no-op. Both were bugs, and both produced archives that were not what the caller asked for.

Local run: `mise run ci` green, including `mise run test:interop` (22 tests).

body:
## Summary
- Fixes #363 — top bar logo failed to load with `net::ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND file:///logo.png`.
- Root cause: `TopBar.jsx` referenced the logo via an absolute `/logo.png` path. That resolves fine against the Vite dev server's `http://` origin, but `vite.config.js` sets `base: './'` specifically because production loads `index.html` via `file://` — under that protocol an absolute `/logo.png` resolves to the filesystem root, not the app directory, hence the 404 in both dev and packaged builds.
- Fix: moved `logo.png` from `renderer/public/` into `renderer/src/assets/` and `import` it in `TopBar.jsx` instead of hardcoding the path. Vite now fingerprints it and resolves the URL via `import.meta.url`, exactly like the JS/CSS bundles already do.

- [x] `npm run lint:all` — clean (pre-existing unrelated warnings in `PlayerBar.jsx` only)

author: richardjiangs
body:
## What

`switch.html` — one **self-contained** file you can drop on a microSD card and play with a controller. All 36 cars, same physics, same circuits, same modes.

The car code is **not modified**. The layer only writes the analog inputs the touch wheel and pedals already use (`state.padThrottle`, `state.padBrake`, `state.touchSteer`) and clicks the existing on-screen buttons — so every car drives exactly as it does in a browser.

## Controls

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| **Left stick** | Steer (analog) |
| **ZR** | Accelerate (analog) |
| **ZL** | Brake (analog). Keep holding once stopped → **reverse**; a dab of ZR takes drive again |
| **Right stick** | On-screen pointer — works over the garage **and** inside a running car |
| **A** | Click / continue |
| **B** | Back to the garage |
| **X** | Horn (hold) |
| **Y** | The car's speed feature — Speed Key / Track Package / Velocity / E85 / DRS, and ERS Override on the F1 cars |
| **L / R** | Gear down / up (bonus; the cars shift automatically) |
| **+** | Show/hide the cheat-sheet (it also fades on its own so it never sits on the telemetry pad) |

## How it's built

`tools/build-switch.mjs` derives `switch.html` from `index-offline.html`, so it never drifts from the real game.

## Verification

`tests/switch-test.mjs` installs a **simulated Switch Pro Controller** (`navigator.getGamepads`) and drives the whole game with it — **14 checks, all passing, no page errors**:

- 36 cards render at 1280×720; virtual cursor present; controller detected
- right stick moves the pointer; **A** clicks a card and boots the car
- **ZR** → `padThrottle` 1.0 · **ZL** → `padBrake` 1.0 · left stick → `touchSteer` 0.76 with `touchActive`, recentres to 0 on release
- **X** horn on/off · **Y** toggles the Speed Key · **B** returns to the garage

Reverse verified separately: `N → R` on held ZL at standstill, back to `G` on a dab of ZR.

`perf-test` and `browser-test` still pass.

## Honest caveats (also in `docs/SWITCH.md`)

I could not test on real Switch hardware from here:
- **Gamepad API** — verified against a simulated standard-mapping Pro Controller, but Nintendo's browser is a limited WebKit build and may not expose `navigator.getGamepads`. If it doesn't, the panel says "no controller" and the touchscreen still works.
- **Memory** — ~12 MB because every car is embedded; the Switch browser has a modest budget. Fallback documented (serve the ordinary lazy-loading `index.html` over Wi-Fi).
- **Face-button positions** — uses the W3C standard mapping by physical position (bottom/right/left/top = B/A/Y/X on a Nintendo pad); a driver reporting them swapped would exchange A/B and X/Y.

`docs/SWITCH.md` also covers both ways to get it onto the console (Wi-Fi server on any Switch; SD card via homebrew).

author: ayanami770
body:
Roadmap item 2.9. Non-breaking.

## Why this is worth more than it looks

Every layout defect this library has had was a **render-at-a-non-default-configuration** bug:

- a section header that ellipsised to "Encrypted tra…" at 200% font scale
- an empty state whose call-to-action fell off a bounded parent
- a list row sitting under the 48dp touch target

None are visible while developing at default settings. That is precisely why all of them survived until an audit went looking — and why the roadmap calls this the highest defects-caught-per-hour item on the list.

## What lands

`Previews.kt` adds a `@KansoPreviews` multipreview — **light / dark / 200% font scale / RTL** — stamped on all nine components. 10 preview functions × 4 configurations = **40 renders**.

Several are written as the regression they guard:

| preview | guards |
|---|---|
| long section header | must wrap, not ellipsise |
| long status value | must wrap in its own half, not starve the label |
| loading button beside idle | width must not change when work starts |
| empty state with CTA | the action must stay reachable |

RTL uses Arabic. kanso uses `start`/`end` throughout, so a preview that mirrors cleanly is the *evidence* for that claim rather than an assertion about it.

## Two departures from the plan

**`@PreviewScreenSizes` dropped.** kanso has no adaptive behaviour yet (roadmap 3.5), so a component at tablet width shows nothing a phone-width one does not — it would have tripled the render count for no signal. Worth adding *with* the adaptive work. Similarly `@PreviewFontScale`'s six steps collapse to the one that actually breaks layouts.

**Two things the plan didn't anticipate**, both surfaced by actually building it:

1. The roadmap said "zero dependency changes — `ui-tooling-preview` is already `api`". It isn't any more: #13 removed it, correctly, since nothing used it. It returns here as `implementation` — the right classification for kanso's own tooling, and it stays off consumers' compile classpath.
2. **material3 no longer brings `material-icons-core` transitively**, so `Icons.Filled.*` doesn't resolve. Rather than add an icon set to a library that deliberately ships none, `Previews.kt` draws a single `ImageVector` inline. The previews are checking layout, not iconography.

Previews render with `dynamicColor = false`: the brand scheme is what's under review, not a wallpaper-derived one.

## Verification

```
:kanso:testDebugUnitTest   10 tests, 0 failures
:kanso:assembleRelease     BUILD SUCCESSFUL
:demo:assembleDebug        BUILD SUCCESSFUL
```

No warnings. Note CI compile-checks the preview code but cannot *render* it — catching what these previews are for still needs a human with Android Studio open, until screenshot goldens land (roadmap 3.4).

author: rbstephenson
body:
## What

Four destructive prune helpers in `scanner.py` each build their own normalized scan-root set and their own membership closure:

- `_prune_stale_paths`, `_prune_stale_stl_files`, `_prune_stale_models` — three byte-identical copies of an exact-or-descendant test
- `_prune_ignored` — a fourth, subtly *different* one: exact membership only, used as the stop condition for the ignore-rule walk-up

Duplicated safety-critical comparison logic that can drift. A wrong answer here either deletes live data or keeps stale rows forever.

Adds `services/path_boundary.py`: a frozen, dependency-free `PathBoundary` with `contains()` (exact-or-descendant), `is_root()` (exact only), and a `normalize()` helper.

## Design points worth a look

**`contains()` and `is_root()` are deliberately not one method.** The ignore prune climbs from a model's folder toward the filesystem root and must stop only when it steps *onto* a scan root. Descendant matching there would halt the climb immediately and silently stop ignoring nested folders. Collapsing them is the obvious future "simplification", so the reason lives in `is_root`'s docstring.

**An empty boundary matches nothing**, and the type cannot express "match everything". "No roots configured" must never decay into handing a destructive prune the whole library.

**`from_paths()` drops blank entries** — `normpath("")` is `"."`, which as a root would match every relative path. Found while writing the test, not the code.

**Deliberately not built on `services/path_guard.py`.** That module resolves symlinks via `realpath`/`commonpath` — right for sanitizing user-supplied paths, wrong here. Prune membership must be a pure string comparison against what's stored in the DB, so a detached mount or a deleted folder compares identically to a live one. Routing it through `path_guard` would make an offline root's contents stop matching, which is the mount-detach data-loss scenario the prune gates exist to prevent. Documented in the module docstring so the two don't get merged later.

Casing follows host filesystem semantics via `os.path.normcase`, unchanged from the closures being replaced. Intentional for this task — making *stored* path identity host-independent is separate work under [STUDIO-357]/[STUDIO-359].

## Scope

**No call sites migrated; no production caller yet.** [STUDIO-230] rewires the four prune helpers onto this. Scanner behavior is unchanged by this PR — which also means the module is unused until 230 lands. That's the sequencing the epic calls for: 230 alone carries the risk of touching four destructive prune paths, and keeping it separate makes that diff reviewable on its own.

## Tests

36 added — sibling-prefix (`STL` vs `STLBackup`), empty/missing input, dedup, immutability, all asserted in both directions.

Includes **characterization tests** that assert the new class agrees with the four closures still inlined in `scanner.py`, giving [STUDIO-230] a pinned baseline to refactor against.

- `test_path_boundary.py` + `test_scanner.py` (172) pass in a throw-away container
- `ruff` clean

⚠️ CI is Linux-only, so the Windows-casing test is `skipif`-skipped there — the suite reports "1 skipped" and would do so even if that branch were broken. Those assertions were run natively on a Windows host to confirm they pass (`os.name = nt`). Flagging because this acceptance criterion is only ever half-verified by CI.

## Feature flag

None — internal refactoring, no user-facing capability.

body:
Closes #862 — the three non-blocking items from the review on #861, all in the sidebar's bulk-selection handlers.

## 1. Bulk entries now require the right-clicked row to be in the selection

Took the issue's first candidate (gate on membership) rather than adopting the right-clicked node, since it can't destroy a selection by accident and matches how file managers behave. New derived value in `Sidebar.tsx`:

```ts
const bulkTarget: "obj" | "db" | null =
  ctxMenu !== null && selectedNodeKeys.has(ctxMenu.nodeKey) ? selectionKind : null;
```

All three gates now read `bulkTarget === "db" && size >= 2`, `bulkTarget === "obj" && insertTarget !== null`, and `bulkTarget === "obj" && size >= 2`.

- Right-clicking database C while A and B are selected shows only **Drop Database…** — no more menu carrying two similar entries aimed at different rows.
- The cross-kind leak is closed without a separate `nodeType` check: an `obj:` key can only be in an object selection, so **Delete N selected objects…** / **Add N selected as Insert Sources** can no longer appear on a database, schema, column, git, or stage row while ≥2 objects are selected.
- Right-click still never modifies the selection.
- `size > 0` on the insert-sources gate became redundant (membership implies non-empty) and was dropped.

## 2. Feedback while the retention fetch runs

`dropSelectedDatabases` and the single-database `dropDatabaseNode` both hold a `message.loading(…, 0)` toast while the per-database Time Travel lookups run, dismissed just before `modal.confirm` opens. The single-node path clears it in a `finally` so the fallback can't leak it.

## 3. One summary toast per batch, all-failed included

`deleteSelectedObjects` and `dropSelectedDatabases` gained an `else` branch reporting `Dropped 0 of N …` as `message.error`. `exportSelectedDatabases`'s blanket `else` was split so an all-failed export is an error rather than a warning reading "0 of N databases exported cleanly".

## Docs

Per the docs-with-code rule: `frontend/src/components/layout/README.md` ("Multi-select") documents `bulkTarget` vs `selectionKind`, why membership pins the node kind, the loading toasts, and the one-summary-per-batch rule; `FEATURES.md` states that bulk entries only appear on a selected row and describes the progress toast and the all-failed summary.

## Test plan

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npm test` — 288 tests / 20 files pass

Item 4 of the review (test coverage for the gesture logic) is deliberately out of scope per the issue — it needs `onSelect`'s inline handlers extracted into a testable module.

author: lyricalmyricalbooks
body:
💡 **What**: Replaced `String.prototype.localeCompare()` with basic string comparison operators (`<` and `>`) inside array `.sort()` callbacks for properties that represent dates (`createdAt`, `latestDate`, `date`, `added`, `last`).

🎯 **Why**: `localeCompare()` is notoriously slow in JavaScript environments because it accounts for complex internationalization (i18n) rules. For standard ISO 8601 date strings or simple timestamp strings, simple lexicographical string comparisons (`<` and `>`) provide the exact same chronological sorting order but execute significantly faster.

📊 **Impact**: Reduces execution time of sorting arrays during rendering. For sorting collections, `localeCompare` can be 10x to 100x slower. By swapping to standard operators, the render-blocking time of sort operations is heavily reduced.

🔬 **Measurement**: Verify that lists sort chronologically as before (e.g., customers list, mailing list, trip chips). Run `npm run test` to verify all 478 tests pass without regression.

author: andtii
body:
Closes #28. Phase 2 of the "express any design system" roadmap.

## Why

A design system couldn't state its motion personality. Timings were inlined in recipes — `0.15s` here, `0.2s` there, **32 literals across the two shipped systems** — so nothing could be retuned in one place. And `prefers-reduced-motion` was handled *nowhere* in the repo, which is an accessibility gap rather than a nicety.

`system.motion` declares `durations` and `easings`, emitting `--duration-*` / `--ease-*`:

```ts
motion: {
    durations: { fast: '150ms', normal: '200ms' },
    easings: { standard: 'ease' },
}
```

```css
transition: background var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard);
```

Both design systems keep their **exact previous timings**, so nothing moves visually. What changes is that the values are named, retunable, and reduced-motion aware.

## Two decisions worth recording

**The neutralizer is emitted per design system, not written into `base.css`** as the issue proposed. Duration *keys* are DS-declared, so `base.css` can only neutralize the recommended ones and would miss a system's own `--duration-emphasized-decelerate`. `base.css` still carries one for the recommended keys, covering apps with no design system at all. Same reasoning that moved `@property` registration out of `base.css` in #30 — the category model paying for itself.

**`0.01ms`, not `0ms`.** A zero duration suppresses `transitionend` / `animationend` entirely, and presence/exit-animation coordination (#29) waits on those events to know when an overlay may close. `0.01ms` is visually instant and still fires them. The selector is `:root, [data-theme]` at (0,1,0), emitted last — `:where(:root)` would lose to every theme block, so reduced motion would silently stop working the moment a theme was selected.

## Looping animations are deliberately not tokenized

Collapsing an infinite spinner's duration would make it spin *absurdly fast* rather than stop — worse than leaving it. It needs `animation: none` under a recipe condition, which is #31. Filed as **#43** and noted in the skill so a generator doesn't get it wrong.

## Incidentally

`motion` is the first category with a nested path (`['motion','durations']`), so it exercises the full-path traversal added in #40 rather than leaving it theoretical.

The validator rejects a unitless duration — CSS ignores `150` outright, so the transition silently never runs and no event ever fires. That's the one grammar where a mistake is invisible, so it's the one that's checked.

## Verification

Browser-verified against the real cascade, not just the emitted text (this PR's sibling, #45, exists because reading the CSS alone missed a bug):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `--duration-fast` with no theme / explicit light / explicit dark | `150ms` in all three |
| switch `transitionDuration` | `0.15s` — identical to the literal it replaced |
| reduced-motion rules present | two: `zero.fallback` (no-DS case) and `zero.tokens` (operative) |
| neutralizer position within `zero.tokens` | index 3, after the last `[data-theme]` block at index 2 — wins the (0,1,0) tie |

`pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (162), `pnpm verify:pack` all green. 20 snapshots updated: literals → tokens, computed values unchanged.

body:
Last of three. #230 built the pipeline, #231 filled it and gated it, this one switches the skill over and deletes the duplicate.

Net: **-7408 lines.**

## What changed

`SKILL.md` starts every component search at [`/llms-components.txt`](https://remocn.dev/llms-components.txt) and reads one component at `/docs/<section>/<name>.md`. Fetching is described in plain prose rather than tied to a specific tool, because the skill installs into Claude Code, Cursor and opencode alike. It is explicitly told to stop and say so when the network is unavailable — a wrong prop name fails at build, but an invented duration silently clips the animation.

Deleted: the 146 bundled component references, plus `design.md`, `motion-principles.md` and `anti-patterns.md` — those three now live under [`/docs/craft/`](https://remocn.dev/docs/craft). Cross-references in `anatomy.md` and `archetypes/` were repointed at URLs.

Kept, per the plan: the two tiers and their differing APIs, the Remotion API sketch, canvas and timing rules, the remocn-specific gotchas, `anatomy.md` and the archetype recipes. A simple animation edit still needs no network at all.

## Guarding the new dependency

The architecture now depends on those URLs staying valid, so `docs-meta.test.ts` gains three checks: every `remocn.dev/docs` URL cited anywhere under `skills/` must resolve to a real page, the component index must still be cited, and the bundled catalog must stay deleted. The URL check was mutation-tested — adding a link to a non-existent page fails it.

## Corrections that came out of this

- **`slide-swap` and `spring-settle` are not `TransitionSeries` presentations.** They are scene sequencers that take a `scenes` array and own the whole timeline. The tier section previously implied otherwise; `SKILL.md` now says so explicitly. They also sit under `/docs/transitions/` despite not being transitions — left alone here, worth a separate look.
- **`ecosystem-constellation` and `live-code-compilation` accept a `speed` prop** that neither page listed. Both now document it, with a note that `live-code-compilation`'s fixed typing constants make it a shift rather than a clean time-remap.

## Sequencing

`/llms-components.txt` and `/docs/craft/*` return 404 on remocn.dev today, because #230 and #231 are on `staging` and the site deploys from `main`. All three move to `main` together, so the URLs come alive in the same deploy that switches the skill over. Worth not splitting them.

## Out of scope, found on the way

Three pre-existing defects, none introduced here and none fixed here:

- `infinite-bento-pan` exposes a `panSpeed` control as `min: 0.25, max: 3` in `config.ts`, but the component applies `Math.min(1, panSpeed)` — the whole 1.0–3.0 range renders identically.

That control is not decoration: on mobile the sheet covers the canvas whose click is the normal way to deselect, so without it a user would be stuck. At `md` and above the markup is byte-identical (`md:static md:w-80 md:shrink-0`) and the dismiss control is `md:hidden`.

## Debt 2 closed — pointer-only placement

The overlay is now focusable, selects on focus, carries `<label>, <type> field on page <n>` plus an `aria-describedby` hint, and accepts arrow keys to move by 1 % (Shift: 5 %) and Alt+arrows to resize.

Purely additive — the pointer path is untouched and the handlers emit the **same** `onStop`/`onResize` percentage payloads, clamped to the page as the keyboard equivalent of `bounds="parent"`. The clamp also re-clamps the *other* axis, so a field already past an edge is pulled back rather than left hanging; a test pins that.

## Verification

- **114 unit tests** across the three envelope-creator suites, including 10 new keyboard-placement tests (focus selects, name and hint, all four directions, the Shift step, clamping at both edges, Alt resize both dimensions, the 1 % floor, ignored keys)
- **New E2E** `e2e/edoc-workbench-closeout.spec.cjs`: **14 passed** on Chromium + Mobile Chrome — named zoom controls with announced level, zoom driven from the keyboard, keyboard move and Alt-resize, **the rail on-screen and dismissible at 412 px** (the previously clipped case), the desktop rail staying inline with no overflow, and a scoped real-browser axe pass
- **Regressions:** `edoc-field-properties-panel`, `edoc-placed-field-overlay`, `edoc-envelope-creator-shell`, `edoc-envelope-sidebar` and the full `edoc-recruiter-send-and-sign` — **53 passed** on both projects
- Full suite: 115 files / **1266 tests** passing. Lint 0 errors, typecheck, build, `git diff --check` clean; tokens confirmed in the built CSS. **No 9/10/11 px interface text and no raw hex remain anywhere in the envelope-creator tree or `EnvelopeCreator.jsx`.**

Two shell assertions were rewritten because the rail's collapsed classes are now responsive — the behaviour they check is unchanged, and I added one covering the mobile dismiss control.

## Debt 3 is NOT closed here

The signing-surface axe findings (`color-contrast x1`, `label x3`) live in `SigningRoom`/`SignerField` — a different surface from the creator. Folding an unrelated component into a workbench diff would make both unreviewable, so they are the subject of the final E-Docs audit, and this slice does not claim them.

author: jeremiedrazic
body:
Second batch of audit fixes — **auth robustness & error handling**. Findings H3, H4, M1, M2, M3, M5, M8.

## High

- **H3 — Atomic registration.** `registerUser` was two sequential steps (Supabase auth account, then Prisma profile) with no rollback. If step 2 failed (e.g. a taken username → P2002, previously a raw 500), a ghost auth account was left behind, permanently blocking the email and breaking login. Now: P2002 → `USERNAME_TAKEN`, and the orphaned auth account is deleted (best-effort compensation). Test added.
- **H4 — No crash on deleted profile.** `auth.me()` only swallowed 401; a valid session with a missing profile row (404) bubbled an `ApiError` to the router's error boundary (crash screen). Now 404 also → `null`, so guards redirect to `/login`. Test added.

## Medium

- **M1** — `FORBIDDEN` added to the client `ErrorCode` union (translated but previously unreachable → 403s showed a generic message).
- **M2** — The error-handler maps Prisma errors that escape the service layer (`P2025` → 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, `P2003` → 409 `INVALID_REFERENCE`) instead of a misleading 500. New codes + EN/FR translations; `isRecordNotFoundError`/`isForeignKeyError` exported from the services package.
- **M3** — `logoutUser` no longer swallows a failed Supabase sign-out: the route logs it but still clears cookies and returns 200. Test added.
- **M5** — Rate-limit 429s carry a typed `RATE_LIMITED` code (+ EN/FR) via `errorResponseBuilder`.
- **M8** — `redirectTo` validation extracted to `parseInternalRedirect`, hardened against `//evil.com` and `/\evil.com` open-redirect vectors. Colocated tests.

## Notes

- New codes keep full EN/FR i18n parity (23 keys), per ADR-0025 (API sends codes, client translates).
- The apps/api db mock now exports `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` — the error-handler's new Prisma checks would otherwise throw on `instanceof undefined` (caught by the test suite).

All green: typecheck (19 tasks), tests, lint, i18n parity.

Kolu's default Nix package carried a second copy of the production workspace, a second Node major, full Git packaging, and build-only pnpm material. **This cuts the exact runtime closure from 1,351,008,904 bytes to 696,462,408 bytes—a 48.4% reduction—while advancing nixpkgs and preserving the application and hosted-terminal toolset.**

The largest win is structural: the commit-specific client derivation now copies and stamps only `index.html`, while its content-hashed assets remain linked to the cache-stable build. The package also aligns TSX with Kolu's stock Node 24.15 runtime, uses Git's minimal output, retains only node-pty's compiled runtime addon, and removes compiler, bundler, test, type-only, and Vazhi-only packages from the shared production tree.

A clean idli check established that `/nix/store/5a8ysg1jnj8jmzzyfcfw7rvpvnp5rfpa-nodejs-24.15.0` was absent before the build. The `ci::nix` log then copied that exact full Node output and `/nix/store/q1r7qkrnbhakljr4j228v2yi2874jkl9-nodejs-slim-24.15.0` from `https://cache.nixos.org`; it never built a Node derivation. author: michaelkrisper
body:
💡 **What:**
Extracted the calculation of `dragSeries` and `withoutDrag` into a top-level `useMemo` block, rather than computing it inline inside the JSX `map` render cycle. Combined the multiple `.find`, `.filter`, and `.map` array scans into a single iterative pass loop for optimal performance.

🎯 **Why:**
The previous implementation performed an O(N) `.find()`, an O(N) `.filter()`, and an O(N) `.map()` on the entire series list repeatedly every render within the loop. Moving this to a memoized top-level calculation and doing the heavy lifting in a single pass significantly reduces rendering overhead, which is critical for smooth high-frequency state updates like drag-and-drop operations.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
In synthetic loop benchmarks simulating 10,000 renders with 1,000 series, the unoptimized approach took ~1050ms, whereas the optimized memoized approach completed in ~34-38ms, representing an approximate 96% reduction in computation time for list construction.

author: inferenceailab
body:
Closes #40. **Test-only — no production changes.**

## Why there is no code

The behaviour was already built: `WorkflowRegistry` keys on `(Id, Version)` and keeps every registered version, `WorkflowClient` starts on the latest or a pinned version, and `WorkflowDispatcher` resolves each step against the version recorded on the instance. Every acceptance criterion on #40 was satisfied by #35 and #36.

What was missing was evidence. The registry keying on `(Id, Version)` proves nothing on its own — the instance record and the dispatcher both have to honour the pin, and only a running instance shows that they do.

## The six facts

- a new start takes the latest registered version
- a start can pin an older one, for a caller that must not drift mid-rollout
- an instance records the version it began on
- a registry that has dropped a version reports so
- **an instance pinned to an unregistered version fails loudly**, with a message naming the version and saying old versions must stay registered until they drain
- a duplicate `(Id, Version)` registration is rejected at startup

That fifth one is the one worth having. Dropping an old definition while instances still reference it is a plausible deploy mistake, and the engine cannot rescue those instances — so the failure has to be loud, and where someone can still act on it.

## Verified

`dotnet build` clean with warnings-as-errors; **36 + 269 + 124** passing with `CI=true`.
