- Load: es 801,183 entries / 1.18M forms / 674k redirects; pt 427,311 / 496k / 348k. DB grew 4.2 → 6.0 GB (matches the ~1.8 GB estimate; prod's 6.35 GB headroom is comfortable).
- **Lemma-ranks acceptance (the go/no-go): es 97.03% mass-matched (30,313 lemmas), pt 95.50% (26,742) — both over the ≥95% bar.**
- Live extraction spot checks: distinción words split correctly (*cerveza* → `cas /θeɾˈbeθa/ lam /seɾˈbesa/`), dialect-neutral words stay shared (*gratis* → untagged), pt bare-tag buckets populate (*saudade* → `br /sawˈda.d͡ʒi/ eu /sɐwˈda.dɨ/`).
- Reflexive routing confirmed the design: es token *ducha* resolves to `duchar` (not `ducharse`), and pt `queixar-se` has **no kaikki entry at all** — the new headword strip variants are the only match path for hyphenated reflexives.

## Backend

- **Loader/scripts**: `es`,`pt` in `LOAD_LANGUAGES` + the `DEFAULT_LANGUAGES` lists of the redirects rebuilder, wordfreq export, and ranks build; es/pt token patterns in `isRealWordToken` (it throws for unknown languages).
- **Extractor** (`extract/ipa.ts`): pt bare-`["Brazil"]`/`["Portugal"]` bucketer (narrower regions like Rio-de-Janeiro dropped, mirroring the bare-US discipline); es θ-twin classifier — exact θ→s twin, else fuzzy (stress-marks stripped + s-degemination, catching seseo merges like `/bisθeˈɾal/`→`/biseˈɾal/`); unpaired θ → `cas` only; non-θ variants stay shared. The `extractGrammarPatch` persistence gate + `GrammarPatch.ipa` type now cover all 7 buckets (a br-only bag — the typical pt case — previously would have been silently dropped).
- **LLM steering**: the `englishIpaDialect` prompt param generalized to a single resolved `ipaDialect` (new `getIpaDialectForTargetLanguage` helper) through all passes and the five service callers; Spanish instructions now dialect-parameterized (Castilian vs LatAm blocks), a new Portuguese instruction block (BR/EU, hyphenated pronominal headwords); `grammar-tool-schema` + `sanitizeGrammarIpa` accept the 4 new buckets; form-facet IPA writes to the pref'd bucket for any dialect language.
- **Checkpoint matching**: `stripReflexiveSuffix` in core (es `-arse/-erse/-irse`, pt `-se`) feeding both `foldUserHeadwordCandidates` and per-part MWE splitting (so *darse cuenta de* reduces to `dar`+`cuenta` — the reflexive spelling could never match token-resolved lemmas); es/pt `MWE_PARTICLES`.

## Packages

- `KAIKKI_LANGUAGES` += es/pt (single allowlist — grounding, badges, checkpoint reviews, sweep, coverage all light up).
- `LANGUAGE_GRAMMAR` es/pt gain `ipa`; `LANGUAGE_CARD_FACE` es/pt recognition backs reveal IPA (mirroring en).

## Deviation from the reviewed plan

The plan said es/pt display forms could use the default path ("verified clean"). Wrong at the mechanism level: es/pt head expansions have no ` • ` separator, so `extractDisplayForm` returns the whole head line (`pie m (plural pies)`) — a card title, not a display form. Both languages now `skipDisplayForm` like en/de, and `display_form` stays out of their grammar-field lists.

Specs (SRS language gate now "ru/en/de/es/pt", READER-SPEC extraction rules, DATA-MODEL bucket docs, SPEC.md five language blocks) and the `add-wiktionary-language` skill (dead `config.ts` step removed, `LANGUAGE_EXTRACTORS` registry + dialect-bucket pattern documented) updated alongside. No user-facing strings — catalogs untouched.

## Tests

- 542 backend unit tests green (incl. new: es θ-twin exact/fuzzy/unpaired/neutral fixtures from real dump entries, pt bare-tag + narrower-drop, `extractGrammarPatch` persistence-gate case, reflexive strip + non-reflexive negatives, pronominal MWE split, es form-facet bucket, es/pt tokenizer). Full integration suite 54 files / 251 passed. Core 118 + web 194 green; `check:types` + `lint` clean.
- Two pre-existing tests used `es` as the canonical *unsupported* language (fast-gloss gate, checkpoint 422) — updated to `fr`.
- Local snapshot now carries all five languages + ranks, so `pnpm db:reset` restores them.

## After merge

1. Trigger `.github/workflows/load-kaikki-prod.yaml` from main in a low-traffic window (grounding + checkpoint matching offline during TRUNCATE+COPY; ~54% more rows than last run). **Check the workflow log shows a cache HIT on `kaikki-raw-v1`** — the extraction rules are validated against that dump; a fresh download needs re-validation first.
2. `doppler run --config prd -- npx tsx scripts/build-lemma-ranks.ts es pt` from apps/backend (per-language atomic publish, safe live).

author: vjsingh1984
body:
## The defect

ADR-0005 D4 defines billable as `fresh input + cache split + output (+ unfolded reasoning)`, and the proxy settles on it. Two other paths kept a narrower `tokens_in + tokens_out`, so **the same call was counted differently depending on who asked**:

| path | formula | a call with 40 fresh-in / 60 cache-read / 20 out |
|---|---|---|
| proxy settle (`billable()`) | D4 | **120** |
| in-process bindings → budget ledger | narrow | **60** ← 2× under-count |
| dashboard + `sandhi usage` | narrow | **60** ← operator sees less than was charged |

The bindings' under-count is the serious half: `bindings/{python,node}/src/lib.rs` recorded the narrow number into a real budget ledger, and the in-process path is how **Victor** consumes Sandhi. Any cache-heavy workload was admitted well past its cap.

The narrowness was deliberate *once* — an ADR-0005 Phase-0 note froze `billable_tokens()` so accounting wouldn't shift while the proxy migrated. Phase 0 is over, and the proxy's own test carried the leftover as a comment: *"unifying the display helpers onto billable() is a tracked follow-up"*. This closes it.

## The fix

- **`billable_parts()` is the one formula** over raw components. `billable()` (UsageV2) and `UsageEvent::billable_tokens()` (flat event) both route through it, so they cannot drift again.
- **`Bucket` exposes the full split** — `cache_creation_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, and an exact `billable_tokens` — surfaced in the dashboard table and `sandhi usage`. What an operator reads is now what the ledger charged.
- **The SQL sums D4 per row.** The reasoning fold is a *per-call* decision, so summing columns and folding afterwards is wrong whenever some calls fold reasoning and others report it separately. `store_matches_core_billable` pins the SQL against the Rust formula **and** asserts the naive aggregate form gives a different answer (41 vs 33 on its fixtures) — so the test can't pass for the wrong reason.

## Behaviour change

In-process spend via the Python/Node `Gateway` **increases** for any call with cache reads/writes or separately-reported reasoning tokens. A cap that was silently admitting more than it should now enforces as written. **Proxy enforcement is unchanged** — it was already correct.

Every affected assertion was re-derived from its fixture, not bumped to match output: bob 240→245, alice 180→190, 300→340/350, 15→17/18, 60→120, 11→15, and 120→135 with its budget probes moved (865 remaining, not 880 — the old probe would have flipped to false).

## Verification

```
cargo fmt --all --check                                   clean
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings      clean
cargo test --workspace                                     16 suites, 0 failures
python -m pytest bindings/python/tests/ -q                 22 passed
(cd bindings/node && npx napi build --platform && npm test) 16 passed
cargo llvm-cov --workspace --fail-under-lines 75            82.16%
```

No wire-contract change: `UsageEvent`'s fields are untouched, `Bucket` is store-internal. Relates to TD-0009 D6 (one semantics, two implementations, proven equal) — this applies that rule to the definition TD-0009 was written against.

## Summary

- remove the separate Webots supervisor artifact and dynamic spawn protocol
- make the Webots controller the externally driven clock and output authority
- add opaque simulation epochs plus serialized reset hooks for simulation-time services
- clear epoch-derived state across the standard stateful services and telemetry stores

## Why

Phase 12 makes Webots own the controller process lifecycle. A controller restart must create a fresh simulation epoch while resident services reset their simulation-derived state without requiring process replacement.

## Impact and migration

This is a pre-v1 breaking simplification. The retired supervisor and legacy simulation messages are removed without compatibility shims. The framework train must publish before the CLI consumer PR merges.

Affected repositories and land order:

1. `phoxal/framework` (this PR)
2. framework release train publication
3. `phoxal/phoxal-cli`
4. `phoxal/organization` standing-document reconciliation

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`
- focused controller, runner, macro, bus, epoch/reset, service-state, and release-coherence tests
- workspace all-target check
- strict workspace Clippy
- full serial workspace test suite
- `cargo xtask coherence`
- `cargo xtask release verify --tag v0.40.1`

All passed locally.

## Independent review

Claude Code Opus reviewed the complete framework change in the same session across two reports. All reported findings were resolved and the affected checks were rerun. Per the maintainer's later direction, no additional Claude session was started.

## Risk

The blast radius includes the framework runner, scheduling, stateful standard services, Webots controller packaging, and the public pre-v1 simulation API. The main failure modes are stale state surviving an epoch change or reset serialization racing normal callbacks; the added unit, trybuild, and service-state tests cover those boundaries.

author: jorgemoralespou
body:
## Summary

Removes Octant from the workshop base image and from the workshop session console options. Covers item 1 of the 4.0 vulnerability triage: **7 CRITICAL + 126 HIGH** vulnerabilities in `base-environment` and the 5 workshop images, on binaries that are archived upstream with no possible fix (no release since `0.25.1`, archived 2023).

## The vcluster question

The wiring suggested Octant was the console used when a virtual cluster was enabled. It is not, and has not been since 2.0.

- `application_vcluster.py` set only `console.octant.version: latest`, never `console.vendor`. Both readers of the vendor default to `kubernetes`.
- Commit `9a072ef` (2022-05-20) *removed* `"vendor": "octant"` from the vcluster patch and taught `start-console` to pass `--kubeconfig`. The next commit re-added only the version pin.
- The 2.0.0 release notes confirm Octant was used with a virtual cluster only when explicitly "selected as the web console to use in place of the standard Kubernetes dashboard".

The dashboard works against a virtual cluster because the same vcluster patch sets `security.token.enabled: false`, so no service account token is mounted and `start-console` falls through to `--kubeconfig $HOME/.kube/config` (the vcluster kubeconfig copied in by `setup.d/01-kubernetes.sh`).

So the only thing the patch still did was pin `0.25.1` over the `0.12.1` default for anyone who opted in explicitly.

## Changes

**Base image** (`workshop-images/base-environment/`)
- `Dockerfile`: dropped both Octant download blocks
- deleted `opt/eduk8s/sbin/start-octant` and `opt/eduk8s/etc/supervisor/octant.conf`
- `opt/eduk8s/etc/profile.d/02-console.sh`: collapsed the vendor `case` to the dashboard, warns and falls back when an unsupported vendor is set
- `opt/eduk8s/sbin/start-container`: dropped `ENABLE_CONSOLE_OCTANT_PROCESS`

**session-manager**
- `application_vcluster.py`: dropped the now-dead `applications` patch
- `workshopsession.py`: the `kubernetes-dashboard-csrf` secret is no longer conditional on the vendor

**CRD + chart**
- removed `session.applications.console.octant` from the Workshop CRD; `vendor` is retained as a deprecated no-op
- regenerated the embedded session-manager tarball via `make refresh-operator-embeds`

**Docs**
- `workshop-definition.md`: Octant example replaced with the deprecation note for `vendor`
- `project-roadmap.md`: dropped the "Octant will be removed" bullet, now done
- `version-4.0.0.md`: Features Changed entry + Deprecations entry

## Compatibility

`vendor: octant` in an existing workshop keeps validating and the session still starts, now with the Kubernetes dashboard and a warning logged. A leftover `console.octant` block is silently pruned by the structural CRD schema rather than rejected, so no existing `Workshop` resource fails admission.

## Verification

- no Octant references remain in tracked files outside the historical 2.0.0 release notes and the intentional deprecation prose
- `bash -n` clean on both modified shell scripts; `py_compile` clean on both handlers
- supervisord includes `supervisor/*.conf` by glob, so deleting the program file is sufficient
- no remaining references to Octant's port `10086`
- repackaged chart tarball confirmed to carry the updated CRD (`vendor` present, `octant` absent); only the session-manager tarball changed

Not yet verified by a live run: a vcluster workshop with `console.enabled: true` rendering the dashboard end to end. Worth doing before merge, particularly the `kubernetes-dashboard-csrf` secret, which session-manager creates in the host session namespace while the dashboard is pointed at the virtual cluster.

body:
## Summary

- replace the simulation command surface with the single source-project-only `simulation webots run` flow
- reuse the ordinary resident project session while excluding all physical drivers
- manage only the Webots application; Webots owns the controller process
- generate one static controller-bearing robot and remove the dynamic spawn/supervisor/watch paths
- treat `.phoxal/webots` as disposable: delete it and recreate exactly `worlds/`, `controllers/`, and `protos/` on every run

## Why

Phase 12 removes the parallel simulation lifecycle and makes Webots a normal resident composition. The generated Webots project is ephemeral project data, so each run recreates it directly before launching Webots.

## Impact and migration

This is a pre-v1 breaking simplification. Removed commands, flags, protocol fields, snapshots, and lifecycle variants have no compatibility shims.

Affected repositories and land order:

1. `phoxal/framework` implementation and release
2. `phoxal/phoxal-cli` (this PR)
3. `phoxal/organization` standing-document reconciliation

Framework `v0.40.2` is published and publicly verified; this branch pins `phoxal` and `phoxal-api` to that exact train.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`
- focused disposable Webots project, static staging, controller provisioning, and command parser tests
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features` (572 passed; 2 environment-dependent tests ignored)
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`

All passed locally. Live GUI/Webots proof remains to be run against the published framework train.

## Independent review

Claude Code Opus reviewed the broader CLI change before the final maintainer-directed disposable-directory simplification. Reported findings were resolved. The final simplification removed mechanisms rather than adding a new architecture; per the maintainer's explicit direction, no further Claude review was requested.

## Risk

The blast radius includes CLI command parsing, resident supervision, router recovery, Webots launch/staging, session snapshots, and TUI visibility. A failed project generation is never launched; the next run rebuilds the disposable Webots tree from scratch.

author: malloythedev
body:
## Why a sandbox at all

Everything through 7.1.4 — cwd confinement, sanitized env, redirected HOME, read-only tool policy — is **defence in depth, not a boundary**. The agent subprocess runs as the operator's UID and can read any **absolute** path it guesses, and encoded exfiltration (base64 / hex / split literals) was measured defeating *every* content scan. OS-level isolation is the only real answer.

## The finding that matters

**`bwrap` is installed on this host and cannot work.**

```
kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1
bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied
```

`unshare --map-root-user` fails identically; `systemd-run --user --scope` rejects `ProtectHome`. **There is no working OS sandbox in this environment.**

Had I shipped the seam and trusted `command -v bwrap`, this repo would now carry a sandbox that never sandboxed — and an operator could reasonably have granted unattended use on the strength of it. **A sandbox that runs but doesn't isolate is worse than none**, because it converts a known gap into a false assurance.

So the design is: **presence is not proof.**

`verify_sandbox()` plants a canary secret *outside* the bound surfaces and asserts the sandboxed process cannot read it. Verified in **both** directions:
- refuses the genuinely-broken `bwrap` here (non-zero exit)
- catches a fake sandbox that executes with **no confinement at all** (reads the canary)

The absence is now a **machine-enforced refusal** (`require_sandbox=True` → `SandboxUnavailable`) rather than an unstated assumption.

## The seam

`SandboxRunner` wraps the agent argv. `BubblewrapSandbox` binds **only** the disposable worktree and the throwaway HOME read-write, the system runtime read-only, with `--unshare-all` (no network, no shared namespaces). The transport wraps when a sandbox is supplied and **never silently degrades** to unsandboxed.

## Verification

Mutation-verified: canary-read detection, non-zero-exit detection, transport wrapping — all **KILLED**.

Two mutation attempts initially **mis-reported**, and both are worth naming since this technique is load-bearing here:
1. one broke a multi-line call into a syntax error → pytest reported a collection *error*, my matcher only looked for *"failed"*
2. one targeted the wrong `if proc.returncode != 0:` — an **earlier occurrence in the same file**

A mutation harness that silently hits the wrong line produces false confidence, which is precisely what mutation testing exists to prevent. Both were re-run precisely.

I also fixed a **flaky test of my own**: `_repo_with_remote` committed with the wall clock, so two fixture repos straddling a second boundary got different base oids and the content-addressing assertion failed intermittently. Fixture commits now use pinned dates.

Gate: ruff/mypy/compile clean, **376 passed, 93.15% cov**, doclint 0/51.

## Deliberately NOT included: the live canary (7.1.5b)

Running the write path **for real** against a repository is the retained human-approval gate this entire ladder has been protecting. It needs your explicit authorization — and on this host it also needs a sandbox that actually works, which means either an AppArmor profile for `bwrap`, relaxing `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns`, or a container runtime. All are host-level changes that are yours to make, not mine.

Under `loop-controller-self-modify`: independent human review; I do not self-merge.

### Motivation
- Provide isolated physical copies for concurrent dungeon runs via a fixed pool of logical instance slots to allow multiple groups (including same-profile groups) to run simultaneously. 
- Protect template worlds from ordinary players and enforce server-authoritative routing/validation for dungeon-bound travel and teleportation. 
- Give players an owner- and run-bound Farrow's Chop flow so cooking binds a return point and eating can return to the exact active-instance location when the lifecycle is valid. 

### Description
- Introduces a ten-slot instance model with `DungeonInstanceSlots`, persists optional `instance_slot` on run records, and adds startup migration and slot assignment logic to `DungeonRunRegistryData` and `DungeonLifecycleService`. 
- Implements server-side travel/routing and enforcement with `DungeonTravelRouter` (template/instance/template-access rules), updates rift and world commands to consult the router, and evacuates unauthorized players to safe spawn. 
- Adds instance refresh and snapshot copy support in `DungeonWorldSnapshotService.refreshInstanceSlot`, copy-on-allocate portal/template linkage via `RiftRegistryData.copyTemplatePortals`, and defensive lifecycle queueing/migration on server start. 
- Implements Farrow's Chop binding and return flow via `FarrowsChopTravelService` and `DungeonReturnTarget`, updates `BeatrixCampfireBlock` and `FarrowsChopItem` to cook/bind/return against the active run, and updates help/docs/translations to match behavior. 

### Testing
- Ran included game tests registered in `DungeonInstanceGameTests`: `slot_mapping`, `legacy_run_codec`, and `farrows_chop_target_codec`, and they passed.

author: cedricziel
body:
## Regression
#684 added `brace-expansion@<=5.0.7 -> >=5.0.8`, which force-upgraded **every** brace-expansion in the tree — including eslint's CommonJS chain (`eslint -> minimatch@3 -> brace-expansion@1.x`) — to the ESM-only 5.x. That changed its export shape and broke the plugin lint on `main`:
```
TypeError: expand is not a function   (@eslint/config-array)
```
(surfaced on #586 and reproduced locally against main).

## Fix
Replace the broad override with major-line-scoped ones that apply the patched version *within each CJS line*:
- `brace-expansion@>=1.0.0 <1.1.16` -> `1.1.16`
- `brace-expansion@>=2.0.0 <2.0.2` -> `2.0.2`

eslint's 1.x consumer stays CommonJS and works again.

## Residual advisory
The brace-expansion advisory reachable via `eslint -> minimatch@3 -> brace-expansion@1.x` is not fully fixable on the 1.x line (only 2.x+/5.x carry the patch, and 5.x is ESM-incompatible with eslint's CJS chain). It remains until eslint bumps minimatch upstream — same class as the residual react-router/thrift advisories.

## Verification
- `pnpm lint` ✅ (0 errors)
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` ✅

author: freethinkel
body:
Closes #2 — image sizes had to be fixed up in another editor before import.

## What

**Props panel** — `w`/`h` fields with an aspect lock for any selected image widget, applied on `change` (blur/Enter) rather than per keystroke.

**Canvas** — corner handles on the selection box of any widget drawn from images. The drag scales the box uniformly and the resource follows by the same ratio, which is what a NUMBER (composed digit box) and a HAND (rotated AABB) need; a ghost box is the live feedback, the commit happens on pointerup. Handles are pulled onto the visible disc, since the round `.canvas-frame` clips the corners a full-screen background would otherwise put them in.

**Non-destructive.** The format draws a widget 1:1 from its resource, so a resize is a rescale of the pixels — but only the preview bitmap is rescaled, off `r.srcBitmap` (the original, pinned at the first resize). The encoded `data` is regenerated from that same source in `flushResized()` inside `buildCurrentBin()`, so the quality drop lands only in what is exported/flashed, and shrink-then-restore is lossless.

Multi-frame widgets (digits, weekday icons) scale every frame by the same ratio. Hands scale their pivot and shift x/y so the rotation center stays put.

## Notes

- `buildCurrentBin()` is now async (no sync JPEG encoder); its four call sites await.
- `accentBitmapFor()` reads pixels off the bitmap instead of `decodePixels()` — a resized resource carries old-size pixels in `data` until build time.
- `Input` gained an `onChange` prop.
- Resource pixels stay outside undo (unchanged from `replaceImage`), so ⌘Z restores position but not size.

## Verification

`npm run check` clean, `tests/editor-resize.svelte.test.ts` covers the rendered box, the deferred re-encode, the hand pivot and the lossless round-trip. Drag interaction checked by hand in the browser: dragging a NUMBER's corner scales all ten digit frames, the background's handles land on the dial.

author: kj299
body:
Fixes the two packaging defects from the first live run in #76. Both were mine, not the operator's.

## 1. The skill was not reachable from a clone

Claude Code discovers skills from three places ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#where-skills-live)):

| Location | Path |
|---|---|
| Personal | `~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` |
| Project | `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` |
| Plugin | `<plugin>/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` |

A top-level `skills/` directory at a repository root is **not** one of them, and this repo's `.claude/` holds only `settings.local.json`. So `/cyber-threat-intel` → `Unknown command` was **a packaging defect, not operator error** — and it follows that **no report has ever been generated from a clone of this repository via the slash command.** Worth weighing before #83 (skill evals).

`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` makes the repo a plugin. Plugin skills resolve at `<plugin-root>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — the layout this repo already had, so **nothing moved and every existing parity check still passes.** The layout was plugin-shaped all along; it was just missing its manifest.

```bash
claude --plugin-dir .     # from the repository root
```

The command becomes `/threat-intel:cyber-threat-intel`; bare `/cyber-threat-intel` also works unless something else claims that name. The manifest also bundles the MCP server, so that one flag covers both halves of a live run (subject to the usual per-server approval).

## 2. The console script was unreachable on Windows

`pip install` puts `threat-intel-mcp` in the interpreter's scripts directory. Windows Store Python puts that at

```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\PythonSoftwareFoundation.Python.3.13_qbz5n2kfra8p0\LocalCache\local-packages\Python313\Scripts
```

and leaves it off `PATH` — pip even warned about it during the #76 run. So `claude mcp add threat-intel-mcp -- threat-intel-mcp` registered a command the host could not resolve, and the health check reported `× Failed to connect`. There was no `__main__.py`, so the obvious PATH-free fallback didn't exist either.

`mcp/src/threat_intel_mcp/__main__.py` re-exports `server:main`, so:

```bash
claude mcp add threat-intel-mcp -- python -m threat_intel_mcp
```

resolves through the interpreter and works wherever the package is importable. It's also what the plugin manifest uses.

## Verification

Both paths were executed, not assumed:

```
$ echo -n "" | python -m threat_intel_mcp
exit=0, no traceback
```

- **431 tests pass** (up from 427), lint clean. Four new tests in `test_entrypoint.py`, including an end-to-end launch asserting the module serves stdio and exits 0 on EOF, plus a guard that `-m` and the console script resolve to the *same* `main` so the two launch paths can't silently diverge.
- The new CI step was checked **in both directions** — it passes on this tree and fails on a deliberately drifted manifest:
  ```
  FAIL: plugin manifest problems:
    'version' is '9.9.9', expected '1.20.0' (spec.yaml skill.version)
    'threat-intel' server must launch with ['-m', 'threat_intel_mcp'], got ['bogus']
  ```
  It validates the kebab-case name, that the skill path exists, that the server launches by module rather than by console script, and version parity with `spec.yaml` — the discipline already applied to the schema, examples, and changelog.

## Docs

`CLAUDE.md` layout, `docs/architecture.md`, `mcp/README.md`, and `docs/report-runbook.md` all updated, per the repo rule that docs describe what the code does. The runbook's invoke step now leads with the discovery constraint, since that is what actually stopped the live run.

## Not covered here

The remaining #76 items are environment-side: `py -3` missing (use `python -m venv .venv`) and the empty `feat/first-connected-report` branch (#96 item 5, needs your credential — mine is refused ref deletion). The full PowerShell runbook variant is still outstanding and deliberately left out of this PR.

author: yongjip
body:
Closes #191, the last defect the fault matrix recorded.

## The lie

SQLite allows one writer. A process holding the write lock past `busy_timeout` (5s) made a queue write raise `sqlite3.OperationalError` — **not** a `MergetrainError`, so it fell past every classified clause to the runner's defensive `except Exception` and retired the job **terminal `failed`** with `note: "unexpected error: database is locked"`.

`failed` is the queue's *"the branch is at fault, rebase and enqueue a fresh commit"* signal — `PushRejected` parks `blocked` precisely to avoid that confusion. Here nothing crashed, no ref moved, and the branch was fine: a second process just held the lock too long, and an agent following `next_action: fix_blocked_job` would rewrite innocent code.

## The fix

`store.immediate()` is the single gate every queue mutation passes through, so contention is classified there rather than at 18 call sites: it becomes **`QueueBusy`**, a typed retryable `QueueError` surfacing as `error.code: queue_busy`, `retryable: true`.

Both runner ladders then park on it by how far the deploy got, because that is what decides what is *knowable*:

| Contention hit | Job lands | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before the push | `queued`, claim released | nothing was touched; the next run picks it up with no operator |
| after the durable marker, push outcome unknown | `needs_reconcile` | the same position an ambiguous push leaves — the remote decides |
| after the refs landed | `deployed` + warning (unchanged) | the code shipped; saying otherwise is the one lie this tool forbids |

Two deliberate details:

- **When nothing shipped, the error is re-raised after parking**, so the caller reports a retryable failure rather than grading a run that never completed. `LostLease` sets the precedent.
- **If the parking write is contended too, nothing is forced.** The row stays `in_progress` with its claim — indistinguishable from a crash, which orphan recovery already resolves. A recoverable orphan beats a wrong terminal status, and this is why the fix is not "retry the write harder".

`queue_busy` is a new `error.code` value, which the compatibility policy lists as additive.

## Verified end state, not just the exception type

Driving the real deploy path with the lock held across the first `mark_job`:

```
status : queued
note   : queue database is busy; another process held the write lock: database is locked
raised : QueueBusy
claim  : ''            <- claimable again
push   : not_run   marker: ''   remote: unchanged
```

- The fault matrix's remaining `@unittest.expectedFailure` becomes a passing test — **the whole suite now has zero expected failures**.
- New `ContentionContractTests` pins what an agent branches on *through the CLI*: `error.code == "queue_busy"`, `retryable is True`, exit 1, the job not terminal, and the remote byte-identical. The fingerprint gate nulls values, so this had to be an explicit test.
- The post-push half is unchanged and still green: contention after a landed push still finalizes `deployed` with a warning.
- 366 tests green, ruff and mypy clean, `scripts/e2e.sh` **PASS=96 FAIL=0**.

Docs: `docs/contract.md` gains the `queue_busy` row and notes the third retryable class; `docs/failure-modes.md` gains a "Queue database contention" section with the landing table and the orphan fallback.

Given this touches the exactly-once deploy path, I am running the adversarial review pass on it before merge.

author: mattiice
body:
Completes the handheld receiving loop from #311: **scan → mint → label**. `POST /receiving/scan/mint` draws the next `coil_abc_num`, stamps `inbound_coil_status`, and prints the ABC label.

## The printer is checked BEFORE anything is minted

Legacy pings the printer and mints nothing if it doesn't answer:

```perl
if ($p->ping($Printer_Add)) { ...NEXTVAL... UPDATE... print... } else { error }
```

**That ordering is the whole point, not incidental.** An ABC number drawn with no label printed is a coil physically on the dock with no tag on it and nothing downstream to reconcile it against.

| situation | result |
|---|---|
| printer unreachable | **503, nothing minted** |
| coil not on any inbound list | **409, no sequence value burned** |
| ok | minted + 2 labels |

## The label

`ZplLabels.CoilAbcLabel` is the legacy payload **byte-for-byte**, pinned by test. The codes that look like noise are load-bearing, and the docs say why:

- the **`I`** in `^BCI` / `^A0I` is **inverted** orientation — this stock comes off the roll upside down relative to the print head, so dropping it prints every label the wrong way up
- `^PW384` / `^LL0203` is the physical label size
- `^PQ1` means *one copy per payload* — which is why the caller sends it **twice**, as legacy does

Get any of those wrong and it only shows up on paper.

## Transport is seamed off, deliberately

`ICoilLabelPrinter` follows the same discipline as the EDI no-transmit transport. The default `NoOpCoilLabelPrinter` doesn't print and reports itself **unreachable** — and because minting checks reachability first, **an unwired deployment mints nothing** rather than burning ABC numbers for labels nobody printed. Wiring a real Zebra socket is a deliberate act.

## One legacy quirk kept, with the silence removed

Legacy's `UPDATE` is unscoped (`WHERE COIL_NUMBER = …`), so every receiving row for that customer coil takes the new number — and a coil that already had one has it **overwritten**, orphaning the label already printed against it. Kept faithful rather than quietly narrowed to one row, because narrowing changes which rows the plant's downstream reconciliation finds. What is *not* kept is the silence: **`replacedAbcNum`** reports the superseded number.

**Tests:** 10 new (label bytes, orientation codes, copy count; mint, overwrite-reporting, multi-row stamping, no-burn on an unknown coil; and that the default printer refuses). 637 API total, green. OpenAPI snapshot regenerated.

⚠ **Still needs hardware:** the real socket transport to `:6101` and the device-IP → printer map (`192.168.10.8/9/10` → `.12/13/14`).

author: ivopogace
body:
Closes #128. Plan doc: `docs/plans/session-revocation.md`.

Overdue security work, not an enhancement: #128 was filed off the #109 (S1) review gate as "a **must** before operator self-registration ships." Self-registration shipped in S6 (#115) — so the account states this was meant to gate exist, and the revocation mechanism that should have accompanied them did not.

## What Detect found

**Suspend did not exist as an action.** `SUSPENDED` was an enum token and a V29 check-constraint value, reachable only by raw SQL (every test did `UPDATE operator SET status='SUSPENDED'`). The trigger surface had to be built before revocation had anything to hang off, which is why this slice is larger than the issue's two bullets suggest.

**The revocation mechanism already existed — for tourists.** `CustomerSessionRevoker` (S8 #113) already killed a customer's sessions after a password reset. That settled the modelling question the issue deliberately left open.

## The design decision

Revocation is **edge-orchestrated, not evented**. The `operator` module owns the state transition and returns a typed outcome carrying the principal name; the platform edge deletes that principal's sessions via Spring Session's principal index. `RESPONSIBILITIES.md` mandates exactly this split — `operator`'s Job is "the approval **state transitions**", while "the register/login/approval **endpoints**" and all login machinery are the platform edge's (RV-BE-11).

An event was rejected for three reasons: revocation must be **synchronous** (an async listener leaves a window where the suspended cookie still works — the whole bug); the session store is **edge infrastructure, not a module**, so there is no subscriber module; and invariant #11 bars mutable business fields in event payloads, so the event could not carry the username its listener needs.

`CustomerSessionRevoker` was **generalized** to `PrincipalSessionRevoker` rather than copied — the logic was never customer-specific, and a second near-identical edge class is a duplicated block the Sonar gate rejects.

## Gap 1 — suspend/rotate now kill live sessions

- `OperatorApprovals` → **`OperatorLifecycle`**, gaining `suspend`/`reinstate`. One purposeful port rather than a fifth narrow one; "approvals" no longer named the conversation.
- Transitions are a guarded `UPDATE … WHERE status = :expected RETURNING username` — atomic, so two concurrent suspends cannot both win, and the username comes back in the same statement so no window opens between the write and the revocation.
- `POST /api/admin/operators/{id}/suspend|reinstate` + `GET …/accounts`, ADMIN-gated like the shipped approve/reject matchers.
- Revocation runs **after** the transactional transition returns, so a rolled-back status change cannot leave sessions deleted for a live account. The residual failure direction is over-revocation, never under.
- **An admin cannot suspend itself** (`409 CANNOT_SUSPEND_SELF`) — the guard needs the calling principal, which is edge knowledge, so it sits ahead of the port. Without it the platform could lock itself out of its own admin surface with one click.
- **Credential rotation**: the boot-time initializer re-stamps the configured password on *every* boot and bcrypt re-salts, so "the hash changed" proves nothing — revoking on it would sign the admin out on every deploy. A genuine rotation is the raw configured password no longer matching the stored hash.

## Gap 2 — a failed sign-out no longer passes silently

The issue blames `OperatorAuth.signOut()`, but S9 (#277) moved that code to the shared `SessionAuth` base, so the fix covers **both** principal types.

`signOut()` now returns `'signed-out' | 'may-persist'`. A `401` counts as success (the server has no such session — that *is* signed out); anything else re-bootstraps CSRF via `GET /api/auth/me` and retries **once**. Local state clears either way. `SignOutNotice` (in `core/`) carries the warning and `SessionAuth` records into it itself, so every call site raises the banner without opting in — the failure being fixed is precisely a silently-dropped signal. The shell renders it **above** the chrome conditional, so it also shows on `/operator/**` where the tourist header is suppressed (the shared-venue-tablet case).

## A second instance found by the generalization audit

The Phase-1 audit asked "what else changes an account's right to its sessions without revoking?" and found one: the S8 authenticated set-password (`/api/me/password`) left every other session of the account alive. Same bug class as the issue's own "password rotation" clause, so fixed here — `revokeAllExcept(principal, keepSessionId)` evicts every *other* session while the caller's own survives.

## Coverage

`PerOperatorLoginIT` lost its request-time-suspension assertion in the S1 migration (session auth has no per-request credential re-check by design). **`OperatorSuspensionRevocationIT` is that replacement coverage** — it logs in over the real Spring Session JDBC store, suspends via the admin endpoint, and asserts the cookie no longer authenticates. Crucially it also replays the revoked cookie against `POST /api/venues`, the sharpest non-venue-scoped hole the issue names, and proves the `401` is the revocation by first showing the same request succeeds on a live session.

- Backend: `OperatorLifecycleIT` (5), `OperatorSuspensionRevocationIT` (5), `OperatorCredentialInitializerTest` (6), `SetPasswordIT` (+1) — all against real Postgres where they touch it
- Frontend: 861 unit tests green (108 files), incl. new `session-auth.spec.ts` and admin suspend/reinstate + a11y specs
- e2e: 74 green, incl. 3 new CI-safe mocked specs; axe runs in three states including the armed-confirmation DOM

## Notes for review

- **No Flyway migration** — V29's constraint already permits `SUSPENDED`; this only starts *writing* a value the schema has allowed since #115.
- **Invariant #13 untouched** — no new venue-scoped surface; `/api/admin/**` is role-gated and venue-scope-exempt.
- **Suspension keeps `operator_venue` rows** — it is reversible, and ownership already resolves ACTIVE-only, so a suspended operator is denied every venue-scoped surface regardless.
- **Suspended accounts stay listed** (badged, with Reinstate) so suspension is never a one-way door.

author: 2imi9
body:
The log-space path was added to stop Chl poisoning the loss under linear z-scoring, but it shipped with four defects. Each is verified against the raw v05 cube (`darwin_v05_L5_chl.npz`), not inferred.

## F1 — `--log-tracers` only covered the Chl family

PIC, POC and FeT are equally strictly-positive, wide-dynamic-range tracers with the identical failure mode. The post-fix depth run makes the split exact:

| tracer | logged | log-range kept | non-physical (≤ 0) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chl1 | yes | **0.971** | **0.00%** |
| FeT | no | 0.665 | 3.5% |
| PIC | no | 0.387 | 13.9% |
| POC | no | 0.336 | 10.2% |

Added to the default here and to `prognostic.py`'s `log_vars`, so training and serving still agree channel-for-channel.

## F2 — the fixed `1e-12` clip floor poisoned the log-space statistics

v05 carries genuinely non-positive cells (**13.34%** of Chl1). Clipping them to `1e-12` parks them at `log = −27.6`, about 21 log-units below a typical Chl of `1.8e-3`. That one artefact inflated the log-space std from **4.808 → 8.255 (1.72×)** and compressed the real signal from ±1.0 to **±0.58** z-units, so roughly 42% of the model's output range was spent representing a spike of clipped zeros.

Replaced with a per-channel floor at the p1 of the **positive train-month** values (leak-free). `--log-floor-pct 0` restores the old behaviour. The floor is written to `config.log_floors` and consumed by `prognostic.py`, which keeps the historical `1e-12` default so existing checkpoints serve unchanged.

## F3 — the climatology baseline was `log(mean x)`, not `mean(log x)`

Those differ by ~σ²/2. Measured on `Chl1_k0`, the ordering displaced the baseline by **+3.21 natural-log units** (median +2.54, max +20.6) = **+0.39σ**, with **29.1%** of cells past 0.5σ. That inflated `skill_vs_climatology` for every logged channel — the metric behind the "+0.240 at 1 step" headline.

Fixing F2 shrinks the std and would have made this *worse* (~0.67σ), so the two land together.

## F4 — the #191 uniformly-sparse guard never fired on real data

It used `ptp(gaps) <= 0.02 * median`. Real every-other-month calendar gaps run 59–62 d, giving `ptp/median ≈ 0.05`, so the guard missed exactly the case it was written for and two-month jumps stayed gradeable as next-month skill. Loosened to `0.15`, which admits calendar month-length variation while still requiring a uniform stride.

## Tests

`tests/test_emulator_log_space.py` pins all four, plus the leak-free property of the floor and the `--expected-step-days` escape hatch. Full suite: **503 passed, 18 skipped** (was 494).

## Also in this PR

Lands `src/darwindiff/e2s/` (`__init__.py`, `datasource.py`, `prognostic.py`) and `tests/test_e2s.py`, which were untracked. Committing only `prognostic.py` would have shipped the package without its `__init__.py` and broken CI.

## What this does not change

The deflation stands. Post-fix, in log space, Chl1 still scores −0.47 to −0.61 vs persistence at every depth level, and the model overall is −0.161 ± 0.013 vs a per-cell seasonal AR(1). These fixes restore physical plausibility and dynamic range; they do not make the emulator skillful.

**Every global emulator figure in the repo predates the log-space work** and should be regenerated before it is shown anywhere.

author: obiemunoz
body:
Closes #249.

## What changed

The suppression explainer already recorded the identifier behind every `TS2304`, so most of the detection was there: what was missing was the meaning of the name and the grouping. For a `TS2304`/`TS2552` whose name sits in a type position it now also records whether a JSDoc tag over the declaration writes the same name, and where the program declares the name when anything does. The report groups those by name.

- `unresolvedIsType` and `unresolvedIsDocumented` on `SuppressionEvidence`, plus the existing `declaredAt`/`declarationKind`/`declaredInProject` fields, now filled in for an unresolved type name.
- `SuppressionReport.unresolvedTypes`: one entry per name with the count, the files that wrote it, how many of its sites a comment documents, and the declaration site.
- The run log names the five largest and counts the rest. `--suppressionReportFile` lists every name with the files that wrote it.
- `fixShape` for `TS2304`/`TS2552` splits into "type name is declared elsewhere and not imported", "type name is declared nowhere", and the old "name does not resolve" for a name in an expression.

Finding the declaration searches module exports and namespace members of the program, cached per name and per program: a global declaration would have resolved, and both of those are invisible to an unqualified reference, which is what makes such a name an import or a qualifier away rather than nonexistent. Nothing about what the migration writes changes, and the work stays inside the existing never-fail wrapper in `printSuppressionReport`.

## Measured on the sample from the issue

ESLint 9.39.4 `lib/{linter,shared,services,types}`, 43 JS files, `init` then `rename` then the default pipeline. The run reproduces the issue's counts exactly: `TS2304  118 diagnostics, 85 commented, 14 files`.

Before, this was the whole of what the run said about them:

```
    TS2304 x118 — 118 name does not resolve
```

After:

```
    TS2304 x118 — 71 type name is declared nowhere
  26 type names in the annotations resolve to nothing, across 118 diagnostics; the comments write 26 of them.
    ASTNode x33 in 7 files — nothing declares it
    SourceCode x15 in 5 files — declared at lib/types/index.d.ts:233:1 (ClassDeclaration), not in scope here
    Directive x7 in 1 file — nothing declares it
    Language x6 in 2 files — declared at lib/linter/apply-disable-directives.ts:13:1 (TypeAliasDeclaration), not in scope here
    Message x6 in 1 file — nothing declares it
    and 21 other names
```

The 26 group counts sum to 118, so every `TS2304` the run wrote is accounted for by a name. 71 of the 118 are names nothing declares, 47 are names declared somewhere the reference cannot see. `T` and `U` in `lib/shared/deep-merge-arrays.ts` show up as the issue described, 2 diagnostics each with nothing declaring them.

The report file adds the full list, every name with its files:

```
Type names that resolve to nothing:
  ASTNode  33 diagnostics in 7 files, 32 written by a comment, nothing declares it
    lib/linter/code-path-analysis/code-path-analyzer.ts, lib/shared/traverser.ts, lib/linter/rule-fixer.ts, lib/linter/source-code-traverser.ts, lib/linter/file-report.ts, and 2 more files
```

One number in the issue does not reproduce: it reports 40 distinct names where this is 26. The 26 names cover 41 name-and-file pairs, which is close to 40, so the earlier figure looks like it counted a name once per file.

## Verification

- `pnpm run build`: pass.
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules npx jest --runInBand`: 64 suites, 1074 tests, all passing.
- `pnpm run lint`: pass.
- The same tree migrated with a build of `origin/master` and with this branch: `diff -rq` reports no difference, so this changes only what is reported. Both runs end at 353 suppressions, 314 comments, 283 explicit `any`.
- Cost of the lookup, warm: the `explain-suppressions` pass takes 40ms here against 48ms on master, over a 60-file program with 26 names to resolve. That answers the question the issue left open.
- 8 new tests in `packages/ts-migrate-plugins/tests/src/utils/suppression-explainer.test.ts` cover the grouping across files, a name that resolves being left out, a name in an expression not counting as a type, the documented count, a declaration found in another module, a declaration found inside a namespace, a declaration outside the project, and the "nothing declares it" case, plus two format tests.

body:
系列第三个（前两个：#4 采集脚本、#5 odometer）。这个只改文档，两条都是"实战里发现文档缺了一块"。

## 1. `SKILL.md` 未提 Remotion 本体的商用授权

这个库对**音频**授权非常严谨——`references/sound-design.md` 有整张免费授权来源清单，甚至有 Kenney 音包"**产品宣传片禁用**"这样的条目。但对整个库赖以运行的 Remotion 本体，`SKILL.md` / `references/` / `template/TEMPLATE.md` 全文未提一字，而 **Remotion 不是 OSS 授权**。

我是把这个 skill vendored 进自己的 harness、准备给公司 repo 出片时才自己去查的。对同样场景的用户，这是实打实的法务暴露，而且 `template/` 一跑起来就已经在用了。

要点（**as-of 2026-07-25**，采购前以官方页面为准）：

- 免费档 = 个人 / **≤3 名员工的营利组织** / 非营利 / 评估期
- 责任主体是 "the entity that ultimately owns the IP of the Remotion project" —— 看**成片 IP 归属方**的 headcount，不是写代码的人
- 团队/公司协作时 "the combined headcount counts for the company size threshold"
- 一个 seat "covers one person who writes Remotion code themselves **or uses agentic coding tools**" —— **让 agent 写 Remotion 代码同样占 seat**。这条对本库的用户尤其相关，因为本库就是给 agent 用的
- 付费档 Creators $25/seat/月

来源：[license](https://www.remotion.dev/docs/license) · [pricing](https://www.remotion.dev/docs/license/pricing) · [FAQ](https://www.remotion.dev/docs/license-pricing-compliance/faq)

同时注明了**镜头卡本身不受此约束**——配方卡是动效词汇表，可以只读卡、换别的渲染管线执行。这句是给 headcount 过线又想用这套知识的人留的出口，也是我自己的实际处置方式。

我把它放在「资产使用方式」的第一条，因为它是使用 `template/` / `assets/lib/` / `demos/` 的前置条件。如果你觉得措辞或位置该改（比如挪到 README 或单独一节），我照改。

## 2. `aesthetic-rules.md` R1 的"真静止"可以自动检查

R1 要求静止期"一切属性锁死，包括辉光/阴影/高光残留"。这**等价于逐像素相同**，所以不用眼看——渲静止段首末帧比哈希就行：

```bash
npx remotion still src/index.ts <Comp> a.png --frame=<静止起点>
npx remotion still src/index.ts <Comp> b.png --frame=<镜头末帧>
shasum -a256 a.png b.png   # 两行哈希不同 = 还有东西在动
```

这个检查在我这次成片里**抓到一处眼睛完全看不出的违例**：`riso-print-hits` B 式的顿推泵是 `1 + 0.08·exp(-t/3)`、窗口 14f，而我把静止起点按并行的错位窗（`SPIN_WIN` 12f）算了。t=12 时 scale 还是 **1.0015** —— 0.15% 的缩放，肉眼零感知，但它让我"收尾 29f 真静止"的说法直接变成假话（真实是 27f，起点晚 2 帧）。

我一开始是靠看静帧确认收尾静止的，四镜全都"看着没问题"；换成比哈希之后立刻现原形。所以补的不只是一条命令，还有那条结论：**静止起点要取所有并行窗口里最晚归零的那个**，不是最先关闭的那个。

这条我放在 R1 的自检后面作为「验法」。`references/final-review.md` 那边要不要也挂一句，你定。

## 说明

两条都不改任何现有规则或参数，只加内容。如果第 1 条你更倾向自己措辞（毕竟是你的库、涉及第三方授权表述），我很乐意只留第 2 条，或者把第 1 条改成你希望的形式。

Verificado diretamente no que o domínio serve agora: | Verificação | Resultado | | :--- | :--- | | `agenciarizzo.com.br` (apex) | `308` → `www.agenciarizzo.com.br` | | `www.agenciarizzo.com.br/` | serve o deploy de produção **deste** projeto (`

Agenda cheia não é sorte.

`) | | `www.agenciarizzo.com.br/robots.txt` | `User-Agent: *` / `Disallow: /` | | meta robots em toda página | `noindex, nofollow` | | `/montar-proposta-online.html` | **404** (`x-matched-path: /404`) — é a landing das campanhas de Ads | Ou seja: o cutover aconteceu sem os passos do `CUTOVER_CHECKLIST.md`. Este PR resolve as partes que são código; o resto (flip do `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_INDEXABLE`, GA4, Search Console) é ação no painel e ficou pro cliente decidir. ## 1 · 301 das URLs legadas (`next.config.ts`) Toda URL do site antigo estava em **404** — 404 descarta o histórico da URL, 301 transfere. 18 regras, cada rota com e sem `.html`: | De | Para | | :--- | :--- | | `/google-ads-medicos` | `/cartas/google-ads` | | `/redes-sociais` | `/cartas/redes-sociais` | | `/branding-medico`, `/sobre`, `/marketingmedicobrasilia`, `/marketingmedicogoiania` | `/` | | `/portfolio` | `/clientes` | | `/clientes.html`, `/contato.html` | `/clientes`, `/contato` | | `/montar-proposta-online.html` | `/contato` | `statusCode: 301` em vez de `permanent: true` — o `permanent` do Next emite 308, que o Google trata igual, mas 301 é o que crawler, Ads e planilha esperam ver. **Dois desvios do checklist**, ambos por relevância do destino (redirect pra página sem relação vira soft-404 aos olhos do Google): - `/portfolio` → `/clientes` (o checklist dizia `/`) — é o equivalente real. - `/montar-proposta-online.html` → `/contato`: o checklist pedia "manter acessível", mas ela **já está quebrada**. 301 pro contato é melhor que 404 em qualquer cenário. Destino definitivo quando as landings dos anúncios forem trocadas. ⚠️ **Isto não resolve sozinho:** enquanto `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_INDEXABLE` não for `true`, o `robots.txt` do domínio serve `Disallow: /` e o Googlebot não pode nem rastrear as URLs antigas pra *enxergar* estes 301s. ## 2 · Landmark `

Zero mudança visual. Além do leitor de tela, o landmark é o que extrator de conteúdo de IA usa pra separar corpo de navegação. ## 3 · Contraste AA no microtexto Teal de marca `#0097A7` sobre papel `#F4EFE6` = **3,06:1**, abaixo do mínimo AA de 4,5:1. author: xpiatio
body:
Reworks the `/display` wall kiosk around three complaints from daily use.

## Layout

The radio log moves from a five-message footer to the full-height left column, **newest message first**, scrollable back through 50 (cap raised from 20). It sticks to the top only when already there, so scrolling back through history isn't interrupted by new traffic. The clock, date, alerts and net status sit in the right column, with the **family presence tiles underneath them**.

```
┌──────────────────────┬─────────────────┐
│ RADIO LOG (newest ↑) │ 14:32           │
│                      │ Saturday        │
│  ...scrolls...       │ ⚠ alert         │
│                      │ Net: Tue 7p     │
│                      ├─────────────────┤
│                      │ [Dad] [Mom]     │
│                      │ [Kid] [Gma]   ↕ │
└──────────────────────┴─────────────────┘
```

## Tiles

Tiles size themselves to the household — 240px for four people, stepping down to a **130px floor** past a dozen, at which point the board scrolls rather than shrinking a name past legibility across a room.

Long-pressing a tile (350ms) during the wake window drags it to re-sort the board; a short tap is still Mark-OK. Keyboard-sortable too (Space, arrows, Space). The order is stored **server-side on the device-token record**, so it survives a browser that forgets everything else and can differ per wall panel. Someone added to the household later joins the end of the board rather than disappearing. E-ink panels keep their tiles fixed — dragging smears them.

## Pairing (the "re-enter the token every visit" bug)

The token was always persisted to `localStorage`. What erased it was a WebSocket close with code `4001`, which the client could not distinguish from "revoked" — **both** auth paths sent a bare, reasonless `4001`, including the fall-through that fired when `_device_token_store` hadn't initialised yet (`if _device_token_store and device_token`). One unlucky close un-paired the kiosk permanently.

- A `device_token` never falls through to session auth; an uninitialised store now closes `1013` (retry) and logs a warning.
- Rejections carry a reason; only `4001 device_token_invalid` is fatal.
- A fatal rejection no longer wipes the pairing — the display keeps retrying behind a banner until an operator taps **Re-pair**.

Two additions so nobody has to type 43 characters: a **six-digit pairing code** (single-use, 10-minute TTL, in-memory only, rate limited 5/min per IP and 20/5min globally — six digits is otherwise guessable), and a bookmarkable **`/display?token=…`** that is scrubbed from the address bar on load. Admins can re-issue a code for an existing display, which keeps its e-ink flag and tile order; revoking still discards everything.

nginx and the vite dev server both needed an explicit route for `/display/pair` — the SPA fallback was answering the POST with a 405.

## Verification

- Backend `1976 passed`; frontend `995 passed`; `npx tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` clean.
- Live against a local ROCm build: bad token closes `4001 device_token_invalid`; bad pairing code returns 404 then 429 after 5 attempts; `display_set_order` round-trips and persists to `device_tokens.json`.
- New tests cover the tier/floor sizing, the order merge rules, `set_order` validation, pairing-code TTL/single-use/reissue/rate-limit, the close-reason semantics both sides, and that the kiosk reconnects on a bare 4001 instead of un-pairing.

**Not covered by tests:** the drag gesture itself — jsdom has no layout, so the reorder maths is unit-tested and the gesture is on the manual checklist. Tests do assert tiles become sortable only while awake and never on e-ink.

## Follow-up

Long-lived tokens still travel in the WS query string (and now optionally in a bookmark URL), so they reach reverse-proxy access logs. The HttpOnly-cookie exchange remains the open fix — noted in the manual as a trade-off.

author: michaelkrisper
body:
💡 **What:** Replaced the O(N) array search (`FUNCTIONS.find`) with an O(1) Map lookup (`FUNCTION_BY_NAME.get`) inside `signatureContext` and `lookupLegacy`.
🎯 **Why:** `signatureContext` parses the formula actively during typing. It looks for the active function to provide the signature context tooltip. The array search is run for every matching parenthesis on key presses, making it an O(N) bottleneck.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** Baseline duration of ~6500ms for 1,000,000 function lookups via `signatureContext`, which improved to ~2687ms with the Map lookup on the same workload. A 2.4x speedup.

author: cameronsjo
body:
## What this fixes

Two issues (#394, #368) were filed as a writer/reader keying divergence in the polish marker — worktree gitdir vs common dir. **That diagnosis is refuted.** `record-polish` and `polish_marker_present` have both keyed on the canonicalized `git_common_dir` since 0.60.0, and the clean worktree case reproduces silent.

The real defect was in the reader's cwd resolver, and it was two characters wide. `CD_PATTERN`'s bare-path class was `[^ &;|]+` — excludes a space, but not a newline. So the shape that actually shipped:

```
cd <worktree>
gh pr create --title x
```

captured the target as `<worktree>\ngh`. No such directory exists, `GitState::resolve` returned `None`, and the gate nudged. The marker had been correct the whole time.

The class is now `[^\s&;|]+`. That is the entire fix.

## Why the newline is NOT a separator

An earlier revision also added `\n` to the separator alternation, which would additionally recognize a `cd` on its own line *after* an earlier command. That edit is deliberately reverted.

It creates no new bypass class — `^`, `&&`, `;`, and `||` all reach the identical steering today, confirmed by a three-way old/new/bash differential. But it converts a rarely-tripped mis-resolution into a routinely-tripped one:

- this repo's own docs carry **7** line-start `cd` occurrences against **1** `;`-spelled
- `\s*` means an indented `cd` inside a fenced code block matches too
- `cd ~/...` expands to a directory that really exists, so those become live re-points

The triggering shape is `gh pr create --body-file - <<'EOF'` with a shell snippet in the body — a routinely composed body. Widening the accidental-trigger surface of a primitive that three block-capable guards resolve through is the wrong trade for a nudge-only false positive.

## #303 — two ship-anchor detection misses

Also included, and independently cleared:

- **`sh -c '…'` wrapper.** A ship wrapped in a shell invocation was invisible because the quoted script collapses to one token. `is_polish_ship_anchor` now evaluates `command_segments`, which expands `sh|bash|zsh|dash -c`.
- **gh global flag before the subcommand.** `gh --repo owner/r pr create` broke the strict `[gh, pr, create]` adjacency window. Detection now walks forward from the `gh` command word, skipping `-`-prefixed tokens and consuming one extra token after a bare `--repo`/`-R`, before requiring a literal `pr`.

Both misses were pre-existing and fail-open — the cost was a missed nudge, never a bypass or a false block. Per-segment draft scoping survives both changes, so `sh -c 'gh pr create --draft'` is still correctly skipped, and every existing negative still rejects because the walk demands a literal `pr` token.

The anchor work was cleared separately: no unbounded loop, no index hazard, fuzzed clean over 4000 random token inputs, 40k x 40k token stress in 0.07s, nudge-only and fail-open.

## Known gap, recorded not closed

The anchor now reads `command_segments` while `parse_work_dir` remains a raw-string scan, so the predicate deciding *whether* a segment ships and the resolver deciding *where* it ships from do not see the same view. In `sh -c 'cd /x && gh pr create'` the ship is seen but the `cd` is not. That gap pre-dates this change; moving the anchor widens it, and closing it belongs with the resolver.

## Verification

author: zeajose
body:
Bumps `vitest` from `^4.0.18` to `^4.1.10`, which clears all four open Dependabot alerts — every one of them lived in the vitest dev dependency tree, so no runtime dependency was affected. The single bump cascades: vitest 4.1.10 patches the UI-server arbitrary file read/exec (#7, critical); vite goes 7.3.3 → 8.1.5, leaving the vulnerable 7.x line behind and dropping its `launch-editor` dep (#10 high, #11 moderate); esbuild is removed entirely since vite 8 no longer pulls it (#8, low); and postcss moves to 8.5.23, also clearing a sourceMappingURL path-traversal advisory that `npm audit` flagged but Dependabot hadn't filed.

That bump then broke CI, because vitest 4.1.10 needs Node `^20 || ^22 || >=24` and vite 8 needs `^20.19 || >=22.12`, while both workflows pinned Node 18 — every job died at startup on `SyntaxError: ... 'node:util' does not provide an export named 'styleText'`. So this PR also moves the test matrix to `[20.x, 22.x, 24.x]`, moves all three integration-test jobs to Node 22, and raises `engines.node` to `>=20.19.0` with matching updates to the README and both `SKILL.md` files.

**Note the support-policy change:** dropping Node 18 is a deliberate call, not just a CI tweak — it reached end of life on 2025-04-30, and leaving `engines` at `>=18` would claim a floor CI no longer tests. Verified with `npm audit` (0 vulnerabilities), `npm run test:unit` (187 tests across 15 files), and the workflow's three `node --check` syntax checks; the 20/22/24 matrix itself is the remaining verification, since only Node 26 is available locally.

author: tricsto
body:
## Ziel
Zweite Absicherung zusätzlich zum Per-Team-Merge, damit im Live-Betrieb (mehrere Handys) wirklich nichts verloren geht.

## Warum
Der entprellte Writer (200 ms) hat drei Restlücken – gerade auf Handys:
1. **Handy sperren / App wechseln / Tab schließen** bevor der Debounce feuert → die letzte Änderung wird nie geschrieben.
2. **Fehlgeschlagene Writes** (Netz weg) werden erst bei der nächsten Änderung erneut versucht – passiert nichts mehr, bleibt die Änderung lokal hängen.
3. **Verpasste Realtime-Events** bei kurzem Verbindungsabbruch werden nicht nachgeholt.

## Lösung
Ein zusätzliches Sync-Sicherungsnetz (`useEffect`, aktiv in einer Sitzung):
- **`visibilitychange` → hidden** und **`pagehide`**: sofortiges Flushen noch nicht bestätigter Änderungen (Best effort).
- **Zurückkehren in den Tab**: eigene Änderungen sichern + Serverstand nachladen und mergen.
- **Periodischer Wächter (alle 5 s)**: hängende/fehlgeschlagene Writes erneut versuchen und den Serverstand über `applyRemote` abgleichen (holt verpasste Live-Events auf).

Der bestehende Per-Team-Merge greift bei jedem Nachladen weiter, sodass nichts überschrieben wird. Im Ruhezustand entsteht nur ein leichtgewichtiger Select alle 5 s pro Gerät.

## Änderungen
- `store.tsx`: neuer Sicherungsnetz-Effect mit `flush()`/`pull()`, Event-Listenern und Intervall.

Build/Typecheck (`npm run build`) grün.

author: sam123ben
body:
Fixes the `v.map is not a function` crash on `/admin/apps/homechef/analytics`.

## Root cause

The page broke *specifically when there was no data to show*. Full chain, reproduced before changing anything:

1. A Go handler returns a **nil slice** — `var activities []Activity` — which marshals to JSON `null`, not `[]`.
2. The gateway did `NextResponse.json(data ?? {})`, rewriting that `null` into **`{}`** — an object.
3. The page's `activity.data ?? []` did **not** catch it: `{}` is neither null nor undefined.
4. `activities.length === 0` did not catch it either — `undefined !== 0`.
5. `activities.map(...)` threw.

```js
const fromGo   = null;            // nil slice
const gateway  = fromGo ?? {};    // => {}
const activities = gateway ?? []; // => {}  (nullish default does not fire)
activities.length === 0           // false
activities.map(a => a)            // TypeError: activities.map is not a function
```

## Fixes

**Gateway (the important one).** Forwards the body unchanged. `null` is a valid JSON body, and forwarding it lets every caller's own `?? []` work as written. This was **not analytics-specific** — the substitution corrupted the shape of every empty response passing through the gateway, so this was latent for any future page consuming a bare list.

**Page.** Uses `Array.isArray(...)` instead of `?? []`. The upstream causes are fixed, but a page should not crash on a shape it did not expect.

## Scope check

Analytics is the **only** HomeChef admin page consuming a bare array (`useSWR<Activity[]>`). Every other page reads the `{data, pagination}` envelope via `data?.data ?? []`, where the nullish default was already correct — they were surviving the gateway bug by luck rather than contract, and are now correct by contract too.

## Companion change

`Home-Chef-App@1d2680c5` fixes the API side so these endpoints emit `[]` rather than `null` — including `GetUsers`, `GetChefs` and the admin order list, which were sending `{"data": null}` for the same reason.

Either fix alone resolves the crash; both together make the contract right at each layer.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` clean. Crash chain reproduced before the fix and confirmed resolved after.

author: doruchiulan
body:
Rebuilds the automations editor around **values you can name and reuse**. Closes #234.

The plan proposed six PRs; the work landed coherently on one branch, so this is the whole feature.

## What changed

- **Every text field in an automation is one field.** `TriggerTextField` replaces the old chip fields: `$name` references, `/` skills and `@` files all fire from the same trigger engine the chat composer uses.
- **A Set value step names a result once**, and later steps type `$name`. Renaming that value rewrites every step that referred to it. Write `${name}` where a bare `$name` would run into surrounding text, as in `todo/${id}`.
- **Each step that produces a value carries its own name** (`outputName`), so reordering steps no longer silently repoints a reference at a different step. Two values sharing a name is reported as an error on **both**, rather than one quietly winning.
- **Webhook triggers register from the editor**, which now shows the signing secret alongside the URL — without it a registered hook rejected every delivery. The secret is returned once on register and revealed on request; reads are structurally incapable of returning it.
- **Problems are reported on the step that caused them**, including the ones the daemon finds at save time (previously a toast). A reference to a name nothing defines is a **warning**, not an error, so a prompt containing `$HOME` no longer blocks saving.
- **One-off (`once`) schedules**, plus the daemon/types groundwork for automation variables.

## Plan

`docs/plans/2026-07-25-todo-234-automations-editor-plan.md` (route `no-spec` — the brief is the spec, no PM stage).

## Product decisions (the user's, taken during the design pass)

1. **Automation text fields behave exactly like the real composer**, including `/` and `@`, with `$` added for variables — the trigger engine was adapted rather than a second mechanism built.
2. **`$name` is plain text, not a chip.** Fields are textareas; losslessness lives on the wire, not in the rendering.

## Planner decisions

1. Route 1 — lift the composer's trigger engine rather than re-implement it.
2. `$` namespace semantics: one flat namespace per automation.
3. Dotted digging (`$result.field`) stays supported.
4. Stale-chip language dropped from the UI copy.
5. `ChipText` stays the wire shape (mobile-co-owned contract, additive only).
6. Webhook **Register** is a real daemon route, not a client-side URL construction.
7. Structural pickers (if-condition left side, repeat list) keep the `TokenRef` model — only prose fields moved to `$name`.
8. `MoreOptions` survives for AskMe/Notify.
9. Rename-rewrite covers `set_variable` names only.

## Review verdicts

`reviewer` + `quality-reviewer` ran on `git diff main...HEAD`; all must-fix findings were routed back and fixed in `82f5ac0b` (naming model, lossless round trip, `${name}` delimited form, unresolved-name warning downgrade, webhook secret handling). A follow-up audit pass caught leftovers the reviews missed — three orphaned `TokenPicker` props and five stale `ChipField` comments — fixed in `860b9a9a`.

## QA (8 scenarios, live Rust daemon on an isolated data dir)

| # | Scenario | Result |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Naming survives reordering (the core defect) | **PASS** — verified twice, second time on current HEAD |
| S2 | Round trip lossless | **PASS** — structural token parts survive persistence |
| S3 | `${name}` delimited form | **PASS** — braced mid-word ref persists; `todo/$agent_result` stays literal, as designed |
| S4 | Duplicate names reported | **PASS** — daemon flags **both** step ids |
| S5 | Unresolved name warns, doesn't block | **PASS** — `$HOME` warns, Save enabled |
| S6 | Webhook signing secret | **PASS** — shown once, same on re-register, absent from DOM/record/list route after reload |
| S7 | Composer parity `/` `@` `$` | **PARTIAL** → fixed in `cf4c7f56` |
| S8 | Nothing else broke | **PASS** — schedules (incl. one-off), add/delete/reorder/save/cancel |

No scenario failed. Two expectations QA couldn't express as written: "change nothing, save" (Save is correctly disabled while clean) and "chips/pills" (this rebuild deliberately replaced chips with text).

**S7's defect, fixed here:** fields belonging to no agent step took the first *installed* adapter, and only Claude answers the skills route — so with Codex installed first, `/` opened nothing in Notify, Set value and action inputs. The fallback now tries each installed adapter until one answers.

## Known gaps, not fixed here

- **Duplicate-name copy overlap.** Typing a name another value already uses is refused at the keystroke, so the step stays unnamed and its card also says "Give this value a name." Both messages are true and the pane explains the real cause. Committing the duplicate instead would make a rename round trip lossy (`x` → `summary` → `x` would rewrite references that meant the *other* `summary`), so the refusal is deliberate.
- **A registered webhook reads as unregistered after reload** — the editor seeds from the list route, which omits `registration`. Re-registering is idempotent and returns the same URL and secret. This is also what makes the secret provably absent after reload; documented in `WebhookTriggerCard.tsx`.
- **Pre-existing, out of scope:** a project-scoped automation can't be saved on a cold load until a project is clicked (the editor reads `store.activeProjectId` instead of the record's own `projectId`). Traced to `6ffd7eca` (#465), which predates this branch — worth its own todo.
- `engine/test_support.rs` is 344 lines, over the 300 cap (already 322 at the merge base).
- Intra-step name collisions still suffix by position (`pr_list` / `pr_list_2`) — deliberate, since a step's own outputs never reorder. An `ask_agent` `expects` key colliding with a `set_variable` name isn't expressible via a per-step ordinal.
- `SetValueConfig`'s keystroke check stays scope-only — a strict subset of `validate`'s, so it never refuses a name `validate` would accept.
- M10 has no automated test (`ComposerInputPluginBridge` isn't exported); lane B skipped N4 (server-side `hookId` uniqueness) and the panel-facing last-rejection reason; lane C's M9 derives `persisted` from the store rather than a prop.

## Verification

UI typecheck clean · `TriggerTextField` 12/12, `TokenPicker` + `ConditionRow` 19/19 · prettier clean on every touched file · changeset included.

author: lzehrung
body:
## Summary

First implementation slice of the [cross-cutting performance program](docs/plans/2026-07-25-performance-program-index.md): git plan Priority 0 + hydrate plan Priority 0. Both are coupled (the git fix determines which code path the bloom fix runs on), so they ship together.

## What changed

**`src/indexer/build-index.ts` / `build-cache/project-snapshot.ts` / `build-cache.ts`**

1. **Untracked-file fast-path gate.** An untracked file already present in the manifest no longer unconditionally disables the whole-snapshot fast path. Git has no diff history for untracked files, so freshness is proven with a single cheap `stat()` comparison against the file's persisted `${mtimeMs}:${size}` signature prefix instead. Unseen files and stat-mismatched files still block the fast path exactly as before.

2. **Persisted bloom filter reuse.** `tryLoadPersistedBloomFilters()` reads the last-written snapshot's bloom section directly (skipping the whole-snapshot identity check that whole-snapshot reuse requires — a bloom filter is a pure function of file text, so it's safe to reuse once cache-hit status has already proven the file's content is unchanged). Applied to both the incremental and full-build cache-hit loops.

## Why the plan text changed mid-implementation

Both original plan sketches turned out to be subtly wrong once I traced the actual code paths:

- The git plan proposed gating on `Object.hasOwn(trackedEntries, file)` alone ("already in the manifest"). That's **unsafe**: it would silently serve a stale snapshot if an already-known untracked file's content changed, since git has no mechanism to prove otherwise for untracked files. Caught this before shipping via a dedicated regression test.
- The hydrate plan's "warm run with zero changed files" framing was already fast before this change, via a pre-existing early-return path (confirmed by an existing, already-passing test). The real gap is a **genuine partial incremental update** — some files changed, most didn't — where the whole-snapshot early return can't fire and the per-file loop used to rebuild every unchanged file's bloom filter from source anyway.

Both plan docs are updated in this PR to describe what shipped, not what was originally sketched.

## Verification

- 3 new regression tests in `tests/cache-invalidation.test.ts`, each confirmed to **fail on the pre-fix code** and pass with the fix (including the near-miss stale-content case).
- Full suite: `npm run test:fast` → 210 files / 2419 tests / 2 skipped, no regressions.
- `npx eslint` clean on all touched files.
- Manually verified end-to-end with isolated fixtures before writing tests (instrumented the compiled output, traced the real code path in 5+ scenarios).
- Real measurement: warm `orient` on this repository with one routine untracked file present: **905ms → 734ms**.

## Docs

- `docs/plans/2026-07-25-git-subprocess-elimination.md` and `docs/plans/2026-07-25-warm-index-hydrate-costs.md` Priority 0 sections marked implemented with corrected acceptance criteria and measured results.
